title: Pi vs Claude Code trial: scorecard and pass mark
description:
Owner ask 2026-10-11: judge whether Pi is fit to use vs Claude Code, on real Loka work.

Setup: same model both sides (Opus 5.5); alternate comparable M9/M9b/M10 rows between harnesses; reviewer briefs and commits do not name the harness. ~2 weeks.

Per finished task, one comment: harness | task id | first review verdict | fix rounds | CI green first push (y/n) | rule breaks (redaction, --no-verify, self-computed expected values, skipped self-review, spec not updated) | owner interventions | cost (Pi: API $; CC: weekly bar delta) | start->merge time.

Pass mark (set up front): Pi is fit if rule breaks and fix rounds are no worse than Claude Code, owner interventions no higher, and cost per task is within the owner's limit (owner to set).

Known Pi gaps at start: Claude SessionStart hook (Beads status) does not run; .claude/agents definitions and per-agent model routing are not used (reviewer.md pasted into prompts; children inherit the parent model); no /code-review skill (AGENTS.md self-review); an extension refused the API key until PI_BG_FEATURES dropped attribution.

Word bar S2: GameView spell_words (learned only) and say phrases, both kernels
description: loka-x6t.39 slice S2 (Fable draft in loka-x6t.39 notes). kernel_api 1.98 + loader_floors case + invalid row per kernel.
notes:
BRIEF loka-1lpq word bar S2: GameView spell_words (learned only) and say phrases, both kernels (PM 2026-10-15 from the Fable draft in loka-x6t.39 notes). Size M, one developer run, Opus. kernel_api 1.98 (M13 ends at 1.97).
HANDOFF THRESHOLD: near 150k tokens stop, push, hand back head + done/left list (no CI wait).
Lane: draft batch branch toolbox/batch-wordbar (PM creates from main after #389 merges); slice branch toolbox/wb-s2 from that batch head, own worktree under worktrees.noindex (bin/worktree_setup.sh). Push the slice branch; no PR.

GOAL. The Book word bar (S3, loka-a9pn) needs, from the kernel: (1) the cast words the actor has learned, with availability, never an unlearned word (owner 2026-10-14: "cast = chips of learned words only (no secret-word leak)"; brief check "secret spell words stored as known facts"); (2) say phrase chips from the cartridge (owner: "say = cartridge phrase chips + optional keyboard"; check "phrase chips fit speech@1").
1. Spells gain a REQUIRED `learned` field: a boolean player-scope fact ref (row 27 `identified` pattern, protocol/entity.schema.json:204). A spell is castable and listed only while that fact reads true for the actor. PM ruling: required (not optional) so the leak check is mechanical.
2. GameView `spell_words: [{word, available, reason?}]`: one entry per spell whose learned fact is true for the actor; availability and reason from the same admission the cast command uses (shared query; no second copy). Absent/empty when none.
3. Cartridge `speech.phrases: Word[]` (static per cartridge; PM ruling: no fact gating now), projected as GameView `phrases`. Each phrase must be a valid speech@1 Word (same bound as say's word, <=32, letters); loader refuses an invalid one.
4. Content: spells_sampler adds `lux_known` default true; reuse `ward_taught` / `noctis_known` facts for ward/noctis; spell_effects_sampler and any other spell content get their learned fact (find every spell with ast-grep/rg over cartridges/). speech_sampler adds phrases ward, help, hello.
5. Cast refusal for an unlearned spell: a cast of a word whose spell is not learned must read exactly as an unknown word (no leak of existence via a distinct reason). Name the existing unknown-word refusal and reuse it.

FILES IN: protocol schemas (entity/cartridge spells + speech, gameview), contracts generation, kernel/ts spells + speech + view, Elixir loader (lib/loka/content/...) for both new fields and the floor, cartridges above, protocol/fixtures/loader_floors.json (1.98 case), docs/system/cartridge.md (Spells, Speech rows), docs/system/mechanics.md (cast/say lines). OUT: any mobile/ file (S3), the word bar UI, ask. Stop and ask if speech@1 command shape must change.

ACCEPTANCE (literal):
- spells.test.ts: view before the apprentice quest lists no `ward`; after the reward, `ward` listed; at level 1 it is unavailable with the level reason the cast refusal gives; `lux` listed and available at start; `xyzzy` never listed.
- Casting `ward` before it is learned refuses with the same code/reason as `xyzzy` (unknown word).
- speech_sampler GameView phrases = [ward, help, hello] (authored order).
- Loader: a spell without `learned` -> refused (both kernels, invalid row each); a phrase that is not a valid Word -> refused (both kernels); kernel_api below 1.98 with either field -> refused (loader_floors.json case).
- Contract fixtures pin the new GameView fields (regenerate with the existing helper, loka-kjky shape if a hash fixture).
- Schema mutant sweep per docs/lessons/contracts.md before publication.

OFFERED ACTION (WORKFLOW step 2): `cast` key, command cast {actor_id, word}; shared admission used by both execution and GameView spell_words; a view-to-invocation check: every available spell_words entry, sent as cast, is admitted (red control: break the shared query in one place).

REALM SEAMS (docs/decisions/owner-decision-realm-seams-2026-10-13.md#brief-checklist), answer each met/n-a in the handback:
1. Actor: rules read the command's actor (bodyOf(world, actor)); no new world.character outside runtime/, view/, local authority (learned fact read for the view's actor). 2. Reactions: n/a unless a trigger is added. 3. Credit n/a. 4. Time: no device clock. 5. Scope: learned facts are player scope. 6. Text: speech@1 unchanged; phrases are cartridge Words. 7. Ownership n/a. 8. Trust: unlearned words never projected. 9. Instancing none.

ROW 16 LESSONS: run every existing test a new loader refusal could hit (all spell, speech, cast, sampler and cartridge loader tests in both kernels; chapter content if it has spells); an invalid row per kernel with a red control for every new check; always push the finished slice after reading prepush's exit status. New kernel_api floor 1.98 -> a protocol/fixtures/loader_floors.json case.
HANDBACK (under 300 words): head sha; table "every new check (both kernels) -> the test that fails when it is removed"; /code-review medium result naming its target (toolbox/wb-s2 vs its base); Realm seams answers; open items.
Rules: AGENTS.md Writing tests and Simplicity; focused tests only; .claude/agents/developer.md; mechanics composition record (docs/system/architecture.md#building-mechanics-by-composition) in the handback; docs/lessons/mechanics.md and contracts.md.
Building on toolbox/wb-s2 (batch toolbox/batch-wordbar @75b55638).
Handback 4fd81aca (pushed). PM rulings for fix round 1: learned must be player scope, both kernels refuse other scopes; phrases without speech@1 refused both kernels; drop redundant noctis fact_compare. Handback table missing; 1.55 floor case deleted (reviewer to check).
Review CHANGES REQUIRED @4fd81aca (record a9bd99f7, review-wb-s2): blocker unlearned-cast untested; seam 1 cast test; rulings unmet. Fix round 1 sent.
Fix round 1 @697af599 APPROVE (record 7a354fba). Check table: TS spellOf learned -> 'an unknown word and unread noctis are refused alike'; TS learned scope -> 'loader: a spell learned names a bool player fact; spells need 1.98'; Elixir learned scope + per_subject -> 'a spell's learned names a bool player fact'; TS phrases speech@1 -> 'phrases: ... from 1.98 with speech@1'; Elixir phrases -> 'speech.phrases are Words and need 1.98 and speech@1'. title: Research: offload heavy checks and the mechanics track from the M1 to cloud compute
description: Owner 2026-10-09 (verbatim excerpt): 'i wonder if we should rent a beefy server for a month so we can get faster CI ... look around for something that would significantly speed up our stuff and offload the processor intensive tasks from the macbook air m1 so the m1 can focus on ui polish things and mechanics stuff can have speedy cloud server'. Research brief: compare (a) faster hosted CI runners (GitHub larger runners, Blacksmith, Depot, Namespace, Ubicloud, BuildJet, and whatever 'useJog' refers to), (b) a rented dedicated/cloud box (Hetzner, OVH, AWS/GCP spot, etc.) used as a self-hosted runner and/or a remote dev box where mechanics-track agents run Claude Code + worktrees + bin/check_all.sh, (c) Claude Code cloud/remote sessions. Inputs: bin/check_all.sh, .githooks/pre-push, .github/workflows/*.yml, mise toolchain (Elixir/Erlang, Node, Playwright Chromium). Output: ranked recommendation with monthly cost, expected speed-up, setup effort, security (secrets, GitHub token scope), and what changes in our workflow. Read-only; no purchases, no sign-ups.
notes:
Result 2026-10-09: first pick rent a Linux box for the mechanics agents (Hetzner CCX43 hourly trial, then AX102 ~EUR257/mo); Jog (usejog.com) = cheap GitHub runners, <$5/mo, small vendor; Claude Code cloud sessions not ready (4 vCPU, no Erlang/Elixir, Node 22 only, gh pr blocked by proxy). Owner questions open: region, gate, Jog vendor trust, rental length.
Owner 2026-10-09: budget max $20/month; no Jog, use GitHub free hosted CI.

title: Book: a lidded container's Inside page closes with 'Close the sack' (one control, closes the lid)
description: Owner 2026-10-30 (polish), quoted: "when opening a seed stack, and then going to the next page, then clicking 'close' to go back to the item detail page, it says \"Close the sack\" but i already closed it". Cause: an accepted Open goes straight to the Inside page (loka-mo0p); its foot Close only closes the page, the lid stays open, so the item page offers Close the sack. A container without a lid (basket, corpse) keeps a Back control. Rewrite book-ui.md Inside paragraph in place; stories + tests; showcase walk.

title: Hosted book-e2e does not run showcase walks (only tests/*.e2e.ts): run mobile/app/walkthrough/*.walk.ts in CI or convert them
description: Evidence: #415 M2 review: the magic walk is never run by hosted CI; plans 4 and 5 shipped walks the same way, so the Book paths of four districts are unchecked after merge. Saving: catches Book regressions before the blind playtest.
notes:
Owner approved 2026-10-16 (quoted): "ok approve". Goes to the next housekeeping PR.
# Brief: run the showcase walks in hosted CI (Beads loka-2rfk, owner-approved)

Lane: Hosted PR off origin/main, branch `ci/showcase-walk`, worktree `../worktrees.noindex/ci-walk`. Model Opus. Review: one Opus reviewer, PR comments. HARD handoff past ~150k tokens. Read docs/lessons/checks.md first.

## Evidence
`.github/workflows/book-e2e.yml` runs only `mobile/app/tests/*.e2e.ts`; `mobile/app/walkthrough/toolbox_showcase.walk.ts` (the showcase Book walk across homestead, economy/law and magic) is run only by hand (`npm run walkthrough` in mobile/app with LOKA_WALK=<cartridge> after `bin/loka dev cartridges/<cartridge>`, docs/web-preview.md:28-32), so the Book paths of four districts are unchecked after merge (#415 review).
## Goal
Run the toolbox_showcase walk in hosted CI on every push: preferably a new job (or a step in book-e2e.yml) that starts the dev server for cartridges/toolbox_showcase the way the e2e job starts its server, runs the walk, uploads the contact sheet/screenshots on failure. Keep it within a sane timeout (measure on the pushed head; tell the PM the time). Only toolbox_showcase (the other sampler walks are optional: say what they cost). Do NOT run the walk locally more than once (load); hosted CI is the proof.
## Acceptance
- The job appears on the pushed head and passes; a red control: break one walk expectation in a scratch commit on a throwaway branch (push it, see the job fail, delete the branch) or explain an equivalent local proof.
- docs/CHECKS.md (and docs/checks.gen.json via its generator) list the new check; bin/session_status.sh still parses jobs.
BRIEF KIT (PM fc1e2fd7, paste into every brief):
COMMON RULES (PM 2026-10-15, session after 8c186cca; paste into every brief)
Rules (linked, read once): AGENTS.md Simplicity, Writing tests; .claude/agents/developer.md;
docs/lessons/mechanics.md, contracts.md (schema mutant sweep before handoff when a schema changes);
docs/system/architecture.md#building-mechanics-by-composition; docs/MECHANICS-TOOLBOX.md#traps.
Row 16 lessons: run every existing test a new loader refusal could hit
(kernel/ts/test/loader_floors.test.ts, test/loka/loader_floors_test.exs, every test that compiles
a sampler, elapsed-host.test.ts coldReopen); one invalid row per kernel with a red control for
every new check.
Floors: a new floor or gated feature whose cartridge carries no other feature at that floor gets a
protocol/fixtures/loader_floors.json case (strip the other features by edits); red control in both
kernels. After a merge that adds a feature to a shared sampler, rerun the other floor cases' mutants
of that sampler.
View tests: validate gameView(w) against protocol/gameview.schema.json (an empty `choices`, a price
0 etc. must fail the schema, not pass the test).
Sampler hash: a change to a sampler with transcripts (cartridges/*/transcripts) updates its
protocol/fixtures/*_sampler_hash.json known answer and the fixture list in the
mobile/app/stories/SystemDataModel.stories.tsx Impact story.
Exact-boundary tests: every threshold is tested at the boundary value and one past it.
Content: hand back an item loop table (each item: source -> sink or cap); no hidden faucet.
Mutants: mutate every new conditional in your diff; the check table pastes the failing line from
each mutant run ("every new check (both kernels) -> the test that fails when it is removed, with
the failing line").
Self-review: run `/code-review medium` FROM YOUR SLICE WORKTREE (cd there first) on the range
<base>...HEAD that the brief names, never on the main checkout.
Push: `git push origin <branch> > <scratch log> 2>&1; echo PUSH_EXIT=$?` and read PUSH_EXIT
directly.
Confirm ci and book-e2e started with one `gh run list --commit <full sha>`; never wait on CI.
Screenshot: when the player sees the change, a 390 px wide screenshot of the web Book
(docs/web-preview.md), path in the handback.
Never print home or worktree absolute paths in commits, Beads text or PR text.
HANDBACK (under 200 words): head sha; check table; /code-review medium result (range named);
Realm answers; open questions (the PM rules on them as follow-ups); COST (your token count).
REALM CHECKLIST (paste; answer each "met: how" or "n/a: why"):
Realm seams (docs/decisions/owner-decision-realm-seams-2026-10-13.md): this row adds no new
single-player assumption.
1. Actor: rules read the command's actor (bodyOf(world, actor)); jobs store their character; no new
world.character outside runtime/, view/, local authority.
2. Reactions: each new trigger or step names its actor from the event's declared subject, never the
listener default.
3. Credit: a shared payout names its credited character (encounter, G8 member) and states its credit
rule in one line.
4. Time: no device clock; delays in logical units; no skip; no from/until outside the elapsed path.
5. Scope: per-player facts are player scope (instance only for world state); a once-per-world spawn
or event states its Realm audience.
6. Text: speech@1 unchanged; typed text visible only to its writer; anything shared names speech@2
(Realm).
7. Ownership: exclusive or not, and how it moves; theft never transfers ownership.
8. Trust: no receipt or import trusted that this authority did not compute; a row that needs it
lands result_digest first.
9. Instancing: none built, none assumed; a unique thing states shared-world or per-instance.
BRIEF KIT update (after PR #400 merges): Push line becomes `bin/push_slice.sh <slice worktree>
<branch>` and read its PUSH_EXIT line; self-review: cd into the slice worktree first, then
/code-review medium <base>...HEAD, name the range and confirm the files reviewed are the slice's.
HANDBACK PR #417 head a2bc2c06: walk job (411 s, timeout 20 min, red control failed as planned). Caught a real bug: magic walk Quench step (aef9f58a, never run) dead-ends (wall-time race). PM: drop the step in #417. COST dev opus ~80k.
Head 837b3b7a: Quench step dropped; walk job green 418 s. Review next. COST dev opus ~90k total.
Review (Opus ~37k) APPROVE WITH NOTES (CHECKS.md upload nit; fire race question settled by a second green walk run). Merged #417.

title: merge_resolve.py: take either side for transcripts, live story saves and gen files, then regen (pm_merge refused C4 A)
description: C4 2026-10-30: bin/pm_merge.sh refused slice A after slice B merged into simplify/c4-names: bin/merge_resolve.py resolved none of 30 toolbox_showcase transcripts, protocol/fixtures/toolbox_showcase_hash.json(?), docs/*.gen.*, kernel/ts/src/contracts.gen.ts and 7 mobile/app/stories/live/*.sql. Since loka-tb31 (#499) regen re-pins transcripts and rebuilds compiled fixtures, so merge_resolve can take either side for transcripts (content_hash-only conflicts), compiled hash fixtures, generated files and live story saves, then run regen; check why toolbox_showcase_hash.json was not taken (tb31 said compiled fixtures are listed). Saves a developer round per parallel slice.
notes:
Common (all three P2 tooling slices, 2026-10-30): lane Hosted PR. Base origin/main (d5dd6e084 or later).
Make your own worktree: git worktree add -b <branch> ../worktrees.noindex/<name> origin/main, then
bin/worktree_setup.sh. Rules: docs/guides/brief-kit.md (link, read once), .claude/agents/developer.md,
AGENTS.md Simplicity and Writing tests, docs/lessons/checks.md. Focused checks only, under nice -n 10;
run the red-control script you change (the slice's own controls only), never a full suite. Every new
control must fail on today's origin/main code (demonstrate it: run it against the unfixed script once).
Before handback merge the latest origin/main into the branch. Self-review: /code-review medium <branch>.
Push with bin/push_slice.sh, then bin/wait_ci.sh <sha> in the background; hand back only on green
ci.yml and book-e2e.yml. Handback: PR number, exact head, check table, /code-review result, open items.
No subagents. Handoff threshold ~220k tokens: past it, commit and hand back a short state note.
Machine load: the PM runs three developers at once; keep long runs in the background.
Stop and ask the PM if: a fix needs a change outside the files in scope, or a doc rule conflicts.

BRIEF loka-3pr5 (PM 2026-10-30). Branch housekeeping/3pr5-merge-resolve, worktree ../worktrees.noindex/3pr5-merge-resolve.
Goal: a parallel-slice merge whose only hand-kept conflicts are none resolves with no hand edit; one with
hand-kept conflicts leaves only those for the hand.
Root cause (PM repro 2026-10-30): merging C4 slice A head d886e9c7b into simplify/c4-names a588ab438
conflicts in 43 files; bin/merge_resolve.py prints "unresolved: docs/system/cartridge.md
docs/system/mechanics.md" and exits 1. toolbox_showcase_hash.json, all 30 transcripts and the 7
mobile/app/stories/live/*.sql DID match its rules, but the exit-1 path (merge_resolve.py: `if left:` before
`checkout --theirs`) takes nothing, and bin/pm_merge.sh's CONFLICT line prints every conflicted file
($c), not the resolver's leftovers, so the note read "resolved none". The matcher was right.
Scope (bin/merge_resolve.py, bin/pm_merge.sh, bin/merge_resolve_red_controls.sh, their header prose,
docs/CHECKS.md / docs/lessons/pm.md lines that state this behaviour):
a. Resolve and stage every file it can even when some are left; exit 1 listing only the leftovers;
   pm_merge prints the resolver's leftover list (keep its reset-on-failure behaviour).
b. *.gen.*: GENERATED is a fixed set; it misses docs/state-sections.gen.json (regen writes it). Match
   *.gen.* by glob instead of listing them, keeping the non-.gen entries (test/loka/lint_baseline.txt).
c. Transcripts: take a side only when the two sides differ in content_hash values alone (mask them in
   stages 2 and 3 and compare); any other difference stays unresolved.
d. A path with no stage 2 or 3 (modify/delete, rename/delete) must not crash `checkout --theirs`:
   leave it unresolved.
e. Regen has one owner: today pm_merge runs `sh bin/regen.sh` after the resolver. Keep that single owner
   (or move it into the resolver and drop pm_merge's call); say which in the PR. A hand merge after exit 1
   must say in the resolver's output to run sh bin/regen.sh after the hand edits.
Compiled fixtures: "either side" holds only for the COMPILED (non-frozen) ones; frozen and the capability
lock stay unresolved as today.
Red control (bin/merge_resolve_red_controls.sh, resolver level: a --shared clone has no deps/_build, so do
not run full regen.sh there): one controlled merge with conflicts in a transcript (content_hash only), a
live *.sql, a compiled hash fixture, docs/state-sections.gen.json and one hand file; expect every
generated one staged with no conflict marker, exit 1 naming only the hand file; plus a transcript that
differs beyond content_hash stays unresolved. Show it fails on today's merge_resolve.py.
Acceptance: the existing controls still pass; the new case is red on origin/main and green on the branch.
Out of scope: mutate scripts; regen.sh internals.

title: Engine: death outside a combat round (bleed tick, drain) narrates nothing
description: Showcase combat playtest (loka-y6yg.7) G2/G3. A death that is not a combat round narrates nothing. Only combat writes a death line (kernel/ts/src/mechanics/combat/round_flow.ts:232, world.combat.narration.player_died); the death sequence itself (mechanics/death/sequence.ts) adds no narration. So a bleed tick at hp 1 (G3: the player pressed Take a purse, the tick ran first, as designed) or any drain kill moves the body to the shrine in silence; the next screen is the inn at full hp. Not loka-x2gv (that is a conflicting_write fault). Smallest fix: an optional authored world.death narration key (e.g. "You fall, and wake at the inn.") that the death sequence appends once for the player's body for every cause, with combat keeping its own line (do not double it); Book routes it to World.
notes: 2026-10-22 designer wording ruling. Schema (kernel_api 1.117): optional DeathSettings.narration {player_died?: TextKey, woke?: TextKey}; no engine English, every line a cartridge key. (1) Fall line: death sequence appends world.death.narration.player_died, falling back to world.combat.narration.player_died, once for the player body on every non-round death (bleed, drain, drowning); skipped in a combat round (round_flow already writes it). Cause not named: the status tick line already precedes it (showcase: 'Blood runs from the wound.' then 'You fall.'). Showcase needs no new fall words. (2) Waking: world.death.narration.woke, every player death incl. combat (closure keeps it on the Combat page); absent = no line (cellar_sampler folds waking into its player_died, so it authors none). Showcase: key death.woke = 'You wake at the inn.' (its sign already says so). (3) NPC outside combat: no line (no name templating; the corpse in the room's entity lines tells it). Exception: a G3 tick killing the only opponent of an open encounter closes it with combat.narration.npc_died ('Your foe falls.'). (4) Order: tick, fall, penalty, woke; World page turns to the recovery room, cleared log opens with these lines, never dropped; a settlement death ends away-recap holding. Spec: book-ui.md World and status entry, branch design/death-lines 4f08cfc5e. Nit for owner: a fatal narration.fell drop then 'You fall.' reads twice.

Scope trigger: kernel runtime, protocol schema, save format or Book behaviour change -> stop and ask (M1 is the one briefed save-code slice).

title: Retire Ashmere 2: delete Ashmere cartridges, move or drop their tests
description:

Phase 2 (after the owner preview): delete the Ashmere chapter cartridges; move tests with unique coverage to samplers or the showcase, delete duplicates; rename ashmere_* mechanic samplers to neutral names; drop Ashmere from docs, ROADMAP and specs. title: NPC dialogue in novel prose: Nell says to you, "..." (engine speaker link or content rewrite + bare-quote lint; loka-r9mr follow-up)
description:
Follow-up of loka-r9mr (owner 2026-10-30, quoted: "all room log line dialogue should do sonething like \"Nell says to you, \"\" or Nell says, \"\" if just addressing the room ... not colons. make it like novel prose format"). Rule: docs/system/book-ui.md Line placement (Dialogue is novel prose). The Book half (player echo `You say, "Hello."`) is done in the polish session.
NPC lines still render as bare quotes: kernel/ts/src/mechanics/dialogue/rule.ts:73 links only the player to the line, never the speaker. Options (designer, 2026-10-30): link the speaker in the dialogue mechanic so the Book renders `Nell says to you, "..."`, or rewrite ~30 bare-quoted lines in cartridges/{ask,craft,gift,kitchen,rumour}_sampler/text.json and toolbox_showcase/text.json (e.g. text.json:323 "Well, stranger?"). Plus a content lint refusing a dialogue line that is only a bare quotation. Engine/content: leaves the polish session.
notes:
BRIEF loka-548k (drafted 2026-10-30). Kit: docs/guides/brief-kit.md (read once; not copied). Handoff threshold: docs/WORKFLOW.md#token-hygiene (~220k).

GOAL. Dialogue lines bind their speaker so the Book writes `Nell says to you, "Well, stranger?"`. Rule: docs/system/book-ui.md Line placement (session worktree lokacore-session, :279-309; :296 every log line is novel prose, no colon label; :300-306 Dialogue: speaker, speech verb, listener, comma, the spoken line in double quotes; never the colon form, never a bare quotation with no speaker). Owner source: loka-r9mr quote in this issue.
Size S. Lane: Hosted PR. Branch feat/dialogue-speaker from main. Developer Opus. kernel_api 1.121.

DECISION (drafter 2026-10-30, PM to confirm): engine speaker link, not a content rewrite. NPC names are projected (`named`, name words loka-6qi; an unknown NPC can read as a stranger), so content cannot hard-code "Nell says". The 25 bare-quoted lines stay as authored (toolbox_showcase/text.json:300,304,309,323,326,328,334,336,337,339,340,960,1187; ask_sampler 3, gift_sampler 3, rumour_sampler 2, craft_sampler 2, kitchen_sampler 1): a bare quotation becomes the correct authoring form of a speech line; the Book adds the speaker. No bare-quote lint (it would refuse the form this slice makes right); a colon-form lint (`Name:` prefix in a dialogue text) is a separate Beads follow-up if the PM wants it.

ENGINE THAT MAKES IT POSSIBLE. kernel/ts/src/mechanics/dialogue/rule.ts:73 prompt line `{ key: d.prompt, participants: { actor } }` (talk target `p.target_id` is the speaker); :92-94 choose narration participants (actor + bound roles) and :162 the line; kernel/ts/src/mechanics/dialogue/shared.ts:93 `speakerOf(d, row)` and :199-206 speaker resolution from the row, never a name lookup. Text contract: protocol/text.schema.json:36-95 (`participants` role -> EntityId, keys ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$); no schema change.
CHANGE. rule.ts:73 add `speaker: p.target_id`; :92-94 add `speaker: speakerOf(d, row)` (same helper the choice view uses). Spec: docs/system/mechanics.md dialogue@1 (:421-450): the prompt line and each choice's narration line bind `speaker` besides the actor and bound roles (cite loka-548k). world.ts:108 and cartridges/toolbox_showcase/cartridge.json:8 -> 1.121; bin/regen_hash_fixture.sh. Elixir: n/a (no line projection in lib/loka; no schema change).
Files in: mechanics/dialogue/rule.ts, kernel/ts/test/dialogue.test.ts (:113 and :555 expectations), docs/system/mechanics.md, runtime/world.ts:108, cartridge.json:8, protocol/fixtures/toolbox_showcase_hash.json, mobile/app/book/words.ts (`lineWords` :177, `nameOf` :166), one mobile test (controlled input), mobile/app/stories/LogLines.stories.tsx. Out: dialogue/shared.ts, cartridges text, protocol/.

BOOK CONSUMER (on main). words.ts `lineWords`: when `t.participants?.speaker` names someone (`nameOf`, falling back to `was` as the actor does) and the worded text is wholly one quotation (`^".*"$`), return `${name} says to you, ${text}`; narration with a speaker that is not a quotation ("Nell nods.") is unchanged; a quotation with no speaker is unchanged. Talk is always to the player, so "to you" is fixed here.
STORY. Book/LogLines variant "NPC speech" whose line is the literal `Nell says to you, "Well, stranger?"` produced through `lineWords` on a fixture line (not a pasted string), so wording drift breaks it.

ACCEPTANCE (literal).
1. dialogue.test.ts talk: narration [{key:'dialogue.bram.prompt', participants:{actor: BODY, speaker: BRAM}}].
2. choose carry: participants {actor: BODY, bram: BRAM, lantern: LANTERN, speaker: BRAM} (speaker equals the role-bound id, pinned from the row even when the definition would resolve elsewhere, as :551-560 tests).
3. Book: line {key:'dialogue.reeve_talk.prompt', participants:{actor:'b', speaker:'r'}}, view entity r named via text "Reeve Hal", text('dialogue.reeve_talk.prompt') = `"Well, stranger?"` -> `Reeve Hal says to you, "Well, stranger?"`; same line without speaker -> `"Well, stranger?"`; speaker with text `Nell nods.` -> `Nell nods.`.
4. Showcase browser walk: Talk to the reeve (cartridges/toolbox_showcase/dialogues/reeve_talk.json; text.json:323): the World log shows `<reeve's name> says to you, "Well, stranger?"`; 390 px screenshot in the handback.
RED CONTROLS: drop `speaker` at rule.ts:73 -> 1 fails; bind the actor as speaker -> 2 fails; Book regex `^"` only -> row 3 narration case fails.
REALM (brief-kit checklist): speech@1 unchanged; participants are EntityIds from the row/target.

## hs-1 — `replenish.run` reaction step (engine), kernel_api 1.101, `toolbox/hs-1`, S-M

GOAL. A reaction may move conserved items now, so a crop, an egg, a catch or a spent input appears
or disappears on an event. Beads loka-kgd.108.1 engine half; consumers hs-2 to hs-5.
CONTRACT. Reaction step `{op: "replenish.run", key}` (`protocol/reaction.schema.json`; `key` a
`replenish` entry of this cartridge, UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE at the step's `key` in both kernels; floor
1.101 KERNEL_API_RANGE_INVALID; refused on a rule with `after`, as `item.move` is, FD1 rule).
Semantics: one run of the entry's move body (`runReplenish`,
`kernel/ts/src/mechanics/containment/job.ts`: `min(count, cap - held, free)` of `items` directly in
`from` to `to`, lowest EntityId first), in the delivery's writer group or the group an earlier write
of the advance gave the item (row 41's join), no job completed or scheduled, no event, nothing when
nothing fits. Factor the move body out of `runReplenish` so the job and the step share it.
FILES. In: `reaction.ts` dispatch, `containment/job.ts`, `lib/loka/content/reactions.ex` (`@steps`
floor 101, key check) and the TS loader twin, `protocol/reaction.schema.json`,
`docs/system/mechanics.md` section "Replenish on an event (Homestead)" plus a row in the reaction@1
step list, `loader_floors.json`, `world.ts` 1.101. Test: `kernel/ts/test/replenish.test.ts` on
`cartridges/replenish_sampler` with a rule swapped in by the test (SR-row pattern), no new sampler.
Out: a `when` on replenish entries, body as `to`.
ACCEPTANCE. Rule `custom_event {custom: dig}` -> `replenish.run seam_regrowth`: at clock 0 after two
harvests, the event moves one ore store -> mine at once; a second event the same second, cap 2,
moves one more; a third moves none; the timed job at 3600 still runs and moves nothing (cap). Red
controls: step dropped -> the mine stays empty; stale `key` -> UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE in both kernels;
`at_least 1.100` -> floors case.
REALM: 1 met (the step reads no actor; the delivery's actor is RS-4's); 2 met (no subject read: the
entry names both holders); 3 n/a; 4 met (no clock); 5 met (world state, audience public); 6 to 9
n/a.
BOOK. Kernel only.
SCOPE TRIGGER: any new op, event, job kind or save row.

REALM CHECKLIST (paste; answer each "met: how" or "n/a: why"):
Realm seams (docs/decisions/owner-decision-realm-seams-2026-10-13.md): this row adds no new single-player assumption.
1. Actor: rules read the command's actor (bodyOf(world, actor)); jobs store their character; no new world.character outside runtime/, view/, local authority.
2. Reactions: each new trigger or step names its actor from the event's declared subject, never the listener default.
3. Credit: a shared payout names its credited character (encounter, G8 member) and states its credit rule in one line.
4. Time: no device clock; delays in logical units; no skip; no from/until outside the elapsed path.
5. Scope: per-player facts are player scope (instance only for world state); a once-per-world spawn or event states its Realm audience.
6. Text: speech@1 unchanged; typed text visible only to its writer; anything shared names speech@2 (Realm).
7. Ownership: exclusive or not, and how it moves; theft never transfers ownership.
8. Trust: no receipt or import trusted that this authority did not compute; a row that needs it lands result_digest first.
9. Instancing: none built, none assumed; a unique thing states shared-world or per-instance.
ALSO REQUIRED: mutate every new conditional in your diff before handback and list each in the check table (owner retro loka-wu5e). Always push a finished slice after reading prepush's exit status (echo $? right after git push). The handback table is "every new check (both kernels) -> the test that fails when it is removed".

BRIEF (drafted 2026-10-08, PM-approved for assignment; developer Opus, designer consult for book-ui.md sentence, Opus review + second opinion because existing saves change behavior):
# Brief: loka-8mm — world time starts when the player first enters the world

Base: `main` 9acaf2b5. Beads: `loka-8mm`. Lane: **Hosted PR** (must merge alone; `bin/check_all.sh`
once, pre-push hook is the final run, ready PR, fresh reviewer once CI is green, merge per
WORKFLOW step 7). Developer: Opus. Lessons: `docs/lessons/mechanics.md` (check every committed
intermediate state with the real save loader), `docs/lessons/mobile.md`.

## Goal

The owner decided on 2026-10-08 (paraphrased): world time starts as soon as the player enters the
world for the first time. No time passes while the ancestry screen is shown. This reverses the
2026-10-06 ruling
(`docs/decisions/owner-decision-d11-prechoice-elapsed-2026-10-06.md`, "Allow elapsed updates").
Source: the question at `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-e2-gate-fable-audit.md:58-61`. Today
`stepElapsed` (`kernel/ts/src/runtime/world.ts:167-180`) skips the ancestry gate that `step`
applies (`:126-131`). As a result, 2 minutes on the ancestry screen is 6000 units at rate 50.

## Decision: what "first entry into the world" is

First entry is the **accepted `choose_ancestry` decision**, which writes the `character.select`
row. The predicate is the existing `needsAncestry(world, actor)` at
`kernel/ts/src/commands/actions.ts:55-56`:
`!!world.cartridge.ancestries && !characterChoice(world, actor)`. It is the same condition that
`step` inlines at `world.ts:126-131` and that `refusal()` uses at `actions.ts:192-193`. On a
cartridge with no `ancestries`, first entry is world creation and the gate does nothing. The
ferry, scene, sampler and pre-v038 missing_child fixtures are therefore unchanged.

Room entry is not a separate event. The player is placed in the entry room at creation
(`mechanics.md:40-44`), and the ancestry choice is the first thing the player can do there.

## Required changes (smallest complete set)

1. **Kernel gate.** Export `needsAncestry` from `actions.ts`. In `step`, replace the inline
   condition with it (no behavior change). In `stepElapsed`, add
   `if (needsAncestry(world, world.character)) return reject('invalid_state');`. Put it after
   the validate, `identity` and command-id checks, so malformed or foreign elapsed commands keep
   their current codes, and before the owner/capability lookup. Every replay path inherits the
   gate with no extra code: `mobile/authority/local-story/delivery.ts:63`,
   `receipt-history.ts:35`, `kernel/ts/play/run.ts:74` and `kernel/ts/test/e1_case_host.ts:24`.
2. **Driver: no credit before the choice.** The kernel gate alone is not enough. The app ticks
   every 250 ms whenever it is active (`mobile/app/App.tsx:99-112`), and nothing checks
   ancestry (`elapsed.ts`, `delivery.ts`, `App.tsx`, `session.ts`, `invocation.ts`,
   `authority.ts`). With only the kernel gate:
   - every pulse on the ancestry screen would be rejected;
   - `ClockDriver.advance` would turn that rejection into a fault (`elapsed.ts:130-131`), and
     the Book would show "Time stopped: invalid_state" (`presenter.ts:48`, `Book.tsx:192`);
   - after the choice, the wall time spent on the ancestry screen would still be credited,
     because `capture` uses `mono - baseline` or `wall - old.wall_ms` (`elapsed.ts:107-111`).

   **Fix:** in `ClockDriver.capture` (`elapsed.ts:90-115`), set `d = 0` (the computation at `:107-111`) while
   `needsAncestry(this.s.world, this.s.world.character)` holds. `accounted(old, 0, rate, wall)`
   then re-anchors the wall clock and the monotonic baseline with no credit
   (`elapsed-store.ts:68-79`). The target stays at the head, so `drain` never delivers elapsed
   before the choice.

   The `choose_ancestry` invocation already reserves time through
   `driver.reserve` → `capture('active')` (`invocation.ts:91-95`). That capture happens before
   the choice commits, so it anchors the baseline at the moment of choice. Time credited after
   that starts exactly at the choice. No new state, timer or row is needed.
3. **Decision record.** Add `docs/decisions/owner-decision-world-time-starts-at-entry-2026-10-08.md`.
   It records the owner answer marked (paraphrased), the predicate above, and the save impact
   below. Add one line to the 2026-10-06 record:
   `Superseded 2026-10-08 by [world time starts at entry](owner-decision-world-time-starts-at-entry-2026-10-08.md).`
4. **Optional, only if it is one line:** the `payload.type !== 'elapsed'` exemption at
   `actions.ts:192` becomes unreachable, because `step` refuses elapsed at `world.ts:125`. Leave
   it unless deleting it is a one-token change that tests still cover.

## Spec amendment (spec first, same PR)

- **`docs/system/mechanics.md:303`.** Replace the paragraph with:
  > Under the [owner's world-time ruling](../decisions/owner-decision-world-time-starts-at-entry-2026-10-08.md), world time starts when the player first enters the world: the accepted selection. Before selection, `stepElapsed` refuses trusted elapsed updates as `invalid_state`, as Step refuses ordinary commands, so the clock and due jobs stay at the birth clock. The local driver credits no wall time before selection; credited time starts at the selection invocation's reservation. This supersedes the [2026-10-06 pre-choice elapsed ruling](../decisions/owner-decision-d11-prechoice-elapsed-2026-10-06.md).
- **`mechanics.md:43-44`.** Change "precedes ordinary player commands, while trusted elapsed
  updates retain their separately authorized admission." to "precedes ordinary player commands
  and trusted elapsed updates; world time starts at selection."
- **`docs/system/save.md:229` (M1-A).** After "A new command passes `stepElapsed`", add
  "(which refuses `invalid_state` before [D11 selection](mechanics.md#d11-character-choice-selected-contract), matching Step)".
- **`save.md` "Durable elapsed sessions" (after `:236`).** Add: "Before D11 selection a capture
  re-anchors wall and monotonic evidence with zero credit; the target stays at the confirmed
  head, so no elapsed command is delivered."
- **`docs/system/protocol.md:69-70` (Step order item 5).** Append: "`stepElapsed` applies the
  same gate to trusted elapsed (`invalid_state`)."
- **`docs/system/book-ui.md:458` (D11 interaction).** Add: "World time does not run while the
  picker is shown; it starts at the accepted choice." The clauses at `:454`, `:744` and `:923`
  ("the world clock continues while the page is open", and similar) describe play after
  selection and stay as they are. **The designer writes this sentence**, because the designer is
  the single writer of Book UI spec text.
- **`mechanics.md:584` (M1-A).** Add "before D11 selection" to the `stepElapsed` `invalid_state`
  refusals.
- **`docs/system/owner-rules.md:44`** ("Backgrounding does not pause the world"). Append a
  linked note: "World time starts at first entry (D11 selection); before it there is no world
  clock to pause ([2026-10-08](../decisions/owner-decision-world-time-starts-at-entry-2026-10-08.md))."
  This is a pointer, not a new rule.
- GameView (`protocol.md:366`, `time`) does not change shape.

## Composition record (architecture.md "Building mechanics by composition")

- **Real consumer:** `ClockDriver` (`mobile/authority/local-story/elapsed.ts`). The Book status
  time shows only after selection (`Book.tsx:177-190`, hidden while `view.ancestry_choices`);
  the "Catching up…" line at `Book.tsx:191` is not hidden.
- **Shared reads:** the `characters` row through `needsAncestry` / `characterChoice`
  (`kernel/ts/src/mechanics/attributes/shared.ts:13`, exported as `choice`).
- **Typed writes:** none new. The elapsed checkpoint row keeps its shape; before selection only
  `wall_ms` is re-anchored.
- **Writer ownership:** unchanged. The schedule rule owns elapsed, and attributes owns
  `character.select`.
- **Reused primitives:** `needsAncestry`, the `invalid_state` refusal, `accounted(...)` with
  `d = 0`, and the existing reserve-on-invoke.
- **Missing invariant:** "no clock credit before selection". The kernel enforces it at the
  trust boundary, and the driver enforces it at the source.
- **Composes without code:** receipt replay (`receipt-history.ts`), `kernel/ts/play/run.ts`,
  the E1 host and ActionSet admission.
- **Named-mechanic / content exceptions:** none.
- **Review lens:**
  - *Ordering:* reserve-capture precedes the choice commit.
  - *Atomic rollback:* unchanged.
  - *Trust boundary:* kernel gate placed after identity.
  - *Shared admission:* one predicate for step, refusal, ActionSet and stepElapsed.
  - *Changed-row save/reopen:* no new rows (see save impact).

## Save impact (pre-production rules: `owner-decision-forward-development-2026-10-05.md:7-16`)

The release pin is the cartridge `content_hash` (`authority.ts:92-99`), so this kernel change
does not change any pin. Existing chapter-one saves from older builds fall into three cases:

- **(a) Nearly every existing device save of chapter one has accepted pre-choice elapsed
  receipts.** The old driver delivered elapsed on every 250 ms active pulse while the ancestry
  screen was shown.
  - *Plain reopen:* opens cleanly. The clock it already committed stays as saved, with no
    rewrite. The driver credits nothing more until the choice.
  - *Reopen through `receiptHistory`* (`exchange-save.ts:25`, `liquid-save.ts:30`, used once
    exchange or liquid history exists): **every such save refuses**, and the label it shows
    says malformed or corrupt. The forward-development policy permits this, so it does not
    block. State it plainly in the PR body so the owner is not surprised to see "corrupt" on
    their own device save. The replay now rejects those receipts, so it throws
    `SyntaxError('malformed JSON: inconsistent accepted history')` (`receipt-history.ts:18-20`).
    This is an **explicit refusal**, never a silent change. The developer must confirm the
    host code it surfaces as (expected `save_corrupt`), state it in the PR, and add **no**
    compatibility code.
- **(b) Older save that closed with pending pre-choice debt** (checkpoint `target > clock`
  before selection). After the change, capture credits 0 but keeps the old target. `drain`
  then delivers, the kernel rejects it, and the Book shows "Time stopped: invalid_state".
  `reserve` drains the existing debt before any invocation, so `choose_ancestry` itself fails
  too. The only way out is Start over, which `Fault` offers for every fault
  (`Book.tsx:192`, `:229-238`). That is explicit, not silent. Record it in the PR.
  Do not clamp the target. Clamping would change a save, and it would add machinery that
  exists only for old data.
- **(c) New saves:** no pre-choice receipts or debt exist.

Under the user's rule, a second-opinion review is needed only if save or reconcile behavior
changes. Reopen of old saves does change, by refusing case (a), so **add the second opinion**.

## Tests and fixtures

**Must change**

- `kernel/ts/test/character_choice.test.ts:71-109`, "trusted elapsed drains a due job before
  ancestry choice…". It pins the reversed rule. Rewrite it as the kernel test in Acceptance 1,

## Acceptance (literal values)

1. **Kernel test**, in `character_choice.test.ts`, replacing `:71-109`. *Breaks: elapsed
   bypasses the D11 gate again.*
   - Setup: fresh v035+ancestries world `w`, run `6f6f6f6f-1111-4222-8333-444444444444`,
     `until = 68400`.
   - Before the choice, `stepElapsed(w, elapsed(from w.state.clock, until 68400), 1)`:
     - `decision` deep-equals `{ kind: 'rejected', error: { code: 'invalid_state' } }`;
     - `result.world === w`.
   - Then `choose_ancestry fen_born` at revision 1 is accepted.
   - The same span at revision 2 is then accepted:
     - `clock === 68400`;
     - the `fen_hounds` job due at `68400` has status `'completed'`.

     one assertion: wrong `world_context_id` → `not_found`.
2. **Driver test**, in `mobile/authority/local-story`. *Breaks: ancestry-screen wall time is
   credited later, or the driver faults on the ancestry screen.*
   - Setup: r9c_interactions cartridge (rate `50`, start `64800`, ancestries), fake clocks.

   - Invoke `choose_ancestry fey_touched`; it is accepted.
   - Advance `60000` ms, then pulse `'active'` until status is ready (at most 16 commits per

   - Add one resume line: close at `120000` before the choice, reopen with the wall clock at
     `3600000`, pulse `'resume'` → `clock === 64800`.
3. **Red controls**, run and quoted in the PR:
   - (i) delete the kernel gate line → Acceptance 1 fails on `accepted !== rejected`;
   - (ii) delete the driver `d = 0` branch → Acceptance 2 fails, at `70800` or "Time stopped:
     invalid_state".
4. **E1 recorder stays at 38 of 38.** Run
   `node kernel/ts/test/e1_cases.ts tmp/e1-selected-v042.json <dir>` (selection per
   `docs/evidence/2026-10-07-e1-coverage-complete/README.md:11-12`). Expected:

   `bin/check_all.sh` once.
6. **PR body** includes: the save-impact cases (a)–(c), with the host code that case (a)
   surfaces as; the plain warning that existing device saves with exchange or liquid history
   will refuse; the superseded decision; "no pin removed".

## Designer

**Consult.** `docs/WORKFLOW.md:231` says a slice that changes what the player sees consults the
designer for its brief, its Book UI spec text and its review. This slice changes what the player
sees in two small ways:

- "Catching up…" (`Book.tsx:191`) no longer appears on the ancestry screen.
- The first time shown after the choice is the chapter start time, not start plus dwell time.

No new element, wording or layout is added. The designer's scope is small:

- write the `book-ui.md:458` sentence;
- confirm that no design-system change is needed;
- review the UI-visible behavior in the PR.

## Scope trigger (stop and ask)

- Any change to the save format, the checkpoint row shape, a protocol or GameView shape, or the
  ErrorCode set.
- `kernel_api` in `INSTALLED`: do not bump it. No documented bump rule exists, and recent bumps
  came with new capabilities (`git log -S"kernel_api: '1.3"`). If a check demands a bump, stop
  and ask.
- Any need for a migration, a clamp or compatibility code for old saves.
- Any E1 case that falls below 38/38 and cannot be explained by this rule.

## Process rules (copy)

- Self-review is ONE pass: `/code-review medium`.
- Narrow mutant runs only (the two red controls). Full-suite mutation sweeps happen only before
  a release (owner rule).
- Run long commands in the background, without polling.
- Review: one fresh Opus reviewer, plus a second opinion (save reopen behavior changes for old
  saves).
- Ponytail before implementation and Ponytail Review before handoff.

## Out of scope

- New UI elements, a clock on the ancestry screen, migrating old saves, and the `actions.ts:192`
  cleanup beyond one token.

title: Verify the fast-jev-compaction fix in a fresh session; file both upstream reports
description: Retro 2026-10-14. Seven Opus subagents died on 'server_tool_use ids must be unique' after compaction (resume or self-resume after a background wait). Patched copy installed in the plugin cache (original kept as hooks/fast-jev.ts.orig-0.3.0); this session still ran the old hook. Next session: run the scratch dangling-parents.py check on one compacted agent transcript (expect 0), then file the bug report (scratchpad fast-jev-compaction-bug-report.md) at tamaratran/fast-jev-compaction and anthropics/claude-code.
notes:
Owner approved 2026-10-14 ("approve all retro items"): goes into the next housekeeping PR.

dangling-parents.py (run: python3 -I dangling-parents.py <subagent .jsonl>; expect 0):
```
# Usage: python3 -I dangling-parents.py <transcript.jsonl>...
# Prints, per file, rows after each compact_boundary whose parentUuid points before that boundary (0 = healthy).
import json, sys
for path in sys.argv[1:]:
    line_of, rows, bounds = {}, [], []
    for i, l in enumerate(open(path), 1):
        o = json.loads(l); rows.append(o)
        if o.get('uuid'): line_of[o['uuid']] = i
        if o.get('subtype') == 'compact_boundary': bounds.append(i)
    bad = sum(1 for i, o in enumerate(rows, 1) for b in bounds[-1:]
              if i > b and line_of.get(o.get('parentUuid') or '', b + 1) < b)
    print(f'{bad}\t{len(bounds)} boundaries\t{path}')
```

Upstream bug report text:
Title: Resumed subagent fails with 400 "`server_tool_use` ids must be unique per assistant turn" after a fast-jev compaction

1. `toSessionMessages` (hooks/fast-jev.ts:143-144) hands kept tool_result user rows back with the engine's `handle`, so Claude Code (2.1.299) reuses its own entry, gives it a fresh uuid, but keeps `sourceToolAssistantUUID` pointing at the pre-compaction assistant uuid.
2. The transcript writer uses `sourceToolAssistantUUID` as `parentUuid`, so on disk the first kept tool_result links back past the `compact_boundary` into the uncompacted history.
3. Live turns are fine (memory is correct); the next resume (SendMessage to a finished subagent, `--resume`) walks the parent chain and gets the uncompacted history spliced to the kept tail (observed). The duplicate id most likely comes from the loader joining the old and new copies of one assistant message (same `message.id`, same `server_tool_use` id, here the advisor tool) into one turn (inferred: the plain chain holds each id once).
4. Seen in 3 of 3 failing subagents: the walked chain is lines 1..217 + 288..374 (boundary at 221), 5-6 post-boundary rows per file have a pre-boundary parent, and the 400 is the first request after the resume prompt.
5. Workaround (plugin): return user rows that carry `toolResults` without the handle, so the engine rebuilds them with no stale link (limit: image blocks in kept results become text). The engine defect (hook-replaced compaction does not re-link `sourceToolAssistantUUID`) should also go to anthropics/claude-code.

Patch:

```ts
// hooks/fast-jev.ts, toSessionMessages
-    if (own) return own;
```

title: Save release pin must change on a kernel contract bump, not only on a cartridge change (old saves open as save_corrupt)
description: Found in #514 (loka-548k) review 2026-10-30: a save pin is the content hash (mobile/authority/local-story/authority.ts:93), which changes only when a cartridge changes. A kernel contract bump that changes what a save receipt must hold (dialogue speaker) does not change the pin of cartridges that did not bump at_least, so their old saves reopen and fail as save_corrupt (dialogue-receipt.ts:83) instead of being refused with Start over. #514 worked around it by bumping at_least on every dialogue cartridge by hand. Fix: make the release pin include the kernel_api (or receipt schema version), so any contract bump refuses older saves on every cartridge with Start over; red test: a save at the previous kernel_api on an unbumped cartridge is refused at the pin.
notes:
BRIEF loka-daha (drafted 2026-10-30, Fable). Kit: docs/guides/brief-kit.md (read once; not copied). Handoff threshold: docs/WORKFLOW.md#token-hygiene (~220k).

GOAL. The save release pin also names the kernel_api the save was made under, so a kernel contract bump refuses every older save at the pin with Start over (`pinned_release_missing`, in place, nothing written), on every cartridge, whether or not its `at_least` changed. A save made under the installed kernel_api on its installed release reopens as today.
Size S. Lane: Hosted PR. Branch fix/daha-kernel-api-pin from main AFTER PR #514 (loka-548k) and loka-oc5i merge (both regenerate pins, touch mobile/app/stories/live/*.sql, and #514 adds release_pin.test.ts, which this slice rewrites). Developer Opus (save slice, docs/WORKFLOW.md:25). Review: fresh Opus reviewer with record PLUS a second opinion (another fresh reviewer): docs/WORKFLOW.md:35-41, a change to save behavior. Save-affecting handback: docs/WORKFLOW.md:211-213 (compact results of saves.test.ts, recovery.test.ts, start_over.test.ts, release_pin.test.ts, with the red control).

DESIGN (drafter; PM to confirm). The pin gains `kernel_api: INSTALLED.kernel_api` (kernel/ts/src/runtime/world.ts:108) at creation and is compared by equality at open, beside the content hash. Rejected: (a) folding kernel_api into the content hash: the hash is a compiler property of the canonical cartridge (lib/loka/content.ex:67; loader check kernel/ts/src/content/cartridge.ts:41 CONTENT_HASH_MISMATCH) and every bump would rewrite every *_hash.json fixture and transcript pin, exactly the #514 churn; (b) a save-format bump (`SAVE_FORMAT`, authority.ts:59): a format is storage layout, and `formatProblem` routes it to unsupported_save_format/save_corrupt, not the pin; (c) `kernel_api` on `Host` or `Release`: every test host (`__tests__/*-host.ts`, saves.test.ts:81) would have to pass it. Equality, not a range: pre-production has no save compatibility (docs/decisions/owner-decision-forward-development-2026-10-05.md), a newer save on an older app must refuse too, and loka-ewtx's rule (a merged slice's kernel_api is strictly above main's) makes every contract change a bump. A pin without `kernel_api` (every existing save) compares unequal and is refused the same way: no migration, no special case. This keeps every cartridge's fixtures stable: no cartridge, hash fixture or transcript pin changes in this slice or in later kernel_api bumps.

CHANGE. mobile/authority/local-story/authority.ts: import `INSTALLED` from kernel/ts/src/runtime/world.ts (line 9 already imports `newWorld` from it); `first()` (:171-186) adds `kernel_api: INSTALLED.kernel_api` to the pin object (:173-181); `openStory` (:93-98) refuses `pinned_release_missing` also when `saved.pin.kernel_api !== INSTALLED.kernel_api` (same reply shape: `pinned: saved.pin`, `installed`; no new kind, SaveError.tsx:13 copy unchanged). `newGame` (:229-244) pins through `first()` and needs nothing. `Meta.pin` (store.ts:82) is `{content_hash} & Record<string, Json>`: no type change. Elixir: n/a (lib/loka compiles cartridges; no save, pin or authority). bin/regen.sh and bin/regen_hash_fixture.sh: untouched and not run for a fixture (no cartridge change); `npm run stories:views` (mobile/app, stories/scenarios.ts:72 opens through openGame -> openStory -> first) rewrites the eight mobile/app/stories/live/*.sql save rows with the new pin; commit them (bin/regen.sh runs it anyway when mobile/ changed).
Outline (ast-grep outline mobile/authority/local-story/authority.ts): 41 `export type Release = { content_hash: string; fresh: World }`; 76 `export function openStory(db, releases, host)`; 164 `function pinned({ fresh }, { world_context_id })`; 171 `function first(content_hash, fresh, host): Meta`; 229 `function newGame(s)`. release_pin.test.ts (#514): `release(canonical)` builds a Release from a canonical string; `open(path, releases)` opens a real SQLite file through openStory.

DOCS FIRST (same PR, cite loka-daha). docs/system/save.md:10-17 (`openStory` opens the save on the release its pin names: add "under the kernel_api the pin names, `INSTALLED.kernel_api`"); :18-20 replace the pre-production clause (an older save's receipt history re-deciding differently opens save_corrupt, not a pin refusal, citing the dialogue-hub decision) with: a kernel contract change bumps `kernel_api`, so older saves are refused at the pin; `save_corrupt` is only a damaged save; note the dialogue-hub record (docs/decisions/owner-decision-dialogue-hub-2026-10-09.md:16-17) describes behavior before loka-daha; :32 the `pinned_release_missing` row: "the pin names a release the app does not carry, or a kernel_api other than the installed one"; :56-58 "exact release pin" = content hash and kernel_api. docs/system/cartridge.md:40-42 "after a content change" -> "after a content change or a kernel_api bump". docs/system/cartridge.md:22 (requires.kernel_api): add one sentence: `at_least` rises only when the content uses a newer kernel feature; a contract bump alone changes `INSTALLED.kernel_api` and never a cartridge. Lessons: docs/lessons/storage.md.

ACCEPTANCE (literal; all on a real SQLite file through openStory, as release_pin.test.ts does).
1. release_pin.test.ts, rewritten to the new break: open the showcase release (protocol/fixtures/toolbox_showcase_hash.json, unchanged canonical, at_least untouched) -> `open`; close; `UPDATE save SET pin = json_set(pin, '$.kernel_api', '1.0')`; reopen on the SAME release -> kind `pinned_release_missing`, `pinned.kernel_api` = '1.0', `pinned.content_hash` = the fixture sha256, `newGame` a function; file bytes unchanged; `newGame()` -> `{kind:'replaced'}` and the new save's pin.kernel_api = INSTALLED.kernel_api.
2. Same with '$.kernel_api' set to '9.0' (a newer app's save) -> `pinned_release_missing`.
3. Same with the key removed (`json_remove(pin, '$.kernel_api')`, a pre-loka-daha save) -> `pinned_release_missing`, not `save_corrupt`.
4. Same-version reopen: a save written by this build reopens `open` under a host whose `kernel_version` differs (saves.test.ts:81 passes KERNEL; pass 'k2' once): the build commit is not the pin.
5. saves.test.ts PIN (:126-135) gains `kernel_api: INSTALLED.kernel_api` (an input from the kernel, not the authority under test); :184, :200, :310 ("an app update reopens a save on its pinned release") and death.test.ts:148 pass unchanged otherwise. start_over.test.ts (10 tests), recovery.test.ts (8) pass.
6. `npm run stories:views` (mobile/app) rewrites only the `save` row's pin in each mobile/app/stories/live/*.sql (diff shows `"kernel_api":"<installed>"` added, nothing else); commit them. No UI change, no story run.
RED CONTROLS: drop the `kernel_api` comparison in openStory -> 1, 2, 3 fail, nothing else; drop `kernel_api` from first() -> 5's PIN deep-equal and 1's newGame pin check fail.
MUTANTS (bin/mutate.sh, narrow against saves.test.ts, release_pin.test.ts): compare `<=` or a range -> 2 fails; compare against `host.kernel_version` -> 4 fails; refuse as `save_corrupt` -> 3 fails (kind and newGame-in-place differ); missing key treated as a match -> 3 fails.

AFTER THIS SLICE. #514's per-cartridge `at_least` bumps become unnecessary: no revert (they are declarations, not compatibility code; a revert would regenerate 10 hash fixtures and ~40 transcript pins for no behavior). Rule forward (PM to record in loka-ewtx's notes and cartridge.md:22): a kernel contract slice bumps only world.ts:108; `cartridge.json` `at_least`, protocol/fixtures/*_hash.json and transcript pins change only when the content does. loka-oc5i (1.125) still bumps at_least if it merges first; later slices do not.
REALM: n/a (local authority only; Trust row 8: the pin is still computed by this authority).
SCOPE TRIGGER: stop and ask if the PM wants a range instead of equality, a new reply kind or SaveError copy (designer), `installed` carrying the kernel_api for the Book, any test host that must build the pin itself, or if lib/ reads a pin.
SHARED FILES: release_pin.test.ts and start_over.test.ts (#514), mobile/app/stories/live/*.sql (#514, oc5i). None with cartridges or protocol/fixtures.
OPEN (PM): (1) confirm equality over range; (2) confirm the save.md:18-20 rewrite supersedes the dialogue-hub decision's save_corrupt line (owner record, paraphrase allowed); (3) confirm no revert of #514's at_least bumps.
PM 2026-10-30 rulings on the drafter's questions: (1) equality, not a range: any kernel_api difference refuses at the pin with Start over (allowed before release by owner-decision-forward-development-2026-10-05). (2) The save.md rewrite narrows the dialogue-hub decision's save_corrupt line to real corruption; cite both records in the PR. (3) No revert of #514's at_least bumps. Run after #514 and loka-oc5i merge; Opus developer, fresh reviewer plus a second opinion (save change).
From #514: kernel/ts/test/reactions.test.ts:53, cartridge.test.ts:15, cartridge_rooms.test.ts:14 hard-code the test host kernel version 1.0; read the kernel's own version (as #514 did for schedule/calendar) in this slice.

title: Log subagent tokens per slice in Beads; sum per batch at merge
description: Retro 2026-10-15 (session b5fe9338). Session ran about 35 subagents (many 40-200k tokens each, e.g. hs-5 developer 82k across three rounds, Fable stub tree 171k, Fable professions design 200k) with no per-slice cost record; the weekly allowance is the binding limit (HANDOFF) and fix rounds are the largest avoidable cost (hs-5: build + 3 fix rounds + 2 reviewers + save second opinion). A Twitter thread on Opus-plans/cheap-agents-execute and Anthropic's dynamic-workflows post make the same point: fewer PM tokens is not fewer tokens. title: Crossed bell deadline: one elapsed advance faults conflicting_write on plan control
description: Found in loka-6ql4 self-review. With the 6ql4 fix, a plan job whose crossed sub-step reaches a bell suppression ends_at inside one elapsed advance runs in a different writer group from the resume job (populationDeadlinePairs, kernel/ts/src/runtime/proposal_deadlines.ts, pairs only rows pending at that exact due), so both writes to population.control fault conflicting_write (scratch: d9 ready(0), advance to 64800, ring_bell, elapsed 64800->241200). Before 6ql4 it faulted nonfuture_job; atomic both times. Relaxing pairing to b.due <= a.due commits and matches job-by-job play but widens protocol.md:1175-1178 (exact-deadline pairing). Question for PM: does the pairing extend to a crossed sub-step that reaches ends_at? Chapter 1 unaffected (host settles one due job at a time); showcase combat district plan has no bell.

comments.author: raymondluong
comments.text: PM decision (per m8-pop review): widen protocol.md:1175 — a plan's current job incl. crossed sub-steps shares one writer group with that plan's resume job when one advance runs both. P2, not in M8 unless cheap.

## 2. The design (how the rush is built from what exists)

The rush is four beats, each already partly in place:

1. **Earned.** Every experience source (quest reward `experience.grant`, a credited kill) ends the step with one
   authored line, the owner's words, with the amount available as `{amount}`: new `world.levelling.gained` TextKey.
   Told from the same site as the level-up line (`closing`), so every source tells once. No Book counting.
2. **Seen.** The level line gains a hairline rule that fills from the level's floor to its next threshold. The view
   gains `from` (the threshold that reached this level, 0 at level 1) so the Book draws `(experience − from) / (next − from)`
   without deriving a level or point (the clause "the presenter never counts experience, levels or points" is kept:
   it computes a fraction of two engine numbers, as hp current/maximum already is).
3. **The moment.** A level is a full-page gilt wash under the ink (the Blow wash mechanism with the gilt role, Flash
   limit and Flashes setting apply), the `level` sound (tokens exist), medium haptic, the authored `level_up` line
   dried in gilt, and the hairline running to its end and starting the next level. Not a card: the card is reserved
   for chapter markers (plan 3.5) and a level card would be a one-off page (room page anatomy decision). Owner Q2.
4. **Named.** Each level names what it opens: content, through one new engine event `level_reached {character_id, level}`
   and the existing reaction machinery: `on: {event: level_reached, level: 3}` with `narrate` (the owner's line for
   that level), `fact.assign` (unlock a spell's `learned` fact or an action's gate), and, for the restore, `resource.adjust`
   admitted in reactions. Abilities themselves gate on the existing `level_compare` leaf. A skill still comes from its
   teacher (`skill.acquire` stays dialogue-only: in the prologue the rites are taught by people, the level is the frame).

Skills: an authored learned line and named ranks come from the skill definition (`learned`, `ranks`) and reach the Book on
the SkillView (`learned`, `rank`), so the Book swaps its composed sentence for the owner's when one is authored and keeps
the composed one otherwise (the sampler cartridges stay as they are). A rank rising tells its own authored line.
Skills page: a sixth Contents section, "Skills", holding plain skills, professions and the Spells (known words) block,
leaving Character with name, position, ancestry, level, conditions, attributes, resources, xp and Raise. Owner Q3.

Why not a skill-point pool, a per-level table in `world.levelling`, or a `restore` declaration: existing levels, attribute
points, reactions and `resource.adjust` already express every one of these as content; the only engine gap is the event
and the two step-context admissions (Ponytail: use what is there).

## E1. `level_reached`, the gained line, the view floor (engine, M, kernel_api 1.131)

The owner's cartridge will use: `world.levelling {thresholds, points_per_level, level_up, gained}`; quest rewards

title: Toolbox row 33: theft, fence, witnessed offense — batch M13
description: Toolbox row 33 (docs/MECHANICS-TOOLBOX.md:187), batch M13: theft, fence, witnessed offense; G7 get lock on the bank vault NPC. Fable brief in notes.
notes:
Fable brief 2026-10-14 (s2):
BRIEF toolbox row 33 — theft, fence and witnessed offense (merges 34) (Fable draft 2026-10-14; PM to store in a new Beads issue under loka-kgd). Batch M13 row 5, after row 16 (the witness read uses `concealed` with `pierced_by`) and RS-8 (merged #386). Size M, one developer run, engine + GameView; the Book shows nothing new (NPC-held items render through the existing `contents` list). kernel_api 1.95 (assumes W15+FD9 takes 1.94; the PM renumbers if W15 needs none). Model: developer, Opus. Reviewer: the batch's Fable review plus a save second opinion only if a save row changes (none planned).
HANDOFF THRESHOLD: near 180k tokens stop, push, hand back head + done/left list (no CI wait).

GOAL. Pickpocket a purse; stolen flag; fence buys stolen only; seen theft sets wanted, unseen does not (docs/MECHANICS-TOOLBOX.md:187; docs/system/mechanics.md:2755 and :2763 "No lock on an NPC (pickpocketing is row 33)", "No `stolen` provenance (row 33)"). Smallest version: theft is the existing `take` of an item a living NPC holds, in a cartridge that declares `world.theft`. It moves items only, never resource pools (the bank vault's pennies are a pool, mechanics.md:2807; `take` never calls `transfer`, kernel/ts/src/mechanics/containment/rule.ts:55-64). The owner requires the G7 `get` lock on the bank vault NPC regardless (docs/decisions/owner-decision-realm-seams-2026-10-13.md "Follow-ups"; docs/rnd/realm-seams-audit-2026-10-13.md row 10): this row adds `NpcDefinition.locks {get}` and a loader check that a cartridge with `world.theft` locks every `vault` NPC a deposit or withdraw names.

PM RULINGS (pre-decided):
1. Theft = `take` from a living NPC in the actor's room, opt-in by `world.theft {skill, attribute, stolen, noticed, narration: {seen, unseen}}` (protocol/cartridge.schema.json `WorldSettings`, :1315). Without it an NPC-held item stays `not_present` and unlisted (Chapter 1, every sampler byte-identical). Rejected: a `steal` command or a recipe target kind (a recipe cannot move an item; a new command duplicates take's custody, carry and lock walk).
2. The outcome is deterministic, no RNG (trap 5): the victim notices when the actor's level of `theft.skill` (kernel/ts/src/mechanics/skills.ts:23) is below the victim's `theft.attribute` (`npcValue`, kernel/ts/src/mechanics/attributes/shared.ts:91; undefined reads as 0). Bystanders: every other living NPC in the room that is not `blind` and for whom the actor's body is not `concealed` (kernel/ts/src/mechanics/status/shared.ts:213, :221; row 16's `pierced_by` makes an alert guard see a hidden thief). seen = noticed or any bystander. New shared query `witnesses(world, body, except?)` in kernel/ts/src/mechanics/senses.ts (G6's home; FD5's filter reuses it), lookups only, no query step.
3. "Seen" reaches content as the existing `custom_event` with the declared `theft.noticed` event and `subject_id` the victim (protocol/event.schema.json custom_event; reaction filter `custom`, kernel/ts/src/mechanics/reaction.ts:67). Its subject is the doer (:203) so a content reaction's `fact.assign wanted true` lands at the thief's player scope. No new event kind, no reaction.ts edit (FD5 owns that file next).
4. `stolen` is a cartridge-declared bool fact, `per_subject`, scope `instance` (world state about a thing), written only by containment as `durability` is written only by its owner (kernel/ts/src/mechanics/fact.ts:120 `Owner` gains `'theft'`, :157 pattern); the loader refuses an authored write of it (RESERVED_FACT where cartridge_scoped_facts.ts refuses durability writes, kernel/ts/src/content/cartridge_scoped_facts.ts:31) and an undeclared or wrongly scoped fact (FACT_SCOPE_UNSUPPORTED at `world.theft.stolen`). The flag is never cleared (no laundering; Known limit). Theft never transfers ownership (seam 7): a G7 entitlement fact is untouched.
5. Fence: `ShopOffer.stolen: true` (protocol/entity.schema.json:845). `exchange` (kernel/ts/src/mechanics/commerce/shared.ts:48) on `sell` refuses `invalid_state` unless the moved instance's `stolen` value equals `offer.stolen === true`; buy is unchanged (a bought stolen item keeps its flag). `shelf` (:88) shows the same refusal. Known limit: a `stock` offer (W11) does not read the flag; the loader refuses `stolen: true` on a stock offer (SCHEMA_VIOLATION at `stolen`).
6. notes:
AUDIT REPORT:
# Simplification audit: Loka v3 (2026-10-28)

Read-only. Owner's goal: fewer concepts, names, files and rules a human or an LLM must hold to
(a) author a cartridge and (b) work on the engine and Book, with no loss of capability, safety or
determinism. Builds on the 2026-10-23 design audit and owner decision (shortcuts in the compiler,
no new grammar, builder later), and on the docs audit `loka-40d4` (merged #479). Not re-proposed:
recipes into actions (.22), behaviours (.16), prototype parameters (.18), source JSON Schema (.17),
WORKFLOW/PM split, the mechanics.md split (deferred, `loka-u15o`), `loka-40d4` P1-P15.

Method: four read-only inventories (cartridge kinds, engine vocabularies, docs, Book UI) plus
direct counts. Line counts are `wc -l`; token estimates use 15 tokens per line.

## Baseline numbers

- Source kinds: 23 directories in `lib/loka/content/source.ex:133-157`; the doc list at
  `docs/system/cartridge.md:17` names 21 (omits `statuses`, 82 files in 28 cartridges, and `blueprints`).
- Cartridges: 106 (104 samplers, `lantern_proof`, `toolbox_showcase`); ~1,700 JSON files; 105 hash
  fixtures in `protocol/fixtures/`. Showcase: 599 JSON files, 140 reactions, 139 items, 63 rooms.
- Engine: `kernel/ts/src` 121 mechanics files (~7,000 lines), content loaders 53 files (5,697 lines),
  runtime 30, view 21. Elixir compiler `lib/loka/content` 75 files (11,022 lines).
- Vocabularies: 54 commands, 29 events, 16 reaction ops, 8 recipe steps, 4 dialogue sequence ops +
  10 bespoke choice effect keys, 11 service benefit kinds, 22 policy leaves, 5 recipe check kinds +
  1 dialogue check kind, 40 diagnostic codes.
- Docs an agent may read: `docs/system/mechanics.md` 3,753 lines, `cartridge.md` 2,278,
  `protocol.md` 1,341, `save.md` 1,150, `book-ui.md` 837; developer read set before the brief
  313 lines, designer 314 + BOOK-UI-COMPONENTS 260 + interaction-patterns 347, PM 683.
- Tests: 319 TS test files (64,465 lines), 170 Elixir (16,603 lines). `bin/`: 60 scripts, 13 of them
  red controls.

## Findings, ranked by saving per effort

Format: what; evidence; saves; risk; size; contract change.

### 1. Delete the retired chapter's half of `cartridge.md` and the stale chapter docs

What: delete `docs/system/cartridge.md:30-160` ("Current bundled chapter" history and "Retired first
chapter", 131 lines), `:843-873` ("Development cartridges": `lantern_proof` as "the R6P proof",
scene/chapters/journal samplers as "historical development proofs") and `:873-1997` (30 sections
named by retired-chapter slice: Maud's Cellar M20-B2, Q2-C stays/rescue return, Q3-B, Q3-F, A3 Green
finale, Peg's B3 shelf, C1 Tobin, B5, B4, B7, C2, B6, C3, C4, D1, B8, D2, B9, D4, D5, D3, D6, D11, D9,
D12, D7, C5, D10, C6, D8: 1,125 lines). Delete `docs/system/e1-certification.md` (298 lines; E1 is
the retired chapter's certification, still listed at `docs/system/README.md:13`), `docs/ROADMAP.md`
(116 lines: "32 of 33 slices", E1-E3 open) or cut it to a pointer, `docs/system/future.md` "Chapter
one and the proof cartridge" (lines 14-40) and `README.md:37`.

Evidence: the chapter was retired 2026-10-21 (`owner-decision-retire-first-chapter-2026-10-21.md`,
"Fully gone now"); retire slice L3 (`loka-4hik.7`, closed) "rewrote" these docs but kept them as
history. 55 retired-name mentions remain in `cartridge.md`, 45 in `mechanics.md`, 9 in `save.md`.
The move-forward decision: closed work keeps only lessons and permalinks. Live links into the
deleted sections: 21 anchors, 17 of them from `mechanics.md`'s own chapter-slice sections
(`a3-green`, `pegs-b3`, `c1-tobin`, ... `c6-s27`), plus `ROADMAP.md`, `e1-certification.md`,
`protocol.md` (`d12-practical`), `save.md` (`a3-green`), `protocol/README.md` and `BUILDERS-GUIDE.md`
(`retired-first-chapter`). `bin/check_docs.exs` gates anchors, so a broken link cannot slip.

Where the chapter-era `mechanics.md` sections (`:873-1972`, "S2 Chandler's Debt" to "D8 crow
scavenging") describe installed mechanics (light@1 under "B4 light and darkness", transport@1 under
"D1 paid ferry", escrow, patrol, population), they stay, but their example prose and links into the
deleted `cartridge.md` sections are rewritten to the showcase. The numbers that lived in the
`cartridge.md` sections are either world parameters (cartridge-owned, so showcase JSON is the
source) or restated in `mechanics.md`.

Saves: about 1,900 lines (~28k tokens) out of the spec set; `cartridge.md` 2,278 to about 1,000.
An agent that reads `cartridge.md` whole saves ~17k tokens per spawn; one that greps it stops
landing in Maud's cellar. Risk: low; everything is in git and the archive repo. Size: S-M (docs,
link fixes). Contract: none.

### 2. One `kernel_api` floor per cartridge instead of a floor per field

What: a cartridge's `requires.kernel_api` is checked once, against the current API; no field,
step, leaf or tag carries its own floor. Delete the per-feature checks, their tests and the doc
clauses.

Evidence: `KERNEL_API_RANGE_INVALID` at 63 sites in `lib/loka/content/*.ex`, 65 in
`kernel/ts/src/content/*.ts`, 104 assertions in `test/`, 113 in `kernel/ts/test/`;
`lib/loka/content/requires.ex` (160 lines), `loader_floors_test.exs` + `loader_floors.test.ts`
(239 lines). `cartridge.md` names 55 distinct floors (81 mentions); `mechanics.md` 95 mentions. The
sentence "needs `kernel_api` at least 1.xx; both kernels refuse the lower floor
(KERNEL_API_RANGE_INVALID at `requires.kernel_api.at_least`)" appears in nearly every
"declarations" paragraph (`cartridge.md:1997-2276`). Open symptoms: `loka-2bt2` (one shared floor
parser), `loka-kgd.169` (tag references carry no floor). AGENTS.md: pre-production, no backward
API compatibility, no older adapters; the only consumers are this repo's 106 cartridges, all at the
current API.

Saves: ~130 code branches, ~220 test cases, 176 doc clauses, and for every future row one branch,
one test pair and one clause per kernel. The authoring rule becomes one sentence. Risk: a cartridge
released later cannot say which minor API it needs; at release, re-add one range check on the
manifest (which is all the per-field floors compose to). Size: M (mechanical deletion in both
kernels, tests, docs; hash fixtures unchanged because the artifact is unchanged). Contract: the
manifest's semantics (no schema change). Owner decision: yes, the floors are a documented contract.

### 3. Drop the `{policy_version, root}` wrapper and make `policy` optional

What: a policy is its tree; `policy_version` goes; a recipe, action, barrier or room whose policy
is absent is always allowed.

Evidence: `policy_version` appears 705 times in 560 of ~1,700 cartridge files (247 of the
showcase's 599); the only value ever written is 1. `ActionRecipe` and `ActionDefinition` require
`policy` (`protocol/action.schema.json`), so 77 of the 156 recipe and action files carry the
always-true block `{"policy_version": 1, "root": {"op": "all", "items": []}}`. `VersionedPolicy`
is embedded by nine schemas (`room`, `entity`, `action`, `cartridge`, `reaction`, `policy`,
`dialogue`, `quest`, `account`).

Saves: two lines and one concept per policy site (~1,400 source lines), the always-true block in
half of all recipes, and the "versioned policy" notion from the author's head; with (5) the
standalone `policies/` kind too. Risk: every artifact hash changes (105 fixtures regenerate with
`bin/regen_hash_fixture.sh`; mechanical). Size: S-M. Contract: yes (policy schema, both loaders).
Do it before .17 so the source schema is written once.

### 4. One step vocabulary for reactions, actions and dialogue choices; one check vocabulary

What: a single `Step` union used by a reaction's `apply`, a recipe's (soon action's) outcome
sequence and a dialogue choice; a single `Check`.

Evidence: reaction ops, 16 (`protocol/reaction.schema.json:525-763`); recipe steps, 8
(`action.schema.json:692-838`); dialogue choice `sequence` ops, 4, plus 10 bespoke effect keys
(`accept`, `hand_over`, `receive`, `availability`, `payment`, `escort`, `exchange`,
`lesson_payment`, `patrol`, `check`; `dialogue.schema.json:200-433`); service benefits, 11 kinds
(`service.schema.json`). Overlap today: `fact.assign` in three lists, `status.apply`,
`status.cure` and `fact.adjust` in two; the other 36 words live in one list each for the same idea,
"change the world". Checks: `RecipeCheck` has 5 kinds (`luck`, `threshold`, `attribute_threshold`,
`opposed`, `track`), `DialogueCheck` has 1 (`opposed`). Three validators per kernel do the same
job: `recipes.ex` 304 + `reactions.ex` 339 + `dialogues.ex` 366 lines; `cartridge_recipes.ts` 264 +
`cartridge_reactions.ts` 208 + `cartridge_dialogues.ts` 293.

Proposal: `Step` = the reaction list plus `event.emit`, `damage`, `light.ignite`,
`resource.adjust`, `build`, `skill.acquire`, `topic.grant`; dialogue's `accept` becomes
`quest.activate` (already a reaction op), `hand_over`/`receive` an `item.move` with a holder,
