   `Diagnostic[]`. "Each cartridge_*.ts becomes an artifact-to-typed-struct builder" therefore has nothing to
   build: S7 is a deletion of 50 validator modules plus the stage calls, not a rewrite. The runtime reads the
   artifact maps directly (`kernel/ts/src/mechanics/fact.ts:24`, `kernel/ts/src/runtime/fresh.ts:286`).
2. **Emit sites.** 328 `diag(` lines in 53 files (5,697 lines). Codes with a compiler twin (Elixir emit sites /

   `SCHEMA_VIOLATION` (hand-written, beyond the generated schema) ~90/~110, `UNDECLARED_CAPABILITY` 20/22,

## 2. Decisions (PM defaults; the owner ratifies the starred ones)

- D1*. **Keep in the loader** (why: each is either integrity, or a property of the installed host that the
  compiler cannot know, or a property whose absence makes runtime lookups fail before any rule runs):
  `ARTIFACT_TOO_LARGE`, `INVALID_JSON`, `UNKNOWN_FORMAT` (`cartridge.ts:61-72`); `schemaStage` generated shape
  (`:115-121`); `CONTENT_HASH_MISMATCH` (`:77-85`); `keyStage` map-key integrity (`:150-173`: a key whose
  `cartridge_id`/`version`/`key` differ from its definition makes every `refString` lookup miss);
  `lockDiagnostics` lock = `requires.capabilities` only (`:253-262`: the runtime gates rules by the lock,
  `world.ts:136`); `installedStage` whole (`cartridge_installed.ts:25-62`, including the one-scope fact rule
  `:36-40` and `scopeSites` `cartridge_scoped_facts.ts:76-115`, whose own header says it is "in the loader
  only": it names what this kernel can read, not what the author wrote).
- D2*. **Drop** everything else the loader repeats from `lib/loka/content`: `timeStage` (`cartridge.ts:175-191`,
  twins `requires.ex:106-125`, `checks.ex` `UNKNOWN_COMMAND`, `recipes.ex` `INVALID_TIME_POLICY`),
  `calendarStage`, the `lockStage` ownership walk (`:214-250`, twin `checks.ex:294`), `lockDiagnostics`'
  position/scene `fact@1` loop (`:263-274`), `scenes(c)`, `refStage`, `declarations()` and the 50 modules
  they call. Reason to drop the walk too: it is the same table-driven check the compiler runs, the runtime
  refuses an unlocked command anyway, and keeping it keeps `nodes`/`parts` and four modules' `uses` exports
  (~250 lines) alive for one duplicate.
- D3. **F2's one check** is `Requires.range/2` in the compiler (`at_least < below`, code
  `KERNEL_API_RANGE_INVALID` at `cartridge.requires.kernel_api`) and `KERNEL_API_UNSUPPORTED` in the loader
  (`cartridge_installed.ts:41-44`). The 63 Elixir floor sites, `features/3`, the `elapsed` floor, `Floors`'
  floor halves, `protocol/fixtures/loader_floors.json` (94 cases), both floors tests and the 104 Elixir
  assertions go. The 65 TS floor sites all sit in code S7 deletes (`cartridge.ts:187-191`,
  `cartridge_refs.ts:247-252`, `cartridge_scoped_facts.ts:60-74`, and the modules), so F2's TS half is
  absorbed by the S7 slices; no separate TS floor slice.
- D4*. **Schema descriptions** that name floors (159 lines) are edited in the docs slice; `bin/regen.sh`
  rewrites `contracts.gen.*`; artifacts and hash fixtures are byte-identical (acceptance row).
- D5*. **Trust boundary after S7**: a self-consistent (hash-valid) artifact with a dangling reference or a
  containment cycle is a runtime error, not a refusal. Accepted pre-production per the owner's yes; the
  re-entry point is PREP-03 (signed artifacts or a server-side compile). The briefs record, per deleted
  check, the compiler twin and its Elixir test, so nothing is dropped untested.
- D6*. **Order against open PRs**: merge #485, #486, #487 first, then cut `simplify/c1-loader` from `main`.
  Otherwise S7's test edits conflict with #487 in the same 100 files and the mutant table cannot use
  `bin/mutate_diff.sh`.
- D7. **Branching for parallel developers**: each slice works on `simplify/c1-<slice>` cut from the current
  head of `simplify/c1-loader`; the developer pushes its sub-branch with `bin/push_slice.sh`; the reviewer
  reviews the sub-branch head against `simplify/c1-loader`; the PM merges the sub-branch into
  `simplify/c1-loader` (`git merge --no-ff`) after APPROVE and pushes the draft branch once per wave. One
  draft PR (`simplify/c1-loader` -> `main`); the Fable final-head review runs on its ready head.
- D8. **Shared files** (`cartridge.ts` `declarations()` list, `cartridge_refs.ts` `refStage` tail,
  `protocol/fixtures/cartridge_loader.json`): edits are delete-only, one statement or one case per line/block,
  and a developer never reformats them; a merge conflict is resolved by taking both deletions. The prep
  commit (section 3, slice 0) makes the lists one statement per line with a group separator comment between
  developer groups so adjacent deletions do not touch.
- D9. The `DiagnosticCode` enum (`protocol/cartridge.schema.json:1198-1239`) does not change: the compiler
  still emits every semantic code; `KERNEL_API_RANGE_INVALID` stays for `range/2`. The loader doc paragraph
  (`docs/system/cartridge.md:619-640`) is rewritten once, in the final slice, not per slice.

## 4. Rules shared by every S7 slice (B1, B2, C1, C2, D1, D2; F differs)

Linked, not copied: [brief kit](docs/guides/brief-kit.md), [developer](.claude/agents/developer.md),
AGENTS.md Simplicity and Writing tests, `docs/lessons/contracts.md` (bullet "A guard implemented in both
kernels needs a red control in each kernel's own suite": after this batch the semantic guards exist in one
kernel, so the rule applies to the kept integrity checks only). Handoff threshold: stop at 220k tokens at the
latest, 180k when a push is near (`developer.md:53`). Lane: Draft PR, batched pushes; sub-branch per D7.

Method per slice (the whole slice is deletion, so the test discipline inverts: no new conditionals, but no
check may be dropped without its compiler twin and that twin's test):
1. Delete your module files whole (`git rm`), their import lines and their call statements in `cartridge.ts`
   `declarations()` (`:284-303`) and `cartridge_refs.ts` `refStage` (`:220-271`), and nothing else in those
   two files. Where a module keeps an export another layer imports (section 1 item 4), delete only the check
   functions and leave a one-line header saying what remains and who imports it.
2. `cd kernel/ts && npx tsc --noEmit -p .` clean. Then enumerate the red tests once:
   `TEST_REPORTER=dot npm run test:nosim > $SCRATCH/red.txt 2>&1; grep -E '^not ok|✖' $SCRATCH/red.txt`.
   This is the focused set for a loader change (160 test files import `loadCartridge`); run it at most

## 7. Risks (honest)

1. **Trust boundary** (D5): after S7 the loader accepts any hash-valid artifact's semantics; a dangling
   reference crashes at `fact.ts:24`/`fresh.ts:286` instead of a refusal. Only compiler output is loaded today;
   PREP-03 must re-add provenance (signature or server compile) before downloadable content.
2. **A loader-only semantic check surfaces mid-slice** (scope trigger in rule 3). Known candidate already
   handled: `scopeSites` (kept). Others are unknown until the twin table is built; budget one PM ruling per
   slice.
3. **Shared-file conflicts** across parallel slices (`cartridge.ts` list, `refStage` tail, corpus): delete-only,
   trivial to resolve, but the PM merges sub-branches serially and reruns `cartridge.test.ts` after each merge.
4. **Test-suite enumeration cost**: each S7 slice runs `test:nosim` once or twice (CI's kernel job is ~394 s;
   locally similar). Three developers at once is the owner's load cap; stagger starts by a few minutes.
5. **#487 overlap**: if C1 is cut before #487 merges, every S7 slice conflicts in the test files it edits (D6).
6. **Mixed tests (~98 files)**: deleting a refusal block inside a file that also plays is the judgment work;
   expect the reviewers' blockers here ("test deleted, twin not cited"). The table rule is the control.
7. **`size: allow` markers** fail the commit hook when files shrink (item 10); the briefs say to remove them.
8. **Story views regen** on every push (`kernel/ts/src/` changed): slow but must be byte-identical; a diff there
   means the loader changed what it returns (it must not: it returns `c` unchanged).
9. **Manifest `at_least` becomes decorative** (item 7): acceptable; a release re-adds one range check against the
   release's API, as the audit said.
10. The sub-branch flow (D7) is my process assumption for parallel developers on one draft branch; the PM may
    prefer one branch and serialized pushes (slower: no parallelism).

BRIEF B5 (Fable 2026-10-28):
# B5 brief (loka-ivjq.28): one Beads sync step for after_merge and beads_checkpoint

Goal: `bin/after_merge.sh` and `bin/beads_checkpoint.sh` share one step that pulls main and folds the
database and main's export together, so the PM never sees "Sync conflict / main changed the export,
merge by hand" for the common case (main's export moved since the database last imported it, while
the PM kept writing Beads in the main checkout). Replaces loka-9ch9's refuse-then-manual loop (4 hits
this week) and the #484 B5 attempt (reverted; its three failure states are the red controls below).

## Evidence behind the design (real br 0.7.6, throwaway workspaces, `--no-auto-import` between steps)
- `br sync --import-only` is row-level last-writer-wins: with a local title edit and a newer main
  priority edit on the same row the title vanished silently; with main older, main's edit vanished.
  So "import-only then flush, no merge mode" cannot refuse a same-row conflict. Rejected.
- `br sync --flush-only` exports dirty rows only: after discarding a dirty export it prints "Nothing
  to export", and with un-imported JSONL rows it refuses (`Refusing to export stale database`). That
  guard, plus the set-aside/checkout dance letting the post-merge hook import a JSONL that lacks the
  PM's new rows, is the whole loka-9ch9 mechanism. The dance goes.
- `br sync --merge` (3-way on `.beads/beads.base.jsonl`, the last local export): different rows
  merge (rc 0, both kept); same row refuses rc 7 `BothModified`, leaving DB, export and base
  untouched; a discarded dirty export (new row + edit) is rebuilt from the database; a database that
  never imported HEAD's export merges main's later move correctly; rerunning after an uncommitted
  merge is a no-op when the export is left in place; `--force-db` / `--force-jsonl` change only the
  listed rows and still merge main's other rows. `AmbiguousBase` appears only when an older JSONL is
  put in front of a base a merge already updated: #484 did that by swapping HEAD's export in.

## Must be true
1. No row is ever lost: every row in the database or on `origin/main` is in the pushed export.
2. The common case needs no human: main's export moved since the last import, local rows differ.
3. A true same-row conflict refuses before any write to DB, export or base (main may already be
   fast-forwarded) and prints the row ids plus steps that work when followed literally.
4. Rerunning either script after a death at any later line works (same outcome, no refusal).
5. Nothing rewrites, deletes or rebuilds `.beads/beads.base.jsonl`; never `--force`/`--force-db`
   inside the scripts; the post-merge import hook never runs under the step.
6. The real-br controls run in hosted CI, not only when a developer remembers.

## Files
- New `bin/lib/beads_sync.sh` (sourced before any `cd`, like `bin/lib/clean_git_env.sh`): `br1`
  (moved from after_merge.sh:21-28, WAL/busy retry) and `beads_sync`.
- `bin/after_merge.sh`: lines 65-75 become `beads_sync || die`; keep the ROADMAP check (67) before
  it; the stale-copy check (35) also diffs `bin/lib/beads_sync.sh`; header comment lines 8-10, 16-17.
- `bin/beads_checkpoint.sh`: lines 16-21 become `beads_sync || die`; line 24 undoes its own commit on
  a rejected push (`before=$(git rev-parse HEAD)` taken before the commit; `git reset -q "$before"`)
  and says `push rejected: main moved; rerun bin/beads_checkpoint.sh`.
- New `bin/beads_sync_red_controls.sh` (real br); `bin/integration_red_controls.sh` after_merge
  (64-146) and beads_checkpoint (743-770) stub cases adapted (below).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` lint job; `bin/prepush.sh`; `docs/CHECKS.md:122-129`; `docs/BEADS.md`
  and `docs/HANDOFF.md:79-83` (br version pin, "pull, merge" wording). No new config or env vars.

## Design: `beads_sync` (about 15 lines)
1. `git fetch -q origin main`.
2. If `origin/main` changed `.beads/issues.jsonl` relative to HEAD: `git checkout -q -- .beads/issues.jsonl`
   (the file is a flush of the database, so nothing is lost; the merge re-exports it). Otherwise leave
   it, dirty or not: after an uncommitted merge the base equals it, and swapping in HEAD's older copy
   is exactly what produced AmbiguousBase in #484.
3. `git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null pull -q --ff-only origin main` (hooks off: the post-merge
   `--import-only` is last-writer-wins and would hide a same-row conflict from the merge). A failed
   pull (main changed docs/HANDOFF.md or ROADMAP under a dirty copy) dies "pull failed; merge that
   file by hand, rerun"; the discarded export is not restored (the rerun's merge rebuilds it).
4. `br1 sync --merge`. On any failure, after br's own row list, print exactly:
   `br sync --merge refused: main is fast-forwarded; the database, export and base are unchanged.`
   `Compare a row: br show <id> --json; grep '"id":"<id>"' .beads/issues.jsonl (main's copy).`
   `Keep this checkout's rows: br sync --merge --force-db  (main's other rows are merged in).`
   `Keep main's rows: br sync --merge --force-jsonl. AmbiguousBase = main holds an older copy of a`
   `row edited here (an earlier run's export was never pushed): --force-db. Then rerun this script.`
5. `python3 bin/check_beads_export.py .beads/issues.jsonl` (machine path: "fix the issue text with
   br update, rerun"; a rerun merges again cleanly, verified).
Each script then does what it does today (br close, worktree/branch cleanup, review index, commit, push).

## Red controls (`bin/beads_sync_red_controls.sh`, real br; bare origin, clone A = integration checkout
with `loka.beads.integrationRoot` set and `.githooks` active, clone M = "main"; rows made with
`br create --silent` in M, flushed and pushed; A imports; A edits row a's title to `one-local`)
- Common case: M edits b to `two-main`, adds d, pushes. `beads_sync` in A: rc 0; export and
  `br show` hold a=one-local, b=two-main, d; `git status` shows only `.beads/issues.jsonl` dirty.
- (a) died after sync: run `beads_sync` once (as above), commit nothing, run it again with main
  unchanged: rc 0, export identical to the first run, no "AmbiguousBase" in the output. Mutant that
  goes red: `git checkout -- .beads/issues.jsonl` unconditionally before the pull.
- (b) same row: M sets a's priority to 0 and b to `two-main`, pushes. `beads_sync`: rc 1, output names
  a's id and `BothModified` and the five lines above; `br show a` still `one-local`, `beads.base.jsonl`
  unchanged (hash), HEAD = origin/main. Then run the printed `br sync --merge --force-db` and
  `beads_sync` again: rc 0, export has a=one-local/p2 and b=two-main. Mutants: `--force-db` in the
  script (first call exits 0, a's title or priority lost); dropping `-c core.hooksPath=/dev/null`
  (hook imports, first call exits 0, title lost); restoring the pre-pull export after the refusal
  (`--force-db` then yields b=two, as in #484).
- (c) base never rebuilt: A pulls M's first commit with the hook refusing (A has a dirty row), so the
  database never imported it; M then edits c and pushes. `beads_sync`: rc 0, export holds
  one-local, two-main and c's new title. Mutant: copy `git show HEAD:.beads/issues.jsonl` over
  `beads.base.jsonl` before the merge (drops two-main).
- Checkpoint rerun (stub br, in integration_red_controls.sh): push rejected by a pre-receive hook ->
  rc 1, HEAD back at the pre-commit sha, export and HANDOFF dirty; remove the hook, rerun -> rc 0 and
  origin holds the row. The `main-changed` case flips from "refused, rc 1" to "rc 0, origin holds
  both rows" (stub `sync --merge` appends `$BC_ROW` instead of overwriting). after_merge stub:
  `sync --merge` re-adds `local-write` when missing; line 110 greps `sync --merge`.
Every expected value is a literal from the setup, not read back from the implementation.

## 2. Decisions (PM defaults; the owner ratifies the starred ones)

- D1*. **Scripted action is the name.** Capability `action_recipe@1` -> `scripted_action@1` (registry key, `feature_registry.json`, `feature.schema.json`, every manifest's `requires.capabilities`); definition kind `recipe` -> `scripted_action`; artifact map `recipes` -> `scripted_actions`; **ref kind `action` for both maps** (`...:action/<key>`; keys are unique across them, `recipes.ex:84 duplicate/3`); types `ActionRecipe` -> `ScriptedAction`, `RecipeTarget` -> `ScriptedTarget`, `RecipeCost` -> `ActionCost`, `RecipeCraft` -> `ActionCraft`, `RecipeNarration` -> `ActionNarration`; TS `mechanics/scripted_action/`, `Offered.scripted`, `world.cartridge.scripted_actions`; Elixir `Loka.Content.ScriptedActions` (`scripted_actions.ex`), `action_tips.ex`; `coverage.ts` `never.scripted_actions`; `why.ts --action <key>`. Two maps stay (the owner's note says renamed, not merged; one map is the L+ contract merge the .22 design check rejected). The compiler resolves an `action/<key>` ref in `defs["action"]` then `defs["scripted_action"]` (one `resolve` clause in `refs.ex`), and `artifact.ex keyed/3` writes `action/` for both kinds (one map lookup). Alternative if the owner prefers fewer moving parts: keep `action_recipe@1` as the capability id and rename only the words; the plan's R slice shrinks by the manifests and registry.
- D2. **One `Step` and one `Check`, in `protocol/step.schema.json`** (`$defs/Step`, `$defs/Check`; `Loka.Core.Contracts` loads `protocol/*.schema.json` by wildcard, `bin/contracts.exs` generates from all). `Step` is the union of the 33 words with each op's full field set (optional subject fields `npc`, `item`, `with`, `room`, `tag`, `co_present` on the ops that have them today; `build {structure, direction, site?, escrow?, fact?}`; `event.emit {event}`; the 12 benefit ops with their fields). `Check` is today's five action kinds plus optional `failure` and `rating` on `opposed`. `ReactionRule`, scripted outcomes, `DialogueChoice` and `ServiceDefinition.benefit` all `$ref` them. `RecipeStep`, `RecipeCheck`, `DialogueCheck`, `ServiceBenefit` and the inline reaction and choice unions go.
- D3*. **The field is `steps`** on all three: reaction `apply`, outcome `sequence`, choice `sequence` -> `steps` (one word to learn; scripted rewrite of 449 source files; 51 kernel test files carry inline shapes). If the owner wants the smaller diff, keep the three field names and only the union changes: say so on return and A, B, C drop their rename rows.
- D4*. **A choice's terms stay fields; only its `steps` use the shared list.** `accept`, `hand_over`, `receive`, `payment`, `lesson_payment`, `exchange`, `escort`, `patrol`, `availability`, `check` and C2's `story_point` are admission terms with fixed event positions (item 3), not ordered effects; moving them into `steps` would change rule order, which the owner excluded. The audit's `accept -> quest.activate`, `hand_over/receive -> item.move`, `payment -> resource.adjust` are therefore not done. Rule for the Builders' Guide: "a choice's terms (what must hold, what changes hands) are fields; what it does afterwards is `steps`." Zero-use `payment` and `availability` are deleted only if their tests are the sole users (scope trigger in C).
- D5*. **A service's benefit is one `Step`** (`benefit: {op: "meal", ...}`; `kind` -> `op`), so `build` is one word with one shape and the Guide has one list. The GameView `ServiceOffer.benefit` follows (pass-through): story views change in that field only, listed in V's acceptance. Cheaper alternative: leave `benefit.kind` alone and only align `build`'s fields; then "service benefits" drops out of F4's title.
- D6. **Each context runs a declared subset; the compiler enforces it, the kernel fails closed.** `lib/loka/content/steps.ex` holds one table, op -> `{refs (from LeafRefs.steps), owning event, contexts, per-context field rules}`, encoding exactly today's rules moved, not changed: reaction = the 16 ops + `event.emit` (owner F7 ruling); scripted outcome = `fact.assign`, `event.emit`, `status.cure` (use target only), `status.apply`/`damage`/`light.ignite` (spell target only), `resource.adjust`, `build` (detail target, success outcome, once); choice = `fact.assign`, `fact.adjust`, `skill.acquire`, `topic.grant`; service = the 12 benefit ops, exactly one. A step outside its context's set, or a field the context does not run (an action's `fact.assign` with `npc`), is `SCHEMA_VIOLATION {error: "invalid_value"}` at the step's `op` or field (today's code for the spell and build placement rules; no new code). Each applier's fallthrough throws `KernelError` instead of treating an unknown op as `fact.assign`. Semantic extras stay where they are (`quest.activate` trigger restriction, `replenish.run` repeat, `status.apply` room/listener, `OUTCOME_MISMATCH`).
- D7. **Rule-order semantics unchanged, by construction.** The three appliers keep their contexts (subject, writer group, event positions); only their types and the new `event.emit` branch change. `COMPOSES` (`decision.ts:214-233`) and the rule map (`world.ts:55-78`) are tables keyed by capability: the rename reorders nothing. Reaction `event.emit` emits `custom_event` with the delivery's subject at the next position in the rule's writer group; its budget is the existing delivery budget (`proposal.ts`), proven by a test.
- D8. **One `Check` type, two evaluators.** `rule.ts resolve` and `sequence.ts checked` stay; the compiler requires `failure` on a choice and refuses it on an action, allows only `opposed` on a choice (today's limit), and keeps key uniqueness across both (`check_kinds.ex`, renamed from `choice_checks.ex`, absorbs `recipes.ex` `shared_checks`, `opposed`, `rater`, `attributes`).
- D9. **One re-pin.** Every slice but Z changes `lib/` or `protocol/`, so `bin/regen.sh` rebuilds all 49 fixtures, the 53 transcript hashes, `schemas/source`, `contracts.gen.*`, story views and live saves at each handback (C2 rules 2 and D10); the batch's final head is the one re-pin against `main`. Transcript replay stays green at every head (keys, not kinds).
- D10. **Order.** R (rename) first and alone: it touches the files every later slice edits. P (shared schema and table) second and alone: A, B, C, V consume it. Then the per-context slices in parallel (disjoint modules, cartridge directories and test files), V and Z last.
- D11. **No new TS table.** Context subsets live in `steps.ex` only; TS appliers narrow by their own `if` chains and the fail-closed fallthrough; `Step` is one generated type.

## 4. Rules shared by every slice

Linked, not copied: [brief kit](docs/guides/brief-kit.md), [developer](.claude/agents/developer.md), AGENTS.md Simplicity and Writing tests, `docs/lessons/contracts.md` (schema mutant sweep for every slice that edits `protocol/`). Handoff threshold 220k tokens (180k near a push). Sub-branch from the current head of `simplify/c3-steps`; the reviewer reviews the sub-branch head against it; the PM merges with `bin/pm_merge.sh` after APPROVE.

1. **Before the regen commit and handback: `git merge origin/simplify/c3-steps`**, rerun the slice's focused tests, then regen once (C1 lesson: parallel slices clash in shared tests; a stale base is the usual cause of a red CI job in code the diff does not touch).
2. **No local suites.** `npm run test:files -- <files>` and `mix test <files>` only; push with `bin/push_slice.sh`; `bin/wait_ci.sh <sha>` in the background; hand back on green only. The hosted kernel and elixir jobs are the red-test list.
3. **Regenerated families are never hand-edited or hand-merged** (`protocol/fixtures/*_hash.json`, `cartridges/*/transcripts/*.jsonl`, `mobile/app/stories/live/*.sql`, `schemas/source/*.json`, `*.gen.*`, `test/loka/lint_baseline.txt`): on conflict `git checkout --theirs -- <paths>`, `sh bin/regen.sh`, commit.
4. **Shared lists, one line each, never reformatted**: `steps.ex` context table (P writes it whole; A, B, C, V do not edit it: a rule a slice finds missing is a scope trigger), `leaf_refs.ex steps/0`, `capability_registry.json`, `cartridge.schema.json` `CompiledCartridge` properties, `protocol/README.md` rows, `docs/features.json`. Take both.
5. **Corpus rewrites are scripted** (`python3 -I` in the scratchpad, JSON-aware, by kind directory and key path, dumped in the file's current style); the script is pasted in the handback. Hand-kept `value` fixtures (item 9) are edited only by the slice whose brief names them.
6. **Check table per handback.** A rename slice lists the renamed symbols (`old | new | files`). A vocabulary slice has one row per compiler check it moved (`old site file:line | rule | new site in steps.ex or check_kinds.ex | Elixir test file:line that asserts it`) and one per deleted test (`test | what it guarded | what guards it now`). Every new conditional has a test and a pasted red-control line (`bin/mutate.sh`; `bin/mutate_diff.sh` lists candidates).
7. **Both kernels stay in step**: `mix test test/loka/cartridge_cross_kernel_test.exs` green; `loadCartridge(toolbox_showcase_hash.json).ok === true`; transcript replay green (`npm run test:files -- test/transcripts.test.ts`); story views and live saves byte-identical except hashes unless the brief lists a field (V).
8. **Handback** under 250 words: head sha, the table, `git diff --shortstat`, the regen commit sha, CI run id, open questions, COST. `/code-review medium simplify/c3-<slice>` before push.
9. **Scope triggers (stop and ask)**: a step whose context rule you cannot express in the `steps.ex` table shape; any change to an applier's event positions, writer group or subject; a transcript that stops replaying; a story view diff the brief did not list; a test whose play depends on a deleted shape; `cartridge_cross_kernel_test.exs` red after regen.

title: Same reaction firing twice in one advance faults conflicting_write (fact rows across job writer groups)
description: Found in loka-qi0r review: with per-hour steps inside one wait, an NPC entering the same reaction room twice (woods at 17:00 and 19:00) faults conflicting_write; hour-by-hour waits commit. Likely pre-existing for two different NPCs firing one fact-writing reaction in one advance (unverified). Same family as loka-x2gv: repeated writes to one row from different job writer groups need to chain in order (as G3 did for status holders). Effect today: a player wait over such a span is refused; elapsed settlement is not affected (host stops at each due job). title: Cast refusal for a learned spell above the actor's level gives no reason (invalid_state, no message)
description: Word bar S3 designer review (loka-a9pn, word_bar.test.ts:116): 'ward, cast: not now' is invalid_state without a message key; the player cannot learn what unlocks the word. Send a message key (or level_too_low) from cast admission, both views. Follow-up of S2 loka-1lpq; word bar batch.
notes:
BRIEF loka-j64e: cast refusal for a learned spell the actor cannot cast yet gives a reason (PM 2026-10-15). Size S, Opus. HANDOFF THRESHOLD: near 100k tokens stop, push, hand back.

GOAL. When the actor has LEARNED the spell and its policy fails, the refusal (command and GameView spell_words reason) carries the failing policy's authored reason, the same way other policy-gated actions surface their reason (find how action policies report a reason today: e.g. recipes/services with a policy `reason`/message key; reuse that, no new mechanism). If the policy has no authored reason, keep today's behavior. Unlearned spells must still read exactly as an unknown word (no leak; S2 test "an unknown word and unread noctis are refused alike" must stay green).
Content: give spells_sampler's ward policy an authored reason text ("Needs level 2" or the cartridge's own wording) so the acceptance has a literal. If this needs a schema field that does not exist, STOP and ask (no new floor expected).
ACCEPTANCE. spells_sampler at level 1 after learning ward: GameView spell_words ward {available: false, reason: <the authored text>}; casting ward is refused with the same reason; the Book chip shows "<word>, cast" unavailable with that reason (update word_bar.test.ts:116 expected text). Unlearned/unknown words unchanged. Red controls: drop the reason pass-through -> the test fails.
REALM SEAMS (docs/decisions/owner-decision-realm-seams-2026-10-13.md#brief-checklist): 1 met (actor's level), 8 met (no leak), others n/a; confirm in handback.
ROW 16 LESSONS: run every test a refusal change could hit (spells, spell_effects, speech, view_actor, word_bar, transcripts if a sampler hash changes: update its known answer and the SystemDataModel Impact story list if needed); red control per new check; push after reading prepush's exit status (echo $? right after git push).

DEV 2026-10-15: BLOCKED, question to PM: no authored policy-reason field exists (VersionedPolicy/ActionRecipe closed); options (a) recipe reason TextKey schema field, (b) engine leaf-keyed text. Worktree kept, no commits.
PM ruling 2026-10-15: option (a) optional authored reason text key on the recipe (whole-policy reason; ward fails on level or wis). Deferred until after the Built rooms batch (needs the next kernel_api floor after 1.99). Not part of the word bar batch.
Fable/PM 2026-10-15: run as its own hosted PR at kernel_api 1.100 right after Built rooms (#392) merges; brief above stands (option a: optional authored reason text key on the recipe).
BRIEF v2 loka-j64e (PM 2026-10-15, supersedes the lane and floor lines above; GOAL/ACCEPTANCE above stand). Size S, Opus. HANDOFF THRESHOLD: near 100k tokens stop, push, hand back.
LANE: Hosted PR. Branch toolbox/j64e from origin/main, own worktree ../worktrees.noindex/j64e (bin/worktree_setup.sh). Push, open a ready PR, confirm ci.yml and book-e2e.yml started with one `gh run list --commit <sha>`, hand back. Never wait on CI.

When a LEARNED spell's policy fails and the recipe has `reason`, the command refusal and GameView spell_words carry that text; no `reason` -> today's behavior. Unlearned/unknown words unchanged (no leak). Compiler (Elixir) and loader (TS) both admit the field: the text key resolves in the catalog (UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE otherwise, both kernels) and needs kernel_api at least 1.100 (KERNEL_API_RANGE_INVALID at requires.kernel_api.at_least). Raise the supported kernel_api to 1.100. Amend docs/system (cartridge.md recipe section, mechanics.md spell words) in the same PR first.

The draw order must stay identical: sim.test.ts and sim_seeds.json digests must not change, which proves it. Pick the highest-ranked command type, in this order:
  - sell, harvest, choose, accept_quest, take, talk;
  - a move to the least-visited adjacent room;
  - otherwise wait to the next hour.

## hs-1 — `replenish.run` reaction step (engine), kernel_api 1.101, `toolbox/hs-1`, S-M

GOAL. A reaction may move conserved items now, so a crop, an egg, a catch or a spent input appears or disappears on an event. Beads loka-kgd.108.1 engine half; consumers hs-2 to hs-5.
CONTRACT. Reaction step `{op: "replenish.run", key}` (`protocol/reaction.schema.json`; `key` a `replenish` entry of this cartridge, UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE at the step's `key` in both kernels; floor 1.101 KERNEL_API_RANGE_INVALID; refused on a rule with `after`, as `item.move` is, FD1 rule). Semantics: one run of the entry's move body (`runReplenish`, `kernel/ts/src/mechanics/containment/job.ts`: `min(count, cap - held, free)` of `items` directly in `from` to `to`, lowest EntityId first), in the delivery's writer group or the group an earlier write of the advance gave the item (row 41's join), no job completed or scheduled, no event, nothing when nothing fits. Factor the move body out of `runReplenish` so the job and the step share it.
FILES. In: `reaction.ts` dispatch, `containment/job.ts`, `lib/loka/content/reactions.ex` (`@steps` floor 101, key check) and the TS loader twin, `protocol/reaction.schema.json`, `docs/system/mechanics.md` section "Replenish on an event (Homestead)" plus a row in the reaction@1 step list, `loader_floors.json`, `world.ts` 1.101. Test: `kernel/ts/test/replenish.test.ts` on `cartridges/replenish_sampler` with a rule swapped in by the test (SR-row pattern), no new sampler. Out: a `when` on replenish entries, body as `to`.
ACCEPTANCE. Rule `custom_event {custom: dig}` -> `replenish.run seam_regrowth`: at clock 0 after two harvests, the event moves one ore store -> mine at once; a second event the same second, cap 2, moves one more; a third moves none; the timed job at 3600 still runs and moves nothing (cap). Red controls: step dropped -> the mine stays empty; stale `key` -> UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE in both kernels; `at_least 1.100` -> floors case.
REALM: 1 met (the step reads no actor; the delivery's actor is RS-4's); 2 met (no subject read: the entry names both holders); 3 n/a; 4 met (no clock); 5 met (world state, audience public); 6 to 9 n/a.
BOOK. Kernel only.
SCOPE TRIGGER: any new op, event, job kind or save row.

## hs-2 — Farming (content), 1.101 (no bump), `toolbox/hs-2`, M

GOAL. Sow a seed in a plot, watch it grow over game days, water it, harvest the crop. Beads loka-kgd.108.1.
MECHANISM, each part's existing mechanism: plot = an authored container item `furrow` on the field's floor, too heavy to take (containment `too_heavy`), with G7 `put` lock on `owns_plot` for the owned plot and none for the public one (row 24 entitlement, `property_sampler` seller). Sow = Put the seed in the furrow (containment@1, offered today). Reaction `item_acquired {item: seed}` (subject = holder, the furrow) -> `status.apply growing` on the furrow (G3 item status, duration one game day, tick every hour; ticks change nothing on an item) and `fact.stamp sown_at {item: furrow}` (FD1, W2 entity fact). Stages = W6 `description_variants` on the furrow reading `time_since {fact: sown_at, item: furrow, at_least}` ("bare earth", "green shoots", "heavy heads"); season by `sky {season}` on the sow rule's `when` (row 31, trap 1: nothing stored). Water = G4 use recipe `water` (tool `{tag: liquid_holding}` holding water, target `has_tag furrow`) -> `fact.stamp watered_at {item: furrow}` through its `custom_event` reaction. Ripen: `status_expired {status: growing}` with `when not time_since {watered_at, item: furrow, at_least 43200}` -> `replenish.run crop` (`{items [turnip_01..03], from larder (sealed), to furrow, cap 1, count 1, every 10^9}`) and `replenish.run spent_seed` (`{items [seed_01], from furrow, to midden}`); the wither rule (the inverse `when`) -> `status.apply withered` (W8 permanent; cured by the next sow: `status.cure` on `item_acquired`) and the same spent-seed move. Harvest = Take the turnip from the furrow. Seed supply: one seed cycling midden -> seed sack by a timed replenish (the `item` filter names an instance, so N seeds would be N rules: state it).
FILES. In: `cartridges/farm_sampler` (field, hut-less; seller; two furrows; larder, midden sealed), `kernel/ts/test/farm.test.ts`, mechanics.md section, `docs/MECHANICS-TOOLBOX.md` row .108.1 status, `docs/features.json` row if the sampler catalogue needs one. Out: engine.
ACCEPTANCE (literals, start clock C0). Put seed at C0: furrow reads "green shoots" at C0+3600, "heavy heads" at C0+64800; watered at C0+50000, at C0+86400 the furrow holds `turnip_01`, the seed is in the midden; never watered: `withered`, no turnip. One advance C0 -> C0+86400 equals hourly steps (mechanics lesson). A stranger's Put on the owned furrow: `permission_denied`; the public furrow accepts. Reopen between sow and ripen, then elapse: same state.
REALM: 1 met (Put, water and Take read the command actor; the furrow's facts are entity facts); 2 met (subjects: the furrow holder, the expiring status's holder); 3 n/a; 4 met (logical seconds; season derived); 5 met (world state; the plot is shared-world, audience public); 7: the owned plot is exclusive by entitlement, moves by none, theft never; 6, 8, 9 n/a.
BOOK. No new component: Item page Put/Take (BOOK-UI-COMPONENTS "Item details"), the furrow's variant text, the watering card on the can's page (G4 pattern). One browser interaction at 390 px with a screenshot. No designer.
SCOPE TRIGGER: any engine edit; `time_since` or `fact.stamp` not accepting `item` on these triggers (stop, report).

## hs-3 — Fishing (content), 1.101, `toolbox/hs-3`, S

GOAL. Cast a rod at the water; what bites depends on hour, season and weather; a miss is a miss. Beads loka-kgd.108.3.
MECHANISM. Water = a `pool` item on the bank, too heavy to take, tag `water` (G1 closed set: reuse an existing tag or add `water` only if none fits; `water` exists as SR7's room tag, not an item tag: the developer checks the `Tag` enum). Cast = G4 use recipe `cast` (tool `{tag: rod}`; target `has_tag water`; `check {kind: luck}`; cooldown; `duration` 60). Success outcome `event.emit bite`; failure narration "nothing bites". Reactions on `custom_event {custom: bite}`: `trout` `when time_window {06:00-18:00}` -> `replenish.run trout`; `eel` `when not time_window ...` -> `replenish.run eel`; `salmon` `when sky {weather: rain}` -> `replenish.run salmon` (rules run in key order; all three may fire on a rainy day, the cap bounds each). Each entry moves one fish larder -> bank, cap 1. Catch = Take. Stock loop: fish eaten or spoiled (row 41 `item.move` to the midden) return to the larder by a timed entry. The seeded draw is the recipe's luck check (an outcome, not variety: trap 5 honoured); no per-plan RNG (row 9) is used, and the brief says so.
FILES. In: `cartridges/fishing_sampler` (bank, larder, midden, rod on the bank, tags), `kernel/ts/test/fishing.test.ts`, mechanics.md, toolbox row. Out: engine; the `rod` tag if it needs an enum change beyond one entry (stop).
ACCEPTANCE. From a seed where the luck check passes (literal from `check@1`'s roll shape, hand-fixed) at 10:00 clear: `trout_01` on the bank, no eel, no salmon; at 22:00: eel only; a rainy day (row 31's per-day hash: pick a seed/day literal with rain) at 10:00: trout and salmon; a failing seed: nothing moves, the cooldown still starts. Without the rod the card is unlisted; with it worn in a sack, refused (held-tool rule).
REALM: 1 met (actor from the perform); 2 met (`custom_event`'s subject is the actor's body; the moves name holders); 3 n/a; 4 met (clock-derived windows and weather); 5 met (bank stock is world state, public); 6 to 9 n/a.
BOOK. No new component: the rod's Item page lists "Cast at the pool" (G4 card pattern); the catch appears in the room's loose items. One browser interaction. No designer.

## hs-4 — Animals (content), 1.101, `toolbox/hs-4`, M

GOAL. Hens in an owned pen; fill the trough; fed hens lay; they breed to a cap. Beads loka-kgd.108.2. Milk and wool are the same shape with a second plan; one species in the sampler.
MECHANISM. Pen = authored room with G7 `enter` lock on `owns_pen` (row 24 entitlement). Hens = population plan `hens` `{home pen, area [pen], cap 4, day_target 2, night_target 2, replacement_delay 86400, wander_interval 3600, birth_when population_count {hens, at_least 2}}` (C3 plan, W12 gate: breeding within a cap, RNG-free). Feed = Put the grain sack in the `trough` (container item, too heavy): reaction `item_acquired {item: grain_01}` -> `status.apply {status: fed, co_present: true}` (W21: every living NPC in the event's room; the developer confirms `eventRooms` gives the actor's room for `item_acquired`) and `replenish.run spent_grain` (trough -> midden); the sack returns to the feed store by a timed entry. Lay = `status_ticked {status: fed}` (G3 NPC tick event, tick every 4 game hours, duration one day) -> `replenish.run eggs` (`{items [egg_01..06], from larder, to nest (container item in the pen), cap 3, count 1}`). Eggs are edible. No young: a birth is a hen (row 45 later; ruling below).
FILES. In: `cartridges/pen_sampler`, `kernel/ts/test/pen.test.ts`, mechanics.md, toolbox row. Out: engine; milk/wool.
ACCEPTANCE (C0 start, two hens at genesis). Grain in the trough at C0: both hens `fed`; nest holds one egg at C0+14400, two at C0+28800, three at C0+43200, still three at C0+57600 (cap); no grain: no egg at C0+14400. Third and fourth hens born at the first occurrence after `population_count` holds (literal time); kill one hen (cap stays, slot refills after 86400). One long advance equals steps. A stranger: pen `permission_denied`.
REALM: 1 met (Put reads the actor; the plan job stores nothing per character); 2 met (`fed` lands on the trough event's co-present NPCs, eggs name holders; tick subject is the hen); 3 n/a (no payout); 4 met; 5 met (hens and eggs are world state, public, once-per-world births); 7: the pen is exclusive by entitlement, moves by none; 9: shared-world; 6, 8 n/a.
BOOK. No new component: Put on the sack's page, Take from the nest (container pattern), hens as entity lines. One browser interaction. No designer.
SCOPE TRIGGER: `co_present` not reaching the hens from a Put (then stop: the fix is in reaction.ts, hs-1's thread).

## hs-5 — Cooking: `edible.applies` (engine S) + kitchen (content), 1.101, `toolbox/hs-5`, S-M

GOAL. Raw food becomes a meal that buffs; a meal spoils. Beads loka-kgd.108.4.
ENGINE. `edible.applies: [status ref]` (`protocol/entity.schema.json`; refs resolve, both kernels, gated 1.101 in a twin like `cartridge_construction.ts`): Eat applies each listed status to the eater's body through the shared apply helper (`statusStep`'s path in `mechanics/status/shared.ts`, so `status_applied` fires, `immune` holds, a refresh is silent), after `restores` and `cures`. No `ate` event (rejected below). Gate: no listed status may `modifies` an hp-maximum attribute (loka-kgd.50): loader check SCHEMA_VIOLATION at `applies[i]`, both kernels, red control.
CONTENT. Cooking is a service at a cook NPC in the kitchen (20a/20b, existing): `stew` commission `{escrow {items [fish_01..05], quantity 2, custody larder, ready_after 300, output stew_01}}`, price 1; `claim` 1. The stew is edible, `applies [hearty]` (row 2c `modifies str +2`, one game hour), takes `spoiling` on `item_acquired` (row 41: to the midden after a day), W6 variant "a cold, filmed stew" after half a day by `time_since`... keep to the status: variant on `status_active` is enough. Spent fish return to the pond larder by a timed entry (closed loop).
FILES. In: `food/shared.ts`, `entity.schema.json`, the TS and Elixir item checks, `cartridges/kitchen_sampler`, `kernel/ts/test/kitchen.test.ts`, mechanics.md, a `loader_floors.json` feature case. Out: recipes consuming items (kgd.83), an `ate` event.

A stew held a day is in the midden. Red controls: `applies` ignored -> no `hearty`; an `applies` naming a con-modifying status -> refused in both kernels.
REALM: 1 met (Eat and the order read the actor; "one open order per service" is 20b's known limit, restated); 2 n/a; 3 n/a; 4 met; 5 met (the buff is a status on the actor's body); 6 to 9 n/a.

## hs-6 — Furnishing and decoration: `item_present` leaf + sampler, 1.101, `toolbox/hs-6`, S-M (Batch B)

GOAL. A placed object changes what a room does or says by its property. Settle S1 and Beads loka-kgd.108.6.
ENGINE. Policy leaf `{op: "item_present", tag}` (`protocol/policy.schema.json`, `mechanics/policy.ts`, `lib/loka/content/policy*.ex` parity, `LeafRefs` if tags are checked; owned by containment@1): holds when an item directly in the room with that G1 tag exists; the room is the described room in a room or blueprint variant (S4's `status_active subject room` shape), else the actor's room; one query step per entity in the room. Bed: reaction `rested {room: hut}` `when item_present {tag: bed}` -> `status.apply well_rested` (positive mv per tick, one hour). Forge: recipe `temper` policy `item_present {tag: forge}` with a skill check. Chest: a container (exists). Decoration: the hut's `description_variants` `when item_present {tag: rug}` -> "A rug warms the boards." Nothing else is stored (trap 11).

Red control: leaf reading the actor's room in a room variant -> the hut page describes wrongly when the actor stands in the yard (test from the yard's examine of... the hut is not visible from the yard; instead test a blueprint variant on a built room later: use the `describe` unit path with a target room). ## hs-7 — Gifting and barter, 1.101, `toolbox/hs-7`, M (Batch B)

GOAL. Liked and disliked gifts move a person's trust; tiers open talk; two pelts buy a knife with no coin. Beads loka-kgd.108.5, loka-kgd.70.
GIFTING is content on rows 15 and W2 (already shown by `standing_sampler`): per NPC, a rule per liked item (`item_acquired {item}` + `fact.adjust trust +1` with `when` on a pair fact so it pays once) and per disliked item (`-1`); dialogue choices gated by `fact_compare` tiers; a W6 room line per tier (trap 8: lines, not gates, except dialogue). Engine for the Book: none (hs-8).
BARTER engine (S): (1) an escrow `output` without `ready_after`: the commission's transition moves the output custody -> body in the same proposal, no job, no claim (`service/shared.ts` `transition`, loader twins allow the pair); (2) `price: 0` on a commission with `escrow` (`service.schema.json` bound; `quoted_price` minimum 0 in `command.schema.json`; both kernels; mutant sweep; the commerce save reconciliation must accept a zero payment: the developer reads `mobile/authority/local-story/store.ts`'s payment path first and stops if it needs more than a bound change). Content: trader `knife_for_pelts` `{price 0, escrow {items [pelt_01..03], quantity 2, custody stall, output knife_01}}`.
FILES. In: `service/shared.ts`, `service.schema.json`, `command.schema.json`, `cartridge_services.ts` / `services.ex`, `cartridges/gift_sampler`, `kernel/ts/test/gift.test.ts`, mechanics.md ("Barter (toolbox row kgd.70)"), floors feature case. Out: `commerce/shared.ts`, Book.

## 1. The engine set (composition over what exists)

Three engine pieces, all under the Homestead floor 1.101 (ruling 9), feature cases in
`protocol/fixtures/loader_floors.json` (format: the "a recipe reason" case, lines 928-941).

**E1 `ActionRecipe.craft`** (hs-10). `craft: {consume?: {items, quantity, to, reason?}, yield?:
{items, from}}`, at least one of the two. `consume`: the first `quantity` of `items` directly in the
actor's body (`selected`, lowest EntityId first), each one Give would let go (`giveRefused`), move to
holder `to` (an `ItemLocation`, not `template`, as replenish refuses) on every accepted perform,
failure included (the semantics of `costs`, `action.schema.json` ActionRecipe: "paid ... failure
included"). `yield`: one of `items` directly in `from` moves to the body unless the outcome is
`failure` (the rule of `action_completed`, `rule.ts:88-89`), with one `item_acquired {item_id,
holder_id: body}` at the next causal position (as Harvest, `harvest.ts:94-100`), so hs-5's spoiling
and hs-7's gifting reactions see a crafted item as they see a harvested one. Carry: `carryingExchange(world, body,
consumed, [yielded], steps)` (`containment/shared.ts:231`) as Harvest does (`harvest.ts:45`).
Admission (read-only, shared by command and GameView): fewer than `quantity` held refuses
`invalid_state` with `message {key: consume.reason}` when declared; an empty `from` refuses
`invalid_state` (stock exhausted: the closed-loop pattern of ruling 7, no text key needed, the card
greys). Both run in `refusalReason` beside `useAdmission` (`actions.ts:260`) and in `advertise`'s
code chain beside `admitted` (`action_lists.ts:217`), so `gameview_agrees_with_admission` holds.
The rule builds the transfers after `admission` (`rule.ts:74-76`) and before the sequence. No new
op, event, job or save row: `entity.transfer` and `item_acquired` exist. Why not hs-1's
`replenish.run` as a recipe step: its `to`/`from` are fixed holders, never the actor
(`job.ts:36-39`), so a recipe could craft only in one authored room and never into hands.

**E2 `SkillDefinition.prerequisite`** (hs-11). An optional `VersionedPolicy` evaluated for the
acquiring actor. `acquire` (`skills.ts:37-41`) throws `precondition_failed` while it fails, and the
dialogue admission that today checks membership (`dialogue/shared.ts:122-124`) returns
`invalid_state` for a choice whose `skill.acquire` names such a skill, so the Talk offer greys and
the command is refused alike. The loader walks its root where it walks `qualification`
(`cartridge_refs.ts:172`; `lib/loka/content/skills.ex:55`), so its leaves need their owners and
short refs expand. The tree is the set of `prerequisite` policies: a box is a skill, an edge is a
`skill_compare`. The engine owns: acquisition order, levels by use (row 5), the leaf. The cartridge
owns: professions (which boxes exist), edges, growth counts, what a box grants.

**E3 RecipeStep `{op: "build", blueprint, direction}`** (hs-12). On a detail-target recipe only;
the site is the target's room, which must declare `site` listing the blueprint and the direction
(the service checks, `cartridge_services.ts` / `lib/loka/content/services.ex:298-312`, re-run at
the step). Admission: `unbuildable(world, {blueprint, site: target.room, direction}, actor_id)`
(`build.ts:33-44`) in `refusalReason` and `advertise` as E1, surfacing the existing texts
`service.site_taken` and `service.construction_full` (the catalog must hold them, as for a build
service: `services.ex:251-253`). Step: `created(...)` exported from `build.ts:49` with
`owner = actor_id`, in `step` (`rule.ts:217-247`), unless the outcome is `failure`. Nothing else:
hydrate, map, weathering, `max_per_owner`, save row and reopen are S2-S4's unchanged
(`docs/system/save.md:338-345`: the identity row is the only trace).

**What a box grants, all content on existing leaves:**
- Schematics: recipes with `policy all [skill_compare {box, at_least}, fact_compare {learned_x,
  equals true}]`; the learned fact is set by a trainer choice, a readable `topic`, or a quest
  reaction, exactly as a spell's `learned` is (`mechanics.md:2496`).
- Actions: any recipe, careful harvest `skill` (`room.schema.json` harvest.careful), dialogue
  check, gated the same way.
- Attribute modifiers: a reaction on the box's acquisition -> `status.apply` of a W8 permanent
  status with 2c `modifies` (UNKNOWN 1).
- Titles: `world.identity.name_variants` with a `skill_compare` condition (FD9).
- XP kinds: each box's `uses_<key>` is its own pool, earned by that box's opposed checks; a branch
  may instead be one skill whose `growth` levels are its boxes. No pooled XP across boxes and no
  XP spending (ruling 4); a later `growth_of: <skill>` field could pool if content asks.

**Quality tiers (c):** tiers are distinct yield items from distinct schematics (`stew_plain` from
the cook's commission; `stew_hearty` at cooking 1; `feast` at cooking 2), each with its own
`edible.applies` (hs-5 engine). Row 21's quality fact is rejected for crafting: it writes on the
recipe target, which is the station, not the yield.

**Elite professions unlock (engine sketch, no lore; several elites, the warden order one of
them).** Each elite is its own novice box: a skill whose `prerequisite` (E2) is that elite's own
secret set, `all` of `skill_compare` at mastery levels, `fact_compare` on quest facts,
`visited_count`, `level_compare`, in any mix; E2 is per skill, so any number of elites costs
nothing more, and two elites share nothing unless their policies name the same leaf. Non-disclosure
by construction: no policy is ever projected (a `SkillView` carries `label`, `requirement`,
`acquired`, `qualified`, `usable`: `protocol/gameview.schema.json` SkillView), a refusal carries a
code only (`invalid_state`), and the trainer that teaches the box is reached only under the same
policy (an NPC `locks`, a storylet, or a choice availability repeating it). One optional field
joins with hs-14: `hidden: true` on a skill omits it from `skills` while its prerequisite fails, so
the tree page shows neither the box nor its requirement text; a hidden box that fails reveals
nothing about another, because each is read against its own policy for the viewing actor only.
Progress is per character and derived: every leaf reads the actor's own player-scope facts
(`skill_<key>`, `uses_<key>`: `docs/system/cartridge.md:389`; quest and story facts), nothing is
stored toward an elite, and reopen, replay and the Realm's player scope need no row. A "stirring"
line before the unlock is an FD2 aside with the same policy, read per actor. Later, if the lore
track asks for SWG's per-character secret set (each character mastering a different subset), a
leaf `mastered {of: [skills], count, pick: "character"}` chooses the subset by a hash of the
character id over `of` (trap 5: never the RNG) and is never printed; not built now.

## 5. PM rulings pre-decided (rejected alternative in parentheses)

1. **Craft is a recipe field, not a step.** `craft` sits beside `costs`; consume behaves as a cost,
   yield as `action_completed`. (A `replenish.run` recipe step: fixed holders, never the actor,
   `job.ts:36-39`. A `yield` step inside the sequence: yield-on-failure would need a per-outcome
   rule and a second admission.)
2. **Craft recipes are station recipes** (detail target with `rating`, opposed check). (A
   use-target craft "pot on fish": the loader refuses an opposed check without a detail rating,
   `cartridge_recipes.ts:202-207`, so no XP; and a use target reads one item, never "two fish".)
3. **Failure consumes the inputs and yields nothing.** (Refund on failure: consume would then be
   per-outcome; the `costs` precedent commits on failure, `rule.ts:12`.) Owner may overrule (Q2).
4. **XP is a use count, never spent; a box is bought with prerequisites and an optional lesson
   fee.** (SWG's XP spend: `uses_<key>` is reserved to skills@1 and bounded by the last growth
   entry, `cartridge_skills.ts:15-18`; a spendable pool is a new fact owner and a new write.)
5. **Prerequisites live on the skill, not on trainer choices.** (Availability policies only: the
   tree is invisible to the engine and the Book, and copied per trainer.)
6. **Tiers are distinct yield items.** (Row 21's quality fact: written on the station target, not
   the yield, `rule.ts:244-245`.)
7. **The beginner tier is the existing NPC service** (cook commission, S2 instant carpenter);
   nothing is removed from hs-5 or build_sampler. (Deleting NPC paths: the owner wants them as the
   paid beginner tier.)
8. **Self-build is a `build` step on a detail recipe, instant.** (A build job from a recipe: 20b's
   order job carries a service ref and `actor_id`, `shared.ts:158-173`; a recipe job kind is new
   state. A workbench NPC provider: a named-mechanic hack.)
9. **Woodcutting is a craft recipe with `yield`, not a Harvest.** (Harvest counts no use,
   `harvest.ts` has no `practised`; adding it restructures `decideHarvest`'s accept path for one
   consumer.) Tool by definition (`has_item axe`) in v1; tool by tag is a later `craft.tool`
   reusing `tagHeld` (`harvest.ts:58`).
10. **Closed loops through sealed rooms, no timed replenish in craft_sampler** (ruling 7 kept):
    consumed inputs return to the yield reserve.
11. **No profession, XP-kind or grant field in the engine.** A profession is the cartridge's set of
    skills and edges; grants are recipes, variants, reactions and titles on existing leaves.
    (A `professions` section: a registry with no mechanic of its own.)
12. **hs-10 and hs-11 join Batch A beside hs-1 and hs-5**; hs-12 and hs-13 open Batch B. (Holding
    all four to B: the content slices hs-2 to hs-4 do not need them, but B would then hold three
    engine threads at once.)

plot and none for the public one (row 24 entitlement, `property_sampler` seller). Sow = Put the seed
in the furrow (containment@1, offered today). Reaction `item_acquired {item: seed}` (subject =
holder, the furrow) -> `status.apply growing` on the furrow (G3 item status, duration one game day,
tick every hour; ticks change nothing on an item) and `fact.stamp sown_at {item: furrow}` (FD1, W2
entity fact). Stages = W6 `description_variants` on the furrow reading `time_since {fact: sown_at,

through its `custom_event` reaction. Ripen: `status_expired {status: growing}` with `when not
time_since {watered_at, item: furrow, at_least 43200}` -> `replenish.run crop` (`{items

BOOK. No new component: room prose variant, service offer. One browser interaction. Reason wording for `nothing_to_mend` is a designer follow-up (as G7's).
SCOPE TRIGGER: a room pool, a resource leaf with a room subject, or a reaction step.

---

### S5 — Raze and tombstone (engine, save), `toolbox/br-s5`, size M

GOAL. The owner pulls the hut down: contents and NPCs move to the plot, the exits go, the row stays. Beads loka-kgd.109.3 (second half). Save change -> second opinion.
CONTRACT. `State.built[id] = {razed_at: LogicalTime}` section; op `built.set {writer_group, entity_id, expected: null | row, value: row}` (`protocol/delta.schema.json`; `compose.ts` and `compose.ex` on the `levelling.set` pattern, `compose_levelling.ts`/`.ex`; `composition.json` cases: expected mismatch -> `precondition_failed`, unknown built id -> `precondition_failed`). Benefit `{kind: "raze"}`: refuses `permission_denied` unless `origin.owner === p.actor_id`, `invalid_state` `service.nothing_to_raze` with no live room; accepted: payment, one `entity.transfer` per item and NPC directly in the room to the site (EntityId order), `built.set`. `hydrate` also reruns when `state.built` changes and omits a razed room's exits and the site's exit to it; a razed row frees its site direction (S2's `site_taken` and load collision read `built`). Load: `razed_at` within the saved clock, id must be a built row, else `save_corrupt`. Ids never reuse (pure minting); the tombstone keeps old receipts resolving.
FILES. In: the above, `created.ts`, `service/shared.ts` + twins, `store.ts` validators, sampler, `built.test.ts`, coldReopen case, save.md. Out: Realm ownership transfer, building off built rooms.
ACCEPTANCE. Chest put in the hut, thief inside at 08:00; `raze` (price 2) -> chest and thief in the lane, north `not_found`, map no longer lists the hut; `raise_hut` again -> a new id, north back. Player standing inside is refused `invalid_state` `service.occupied` (the owner uses the service at the lane, so only an NPC can be inside; keep the check). Red controls: forged `razed_at` beyond the head clock -> `save_corrupt`; `built.set` with stale `expected` -> `precondition_failed` in both kernels.
REALM: 1 met (owner from the row vs `p.actor_id`); 7 met (raze is the owner's act); 9 as S2; others n/a.
BOOK. No new component: service offer; the room page and minimap simply lose the room. One browser interaction.
SCOPE TRIGGER: anything that re-reads statuses in `hydrate`.

---

## PM rulings pre-decided (rejected alternative in parentheses)

1. **Hydrate overlays `World.rooms`/`roomIds`**; the "world-graph contract" change is documented, not a new reader. (Design §5.1 `exits(world, roomId)`: ten call sites, each a regression surface.)
2. **Building is a service@1 benefit at a carpenter NPC**, policy-gated on row 24's plot entitlement. (Recipe step `build` plus `built.set` op: re-implements escrow, jobs, cancel and offers that 20a/20b already give; G7 `build` access type: a new lock type for one consumer, the action policy does the same.)
3. **No fixtures at completion** in this batch; Settle S1 furnishing places objects by the existing put. (Epic .2 text "fixtures as a registered source": a second created-entity kind with its own custody validation and red controls.)
4. **No numeric `condition`**; ruin is a permanent status after `weathering` expires. (Resource on the room: a room pool, a tick that today changes nothing on rooms, and a resource leaf with a room subject, three engine changes for a number nobody reads.)
5. **No `built_count` policy leaf**; caps are checked in `transition`. (A leaf with no consumer beyond the cap.)
6. **Ruin keeps its locks** (a ruined house is still yours). (Design "locks stop holding": needs hydrate to read statuses.)
7. **Spent materials stay in the custody room** as in 20b; no consumed-holder return path. (Design's `consumed -> holder` move: compose refuses transfers out of `consumed` in both kernels.)
8. **S5 raze is independent and last**: the PM may postpone it to Homestead with no loss to S1 to S4.
9. **`exits_resolve` statement unchanged**; the mechanics section states it ranges over hydrated rooms.

## Owner questions (recommendation first)

1. **Carpenter, not a free-hand build.** Building through a hired NPC at the plot (recommended: reuses every service mechanism and reads well in a MUD) vs. a player verb at the plot with no NPC (the design's wording; costs a recipe step, a new op and the escrow machinery again). Only the owner can call the fiction.
2. **Raze now or in Homestead?** Recommend now only if S1 to S4 land cleanly in one batch; otherwise Homestead (ruling 8).

Skipped: I did not verify that `status.transition` can be emitted from `transition` with a room holder (S4 developer confirms against `status/shared.ts`), nor the `orderReady` body (grep found only its dispatch at `schedule/rule.ts:93`). Risk: S4's `subject: "room"` leaf and S5's second `hydrate` trigger are the two places where "smallest" could grow; their scope triggers stop the developer there.

title: Toolbox row 17: ranged combat (batch M9b)
notes:
Written 2026-10-12 04:35 UTC in the Pi harness by anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 (brief drafter)

BRIEF loka-kgd.110: toolbox row 17, ranged combat (batch M9b). Size M, one developer run, no split (engine plus sampler; no new Book element).

GOAL
Owner answer 2 (docs/decisions/owner-decision-mechanics-toolbox-2026-10-08.md:37; docs/MECHANICS-TOOLBOX.md:54): ranged combat starts with a same-room first strike. Shooting into adjacent rooms comes later and is out of scope. Row text (docs/MECHANICS-TOOLBOX.md:150): "bow strikes first at a foe in the same room; ammo consumed; melee follows". Deps 6a and G2 are done (#366, #351).

LANE
Batch M9b item lane, as M9 ran it. Branch toolbox/m9b-ranged off toolbox/batch-m9b (head d461c38e), in your own worktree under worktrees.noindex; run bin/worktree_setup.sh first. Commit and do not push. Hand the branch and exact head to the PM, who runs a PR-less Opus item review and merges the item into the batch. Hosted CI runs on the batch PR head. Locally, run only the focused tests listed below, under nice -n 10.

SPEC GAP: FIRST TASK IS THE docs/system AMENDMENT (same branch, its own first commit)
docs/system has no ranged mechanic. combat@1 says Attack "does not attack immediately, advance time or draw RNG" (docs/system/mechanics.md:736-740) and "Odd rounds give the player the first opportunity" (mechanics.md:751-752). Cite the row text and the owner answer above.

Add a section "## Ranged first strike (toolbox row 17)" at the end of docs/system/mechanics.md, after "Movement on a status (toolbox row SR7)", in the bullet shape of 6a and 6b (mechanics.md:2110-2121, 2253-2267). Also add a one-sentence pointer at mechanics.md:751. Decided design:
- Shot. A shot happens in an encounter's round 1 (the encounter row's `round` is 1; foundation/compose_encounter.ts:44) when all of these hold at the player's turn:
  - the player wields an item whose `weapon` has `ranged {ammo}`;
  - the weapon's skill is usable (as G2, mechanics.md:1872-1873);
  - the player's body holds at least 1 in the ammo resource pool;
  - the existing turn guards pass: standing, and statusAllows 'attack' (SR4).
  The player's opportunity is then the shot. It uses the weapon's own `attack` profile, with G2 kind, crit and the item's tags as materials, plus row 2 bonuses. Attack admission and Attack itself are unchanged: still no RNG at Attack.
- Foe waits. The foe's round-1 opportunity is skipped exactly when the shot was taken, hit or miss. This covers the ordinary round's NPC and the pack round's selected member. The pack cursor, round order and successor job are unchanged. The 6b ally turn is unchanged.
- Ammo. Each shot writes one `resource.adjust -1` on the body's ammo pool in the round's writer group. It is an existing op, with no new delta, event, job or save row.
- Melee follows. After round 1, and in any round without a shot, a wielded ranged weapon never strikes. The player strikes with `world.combat.player_attack`, the unarmed profile.
- Any opener. The rule applies to round 1 of every encounter: Attack, a hostile NPC's engage, or a spell's fightBack (mechanics.md 29b, "Kill credit and the fight"). State this as deliberate.
- Budget. A shot spends the player's usual hit draw, plus a damage draw only for variable damage. It adds no draw to the eight-draw round budget (mechanics.md:757; 6b budget note).
- Kill and credit. A shot that kills goes through the existing round path (injure, deathSequence, deathCredit). Nothing new.
- Narration. Optional `world.combat.narration.shot_hit` and `.shot_miss` (TextKeys). Both are required when any item declares `weapon.ranged`; otherwise SCHEMA_VIOLATION, mirroring ally_hit/ally_miss (docs/system/cartridge.md:476-479). Text is content.
- Known limits:
  - Ammo is a counted resource pool, not items. Item consumption needs the foundation consumed-holder change in Beads loka-kgd.83. The 29a ruling that reagents are pools is the precedent.
  - A pool shows in the GameView as a resource meter whose 0 band reads danger (loka-kgd.83 comment), so keep ammo pools to samplers.
  - No adjacent-room shot (owner answer 2). No weapon switching mid-fight.
- Also write: Opt-in (next minor), Book (no new element: two text lines and the existing resource meter; propose sampler wording for the designer), Traps (none applies: the outcome RNG is not variety (trap 5) and the pool is a counted resource, not a status row (trap 11)), Sampler, and the Composition record below.

Add "## Ranged weapon declarations" after "## Damage declarations" (docs/system/cartridge.md:1530). It covers `weapon.ranged.ammo`, a resource ref given as a short key in source and named like allies; the narration pair; and the floor (compiler lib/loka/content/combat.ex, loader kernel/ts/src/content/cartridge_combat.ts).

COMPOSITION RECORD (docs/system/architecture.md:89)
- Consumer: the combat round's player and foe opportunities (round.ts ordinaryRound, round_flow.ts packTurns) and round narration.
- Reads: the wielded item's `weapon.ranged`, the ammo pool level, skill usability, statusAllows, and the encounter row's `round`.
- Writes: an ammo `resource.adjust` (existing op). Events, jobs, delta ops and save rows: none new. attack_result is reused, so reactions and the attacker filter see the shot as the player's blow.
- Reused: attack(), attackProfile/equipped, bonused, skills status, statusAllows, resource adjust, injure/deathSequence/deathCredit, the round order, allyOf, narrate, KERNEL_API_RANGE_INVALID, SCHEMA_VIOLATION.
- New: `WeaponProfile.ranged {ammo}`, the narration keys `shot_hit`/`shot_miss`, one shot predicate shared by both round kinds, the round-1 foe skip, and the next-minor floor. No foundation change.

FILES IN SCOPE (signatures from ast-grep outline; read only these ranges)
- kernel/ts/src/mechanics/combat/round_attack.ts:
  - 49 `export function attack(world, command, mint, encounter_id, row, attacker_id, r, close)`: spend the ammo when shooting.
  - 202 `function equipped(world, body, slot)`.
  - 212 `function attackProfile(world, row, attacker_id, player, r): Profile`: shot uses weapon.attack; otherwise a ranged weapon falls back to player_attack.
- kernel/ts/src/mechanics/combat/round.ts 100 `function ordinaryRound(...)`, order at :113.

  - 103 `function packTurns({...}: PackContext)`, order at :117.
  - 230 `export function narrate(world, row, events)`: shot_hit/shot_miss.

- kernel/ts/src/content/cartridge_combat.ts:
  - 8 `combat(c, named)`.
  - 38 `allies(c, named)` (mirror it for the narration pair and named ammo).
  - 55 `damageApi(c)` (floor).
- kernel/ts/src/content/cartridge_skills.ts:36 weapon check.
- lib/loka/content/combat.ex:83 `damage_api`.
- lib/loka/content/skills.ex:126 `defp weapon(m, defs, rel, item)` (Elixir compiler parity).
- protocol/entity.schema.json:1083 WeaponProfile (add optional `ranged {ammo: DefinitionRef}`, additionalProperties false).

- protocol/fixtures/invalid.json.

- New sampler cartridges/ranged_sampler/** (neutral ids).
- New tests: kernel/ts/test/ranged.test.ts and test/loka/content_ranged_test.exs.
- Docs: docs/system/mechanics.md and docs/system/cartridge.md as above. The docs/MECHANICS-TOOLBOX.md row 17 last column gets "done #N (batch M9b)" plus a rules link; the PM fills N. Regenerate docs/toolbox.gen.json and docs/system-graph.gen.json if their generators change them.
Model commit for shape: 7a6eaf32 (`git show --stat`, then only the hunks you mirror).

OUT OF SCOPE
- Attack admission and rule (combat/rule.ts) and the GameView/offered actions. No action changes, so the keyed-admission check does not apply.
- Foundation/compose in either kernel. Encounter row and delta schemas.
- Item ammo or the consumed holder (loka-kgd.83). Adjacent rooms.

- Row 21 durability: same files; do not pre-build wear.

KERNEL_API

GOAL

Sampler acceptance (docs/MECHANICS-TOOLBOX.md:151): "sword breaks after N hits; forge check sets a quality band; the smith repairs it for two pennies and it strikes again".

SPEC GAP: TASK 1 IS THE docs/system AMENDMENT, IN THIS PR, BEFORE CODE

Add the section "## Durability, crafting quality and repair (toolbox row 21)" to docs/system/mechanics.md, after "Movement on a status (toolbox row SR7)". Cite the toolbox row text (docs/MECHANICS-TOOLBOX.md:151: "wear per use, a quality band from the forge check, and a repair service (mechanics/service/) that restores durability for a fee (review 3)"). Also cite docs/reviews/2026-10-10-mechanics-review-3.md:37 (repair merged into row 21) and the archived plan docs/archive/LATER-MECHANICS.md:114 (C3-M03: "two committed uses→0 ... Quality bands/salvage need their own actual selected consumer"). Add "## Durability declarations" to docs/system/cartridge.md after "Harvest tool declarations" (:1635). Use the shape of rows G4/19: Opt-in, Book, Traps, Sampler, Composition record. Settle the design below in the spec text. The PM pre-decided it. Ask only if the code cannot honour it.

PRE-DECIDED DESIGN
1. Durability is a W2 entity fact, not a new pool. WeaponProfile (protocol/entity.schema.json:1083) gets optional `durability: {fact, wear}`. `fact` names this cartridge's bounded int fact with `per_subject: true` and scopes ["instance"]. Safe integer minimum and maximum are required (fact.ts:163 `bounded` needs both). The fact's default is the new weapon's value. `wear` is an int from 1 to 2^31-1. The cartridge owns every number: maximum, default, wear, repair amount and price (owner world-parameters decision, docs/decisions/owner-decision-world-parameters-2026-10-02.md). No engine literal.
2. Wear. In combat@1, when the player's attack hits (`attack_result.hit` true, including a fully resisted `loss: 0`), the wielded weapon's own durable attack struck, and that weapon declares `durability`, the round writes `fact.assign` on that item (subject = the weapon EntityId). The new value is the current value minus `wear`, clamped to the fact minimum (`bounded`). A miss or an unarmed strike does not wear. Hit is the unit ("breaks after N hits").
3. Broken = the fact reads at or below its minimum. Add this clause to the existing usable-weapon test in `attackProfile` (round_attack.ts:212; spec mechanics.md:937-942, "otherwise use the existing unarmed profile"): a broken weapon falls back to `world.combat.player_attack` with no tags (G2 materials, mechanics.md:1873), and it takes no further wear. The Attack offer itself is unchanged. The item stays wielded.
4. Repair. Add a fourth ServiceBenefit, `{kind: "repair", fact, amount}` (protocol/service.schema.json). Its target is the item directly in the actor body's `wield` holder whose `weapon.durability.fact` is `benefit.fact` (the same lookup as round_attack.ts:202 `equipped`; move that helper to a shared place, do not copy it). The new value is the current value plus `amount`, capped at the fact maximum. Refusals, after the existing quote/provider/payment checks and in recovery()'s order:
   - no such wielded item: `invalid_state` with key `service.nothing_to_repair`;
   - value already at the maximum: `invalid_state` with key `service.full_durability`.
   Both refuse before any charge. The cartridge supplies both texts; extend cartridge_services.ts:31 `reasons`. use_service's payload is unchanged: it has no item field, so a weapon carried but not wielded cannot be repaired (state this as a known limit). The GameView offer reuses `availability` (view/services.ts:24) unchanged, so offer and execution share one admission query.
5. Writer ownership. Extend fact.ts:101 `ownership` with the owner 'durability'. A fact named by any item's `weapon.durability.fact` may be assigned only with that owner. A recipe, dialogue or reaction write throws precondition_failed, the same guard as entitlement facts (mechanics.md:1424 "Only service writes its opted entitlement fact"). Combat wear and service repair pass the owner. This prevents the two-writer conflicting_write class seen in batch M2.
6. Quality band: content only, no engine code. The forge is a G4 use recipe (mechanics.md:2273-2285) on the existing blade item, with a check. The outcomes' `fact.assign` sets an enum entity fact `quality` on the target: success gives `fine`, failure gives `crude`. Its consumer is a W6 short variant through `fact_compare {subject: "target"}` (mechanics.md:2056-2069). The recipe policy `fact_compare quality = unforged` stops a re-forge. Known limit, to state in the spec: there are two bands (pass/fail), and quality does not change durability or damage. Add those when content selects that consumer (for example S5's Armorer's test).
7. Floor: these fields need kernel_api at least the next free minor at merge (base installs 1.66 in kernel/ts/src/runtime/world.ts:107; sibling M9b rows may claim minors first, so take the next one at merge). A lower floor gives KERNEL_API_RANGE_INVALID at the weapon's `durability` and the service's `benefit`, in both kernels' loaders.

notes:

GOAL
A worn item whose identity the player does not yet know still applies its affects. The GameView hides that it does so. Identifying it reveals its true name and its "(+N worn)" note. Row text (docs/MECHANICS-TOOLBOX.md:152): "Unidentified items (C2-M06); the unidentified name is a W6 variant ... "a dull ring" shows +2 after a sage identifies it; affect applies before". C2-M06 (docs/archive/LATER-MECHANICS.md:86): "Identifying one item definition changes the player's knowledge and projection; its actual mechanics already apply while unknown ... Unknown display hides real name/affect; identification reveals both; save/reopen retains knowledge ... pre-identification output must fail."

SPEC GAP (task 1, same PR, before any code)
docs/system has no unidentified-items section. Write these amendments, citing row 27 (MECHANICS-TOOLBOX.md:152) and C2-M06:
- docs/system/mechanics.md: add a new section "## Unidentified items (toolbox row 27)" after row 28 (ends ~2398). Give it bullets in the house shape: Identity, Name, Affects, Opt-in, Book, Sampler, Composition record, Known limits. Also update the row 28 "Hidden until worn" known limit (mechanics.md:2394) to say: an identify fact in the cursed name's any(...) reveals a curse before wear. That is content, and no engine code is needed.
- docs/system/cartridge.md "Item affect declarations" (:1514): add the field, its checks and its floor.
- docs/system/book-ui.md "Worn affects details" (:997): `worn` sums identified items only. Mark it "proposed, designer to approve". The presenter needs no change.

PRE-DECIDED DESIGN (PM may overrule; do not reopen)
1. Field. `ItemDefinition.identified` (protocol/entity.schema.json ItemDefinition, :152) is a DefinitionRef to a boolean fact that is NOT per_subject. The item counts as identified while that fact reads true for the player (`value`, kernel/ts/src/mechanics/fact.ts:52). The item is unidentified while the fact is false or has no row (its default). An item without the field is always identified.
   Why a plain fact, not a pair or entity fact: C2-M06 says knowledge is per item definition. A plain fact is also what a topic, a dialogue or a reaction already writes. It needs no subject plumbing.
2. Mechanics untouched. attributes@1 `value` (kernel/ts/src/mechanics/attributes/shared.ts:29) still adds every worn affect. Every reader therefore sees the affect before identification: stat_compare, derived stats, hp_max. Only the GameView note changes: `attributeViews` (kernel/ts/src/view/skills.ts:69) sums the affects of identified worn items alone. So the Character page reads "PER 12" before identification and "PER 12 (+2 worn)" after. Implement this as one optional filter on `worn` (attributes/shared.ts:51; it iterates `wornItems` :39), or as a sibling view-only sum. Do not change `value()`.
3. Names. These are content on W6 (mechanics.md:2060): short_variants and description_variants with `fact_compare {fact, equals: true}`. The BASE text is the unidentified name ("a dull ring"). The VARIANT is the true name.
   Reason: per W6 "Where shown" (mechanics.md:2061), shop lines, the text player's take/drop/give narration, disambiguation and other readers show only the base text. - Membership. `world.group {member}`: `member` names a bool pair fact (W2: `per_subject: true`, `scopes: ["player"]`). An NPC is in the character's group while that fact is true for (NPC, character); the character is the leader. Join and leave are content: a dialogue's `fact.assign` at the speaker, or a reaction's. Nothing stored is new.
- Co-move. When Move, Flee or a transport moves the body, every living NPC directly in the source room whose member fact is true moves to the same destination in the same writer group, in EntityId order. One place: `travel` (kernel/ts/src/mechanics/escort/shared.ts:122; called at movement/sequence.ts:52, transport/shared.ts:89). Find candidates with `npcsIn(world, [source])` (kernel/ts/src/mechanics/speech/shared.ts:20) and `value(world, actor, fact, npc)` (kernel/ts/src/mechanics/fact.ts:52). A member elsewhere stays put (no fault, no write; it follows again once co-located). The escorted NPC is skipped by the group walk, so it moves once.
- Shared credit and fighting. A member counts as an ally of its leader's character: `ally` (kernel/ts/src/mechanics/combat/shared.ts:67) gains the character argument and is true for a listed ally or a member. Attack on a member is refused `invalid_target` and not offered. `allyOf` (:74): the first listed ally living in the encounter room, else the first member there (EntityId order) with an `attack`. One ally turn per round, so the eight-draw budget is unchanged. Party credit follows (credit.ts:123).
- Death writes nothing: membership survives; the body returns alone.
- Known limits: members ride free and pass every exit the leader passes, with no `entity_entered_room` (escort precedent); a schedule or wander still moves a member; NPC-led groups and parties wait for the Realm; members take no combat damage (6b).
- Opt-in 1.71: `world.group` below it is KERNEL_API_RANGE_INVALID at requires.kernel_api.at_least.
