- Wage job: a cartridge with world.group.wage gets one fresh-world job {kind 'wage', key
  'group'}, first due at fresh clock + every, minted after the replenish jobs (so cartridges
  without wage keep their ids). Fixed grid like runReplenish: a run at `at` schedules the next
  at at + every; a next time the same advance also crosses returns as `next` (its own drain
  step). Each due settles exactly once; the elapsed host already stops at every pending
  non-calendar job (mobile/authority/local-story/elapsed.ts:61-70). Wages run whether or not
  anyone is a member (no member = no ops but the reschedule).
- A run pays, in EntityId order, every living NPC whose member fact is true at world.character,
  amount each, from world.body to the NPC, against a running balance: the payable members are
  the longest EntityId-order prefix the player's balance covers (value - k*amount >= minimum)
  and each NPC's row takes (value + amount <= maximum). Ops: one `adjust` per side threaded

waypoints for a fee; the trip ... is instant with no clock change, never a clock skip"). The
06:31 ruling assumed transport routes have no availability gate. They do: every transport names
an ActionDefinition, and every ActionDefinition carries a required `policy`. Transport admission
goes through it: kernel/ts/src/mechanics/transport/shared.ts:33-40 `availability()` ->

a.policy.root, ...)`, else invalid_state), and the GameView offer shows the same refusal
(kernel/ts/src/view/transports.ts:6-45, available false, reason code). So a transport action
whose policy is `visited_count {room: <destination>, at_least: 1}` (policy.ts:83-84, variety@1)
is fast travel between visited waypoints. No engine change. Deliver a sampler, a test and the spec.

LANE
Branch toolbox/m10-fast-travel off toolbox/batch-m10 at the head the PM gives (b6156e83 = 04f46aaf
plus W9 sleep 1.76). Own worktree under worktrees.noindex; bin/worktree_setup.sh first. Push;

notes:
[Pi · anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 · session 01a12efa]
Written 2026-10-12 12:05 UTC in the Pi harness by anthropic/claude-opus-5-5

BRIEF loka-kgd.121: Toolbox row 41, decay (batch M10, wave 4). Size M, one run, no split.
kernel_api 1.78 (PM assignment, plan 06:31 "1.78 only if engine": it is engine, below). Row 41
moved M13 -> M10 (PM 2026-10-11 19:09: content only on G3 + W1, both done, so decay lands with
19b restock); the toolbox table edit is the PM's, in the batch PR.

GOAL
Toolbox row 41 (docs/MECHANICS-TOOLBOX.md:180: "a status with expiry on a thing (G3) whose expiry
reaction (W1) moves it to the terminal consumed holder"; sampler "fish spoils after a day while
smoked fish lasts; a corpse and a dropped rag are cleaned up"). The plan asked the brief to
confirm a reaction step can move a thing to 19b's reserve; none can. The reaction apply steps
(protocol/reaction.schema.json apply oneOf) are fact.assign/adjust, quest.*, population.suppress,
status.apply/cure, barrier.set, experience.grant: nothing moves an item. And D4's consumed holder
takes only edible items from a body (kernel/ts/src/foundation/compose.ts:243-262 and the
containment invariant). So row 41 adds one reaction step, `item.move`, which moves the event's
subject item to an authored room; a sealed room is then both the decay sink and a 19b replenish
reserve, closing 19b's known limit ("a finite reserve is the lifetime supply until decay (row
41) feeds it back", mechanics.md Replenish). Every number (durations, room, grid) from the cartridge.

LANE
Branch toolbox/m10-decay off toolbox/batch-m10 at the head the PM gives (b6156e83 = 04f46aaf plus
W9 sleep 1.76). Own worktree under worktrees.noindex; bin/worktree_setup.sh first. Push; hosted
CI on the head (developer.md step 1). Before handoff: full `npm run typecheck` in kernel/ts;
prettier as .github/workflows/ci.yml runs it; `elixir bin/contracts.exs --check`; `node
bin/check_ts_size.mjs` from the repo root AFTER committing (tracked files only); `elixir
bin/check_size.exs`; mix format --check-formatted, mix compile --warnings-as-errors, mix credo
--strict. Never end a turn waiting on a bg_run. No new import cycle (below).

SPEC FIRST (same branch, first commit)
docs/system/mechanics.md: append "## Decay (toolbox row 41)" after "## Sleep (toolbox row W9)"
(the file end, :2595-2608 on b6156e83); add `item.move` to the reaction@1 step list (section
:581; the subject table text near :616); rewrite the Replenish known limit (:2510-2526) to point
at row 41. docs/system/cartridge.md: an "item.move" declaration paragraph after the W22
barrier.set reaction-step paragraph (:1695). Decided design:
- New apply step `{op: "item.move", room: DefinitionRef}` (both required, additionalProperties
  false), after experience.grant in protocol/reaction.schema.json (:625-634).
- Behaviour: the step reads the rule's subject (reaction.ts SUBJECT map :179-190; status_expired,
  status_applied and status_ticked give the status holder; item_acquired the acquirer; entity_died
  the victim; item_dropped none, so the actor's body). If the subject is an item entity whose
  container is not already that room, the step emits one entity.transfer of it from its current
  container (room, body, NPC or container item) to the room, in the delivery's writer group. Any
  other subject (body, NPC, room) or an item already there: nothing. No event, no narration, no
  capacity or reach check (the room is an authored sink). If an eaten (consumed) item can still be
  a status holder at expiry (probe it; see FILES), the step also does nothing for an item in
  world.consumed; if the eat removes the status row, no guard and say so.

title: Toolbox row G7: access locks (enter, traverse, get, put) — batch M11
description: docs/MECHANICS-TOOLBOX.md row G7. Brief in notes.
notes:
[Claude Code · anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 · session 01FtwqZjvGA5A9sL3d8WjiJz]
Written 2026-10-13 UTC in Claude Code by anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 (drafted, adopted by the PM)

BRIEF loka-kgd.123: Toolbox row G7, access locks (batch M11, wave 1). Size M, one run, no
split. kernel_api 1.78 (engine: new schema fields and three admission hooks). Line numbers below are
on toolbox/batch-m10 b6156e83; M10 wave 4 (rows 32, 41) lands before toolbox/batch-m11 is cut, so
docs line numbers shift. Re-find a range by its heading or function name, never by number alone.

GOAL
Toolbox row G7 (docs/MECHANICS-TOOLBOX.md:161; sampler "a guest may enter an owned hut but not take
from its chest; revoke the grant and entry refuses; a stranger is refused"). Today an action's
policy gates a whole verb (commands/actions.ts refusal :220-259), and a barrier's `opens_when` gates
one door's open (barrier/rule.ts:93). Nothing gates one exit, room or container per actor. G7 adds
an optional `locks` map: an access type to a VersionedPolicy, on an exit, a room or an item. The
existing evaluator reads it (mechanics/policy.ts `holds`) at the shared admission of the matching
verb. Grants and roles are W2 pair facts (mechanics.md:2170 "A G7 grant is a pair fact on the thing
and the grantee"), written by the writers that already exist. The design adds no policy leaf and no
grant command (see Decided design and PM questions 1-2). Every world value (who is granted, which
role opens what) comes from the cartridge.

LANE
Branch toolbox/m11-locks off toolbox/batch-m11 at the head the PM gives. Own worktree under
worktrees.noindex; bin/worktree_setup.sh first. Push; hosted CI on the head (developer.md step 1).
Before handoff: full `npm run typecheck` in kernel/ts; prettier as .github/workflows/ci.yml runs it;
`elixir bin/contracts.exs --check`; `node bin/check_ts_size.mjs` from the repo root AFTER committing
(it reads tracked files only); `elixir bin/check_size.exs`; mix format --check-formatted, mix compile
--warnings-as-errors, mix credo --strict. Never end a turn waiting on a bg_run. No new import cycle
(locks.ts imports policy.ts; check that nothing policy.ts reaches imports locks.ts back).

SPEC FIRST (same branch, first commit)
docs/system/mechanics.md: append "## Access locks (toolbox row G7)" at the file end (after Decay,
row 41). In "## barrier@1" (:63-83) add one sentence: an `opens_when` is the barrier's open lock, and
G7 adds no second spelling of it. In "## containment@1" (:85-151) add one sentence each: take
honours `get` locks, put honours `put` locks. docs/system/cartridge.md: append "## Access lock
declarations" at the file end. Cite architecture.md:89-128 ("Building mechanics by composition")
in the composition record. Decided design:
- Fields (schema, both kernels): `Connection.locks {traverse}` (protocol/room.schema.json Connection
  :17), `RoomDefinition.locks {enter}` (:391), `ItemDefinition.locks {get?, put?}`
  (protocol/entity.schema.json :152). Each is an object of VersionedPolicy, minProperties 1,
  additionalProperties false, so an unknown or misplaced access type is a SCHEMA_VIOLATION. A `put`
  lock needs `container: true` on the item; the loader refuses it otherwise (SCHEMA_VIOLATION
  invalid_value at `.locks.put`, both kernels).
- Evaluation: `holds(world, actor, lock.root, {target, steps})`. The target is the item that holds
  the lock, for `get` and `put`. A room or exit lock has no target, so `fact_compare
  {subject: "target"}` is never true there. The loader refuses it there (FACT_SCOPE_UNSUPPORTED, TS
  loader only, as for the other targetless sites). A failing lock refuses `permission_denied` (in
  error.schema.json and error_registry.json:18, "The actor may not do this"; no protocol change).
- Where each lock is checked (the shared admission the GameView already uses, so the view and
  execution cannot disagree):
  traverse and enter: movementPlan (mechanics/movement/sequence.ts:111-138), right after `passage`
  (:124-125), so hidden (not_found), closed or locked door (exit_closed or exit_locked) come first.
  The exit's `traverse` lock, then the destination room's `enter` lock. Step, flee and the
  GameView's exits (view/view.ts:255-259) all call movementPlan.
  get: take, after reach and before carrying, in BOTH the rule (containment/rule.ts:52-60) and the
  view's takeAdmission (view/action_lists.ts:117-130), through one shared helper. Walk from the item
  up State.containers to the room or the body: the item's own `get` lock, then each container item
  on the way. Charge one query step per edge (reach's budget rule, lookups.ts:67-89).
  put: putRefused (containment/shared.ts:177-223), after the lid check and before capacity: the
  destination's `put` lock.
- Grants are content: a pair fact (`per_subject: true`, `scopes: ["player"]`, any type) on an NPC
  or item and the character. Today's writers already write one: a dialogue's fact.assign at the
  speaker, a reaction's fact.assign at its named npc or item, a recipe's fact.assign at its target.
  A role is an enum pair fact. "owner", "guest" and "holder" are authored `fact_compare` and `any`

SPEC FIRST (same branch, first commit)

cartridge.md: a declarations note after the claim/cancel declarations. Decided design:
- Property (content only): service `buy_hut` {benefit entitlement, fact owns_hut} with its price;
  hut room `locks.enter` and chest `locks.get`/`locks.put` = fact_compare {fact owns_hut, equals
  true} (player fact). The key: a barrier `hut_door` with key_item `hut_key`; the key is handed over
  by an existing writer after purchase (a reaction on the service's existing event giving the key
  is NOT available: check whether an existing reaction step or the entitlement can deliver an item;
  if none, the key lies in the hut and the owner takes it on first entry; state which). "Lock it" is
  the existing barrier lock verb with the key. "Stranger refused": before purchase the player is
  refused by the enter lock; a walking NPC (W26 `walks`) is refused by any G7 lock regardless.
- Bank (engine): new benefit kind `{kind: "deposit", account: <fact>, amount: int 1..1000000}` and
  `{kind: "withdraw", account: <fact>, amount}`. The account is a bounded int player fact
  (minimum 0), service-owned (as entitlement facts are: only these benefits write it; reuse the
  ownership rule). The service price (minimum 1) stays a fee; the deposited money is `amount`, separate
  from the fee. Ops: payment
  as today (fee to the recipient), resource transfer of `amount` from the player's pool to the
  bank's vault pool, fact.adjust account +amount. Withdraw: refuse invalid_state `service.no_funds`
  when account < amount; ops: fee, transfer `amount` vault -> player, fact.adjust -amount. The vault
  is an NPC with a currency pool (resource_starts; NPCs are the only entities with pools,
  runtime/fresh.ts), named by the service as `vault: <npc>`; both branches name the same vault NPC,
  so a deposit at branch A is withdrawable at branch B. Conservation: player + vault totals constant
  apart from fees; an invariant check exists for resource transfers (reuse; no new invariant unless
  the reviewer of the pattern requires one).
  Offer/use parity through `transition` as 20a did.
- Loader (both kernels): deposit/withdraw need 1.83; account is a bounded int player fact with
  minimum 0 and is named by no other kind of benefit or writer; vault is an NPC with a pool of the
  service's currency.
- Book: no new element (two more service offers; the account balance shows if the fact is shown
  today; else no line, known limit).
- Known limits: one currency; no interest; item deposit is the locked chest (content), not a bank
  benefit; the vault NPC must not be killable in content that uses it (authoring rule).

bounded player fact -> refused; vault not an NPC with the currency -> refused; account named by

GOAL
Row 37a (docs/MECHANICS-TOOLBOX.md row 37a; sampler "full-moon raid spawns one bundle per cycle;
reopening does not respawn it"). The trigger is content on what exists: a reaction on the existing
`clock_hour` event (protocol/reaction.schema.json, kernel_api >= 1.46) whose `when` reads the `sky
{lunar}` leaf (row 10/31) and a once-per-cycle fact. The one engine piece: no reaction step can
spawn an NPC (apply ops: fact.*, quest.*, population.suppress, status.*, barrier.set,
experience.grant, item.move). Row 39 reuses the step.

LANE
Branch toolbox/m12-raid off toolbox/batch-m12 at the head the PM gives. Own worktree under
worktrees.noindex; bin/worktree_setup.sh first. Push; hosted CI on the head. Before handoff: full
typecheck; prettier; contracts --check; check_ts_size (repo root, after commit) and check_size; mix
format/compile --warnings-as-errors/credo --strict; schema mutant sweep (docs/lessons/contracts.md).

SPEC FIRST (same branch, first commit)
docs/system/mechanics.md: "## Phased world events (toolbox row 37a)" at the file end; add
`population.spawn` to the reaction@1 step list. cartridge.md: a declarations paragraph after the
item.move one. Decided design:
- New apply step `{op: "population.spawn", plan: DefinitionRef}` (additionalProperties false),
  after item.move in protocol/reaction.schema.json; regenerate contracts.gen.ts.
- Behaviour: births ONE bundle of the named population plan into the plan's `home`, now, through the
  existing `birth()` (population/birth.ts: plan, slot, generation, occurrence_id, at, mint,
  writer_group) at the lowest free slot under the plan's `cap`; no free slot: nothing (no fault, no
  event beyond what birth emits). No RNG draw (a plan's `chance` is for its own job only; the step
  ignores it). The spawned members then behave as that plan's members (wander, combat, death) and
  count toward its cap; the plan's own job is unchanged.
- Any trigger may use it (not only fact_changed, unlike population.suppress).
- Once per cycle is content: the sampler raid rule is `clock_hour` with `when` all[sky {lunar:
  full}, fact_compare raided equals false] and apply [population.spawn {plan raiders}, fact.assign
  raided true]; a second rule `clock_hour` with `when` sky {lunar: new} applies fact.assign raided
  false. Reopen does not respawn: the reaction's writes are committed with the hour's advance.
- Loader (both kernels): the step needs 1.84 (KERNEL_API_RANGE_INVALID); `plan` resolves to a
  population plan (UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE at the step's `plan`); the population capability is declared.
- Book: no new element (spawned NPCs show as today).
- Known limits: spawn location is the plan's home (no per-step room); one bundle per step.

title: Toolbox row FD3: storylet deck (quality-based opportunities) — batch M12
description: Gap 3. storylets [{when, weight, scene|dialogue}] picked by W7 hash on entity_entered_room/clock_hour. After 37b. Fable #7. Source: docs/rnd/depth-and-ux-2026-10-13.md (Fable audit, owner approved 2026-10-13).
notes:
Priority plan 2026-10-14 (owner-adopted): FD3 moves from M12 to the head of M13.
BRIEF (Fable draft, PM-approved 2026-10-14; rulings A-F: derived hash pick no state; recipe target.kind storylet; widen legacyStarts bounded; GameView.storylet; actor in hash (per-player draw); after FD2):
BRIEF loka-kgd.140 FD3 storylet deck: quality-based opportunities drawn by hash, offered as one Book Action card. Batch M13, head row (parallel with FD2). Size M (one developer run; engine + Book halves together; a design note first). kernel_api 1.92 (PM assigns; FD2 takes 1.91 and merges first).
HANDOFF THRESHOLD: near 180k tokens stop, push, hand back head + done/left list (no CI wait).

GOAL. The world offers things by player state: a cartridge declares storylets, each a holding condition, a weight, where it may appear and what accepting it does; in a room, at an hour, the engine draws one holding storylet by hash (W7 pattern, no RNG) and the Book shows it as one Action card ("A stranger beckons..."); accepting runs it. The same room and hour draw the same card; a new hour or room redraws. Smallest version: no new story format. A storylet is an existing `ActionRecipe` with a new `target.kind: "storylet"`; its consequences are what a recipe already composes (narration, `fact.assign`, `status.apply`, `resource.adjust`, `event.emit`; `action_completed` reactions; a modal `scene@1` whose `on.action` names it). "Dialogue" storylets are content on that: a reaction `population.spawn` or a W10 conditional schedule brings the speaker, then Talk is offered as today; no direct dialogue reference (Known limit). Source: `docs/rnd/depth-and-ux-2026-10-13.md` section 3 row 3; priority plan `docs/briefs/toolbox-priority-plan-2026-10-14.md` section 3 row 2 (M12 -> M13 head; "new module + W7 hash + Book card; no `policy.ts`"). The owner asked whether storylets are worth it; the PM kept them as a cheap selector over existing scenes and dialogue: build only the selector and the card.

LANE. Draft PR, batched pushes. Branch `toolbox/m13-fd3` off the M13 batch branch the PM names (`toolbox/batch-m13`); own worktree `../worktrees.noindex/m13-fd3`, `bin/worktree_setup.sh`. Draft PR against the batch branch; one push per wave. FD2 runs in parallel and merges first; before marking ready, merge the batch branch (never rebase): expect conflicts in `mobile/app/book/pages.tsx` RoomPage, `kernel/ts/src/view/view.ts` gameView, `protocol/gameview.schema.json`, `kernel/ts/src/runtime/world.ts:107`, `docs/system/mechanics.md`, `cartridge.md`, `book-ui.md`, `docs/BOOK-UI-COMPONENTS.md`, `docs/MECHANICS-TOOLBOX.md` (both append; keep both; regenerate `contracts.gen.ts`).

STEP 1, DESIGN NOTE (timebox ~25k tokens, no code, at most 40 lines to the scratchpad file `fd3-design.md`; wait for PM approval, then build in the same run). Confirm or refute each ruling with a `file:line` reason; the PM decides.
A. Pick is derived, not stored (recommended). The offered storylet is a read over committed state: hash of `<actor>:<room key>:<hour index>` (SHA-256 of the UTF-8 string, first four bytes big-endian, as `kernel/ts/src/mechanics/variety.ts:14-15`), `hour index = floor(clock / units(cartridge).hour)` (`kernel/ts/src/mechanics/calendar.ts:9-13`), modulo the sum of the holding storylets' weights, walked in key order. It changes exactly at `entity_entered_room` (the actor's own body) and `clock_hour`, so no trigger, step, job, event or save row exists (architecture: "prefer a derived query where no history is needed"; traps 1 and 5). Alternative (rejected unless the note shows a need): a reaction on the two triggers writes the pick into a fact (a new step, a fact row, replay surface).
B. A storylet is a recipe whose target is `{kind: "storylet", rooms?: [room refs], weight?: int >= 1 (default 1)}` (recommended): acceptance is the ordinary `perform {action}` with no `target_id`/`item_id`; policy, costs, cooldown, check, outcome, narration, `action_completed`, cooldowns and `time.advance` are unchanged (`docs/system/mechanics.md` "action_recipe@1"). Alternative (rejected: a protocol command, more code): a `storylets` section naming a scene or dialogue plus a new `storylet.accept` command.
C. Scene from a storylet (recommended, bounded): `legacyStarts` (`kernel/ts/src/mechanics/scene/shared.ts:46-78`) requires `s.on.detail` and `s.on.room` for an `on.action` start (lines 59-64) although the schema has both optional (`protocol/scene.schema.json:30-50`); add: an `on.action` without `detail`/`room` starts when the completed action's key matches, for `e.actor_id`, and the loader/compiler allow omitting them only when the named recipe's target kind is `storylet` (otherwise the existing requirement). Without C the sampler still works (facts, reactions, quest offer) but the row's "scene" value is absent; say which you build.
D. The Book knows the card by one optional GameView field `storylet?: Key` (the offered action key), recommended; the action itself stays in `GameView.actions` as a place action (`target {kind: "none"}`, `command: "perform"`), so admission and projection share one query. Alternative (rejected: touches every action): a flag on `AdvertisedAction`.
E. Holding set and listing: a storylet is listed only when it is the pick; unpicked and non-holding storylets are not listed at all (not as unavailable); the pick's own availability then follows `advertise` as any action (policy, cooldown, costs).
F. Hash input includes the actor (per-player draw, audit "SP+R (per-player draw)"); state why or propose the room-only form.

DOCS/SYSTEM CLAUSES:

## Goal

The Journal recounts the run: every committed narration the player saw, grouped by game day,
with the receipts that reached a story point marked. Nothing is stored or computed in the
kernel: the host reads the receipts the save already holds, the Book draws them.

## Lane, model, size, version

- Lane: Draft PR; slice branch `toolbox/m15-fd6` from `origin/main`; worktree
  `../worktrees.noindex/m15-fd6`. Developer: Opus. Size S-M (host read + Book page). No
  kernel_api, protocol or save change.
- Designer: one Fable designer message before the push (section word, day heading, the
  milestone look, collapsed days).
- Handoff threshold: per COMMON RULES.

## Contract (write these clauses first)

### docs/system/mechanics.md, new section "Chronicle (toolbox row FD6)" after "Away recap
(toolbox row W27)"

- **Nothing stored.** The Chronicle is a host projection of the story's accepted receipts
  (`receipt` table, scope `story/<lineage>/<character>`, revision order): each receipt's
  committed narration (`response.narration`, routed as the log routes it:
  `mobile/authority/local-story/narration.ts`) and whether its events hold a
  `story_point_reached`. No kernel field, command, op, receipt or save change; GameView
  unchanged.
- **Day.** A receipt's day is `floor(clock / units(cartridge).day) + 1`
  (`kernel/ts/src/mechanics/calendar.ts` `units`: the authored `units_per_hour × hours_per_day`,
  else the legacy 24 × 3600), where `clock` is the clock after that receipt: the fresh world's
  clock advanced by every `time.advance` op (`delta.ops`, `to`) of the accepted receipts up to
  and including it; commands without one keep the clock. So an elapsed settlement's lines are
  listed under the day it ends on (known limit: a long absence's lines land on its last day).
- **Lines.** A receipt contributes its non-combat lines (what the World page or a detail showed,
  `rendered(record, view, text, false)` in `mobile/app/book/logs.ts`), one entry per receipt as
  the log shows it; receipts with only combat lines, rejections and faults contribute nothing.
  A receipt whose events include `story_point_reached` is a **milestone**.
- **Opt-in.** None: every cartridge's Journal has it, Chapter 1 included; a save with no
  narration shows no Chronicle.
- **Composition record.** Consumer: the Journal page. Reads: receipts (response narration,
  events, `time.advance` ops), the fresh world's clock, the cartridge's day units. Writes,
  events, jobs, save rows: none. Reused: `narration`'s routing, `rendered`, `grouped`
  (`mobile/app/book/recap.ts`), the Away recap's Tap heading, `units`. New: `chronicle()` on
  the host `Game` and the Book's day grouping; no foundation change.

### docs/system/book-ui.md, "Chronicle details" after "Lore details" (and after G10's "Notes
and pins details" when it lands)

The Journal's last section, **Chronicle**, shown when at least one entry exists: one block per
day in ascending order, headed "Day N" as the Away recap's Tap heading (name adds ", show" or
", hide"); the latest day open, earlier days collapsed; open, each distinct line once in
first-seen order with " (N times)" after a repeated line (the recap's grouping), ordinary lines
in the log's dim system look, a milestone's line in ink (`type.log` `fg`) (proposed, designer to
approve). Lines are the receipts' authored narration; the Book adds no words but the heading
and the count. Opening the Journal reads the receipts once; the page is not live-updated while
open (a press returns to World anyway).

### docs/system/save.md "Narration on reopen": one sentence: the Chronicle reads the same
receipts, never memory.

The NPC's knowledge is declared: `NpcDefinition.ask {unknown: TextKey, answers: [{topic: DefinitionRef, text: TextKey, when?: VersionedPolicy, grants?: DefinitionRef}] (1 to 32)}` (protocol/entity.schema.json:485). An NPC without `ask` is `invalid_target`. The first answer, in authored order, whose `topic` matches and whose `when` holds (actor as actor, the NPC as target, so `subject: "target"` reads the NPC's pair fact, as G11 does) is the answer; none -> `unknown`. 3. Admission, in order (model: kernel/ts/src/mechanics/speech/rule.ts:9-28): no body or a pending conversation -> `invalid_state`; target not an NPC -> `not_found`; not alive in the actor's room -> `not_present`; no `ask` -> `invalid_target`; hostile (`disposition`, kernel/ts/src/mechanics/disposition.ts:23) -> `invalid_state` (as talk, mechanics.md:2329); `topic` not a declared topic or its fact not true for the actor (`value`, kernel/ts/src/mechanics/fact.ts:70) -> `invalid_state`.

title: Toolbox row 35: trial (C3-M08), batch M14
description: Row 35 of docs/MECHANICS-TOOLBOX.md; part of loka-kgd.164. Brief in notes when drafted.
notes:
BRIEF M14 35-engine (Fable draft, PM session 93636711):
BRIEF loka-kgd.165 row 35 TRIAL, engine half: the arrest (a disposition that stops instead of brawling and relocates the body). Batch M14, draft branch `toolbox/batch-m14`. Fable draft 2026-10-16 (session 93636711); PM rulings below are defaults the PM edits.
HANDOFF THRESHOLD: near 180k tokens stop, push, hand back head + done/left list (no CI wait).

GOAL. A wanted player who walks into the guard's room is stopped, not fought: the guard's `disposition` declares `arrest {to, narration}` instead of `engage`, and the move ends with the body in `to` (the cell), the arrest line in the receipt, no encounter. This is showcase findings 1 and 2 (`docs/showcase/economy-law-district.md` "Toolbox findings": "the guard's engage should relocate the body instead"; "a disposition that engages without a fight (a stop, not a brawl)") and the law exit of `wanted` (Beads loka-kgd.163 item 4). The trial itself (the charge read, the fine or the sentence) is content on this engine: a `narrate` reaction on entering the cell and a jailer dialogue (35-content.md). No scene@1 change: a modal scene starts only from a dialogue-bound story point, a quest outcome or a recipe (`protocol/scene.schema.json` `on`, L21-53), so a scene would need a fourth start kind for a narration-only ceremony (PM ruling 1).

PM RULINGS (defaults).
1. Trial = narrate reaction + dialogue, not scene@1 (above). The row's reuse column (`mechanics/scene/rule.ts`) is amended at the row flip in 35-content.
2. The arrest is a disposition reader (one more branch of `engage`), not a reaction step: it reuses `hostileAt`'s candidate rule (living, unengaged, hostile, sees the body per SR8, first in EntityId order, never in a sanctuary or during a scene) and so inherits concealment (row 16) for free. A reaction step `body.move` would lose the perception rule and need a new op (reaction.schema.json has `npc.move` only, L713-724).
3. No served sentence (owner 2026-10-10, toolbox row 36): the engine adds no job, timer or sentence state. Release is content (the fine, a door, a tunnel).
4. One relocation per move: after the arrest the body's arrival in `to` runs no entry check (as a transport arrival engages no one, G11 limits), so a guard in the cell cannot chain-arrest, and an arrest whose `to` is the room entered (`there === to`) does nothing.

LANE. Draft PR, batched pushes. Branch `toolbox/m14-35-engine` off `toolbox/batch-m14`; own worktree `../worktrees.noindex/m14-35-engine` (`bin/worktree_setup.sh`). Draft PR against the batch branch. Developer model: Opus. Size: M (one run). Parallel with 43a (shares `movement/sequence.ts`, different functions: 43a edits `movementPlan`, this row edits `routeProgress`; and `entity.schema.json`, different regions: 43a the `Tag` enum, this row `disposition`); regenerate `contracts.gen.ts` after merging the batch branch, never hand-merge it. FD10 and 43b start after this merges (they touch `NpcDefinition`, `npc_fields.ex`, `travel`).

kernel_api 1.105. Set `kernel/ts/src/runtime/world.ts:108` `kernel_api: '1.103'` to `'1.105'` (#411 takes 1.104; if 1.104 is not yet on the batch base, still set 1.105 and say so in the handback). Floor: any `disposition.arrest` needs at_least 1.105 (KERNEL_API_RANGE_INVALID at `.cartridge.manifest.requires.kernel_api.at_least` loader / `cartridge.requires.kernel_api.at_least` compiler), plus a `protocol/fixtures/loader_floors.json` case `{floor: "1.105", below: "1.104", source: "cartridges/trial_sampler", compiler: [...], loader: [...]}` (model: the theft_sampler case at L938-949).

DOCS/SYSTEM TO AMEND FIRST (same PR, before code; cite in the PR).
- `docs/system/mechanics.md` "Standing and disposition (toolbox rows 15 and G11)": the **Disposition (G11)** bullet gains `arrest?`; the **Readers** bullet's "Combat:" sentence gains "or, when the NPC declares `arrest` instead of `engage`, is arrested (row 35)". Add a new section at the end of the file (after "Settle S3-1: narrate (N1)") titled "Arrest and trial (toolbox row 35)" with the bullets below (Declaration, Reader, Effect, Known limits, Opt-in, Book, Sampler, Composition record, Realm seams); 35-content extends it with the trial sampler and the Book line.
- `docs/system/cartridge.md` "Standing and disposition declarations": one sentence: `disposition.arrest {to, narration}` (a room short key, a catalog key) is allowed only with `hostile` and never with `engage` (SCHEMA_VIOLATION `invalid_value` at `npcs/<key>.disposition`), unresolved `to` or `narration` is UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE at `npcs/<key>.disposition.arrest.to` / `.narration`, spawn templates refuse as for any disposition, floor 1.105.
- `protocol/entity.schema.json` `disposition` (L552-): add `arrest {to: identity.schema.json DefinitionRef (room), narration: TextKey}`, both required, `additionalProperties: false`; extend the description ("Toolbox row 35 (kernel_api at least 1.105): with `arrest` instead of `engage`, a hostile NPC stops a player who walks in and the body goes to `to`").
- `docs/MECHANICS-TOOLBOX.md` row 35: `in progress #N` (35-content flips it to done).

THE RULE (exact clauses).
- Shape (both kernels, `cartridge_standing.ts` `standing()` / `standing.ex` `shapes/1`): today `engage` present iff `hostile && attack`. New: if `arrest` present: `hostile` required and `engage` absent (`attack` may be present or not: an arresting guard may also be attackable); else the existing rule. Violations: SCHEMA_VIOLATION `invalid_value` at `.cartridge.npcs[<ref>].disposition` (loader) / `npcs/<key>.disposition` (compiler). `to` resolves to a room of this cartridge, `narration` to a catalog key (UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE at the member). The compiler expands `to` from a short key: add `arrest` to the fields `lib/loka/content/npc_fields.ex` expands (`variants/3`, L29-37, with `Map.update!(a, "to", &ref(&1, "room", m))`; the policy fields there go through `expand.(v, m)`, `arrest` is a plain map, so give it its own line) and its text to the NPC texts `lib/loka/content/entities.ex` checks (as `disposition.engage` is checked). Loader: the `to` ref through `named(ref, 'room', path)` (`cartridge_refs.ts` `checkers`), the text through `Object.hasOwn(c.text, …)` as `d.engage` at `cartridge_standing.ts:34`.

description: Row 43a of docs/MECHANICS-TOOLBOX.md; part of loka-kgd.164. Brief in notes when drafted.
notes:
BRIEF M14 43a (Fable draft, PM session 93636711):
BRIEF loka-kgd.167 row 43a TERRAIN MOVEMENT COSTS (C3-M10): per-room fare multipliers keyed by terrain tag. Batch M14, draft branch `toolbox/batch-m14`. Fable draft 2026-10-16. One brief (engine + sampler): sized S here, not M; the sampler is four rooms and no NPC, so a content half would have nothing to build (PM may still split; the sampler section below is the content half if so).
HANDOFF THRESHOLD: near 180k tokens stop, push, hand back head + done/left list (no CI wait).

GOAL. "Road costs one, fen refuses." A cartridge declares `world.movement.terrain {<tag>: <percent>}`; a move into a room multiplies the fare by each matching tag of the destination room, in the room's authored tag order, each step rounded down (SR7's status rule, `fare` in `movement/shared.ts`). "Refuses" is the existing `insufficient_resource`: a fen that costs more mv than the body has is refused and the GameView lists the exit unavailable with that reason. No new tag semantics beyond cost: the barred terrains stay SR7's `air`, `chasm`, `water`. Two new `Tag` members, `road` and `marsh` (generic; the Tag set is closed and rows add members, as SR7 did). `world.movement.cost` becomes optional, so a cartridge can scale the default 1 mv fare.

PM RULINGS (defaults). (1) A world-level table keyed by tag, not a per-room `cost_percent`: rooms carry tags already (G1), 43b's mount admission reads the same tags, and the numbers live in one place. (2) Terrain applies after the status percents (base x flee multiplier, then statuses in definition order, then the destination's tags in authored order), floor at each step. (3) NPC movement pays nothing today and stays so (SR7 known limit). (4) `water` entry cost (D6) is not scaled (SR7 rule kept).

HANDOFF THRESHOLD: near 180k tokens stop, push, hand back head + done/left list (no CI wait).

GOAL. "Horse on road moves both once; fen refuses and moves neither; dismount leaves the horse." The mount is an NPC with `mount {terrain, cost_percent?}`; riding is a bool pair fact the cartridge names in `world.mount {riding}` and writes by its own dialogue choices (mount, dismount), exactly as G8's `member`. The engine reads it in three places that already exist: `movementPlan` (admission: the destination must carry one of the mount's `terrain` tags, else `invalid_state`, shared by step, flee and the GameView), `fare` (the mount's `cost_percent` after 43a's terrain), and `travel` (the mount transfers with the body, as the escort and members do). No new verb, op, event, job or row.

PM RULINGS (defaults). (1) Mount/dismount are dialogue choices at the mount (hireling precedent: `hireling_sampler/dialogues/hal_talk.json`), not engine verbs. (2) "Mounted" = the first living NPC in the actor's body's room (EntityId order) whose definition has `mount` and whose `riding` fact is true for (NPC, character); a true fact on a horse elsewhere or dead means on foot and writes nothing (G8's "a member elsewhere stays put"). (3) The mount's `terrain` is a positive list: a mounted move is admitted only into a room carrying at least one listed tag (C3-M10 "road-only admission"); untagged rooms refuse, so stables and yards carry `road`. (4) `cost_percent` default 100; applied last (base x flee -> statuses -> 43a terrain -> mount), floor each step. (5) Death, transport and combat change nothing for the mount (the fact persists; the horse boards a ferry with the body since `travel` is shared; the horse is not an ally and can be attacked unless it is also a G8 member). (6) Exclusivity is not enforced: two Realm characters could both "ride" one horse (seam 7, stated, not built).

(never a level) and whether held items go to the corpse or stay on the body. The engine owns
the arithmetic; the cartridge the numbers and the line. Row: docs/MECHANICS-TOOLBOX.md row 47
("cartridge chooses XP loss on death; sampler loses 10%"). Ghost-walk death (loka-kgd.69) is not

### docs/system/mechanics.md, new section "Death penalties (toolbox row 47)" after
"Experience and levelling (toolbox row 4)"

- **Declaration.** `world.death.penalty` (`protocol/cartridge.schema.json` `DeathSettings`),
  optional: `experience {percent, narration}` (`percent` an integer 1 to 100; `narration` a
  TextKey) and `items` (`"corpse"` or `"kept"`; absent reads `corpse`). `penalty.experience`
  needs `world.levelling` (SCHEMA_VIOLATION at `world.death.penalty.experience`, both kernels);
  the narration key must exist in the catalog (UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE at
  `world.death.penalty.experience.narration`). `penalty` needs kernel_api 1.109
  (KERNEL_API_RANGE_INVALID at `requires.kernel_api.at_least`, both kernels).
- **Experience.** When a player body dies and `penalty.experience` is declared, the
  [death sequence](#death1--corpse-custody-and-same-body-return-m5-b-foundation)'s return writes
  the character's levelling row with experience reduced by `floor(experience × percent / 100)`,
  but never below the threshold the character has reached (the largest `thresholds` entry at or
  below the current experience; 0 below the first), so the level and the spent points never
  fall and unspent never goes negative. A loss of 0 writes nothing. The write is one
  `levelling.set` in the fatal writer group and composes with every other experience source of
  the proposal through `oneWrite` (a reaction on `entity_died` that grants experience adds to the
  reduced row). The cartridge's `narration` line is appended once at the end of the receipt's
  narration when the stored row's experience is above the proposal's last write (the same site
  and actor rule as `level_up`; a death inside a job narrates in that elapsed receipt).
- **Items.** `items: "kept"` leaves the player's held and worn roots on the body: no
  `entity.transfer` to the corpse; the corpse is still created, empty, in the death room (corpses
  persist when empty). `"corpse"` and absent: unchanged custody. NPC deaths never read `penalty`.
- **Composer.** `levelling.set` now composes when `expected` matches and no allocated count
  falls; experience may fall (both kernels). The story rules keep the level floor.
- **Opt-in.** Chapter 1 and every sampler but `penalty_sampler` declare no `penalty`: bytes,
  hashes, receipts and GameView unchanged.
- **Book.** No new element: the loss shows as the receipt's authored line in the World log and
  as the Character page's `xp` line (`levelling details`); kept items show by not being in the
  corpse. No designer text: the line is the cartridge's.
- **Known limits.** A character at exactly a threshold loses nothing (the floor binds); a
  cartridge wanting level loss needs a later row (allocated points would have to be returned).

## Goal

A player writes short notes into the Journal and labels the place they stand on the map,
through kernel commands into a player-scoped save row, with the same save, replay and reopen
guarantees as any state. Nothing reads the text but the writer's GameView.

## Lane, model, size, version

- Lane: Draft PR; slice branch `toolbox/m15-g10` from the batch head (after 47; it touches
  `delta.schema.json`, `rows.ts`, `compose_rows.ts`, `invariants_delta.ts`, `compose.ex`,
  `contracts.gen.ts`, `verbs.ts`, `actions.ts`). Worktree `../worktrees.noindex/m15-g10`.

## Contract (write these clauses first)

### docs/system/mechanics.md, new section "Journal notes and map pins (toolbox row G10)" after
"Lore codex and deduction (toolbox row 46)"

- **Capability.** `notes@1` (`protocol/capability_registry.json`: portable, commands `note`,
  `erase`, `pin`, `unpin`, no events). Offered only to a cartridge locking it; Chapter 1 and the
  corpus lock none: ActionSets, bytes and GameView unchanged.
- **Row.** One `notes` row per character (`State.notes[character_id]`, `NotesRow`):
  `{notes: [{id, text, at}], pins: {<room EntityId>: text}}`; `id` a positive integer, strictly
  increasing in the array; `at` the LogicalTime of the write; at most **32** notes and **64**
  pins; a note's `text` 1 to **160** code points, a pin's 1 to **40**. Absent reads as empty.
  Written only by the delta op `notes.set {character_id, expected, value}`, which composes, in
  both kernels, only when the stored row equals `expected` (null when absent): the `levelling.set`
  pattern (`compose_levelling.ts`, `compose_levelling.ex`). The op's schema carries the caps
  (`maxItems`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, `minimum`).
- **Text.** `text` is an `ActionInput` field (`protocol/action.schema.json`: a string, 1 to 160
  code points, `ActionInputParameter` `text`); `note` is an input naming a note `id` (integer
  at least 1, parameter `note`). The rule refuses `invalid_state`, even when a host skips the
  schema: a non-string, an empty or over-long text (code points, `[...text].length`), any
  control character (U+0000 to U+001F, U+007F to U+009F), or a text that is only whitespace. The
  text is stored as typed (no trimming, no folding) and never reaches narration, an event, a
  reaction or another actor's view (trap 9; Realm seam 6).
- **Commands.** `note {text}` (target none) appends `{id: 1 + the last id (1 when empty), text,
  at: clock}`; with 32 notes it is listed unavailable and refused `invalid_state`. `erase {note}`
  (target none) removes the note with that id; an unknown id is `not_found`; offered only while
  a note exists. `pin {text}` (target none) sets the pin of the room holding the actor's body,
  replacing any; `unpin` (target none) removes it; offered only while that room is a visited
  room of the actor (knowledge@1's visit row; without knowledge@1 nothing is visited and
  neither is ever offered), `unpin` only while a pin is there, `pin` unavailable `invalid_state`
  at 64 pins on other rooms. Outcomes `noted`, `erased`, `pinned`, `unpinned`; no narration, no
  event, no duration; replay returns the original receipt. Scene, combat and conversation
  admission win as for any verb (they refuse `unsupported_capability`).
- **GameView.** `notes` (absent when empty; the actor's notes in id order, each `{id, text,
  day}`, `day` = `floor(at / units(cartridge).day) + 1`, `kernel/ts/src/mechanics/calendar.ts`
  `units`), and `KnownRoomView.pin` (the room's pin text, absent without one; the map lists only
  visited rooms, so every pin is drawable). Nothing on `place`.
- **Save.** The row persists in the `notes` section through the normal changed-row transaction.
  Load (`mobile/authority/local-story/notes-save.ts`, called beside `factsValid`,
  `store.ts:148`) refuses `save_corrupt`: a row not keyed by this save's character, a shape
  other than `NotesRow`, ids not strictly increasing, more than the caps, a text outside its
  bounds or holding a control character, `at` not a non-negative integer, a pin keyed by an id
  that is no room of the world. Older saves have no rows and load as empty. No format bump.
- **Known limits.** Pins are placed where the actor stands (remote pinning is Book polish,
  loka-x6t.49). A note write at the cap carries the whole prior row in `expected` (about 8 KB);
  if receipts grow, per-note rows are the next shape. Day numbering uses the legacy 24-hour day
  for a cartridge without a calendar.

0 etc. must fail the schema, not pass the test).

protocol/fixtures/*_sampler_hash.json known answer and the fixture list in the
mobile/app/stories/SystemDataModel.stories.tsx Impact story.
Exact-boundary tests: every threshold is tested at the boundary value and one past it.
Content: hand back an item loop table (each item: source -> sink or cap); no hidden faucet.
Mutants: mutate every new conditional in your diff; the check table pastes the failing line from
each mutant run ("every new check (both kernels) -> the test that fails when it is removed, with
the failing line").
Self-review: run `/code-review medium` FROM YOUR SLICE WORKTREE (cd there first) on the range
<base>...HEAD that the brief names, never on the main checkout.
Push: `git push origin <branch> > <scratch log> 2>&1; echo PUSH_EXIT=$?` and read PUSH_EXIT
directly.
Confirm ci and book-e2e started with one `gh run list --commit <full sha>`; never wait on CI.
Screenshot: when the player sees the change, a 390 px wide screenshot of the web Book
(docs/web-preview.md), path in the handback.
Never print home or worktree absolute paths in commits, Beads text or PR text.
HANDBACK (under 200 words): head sha; check table; /code-review medium result (range named);
Realm answers; open questions (the PM rules on them as follow-ups); COST (your token count).
REALM CHECKLIST (paste; answer each "met: how" or "n/a: why"):
Realm seams (docs/decisions/owner-decision-realm-seams-2026-10-13.md): this row adds no new
single-player assumption.
1. Actor: rules read the command's actor (bodyOf(world, actor)); jobs store their character; no new
world.character outside runtime/, view/, local authority.
2. Reactions: each new trigger or step names its actor from the event's declared subject, never the
listener default.
3. Credit: a shared payout names its credited character (encounter, G8 member) and states its credit
rule in one line.
4. Time: no device clock; delays in logical units; no skip; no from/until outside the elapsed path.
5. Scope: per-player facts are player scope (instance only for world state); a once-per-world spawn
or event states its Realm audience.
6. Text: speech@1 unchanged; typed text visible only to its writer; anything shared names speech@2
(Realm).
7. Ownership: exclusive or not, and how it moves; theft never transfers ownership.
8. Trust: no receipt or import trusted that this authority did not compute; a row that needs it
lands result_digest first.
9. Instancing: none built, none assumed; a unique thing states shared-world or per-instance.

title: Undecodable area bundle cascades UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE diagnostics
description: An undecodable area bundle (areas/<name>.json that is not valid JSON or not an object) adds no definitions, so every reference into it also reports UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE (e.g. cartridge.entry), burying the one real INVALID_JSON. Found in the PR #471 review (loka-kgd.194.5). Fix: suppress reference diagnostics whose target lives only in a refused bundle, or report the bundle once and stop.
notes:
BRIEF A (covers .12 .13 .14):
## Brief A: diagnostics at the author's line (loka-kgd.194.12, .13, .14)

**Lane, branch and model.**
- Draft PR, batched pushes, on `toolbox/authoring-batch-a`. Work in the worktree that
  `bin/new_batch.sh` printed.
- Opus developer. Handoff threshold: about 220k tokens. At the threshold, stop and hand back.
- Read the brief kit (`docs/guides/brief-kit.md`) once; this brief does not copy it.

**Goal.** Three source-shortcut refusals today report at paths the author never wrote. Make each
report at the author's site. The artifact of every valid cartridge is unchanged.

**Spec.** `docs/system/cartridge.md` Source shortcuts: Area bundles (line 362), Inline prose (line
412) and Signals (the refusal table, about line 464). Lessons: `docs/lessons/contracts.md`.

**Signatures you touch.** `ast-grep outline` does not support Elixir, so these are `def`/`defp`
lines.
- `lib/loka/content/bundles.ex`: `split(files, dirs)` :18, `open/2` :24/:26/:29/:31,
  `member(rel, {dir, defs}, dirs)` :33.
- `lib/loka/content/compiler.ex`: `compile(files, loaded, registry)` :38, `split(lists)` :62,
  `text/1` :186-193.
- `lib/loka/content/prose.ex`: `lower(files)` :16, `catalog/3` :28,
  `add({key, words, at}, {text, faults})` :33.
- `lib/loka/content/signals.ex`: `lower(files)` :31 (with `sent` at :32-38), `listen/2` :50,
  `sending/2` :73, `fact(name)` :104.
- `lib/loka/content/source.ex`: `load(dir)` :49, `shortcuts/2` :58.

### A1: an undecodable bundle cascades (.12)

**What happens today.** Probed on main: compiling `cartridges/speech_sampler` with
`areas/village.json` = `{` gives
```
{"INVALID_JSON", "areas/village", %{}}
{"UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE", "cartridge.entry", %{"target" => "speech_sampler@0.0.1:room/square"}}
```

**Why.** `bundles.ex:24` adds nothing for an undecodable bundle. A `DUPLICATE_KEY` arrives as
`:invalid` there too (`source.ex` `checked/3`). `:29` adds nothing for a non-object bundle, and
`:36` nothing for a non-object member. The references then fail in `refs.ex:52-55`, and the entry
check fails at `compiler.ex:152`.

**Fix.** While any bundle refusal stands, the compile result
leaves out every `UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE`. Every other diagnostic stays.
- A refusal here means: a bundle that did not decode (INVALID_JSON or DUPLICATE_KEY), is not an
  object, has an unknown member, or has a member that is not an object.
- Carry that fact from `Source.load` to `Compiler.compile` without parsing diagnostic paths. One
  way is to keep a `{rel, :bundle, :invalid}` entry in `files` and check it there. Every pass
  already ignores a non-definition entry; verify that in `extends.ex:20-23`,
  `prose.ex:40-45`, `signals.ex:33`, `zones.ex:28-29` and `lint.ex:31`.

**Acceptance.** All of these build on `cartridges/speech_sampler`. All three cases were probed on
main: today each returns the row below plus only `UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE` rows. The `romos` case
adds four NPC `.room` rows and `cartridge.entry`.
- `areas/village.json` = `{`: the diagnostics are exactly
  `[{"INVALID_JSON", "areas/village", %{}}]`.
- The bundle is `[]`: exactly
  `[{"SCHEMA_VIOLATION", "areas/village", %{"error" => "invalid_type"}}]`.
- The `rooms` member is renamed to `romos`: exactly
  `[{"UNKNOWN_FIELD", "areas/village.romos", %{}}]`.
- Control: with the bundle intact and `cartridge.json` `entry` set to `nowhere`, the
  `UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE` at `cartridge.entry` is still reported. The filter is off when no bundle
  is refused.
- Red control: remove the filter, and the first case fails with the `cartridge.entry` row back.
- `test/loka/content_bundles_test.exs` "a bundle refuses a non-object bundle, ..." (:17) may need
  its expected list updated. The update must stay exact.

**Docs.** Rewrite the Area bundles bullet "A bundle that fails to decode adds nothing; its
`INVALID_JSON` fails the build" so it also says unresolved references are held back while the
refusal stands.

### A2: inline prose that is too long (.13)

**What happens today.** Probed on main: speech_sampler with `npcs.elder.short` = `{"prose": <4097
x>}` gives only `{"SCHEMA_VIOLATION", "text[\"npc.elder.short\"]", %{"error" => "too_long"}}`.

**Why.** `prose.ex:33-37` adds the words unchecked, and `compiler.ex:189-193` refuses the whole
catalog at the generated key.

**Fix.** In `Prose.add/2`, check the line with `Contracts.validate("TextCatalog", %{key => words})`.
Do not use a literal 4096. `TextValue` is the wrong def: it describes an interpolation value. On
main this returns `:too_long` for 4097 characters and `:pattern_mismatch` for a key over 128. For
each error, add a fault at the marker's location (`at`), with data `%{"error" => <code>}`. A
TextKey error at the marker is already reported through the field's own schema, so keep only one
row per code at the marker. Still add the words to the
catalog. The report goes "too", not "instead": dropping the words would add an
`UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE` at the same marker. The existing TextKey rule already reports at both sites.

**Acceptance.**
- 4097 characters: exactly
  `[{"SCHEMA_VIOLATION", "areas/village.npcs.elder.short", %{"error" => "too_long"}}, {"SCHEMA_VIOLATION", "text[\"npc.elder.short\"]", %{"error" => "too_long"}}]`.
- 4096 characters: compiles. This tests the exact boundary.
- One case in a plain file, so the path has no bundle prefix: `npcs/<key>.short`.
- Red control: remove the new check, and the 4097 case loses its marker row.

**Docs.** Replace "a word-length error is reported only at `text["<key>"]`" with "is reported at
the marker and again at `text["<key>"]`".

### A3: a signal name too long for its fact (.14)

**What happens today.** Probed on main: `test/fixtures/signal_sugar` with a 58-character name (`s`
× 58) in both `reactions/ring.json` `apply[0].signal` and `reactions/hear.json` `on.signal` gives
```
{"SCHEMA_VIOLATION", "facts.facts.signal_<58 s>", %{"error" => "too_long"}}
{"SCHEMA_VIOLATION", "reactions/hear.on.fact", %{"error" => "too_long"}}
{"SCHEMA_VIOLATION", "reactions/ring.apply[0].fact", %{"error" => "too_long"}}
```

**Why.** `signals.ex:36` admits any Key name, and `signal_` adds 7 characters to a Key that may
be at most 64 (`protocol/action.schema.json` `Key.maxLength`).

**Fix, part 1.** A name is lowered only when both `name` and `fact(name)` are Keys. Otherwise the
sending step stays unlowered, and the schema refuses it at `apply[i].op`.

**Fix, part 2.** A listener whose name some step sends, but which could not be lowered, becomes
`:invalid` with no diagnostic of its own. Today it gets a false "no sender"
`UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE`; probed on main with the non-Key name `Bell`, both kinds of name do this.
A listener whose name no step sends at all keeps its `UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE`.

**Acceptance.**
- 58 characters: exactly
  `[{"SCHEMA_VIOLATION", "reactions/ring.apply[0].op", %{"error" => "unknown_variant"}}]`.
- 57 characters: compiles. This tests the exact boundary.
- Name `Bell` in both files: exactly the same single row.
- The listener-only case keeps
  `{"UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE", "reactions/hear.on.signal", %{"target" => "gong"}}`, as in the
  existing test at `content_signal_zone_test.exs:27`.
- The existing rows at `content_signal_zone_test.exs:72` and `:93` stay unchanged. In both, the
  sender's name changes to `1` or `Bell!` and the listener still names `bell`, which no step sends.
- Red controls: drop the `fact(name)` check, and the 58 case shows the three generated-path rows.
  Drop the silent-listener branch, and the `UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE` row returns.

**Docs.** Amend the Signals refusal table row: "A sending step whose name is not a Key, or whose
`signal_<name>` is not (a name over 57 characters), ...". Add the line "its listeners report
nothing of their own".

**.14's second question, ruled.** An abstract rule with an unknown zone compiles silently. This is
intended: cartridge.md says an abstract definition "is never validated", and `extends.ex:33`
drops it before `Zones.expand` (`source.ex:58-63`). No code changes. Pin it with one test: a
concrete child that `extends` the abstract rule inherits `"zone": "nowhere"` and is refused at its
own path, exactly `{"UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE", "reactions/<child>.zone", %{"target" => "nowhere"}}`.
Add one sentence under Zones.

**Out of scope.** Any new diagnostic code. Any change to `protocol/`. Any change to the artifact
of a valid cartridge. Lint.

**Scope trigger: stop and ask** if a fix needs a new diagnostic code, a protocol edit, or touches
more than the files listed in the plan row.

**Handback.** Per the brief kit, including the check table. Every new branch has a mutant, with
the failing line pasted.

notes:
BRIEF B:
## Brief B: compile-time behaviours (loka-kgd.194.16)

**Lane, branch and model.**
- Draft PR, batched pushes, on `toolbox/authoring-batch-a`, after Brief A's head.
- Fable developer. Handoff threshold: about 220k tokens.
- Read the brief kit (`docs/guides/brief-kit.md`) once. Lessons: `docs/lessons/contracts.md`.

**Goal.** A named, reusable set of reactions is attached to many NPCs or items and expands to one
reaction per holder (owner decision record, effect 2). The artifact has no behaviour in it, and the
loader is unchanged.

**Spec to write.** A new "Behaviours" paragraph in cartridge.md Source shortcuts, after Zones,
with the same shape as Zones: bullets, then a refusal table, then the working example. Also update
the pass-order sentence at line 357.

**Signatures to reuse.**
- `zones.ex`: `expand(files)` :19, `rule/2` :43-62, `copies/4` :64-66. This is the copy pattern:
  key, location, and `Bundles.unique` on the copies.
- `bundles.ex`: `unique(files)` :45.
- `source.ex`: `load/1` :49-56, `shortcuts/2` :58-63, `@dirs` :133, `classify/1` :159.
- `prose.ex`: `definition/2` :40-45. Prose lowers any `{kind, key, steps}` entry, so behaviour
  files get keys `behaviour.<name>.reactions.<rule>...` that all copies share, as zone copies do.

**Design.**
1. **Source.** `behaviours/<name>.json` holds `{"reactions": {"<rule>": <ReactionRule without
   key>}}`. Add `"behaviours" => :behaviour` to `@dirs`, so area bundles carry them for free
   (`areas/x.json` `{"behaviours": {...}}`). An NPC or item lists `"behaviours": ["<name>", ...]`.
2. **The holder.** Inside a behaviour's rules, the marker `{"param": "holder"}` (an object whose
   only member is `param`) is replaced by the holder's key, wherever it appears. Before and after,
   for `fishing_sampler`:
   - `behaviours/spoils.json`:
     `{"reactions": {"take": {"on": {"event": "item_acquired", "item": {"param": "holder"}}, "apply": [{"op": "status.apply", "status": "spoiling", "item": {"param": "holder"}}]}}}`
   - `items/trout_01.json` adds `"behaviours": ["spoils"]`.
   - Result: reaction `take_trout_01`, byte for byte today's `reactions/take_trout_01.json`.
   - Any other marker stays, and the schema refuses it at its site (.18 adds declared
     parameters).
3. **Key.** A copy is `<rule>_<holder>` (zones scheme). A copy carries the
   behaviour rule's location, so each of its diagnostics reports once at
   `behaviours/<name>.reactions.<rule>...`. A name listed twice on one holder counts once.
4. **Order in `Source.load`.** Bundles, unique, extends, prose, **behaviours**, signals, zones,
   unique.
   - After extends: an abstract NPC may carry `behaviours`, and its children inherit them; a list
     replaces.
   - After prose: copies share the behaviour's text keys.
   - Before signals and zones: a behaviour rule may send a signal or name a zone.
   - The final `Bundles.unique`, inside `Zones.expand` (`zones.ex:24`), refuses a clashing copy.
5. **Stripping.** The pass removes every `:behaviour` entry and strips `behaviours` from every NPC
   and item, so neither the compiler (`compiler.ex` `@kinds`) nor lint (`lint.ex:23-31`) sees
   them. `behaviours` on any other kind stays, and the schema reports `UNKNOWN_FIELD` there. A
   behaviour that no holder uses is dropped silently; .19 covers dead wiring and is not in this
   batch.

**Refusals (put this table in cartridge.md).**

| Case | Code | Path | data |
|---|---|---|---|
| `behaviours` is not a list of Keys | `SCHEMA_VIOLATION` | `<src>.behaviours` | `{"error": "invalid_type"}` |
| A name with no behaviour | `UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE` | `<src>.behaviours[<i>]` | `{"target": "behaviours/<name>"}` |
| A behaviour member other than `reactions` | `UNKNOWN_FIELD` | `behaviours/<name>.<member>` | `{}` |
| `reactions` is not an object | `SCHEMA_VIOLATION` | `behaviours/<name>.reactions` | `{"error": "invalid_type"}` |
| A copy key equal to another reaction's | `DUPLICATE_DEFINITION` | each site | `{}` (existing check) |
| A copy key over 64 characters | `SCHEMA_VIOLATION` | the behaviour rule | existing check, as for zones |

**Acceptance.**
1. **Gate D (byte-identical).** Re-express `cartridges/fishing_sampler`: delete the four
   `reactions/take_*.json`, add `behaviours/spoils.json`, and add `"behaviours": ["spoils"]` to the
   four items.
   - The artifact's sha256 must equal
     `df64a9a2fe29ad1037ea24176a58a1e1964390f06b0f837d7d45e13b5b00a482`. That is the hash of
     `Loka.Content.compile("cartridges/fishing_sampler")` on main at 9cf4619c4, recorded before

   - A test asserts that literal. Record the line and file count before and after for the

2. Each refusal row above has one test, with an exact
   `{code, path, data}` list on a copy of fishing_sampler (`Loka.ContentSource.copy/compile`, as
   `content_signal_zone_test.exs:8-12` does).
3. Inheritance: an abstract item carrying `behaviours`, extended by two concrete items, yields both
   copies.
4. Copy location: a bad `status` in the behaviour rule reports once, at
   `behaviours/spoils.reactions.take.apply[0].status`. Mirror "a check on a zone copy reports

Biggest stability gain per PM. Owner asked to file 2026-10-24.
notes:
BRIEF D:
## Brief D: source JSON Schema for editors and LLM authors (loka-kgd.194.17)

**PM ruling.** Opus brief: a tooling schema, not a protocol, save or compiled-cartridge contract.
It holds only while the hard trigger below holds.

**Lane, branch and model.**
- Draft PR, batched pushes, on `toolbox/authoring-batch-a`, after Brief C.
- Opus developer. Handoff threshold: about 220k tokens.
- Read the brief kit once. Lessons: `docs/lessons/contracts.md` and `docs/lessons/checks.md` (a
  generated file can drift).

**Goal.** Editors and LLM authors see a bad field while writing, before compile. Publish one JSON
Schema (draft 2020-12) per source file kind, generated from the compiler's own accepted source,
with a test that keeps it in step.

**Spec.** Add a short "Source schema" paragraph in cartridge.md, after Source shortcuts. In
`docs/BUILDERS-GUIDE.md`, add how to point an editor at it: VS Code `json.schemas` `fileMatch`.
Not through `$schema` in a source file, because a `$schema` member is `UNKNOWN_FIELD`.

**Where the truth is.**
- `source.ex` `contracts/0` :256: the source view of `Contracts.defs()`, with short DefinitionRefs
  and the schedule override at :275.
- `compiler.ex` `@kinds` (about :195-219): each directory's contract.
- `compiler.ex` `validated/5` :354: how the compiler validates.
- `Loka.Core.Contracts.validate/3` (`contracts.ex:66-68`): takes a defs map.

**Design constraints.**
1. **Output location.** Outside `protocol/`, for example `schemas/source/<kind>.schema.json` plus
   one shared defs file. Write it with a new `mix loka.source_schema` task.
2. **One schema per kind.** One for each `@dirs` directory, `areas/`, `behaviours/`, and the root
   files (`cartridge.json`, `facts.json`, `text.json`, `resources.json`, `attributes.json`,
   `map_positions.json`).
3. **Accepts every shortcut.** That is: no `key` member; `extends`; `abstract` (an abstract
   definition is not validated, so its schema is loose); `params` and `with`; `{"prose": "<non-empty>"}`
   wherever a TextKey goes; the signal step and trigger; `zone` on a reaction and `zones` on a
   room; `behaviours` on an NPC or item; `{"param": ...}` markers in behaviours and abstract
   parents. `wait` is out (.15).
4. **A child with `extends`** omits inherited required members. Its schema must not demand them.
5. **Standard refs.** Contracts use bare-name refs (`"$ref": "Key"`). The emitted file uses
   standard `#/$defs/...` refs, or relative refs to the shared file.

**Acceptance.**
1. Drift: a test regenerates the schemas in memory and asserts they equal the committed files byte
   for byte.
2. No false refusals: every `.json` source file under `cartridges/*/` validates against its kind's
   schema. Each area bundle member validates against its directory's schema.
   - Validate with ajv (draft 2020-12, `ajv/dist/2020`), added as a dev dependency only (owner
     2026-10-28), against the committed files with their standard refs.
   - Include `shoo_sampler/npcs/oak_deer.json` (an `extends` child) and `npcs/wild.json`
     (abstract).
3. Structure: every `$ref` in the committed files resolves to a `$defs` member or a sibling file.
4. Red controls. Each must be refused by its schema, and passes when the targeted rule is removed
   from the generator:
   - a room with `"titel"`;
   - `{"prose": ""}`;
   - `"extends": 1`;
   - a signal step with `amount`;
   - `"behaviours": "spoils"`.
5. No hash fixture changes; `git diff --stat protocol/` is empty.

**Split rule.** If this sizes past M, deliver plain kinds, areas and extends first. Then hand back;
the PM briefs the shortcuts as D2.

**Hard scope trigger: stop and ask** before any of these:
- any file under `protocol/`;
- any change to `contracts.gen.ts`;
- making the compiler or loader read the new schema;
- adding an npm or hex dependency.

**Realm.** n/a: authoring tooling.

title: Prototype parameters: extends with per-child arguments for families of similar definitions
description: Next step after extends (#469): e.g. extends rat with {hp: 8} filling declared parameters in an abstract parent. Decide whether plain field override already covers it before building. Owner asked to file 2026-10-24.
notes:
BRIEF C:
## Brief C: parameters for extends and behaviours (loka-kgd.194.18)

**Lane, branch and model.**
- Draft PR, batched pushes, on `toolbox/authoring-batch-a`, after Brief B.
- Fable developer. Handoff threshold: about 220k tokens.
- Read the brief kit once. Lessons: `docs/lessons/contracts.md`.

**Goal.** A family of near-identical definitions whose differences sit inside lists collapses to
one abstract parent plus one-line children. A behaviour takes per-holder arguments, such as a line
that names the NPC.

**Spec.** In cartridge.md Source shortcuts, add a "Parameters" paragraph under `extends` and a line
in Behaviours.

**Evidence that override does not cover it.** Measured on main:
- `cartridges/toolbox_showcase/reactions/wheel_{1,2,3}_x_shows_{0..9}.json` (30 files of 19 lines)
  are identical once these 4 fields are normalised; this was checked by script over all 30. They
  differ in `on.action`, `when.root.fact`, `when.root.equals` and `apply[0].text`.
- `apply` is a list. `extends.ex:101-104` merges only objects, so a child must restate the whole
  list.

**Signatures you touch.**
- `extends.ex`: `flatten(files)` :19, `own/5` :53-67, `inherit/2` :69-72, `merge/2` :101-104.
- `behaviours.ex` (Brief B): its marker substitution. Make that one function that both passes
  call.

**Design.**
1. **Declaration.** An abstract definition may declare `"params": ["<Key>", ...]`. In a behaviour,
   `params` sits beside `reactions`. `holder` is reserved and is always bound in behaviours.
2. **Marker.** `{"param": "<name>"}` anywhere inside the declaring definition is replaced by the
   argument's value. A value replaces the whole marker; there is no string interpolation.
3. **Extends.** A child's `"with": {"<name>": <value>}` fills its direct parent's markers before
   the child merges over it (`inherit/2`). `with` and `params` never reach the artifact. Only the
   direct parent is filled. A marker left unfilled stays, and the schema refuses it at its site.
4. **Behaviours.** An attachment may be `{"behaviour": "<name>", "with": {...}}` instead of
   `"<name>"`.
   - Prose inside `with` is lowered with the holder, before behaviours, as
     `<kind>.<holder>.behaviours.<i>.with.<arg>`. So each holder gets its own line.
5. No defaults, no append, no interpolation (ponytail; audit finding 21).

**Refusals (put this table in cartridge.md).**

| Case | Code | Path | data |
|---|---|---|---|
| `with` names an undeclared parameter | `UNKNOWN_FIELD` | `<src>.with.<name>` (in a behaviour: `<src>.behaviours[<i>].with.<name>`) | `{}` |
| A declared parameter missing from `with` | `SCHEMA_VIOLATION` | `<src>.with` | `{"error": "missing_property"}` |
| A marker naming no declared parameter | `UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE` | the marker's site in the parent or behaviour | `{"target": "<name>"}` |
| `params` is not a list of Keys, or lists `holder` in a behaviour; `with` is not an object | `SCHEMA_VIOLATION` | that member | `{"error": "invalid_type"}` / `{"error": "invalid_value"}` |
| `params` on a non-abstract definition | `UNKNOWN_FIELD` | `<src>.params` | `{}` (the schema, unchanged) |

**Acceptance.**
1. **Gate D (byte-identical).** Re-express the 30 wheel rules as one abstract
   `reactions/wheel_shows.json` (`params: ["action", "fact", "n", "line"]`) plus 30 children of
   `extends` and `with`.
   - `test/loka/content_showcase_test.exs` must pass unchanged against
     `protocol/fixtures/toolbox_showcase_hash.json`, so the hash does not move.
   - All 7 showcase transcripts must still replay (`kernel/ts/test/transcripts.test.ts`).
   - Report lines and files before and after.
2. A behaviour test, on an in-test copy (`Loka.ContentSource.copy` plus changes). The committed
   `fishing_sampler` stays as Brief B left it, so its literal sha and `fishing.test.ts` hold.
   `spoils` gains a param `line` used in a `narrate` step, and two items pass `{"prose": ...}`
   lines. The artifact has `item.trout_01.behaviours.0.with.line`
   and `item.eel_01.behaviours.0.with.line` with their words.
3. Each refusal row has one test with an exact `{code, path, data}` list.
4. Red controls: fill after merge instead of before (gate 1 fails); skip the missing-argument check
   (row 2's test fails); drop `with` stripping (`UNKNOWN_FIELD` at a child's `with`).
5. Grep for tests that read `reactions/wheel_*` source files directly, and keep them green.

**Out of scope.**
- Grandparent filling.
- Defaults.
- Parameters on root files.
- The `lever_*` rules. List them in the handback as the next candidates.
- `protocol/`.

**Scope trigger: stop and ask** if gate 1's hash moves for a reason other than your pass, or if a
parameter needs interpolation inside a string.

**Realm.** n/a: compile-time only. Say why in one line per item.
