title: coverage.ts: transcript coverage of reactions, recipes, choices and quests (dead rules by evidence)
description: Approach F of docs/rnd/design-audit-abilities-authoring-2026-10-23.md: a play tool listing definitions no transcript of a cartridge exercises; run on the showcase. No contract change.
notes:
BRIEF (PM-adopted 2026-10-23):
# Brief loka-kgd.194.2: `coverage.ts`, transcript coverage play tool

Read once, then follow: [brief kit](docs/briefs/brief-kit.md) (common rules, handback, Realm
checklist); `AGENTS.md` Simplicity and Writing tests; `.claude/agents/developer.md`;
[WORKFLOW step 3](docs/WORKFLOW.md#loop). Lessons: `docs/lessons/checks.md` (a coverage witness
compares resolved ids, never titles; red controls), `docs/lessons/mechanics.md`,
`docs/lessons/contracts.md` (kit rule; nothing here touches a schema). Plan and rationale:
`docs/rnd/design-audit-abilities-authoring-2026-10-23.md` on branch
`docs/abilities-authoring-2026-10-23` (read it with `git show`), findings 16 and 23, approach F,
plan phase 4. Owner approval: Beads epic `loka-kgd.194` (the owner order of 2026-10-23: phase 0,
then 4, then 3).

**Handoff threshold 220k tokens.** Past it, hand the remaining work to a fresh agent with a
short brief. No subagents.

## Goal

A play tool that replays a cartridge's transcripts (`cartridges/<id>/transcripts/*.jsonl`) and
lists the definitions that no transcript exercises:

- reactions whose steps never ran;
- recipes never completed;
- dialogue choices never chosen;
- quests never resolved.

It is a report for authors. Nothing is committed, and CI does not check the report itself.
Only its unit test runs.

## Lane and size

Hosted PR, alone. Branch `toolbox/kgd194-coverage` from current `main`, in your own worktree.
Size **S**. One new tool, one test file and one docs subsection. Contract: none (protocol,
save, kernel_api unchanged; no file under `kernel/ts/src/` changes). `loka-kgd.194.3`
(`why.ts`) imports this tool's replay and marker helpers. It starts after this PR merges, so
keep their names and shapes as below.

## Spec first (same PR, first commit)

Add `### Transcript coverage (loka-kgd.194.2)` to `docs/system/cartridge.md`, under
[Content reports](docs/system/cartridge.md#content-reports). Put it after the
"Refusal and friction report (balance tool 8)" subsection and before
`## Installed capabilities` (now line 598). Write the command, the exit codes, the output and the
evidence rule for each kind below. Add one `ponytail:` line for the limits listed under Design.
Link the reaction@1 clause instead of restating it.

## Evidence per kind (verified on `main`, cite these in code comments)

No committed event names the reaction that produced it. `sequence` emits plain payloads
(`kernel/ts/src/mechanics/reaction.ts:144-146`). The trace keeps `delta_digest`, not the
delta (`kernel/ts/play/run.ts:124-127`). So reaction firing is rebuilt by replay:

| Kind | Exercised when | Engine `file:line` |
|---|---|---|
| reaction | its `apply` steps ran in some replayed step: the `when` held at `reaction.ts:152` and (for `after`) its job ran (`mechanics/delayed.ts:53-61`) | marker below; `reaction.ts:188` pushes a `narrate` step's line; `runtime/proposal.ts:242` and `:276` carry it into the decision |
| recipe | a committed `action_completed` whose `action` is the recipe's `key` (spells too: cast goes through the same rule) | `mechanics/action_recipe/rule.ts:78` (`action = recipe.key`), `:99-101` (none on a `failure` outcome) |
| dialogue choice | a committed `choice_resolved {continuation_id, choice_id}`, attributed to the dialogue `world.state.choices[continuation_id].source` of the world **before** that step; rows whose `source.kind` is `scene` are not dialogue choices | `mechanics/dialogue/rule.ts:53-57`, `:137-138` |
| quest | a committed `quest_resolved {quest}`; `quest_failed` does not count | `mechanics/quest/lifecycle.ts:261` |

**Marker (no kernel change).** Replay from a copy of the loaded cartridge. In the copy, each
`reactions` entry gets one more `apply` step, `{op: 'narrate', text: <unique key per rule>}`.
Map the key back to the rule's DefinitionRefString. Do not mutate the loaded object.
Narration is not part of a trace line (`run.ts:124-130`). It never enters state:
`runtime/proposal_adopt.ts:39-51` adopts the delta only. So the marked replay must still equal the
recorded bytes. The tool checks that on every transcript, so a marker that ever changes a
decision becomes a loud failure, not a wrong report. The known way that can happen is
`output_bytes` (`proposal_adopt.ts:36`) or the 64-line narration cap near its limit. A spike
on `main` found the marked replay byte-identical on all 7 showcase transcripts and on
`scene_sampler`. Rejected alternative: matching with `triggered()` only. That counts a rule
whose `when` failed as fired (mutation 1).

## Design

- `kernel/ts/play/coverage.ts`, in the `reach.ts` / `friction.ts` pattern. The header comment
  names the cartridge.md section. Exports:
  - `marked(c: Cartridge): { cartridge: Cartridge; ruleOf: (key: string) => string | undefined }`
  - `replay(c: Cartridge, trace: ReturnType<typeof replayRecords>, each?: (before: World, d: DecisionResult, ordinal: number) => void, upTo?: number): void`.
    It starts a `Run` with the trace head's own ids (`start` in `run.ts:26`, with
    `head.ids.content_hash`, so the header bytes match even for an edited cartridge). It
    decides each entry with `decideReplay` (`run.ts:69`). It compares **line by line**: the
    header with recorded line 0, then each produced trace line with the recorded line at its
    ordinal (`file.split('\n')[ordinal]`). A shortened `entries` (rows B and C) must therefore
    pass. At the first difference it throws `<transcript>: replay differs at ordinal <n>`, the
    transcript named as `relative(ROOT, path)`. Never print an absolute path (AGENTS.md "All
    work"). This is not the whole-file `assert.equal` of `transcripts.test.ts:50-52`. `upTo`
    stops before that ordinal without comparing it, for `why.ts`.
  - `coverage(c: Cartridge, traces: ReturnType<typeof replayRecords>[])` returns
    `{cartridge: "<id>@<version>", transcripts: <count>, never: {reactions, recipes, choices, quests}}`.
    `reactions`, `recipes` and `quests` are sorted DefinitionRefStrings (the cartridge map
    keys). `choices` is `[{dialogue: <DefinitionRefString>, choice: <choice key>}]`, sorted
    by dialogue, then choice.
- CLI: `node kernel/ts/play/coverage.ts <artifact> [<transcript.jsonl> ...]`. With no
  transcripts given, it uses `cartridges/<manifest.id>/transcripts/*.jsonl` under `ROOT`
  (`play/obs.ts:13`), sorted. It loads and refuses as `reach.ts` does (`play/reach.ts:120-132`:
  the loader diagnostic on stderr, exit 1). It reads each trace with `replayRecords(path, <the
  trace's own pinned hash>)` (`play/replay.ts:6`). A replay that differs prints the error and
  exits 1. Bad arguments exit 2. Otherwise it prints one canonical JSON document (`encode`) and
  exits 0.
- ponytail limits (one docs line): firing means steps ran, so a delayed rule whose job never ran
  in a transcript shows unfired; scene choices and cartridge `actions` are out of scope;
  transcripts only, not browser walks.
- Size rules: files 300 lines, functions 40 (`docs/CHECKS.md` Size). No new `size: allow`.

Signatures you call (from `ast-grep outline`):
```
kernel/ts/play/replay.ts   6: export function replayRecords(path: string, content_hash: string)
kernel/ts/play/run.ts     26: export const start = (cartridge, content_hash, run_id, context, seed, version): Run
                          41: export const header = (r: Run) =>
                          69: export function decideReplay(r: Run, command: Command)
kernel/ts/play/obs.ts     13: export const ROOT   24: export function line(record: unknown): string
kernel/ts/play/reach.ts  120: if (import.meta.main) (CLI block to copy for load/refuse)
kernel/ts/src/runtime/decision.ts: refString
```

## Files

In scope: `kernel/ts/play/coverage.ts` (new), `kernel/ts/test/coverage.test.ts` (new),
`docs/system/cartridge.md` (one subsection).
Out of scope: everything under `kernel/ts/src/`, `protocol/`, `lib/`, `cartridges/` (no sampler
or transcript lands on disk, so the kit's sampler-hash and floors rules are n/a),
`mobile/`, the other play tools, and `kernel/ts/test/transcripts.test.ts`. If a helper there
would help, import it. Do not move it.

## Acceptance (literal expected values; independent sources named)

Fixtures: the known answers `protocol/fixtures/cartridge_scene_hash.json` (manifest
`scene_sampler`) and `protocol/fixtures/cartridge_dusk_hash.json` (manifest `check_sampler`),
with their transcripts `cartridges/scene_sampler/transcripts/scene.jsonl` and
`cartridges/check_sampler/transcripts/schedule.jsonl`. For in-test edits, copy the canonical
JSON, edit it, re-hash it and load it as `kernel/ts/test/ferry_probe.ts:30-47` does. Read each
trace with its own pinned hash. Never write a rule or file to disk. A spike confirmed that the
loader accepts the three edits below and that the edited cartridge replays `scene.jsonl` byte
for byte.

In-test edits to scene (prefix `scene_sampler@0.0.1:`):
- `reaction/never_matched`: `bell_after`'s compiled body with key `never_matched`,
  `on: {event: custom_event, custom: rope_coiled}`, and no `when`. `rope_coiled` is emitted
  only by `coil_rope`, which the transcript never performs.
- `reaction/never_held`: `bell_after`'s body with key `never_held`, the same trigger
  (`fact_changed` of `scene_bell_rung`), and `when: fact_compare search_plan equals "party_led"`.
  At ordinal 4 the transcript chooses `carry`, which assigns `player_led`
  (`cartridges/scene_sampler/dialogues/bram.json`).
- `dialogue/bram_twin`: `bram`'s body with key `bram_twin` and
  `policy: quest_state lantern state "failed"`. It never opens.

Independent facts used for the answers come from the recorded committed events in `scene.jsonl`:
`quest_activated lantern` at 1, `choice_resolved carry` and `quest_resolved lantern` at 4,
`fact_changed scene_bell_rung` at 4-7, and `fact_changed bell_heard` at 7 only (bell_after is
the only writer of `bell_heard`). Scene fact values are 1..n shown and -1 ended
(`docs/system/mechanics.md:556`).

| # | Input | Expected `never` | Break it catches | Engine line |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | edited scene, full transcript | `reactions: [".../reaction/never_held", ".../reaction/never_matched"]`, `recipes: [".../recipe/coil_rope"]`, `choices: [{bram, leave}, {bram_twin, carry}, {bram_twin, leave}]`, `quests: []` | trigger counted as fired (never_held missing); choice keyed by `choice_id` alone (bram_twin carry missing); marker mapped to the wrong rule | `reaction.ts:152`, `:188`; `dialogue/rule.ts:53`, `:137` |
| B | edited scene, ordinals 1-3 only (pass a trace whose `entries` is the first 3) | `reactions: [bell_after, never_held, never_matched]`, `recipes: [coil_rope]`, `choices: [{bram, carry}, {bram, leave}, {bram_twin, carry}, {bram_twin, leave}]`, `quests: [".../quest/lantern"]` | `quest_activated` counted as resolved | `quest/lifecycle.ts:261` |
| C | check (dusk known answer), ordinals 1-6 | `recipes: ["check_sampler@0.0.1:recipe/pick_lock"]`, every other list `[]`. Recorded: `ring_bell` completes at 2, `pick_lock` fails at 5 and 6 and first succeeds at 7 | an accepted `perform` (a failure outcome) counted as performed | `action_recipe/rule.ts:99-101` |
| D | check, full transcript | `recipes: []` (`pick_lock` completes at 7) | a wrong recipe-to-action mapping | `action_recipe/rule.ts:78` |
| E | scene with `bell_after.when.root.equals` set to `1` in-test (at ordinal 4 the scene fact becomes 1, `mechanics.md:556`, so the rule now writes `bell_heard` there, which the recording lacks) | `coverage` throws a message containing `replay differs at ordinal 4` | the byte guard missing (coverage of a stale transcript) | `replay`'s line-by-line comparison |
| F | CLI on a scratch artifact `{"cartridge":<scene canonical>,"content_hash":<sha256>}`, transcript `cartridges/scene_sampler/transcripts/scene.jsonl` | exit 0. stdout parses to `never.recipes == [".../recipe/coil_rope"]`, `never.choices == [{bram, leave}]`, `never.reactions == []`, `never.quests == []`. No arguments: exit 2 | the CLI wiring | `play/reach.ts:120-132` |

Keep A-F as few `test()` blocks as the breaks allow, and name the break in each header.
Rows A and B share one edited cartridge. Expected values are literals in the test, never
computed with the tool or kernel helpers.

**Showcase run (hand back, not asserted).** Compile and run
`node kernel/ts/play/coverage.ts <showcase artifact>`. A spike on `main` replayed all 7 showcase
transcripts (commerce, food, knowledge, light, liquid, readable, service) byte for byte with

BRIEF:
# Merge recipes into actions (loka-kgd.194.22): design check and Brief C2

Owner decision 2026-10-28 (Beads loka-kgd.194.22, quoted in the issue): one authoring kind,
`actions/<key>.json`, that either names a built-in `command` or carries authored `outcomes`; a mix
is refused. Repo read on main at d2b1d64e2; batch-a head f88f449d4.

## Part 1: design check

### What the split protects today (and whether a merge would break it)

| Seam | Where the split lives | Contract merge (artifact `actions` and `recipes` become one map) | Authoring-only merge (compiler routes `actions/*.json` by shape into today's artifact maps) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Artifact and DefinitionRef kinds | `protocol/cartridge.schema.json:42` (`actions`, required) and `:137` (`recipes`, optional); refs are `…:action/<k>` vs `…:recipe/<k>`; `protocol/action.schema.json:373` ActionDefinition (8 required fields, `additionalProperties: false`) vs `:889` ActionRecipe (7 required; `label` is a TextKey, `target` is RecipeTarget not TargetSpec) | Breaks: two different `target` and `label` types under one map need a `oneOf` in protocol, a new ref kind, `contracts.gen.ts` regeneration, every `_hash.json` fixture (recipe-bearing samplers: 8 with transcripts, `toolbox_showcase` alone 7), `protocol/fixtures/invalid.json:11264` and `e1.test.ts:34` artifact pointers (`/recipes/…:recipe/…`) | Untouched. The artifact, refs, hashes and transcripts are byte-identical, which is the gate |
| Kernel ActionSet and keyed admission | `kernel/ts/src/commands/actions.ts:117-144` builds the set from `world.cartridge.actions` and `world.cartridge.recipes` (`:272 allRecipes`); `:248-268` perform admission by `a.recipe`; 38 kernel files name `recipes` | Breaks: every consumer re-keyed; admission query, `view/action_lists.ts:72,154,203`, `view/use.ts`, `view/spells.ts`, `cartridge_recipes.ts` loader | Untouched |
| NoticeView projection of a detail recipe | `docs/system/mechanics.md:215`; `action_lists.ts:96 detailRecipe` | Rewritten | Untouched |
| Room contributions | `action.schema.json:463 ActionContribution`: a key names a verb, action or recipe; compiler `recipes.ex:285-300 contributions/known` | Unchanged semantics but new ref kinds | Untouched (keys are kind-free) |
| coverage.ts / why.ts | `kernel/ts/play/coverage.ts:103`, `why.ts:128` read `c.recipes` | Rewritten | Untouched |
| Save and replay | `perform {action}` payload and `action_completed` carry keys, not kinds (`mechanics.md:375`); `e1_obligations.ts:288` builds `/recipes/…:recipe/` artifact pointers | Replays break on the pointer; `perform` itself survives | Untouched |
| Protocol fixtures with source paths | `protocol/fixtures/loader_floors.json` (31 `recipes/<file>.json` edit rows, e.g. `:13`), applied to source by both kernels (`kernel/ts/test/loader_floors.test.ts:49-68`, `test/loka/loader_floors_test.exs`) | Changed | Changed: 31 path strings only, no schema or behaviour change |
| Compiler stages keyed by source dir | `source.ex:135-139 @dirs` (`actions`→`:action`, `recipes`→`:recipe`); `compiler.ex:196-220 @kinds` (`{"action", :action, "ActionDefinition"}`, `{"recipe", :recipe, "ActionRecipe"}`); every stage reads `defs["recipe"]` (`recipes.ex:20`, `spells.ex:28,81`, `construction.ex:43`, `replenish.ex:58`, `trails.ex:95`, `derived.ex:53`, `skills.ex:192`, `scenes.ex:173`, `checks.ex:240`, `cues.ex:15`, `position.ex:108,140`, `recipe_tips.ex:18`) | All rewritten | One seam: `compiler.ex:239 kinds/1` routes `:action` files into `"action"` or `"recipe"` by shape; `defs["recipe"]` stays |
| Lint by path prefix | `lint.ex:52,136,195` match `["recipes", _]`; `lint_pages.ex:25` matches `"recipes/" <> name`; `test/loka/lint_baseline.txt` has 31 `recipes/` lines | Changed | Changed (prefix to `actions`); baseline regenerated |
| ActionSet identity | `cartridge.md:261`; `recipes.ex:84 duplicate/3` (`r["key"] in ctx.actions`) | Same | One directory makes an action/recipe key clash impossible by file name; via an area bundle it is already `Bundles.unique` (`bundles.ex:45`) `DUPLICATE_DEFINITION`. The `recipes.ex:84` check stays for command and reserved keys |
| Tests and Book tests with source paths | 155 `"recipes/` strings in `test/loka/*` (biggest: `content_lint_test` 18, `content_spells_test` 16, `content_recipes_test` 16, `content_dusk_test` 16); `mobile/app/book/cast_pick.test.ts:29-33`, `cast_death.test.ts:29` edit `recipes/flamma.json` | Changed | Changed, mechanically (`recipes/` → `actions/` in paths) |
| Docs and the Book | `cartridge.md:17` layout table, `:297`, `:2117`, `:2119`; `BUILDERS-GUIDE.md:98`; `MECHANICS-TOOLBOX.md:109`; mechanics.md keeps "recipe" as the engine name for the authored-outcomes shape (136 mentions) | Rewritten | Author-facing lines only |
| Brief D (`.17`) source schema | "one schema per `@dirs` directory" | Needs the merged kind either way | `actions.schema.json` becomes `anyOf` of the two source shapes, discriminated on `command` |

### Recommendation: authoring-only

The split is an engine fact (two record types with different `target` and `label` types,
different admission, different projection) and an artifact fact (two maps, two ref kinds, hashes,
E1 pointers). Merging it at the contract level touches 38 kernel files, protocol, `contracts.gen.ts`,
every recipe-bearing hash fixture and the E1 obligations for no player-visible gain; it is an L+
slice with a second-opinion review. Merging it at the source level gives authors exactly what the
owner asked for, one directory and one concept, with the lowering already how every source
shortcut works (`cartridge.md:352` "the compiler rewrites the source before any other stage reads
it"; the artifact never carries a bundle, `extends` or prose). The one new rule is: an
`actions/<key>.json` with `command` is a built-in action (ActionDefinition), without it an
authored-outcomes action (ActionRecipe). Mixed fields are refused for free: both contracts are
`additionalProperties: false`, so `outcomes` beside `command` is `UNKNOWN_FIELD` at
`actions/<key>.outcomes` (`source.ex:234`), and a file with neither is `SCHEMA_VIOLATION`
`missing_property` at `actions/<key>.outcomes` (`contracts.ex:169 child(path, k)`).

Residue the owner accepts with this shape (decide): the artifact and its diagnostics still say
`recipe` where a ref kind shows, for example `UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE` `data.target`
`"x@0.0.1:recipe/nap"` and `kernel/ts` names. Authors never write that string (short refs are keys,
`cartridge.md:21`). Renaming the artifact kind is the contract merge above and is out.

Second-opinion review: not needed. No save, protocol-schema or kernel change; the only `protocol/`
diff is 31 source-path strings in `fixtures/loader_floors.json`. Ordinary fresh reviewer, PR
comments, no review record (PM step 4).

Size: M, one brief. About 15 lines of compiler code; the rest is a `git mv` of 117 files and a
path substitution across tests, fixtures, lint and docs. Not L, so no split.

## Part 2: Brief C2, merge recipes into actions (loka-kgd.194.22)

**Lane, branch and model.**
- Draft PR, batched pushes, on `toolbox/authoring-batch-a` (PR #480), after Brief C (.18, in
  progress in that worktree; it touches `extends.ex`, `behaviours.ex` and
  `cartridges/toolbox_showcase/reactions/wheel_*`; none of those is in this slice's engine diff, but
  the `git mv` below touches `toolbox_showcase/recipes/` so start from C's head, not from main).
  Brief D (.17) follows and must cover the merged kind.
- Opus developer. Handoff threshold: about 220k tokens
  ([token hygiene](../WORKFLOW.md#token-hygiene)); the bulk is a mechanical rename, so
  hand off before the docs if the rename plus tests cross it.
- Read the [brief kit](../guides/brief-kit.md) once. Lessons: `docs/lessons/contracts.md` (a
  fixture change needs the test that fails without it), `docs/lessons/checks.md` (the lint
  baseline is a generated file; regenerate it, never hand-edit).
- Owner decision 2026-10-28 in Beads loka-kgd.194.22 (quoted there): one kind, mix refused.
  PM design ruling (Part 1 above): authoring-only; no protocol, kernel or artifact change.

**Goal.** An author writes every player action as `actions/<key>.json`: with `command` it binds a
built-in command; with `outcomes` it carries authored behaviour. `recipes/` is gone. The compiled
artifact, every hash fixture and every transcript are byte-identical.

**Spec.** Edit `docs/system/cartridge.md`:
- Source layout table (`:17`): drop `recipes/` from the directory list; add one row:
  `actions/<key>.json`: with `command`, an ActionDefinition; without it, an ActionRecipe (an
  action whose `outcomes` the author writes; `action_recipe@1`, [mechanics](mechanics.md#action_recipe1-mechanicsaction_reciperulets)).
  The compiler routes the file by that one field before any other stage reads it; the artifact keeps
  its `actions` and `recipes` maps and ref kinds unchanged.
- Source shortcuts (`:352`): one paragraph "Actions with outcomes" stating the routing rule and the
  refusals table below.
- `:297`, `:2117`, `:2119`: `recipes/<key>` → `actions/<key>` in the cited paths.
- `docs/BUILDERS-GUIDE.md:98`: the "A player action" row names `actions/<key>.json` and links
  `cartridges/recipe_sampler/actions/ring_bell.json`. `docs/MECHANICS-TOOLBOX.md:109` path.
- Do not rewrite mechanics.md: "recipe" stays the engine's name for the authored-outcomes shape.

**Where the truth is (`ast-grep outline` does not cover Elixir; signatures by grep).**
- `lib/loka/content/source.ex`: `@dirs` `:135-158` (`"actions" => :action`, `"recipes" => :recipe`),
  the kind type `:25`, `load/1` `:49`, `of_kind/2` `:171` (`{key, location, value}` per file of a
  kind), `schema/4` `:230` (unknown_property → `UNKNOWN_FIELD`, else `SCHEMA_VIOLATION` with
  `data.error`).
- `lib/loka/content/compiler.ex`: `@kinds` `:196-220`; `kinds/1` `:238-243`; `files/3` `:260`
  (`collect(for {k, r, v} <- of_kind(files, kind), do: {k, definition(r, [], k, v, contract)})`);
  `definition/5` `:325` (adds `key` from the file stem; an authored `key` is `UNKNOWN_FIELD`).
- `Loka.Core.Contracts.validate/3` `lib/loka/core/contracts.ex:66`; `required` `:168-170` reports
  `missing_property` at the missing member's path.
- Lint path matches: `lib/loka/content/lint.ex:52,136,195`; `lib/loka/content/lint_pages.ex:25`.
- Test helpers: `Loka.ContentSource.copy/1` and `compile/2` (`test/test_helper.exs:9,24`).

**Design.**
1. **One directory.** `source.ex @dirs`: delete `"recipes" => :recipe`; delete `:recipe` from the
   kind type. A `recipes/` directory is then `UNKNOWN_FIELD` at `recipes/<file>.json` like any
   unrecognised path (`source.ex:87`), with no new code.
2. **Route by `command`.** In `compiler.ex kinds/1`, the `:action` files split once:
   `{"action", …, "ActionDefinition"}` validates those with `"command"`, `{"recipe", …,
   "ActionRecipe"}` those without. Smallest form: give `files/3` an optional filter, or partition
   `of_kind(files, :action)` once in `kinds/1` and feed each half to `collect/1` with its contract.
   `defs["recipe"]` keeps its name so no downstream stage changes. Diagnostics keep the file's
   real path, `actions/<key>…`.
3. **No new refusal code.** A mixed file is refused by the contract it is routed to (table below).
4. **Rename.** `git mv cartridges/*/recipes/*.json` to `actions/` (117 files, 50 cartridges;
   `craft`, `durability`, `farm`, `harvest`, `kitchen` and `toolbox_showcase` already have an
   `actions/` directory and no key clashes, check with `comm` before moving). Then `recipes/` →
   `actions/` in: `test/loka/*.exs` (155 strings, path and copy sites), `protocol/fixtures/loader_floors.json`
   (31 edit rows; nothing else under `protocol/`), `mobile/app/book/cast_pick.test.ts:29-33` and
   `cast_death.test.ts:29`, `lint.ex` (3 heads), `lint_pages.ex:25`, and regenerate
   `test/loka/lint_baseline.txt`.
5. **`content_recipes_test.exs:146-147`.** The action-vs-recipe key clash can no longer be two
   files. Replace it with the bundle form: `areas/x.json` `{"actions": {"ring_bell": <action>}}`
   beside `actions/ring_bell.json` is `DUPLICATE_DEFINITION` at both sites (`bundles.ex:45`). Keep
   `:149-155` (a recipe keyed as a command, `look`).
6. Brief C's `extends` is unaffected: a parent and child of kind `:action` merge by key before
   routing; a child that inherits `outcomes` and adds `command` is refused by row 1.

**Refusals (put this table in cartridge.md).**

| Case | Code | Path | data |
|---|---|---|---|
| `command` and `outcomes` (or any ActionRecipe-only field: `check`, `costs`, `cooldown`, `duration`, `craft`, `aliases`, `tip`, `reason`) in one file | `UNKNOWN_FIELD` | `actions/<key>.<field>` (one per field) | `{}` |
| neither `command` nor `outcomes` | `SCHEMA_VIOLATION` | `actions/<key>.outcomes` | `{"error": "missing_property"}` |
| a `recipes/` directory | `UNKNOWN_FIELD` | `recipes/<file>.json` | `{}` (unchanged `source.ex:87`) |

**Acceptance.**
1. **Gate, byte-identical.** `test/loka/content_showcase_test.exs:161-164` passes unchanged against
   `protocol/fixtures/toolbox_showcase_hash.json`; `kernel/ts/test/transcripts.test.ts:23` replays
   every `cartridges/*/transcripts/*.jsonl` (recipe-bearing: bleed 1, check 1, ferry 2, gate 2,
   recipe 1, resource 1, scene 1, showcase 7); `git diff --stat protocol/` lists only
   `fixtures/loader_floors.json`; no `*_hash.json` moves. Engine seam: `compiler.ex:239`.
2. **Routing.** On a copy of `recipe_sampler` (`ContentSource.copy`): `actions/ring_bell.json`
   with `"command": "look"` added to the recipe (fields on main: `aliases, label, outcomes,
   policy, priority, target`) is routed to ActionDefinition and compiles to exactly, in path order
   (`cartridge.md:206`):
   `[d("SCHEMA_VIOLATION", "actions/ring_bell.accessibility", %{"error" => "missing_property"}),
   d("UNKNOWN_FIELD", "actions/ring_bell.aliases"),
   d("SCHEMA_VIOLATION", "actions/ring_bell.input", %{"error" => "missing_property"}),
   d("UNKNOWN_FIELD", "actions/ring_bell.outcomes")]`. Seam: `source.ex:234`,
   `action.schema.json:373` (`required` 8 fields, `additionalProperties: false`).
3. **Neither.** The same file with `command` and `outcomes` both removed and no other
   recipe-only field: exactly `[d("SCHEMA_VIOLATION", "actions/ring_bell.outcomes", %{"error" =>
   "missing_property"})]`. Seam: `contracts.ex:169`.
4. **Old directory.** `recipes/ring_bell.json` present again (copy of the moved file): exactly
   `[d("UNKNOWN_FIELD", "recipes/ring_bell.json")]` beside the compile's other result, i.e. the
   build fails. Seam: `source.ex:87`.
5. **Bundle clash.** Design 5's `DUPLICATE_DEFINITION` at both sites, exact list.
6. **Both kernels' floors.** `kernel/ts/test/loader_floors.test.ts` and
   `test/loka/loader_floors_test.exs` green on the edited fixture; `mobile/app/book/cast_pick.test.ts`
   and `cast_death.test.ts` green.
7. **Lint.** `mix loka.lint cartridges/toolbox_showcase` output equals the regenerated baseline;
   the 31 renamed lines read `actions/<key>.json: …`; `lint_pages` still lists a detail's aimed
   actions (an existing `content_lint_test` row covers it after the path edit; name which).
8. **Red controls.** (a) Route by `outcomes` instead of `command`: row 2's expected path changes
   to `actions/ring_bell.command`, so row 2 fails. (b) Keep `"recipes" => :recipe` in `@dirs`:
   row 4 passes the build, so it fails. (c) Revert `lint_pages.ex:25` to `"recipes/"`: row 7's
   page lines vanish, so it fails. Paste each failing line in the check table.
9. Grep for tests that read `recipes/` source files directly (TS, Elixir, mobile) and keep them
   green; `kernel/ts/test/e1.test.ts:34` and `e1_obligations.ts:288` are artifact pointers and
   stay `/recipes/…:recipe/…`.

**Out of scope.**
- The artifact's `recipes` map, `recipe` ref kind, `action_recipe@1`, any `kernel/ts/src` file,
  `contracts.gen.ts`, any `protocol/*.schema.json` (the DUPLICATE_DEFINITION description there
  stays true through bundles).
- Renaming "recipe" in mechanics.md, the Book or the kernel.
- Brief D's schema; hand back that `actions/` is `anyOf` two source shapes keyed on `command`.

**Scope trigger: stop and ask** if gate 1's hash or any transcript moves; if any file under
`protocol/` other than `fixtures/loader_floors.json` needs a change; if a cartridge has both
`actions/<k>.json` and `recipes/<k>.json` (none found on main, recheck on C's head); if a
downstream stage needs the source kind rather than `defs["recipe"]`.

**Realm.** n/a: compile-time only; the artifact is byte-identical.

**Handback adds.** Files moved (count per cartridge), the three red-control lines, the exact
`content_lint_test` row for acceptance 7, and the one-line note for Brief D.

title: Authoring tools for hand-written content: keep my place, checkpoints, author column, scene files, placeholder check
description:
Owner 2026-10-31, quoted: "i want to handwrite everythign"; accepted the PM recommendation ("okay i will go with yoru recommendation") and asked for a Fable agent to brief and implement it "so we can just start authoring right away".
Build, in order: keep my place (replay inputs after each recompile, name the failed step); named checkpoints; author column in the web author preview only; prose-first scene files for dialogue and quest text, compiled to today's JSON; "still to write" list by beat. AI may create structure with empty text; every word the player reads is the owner's. Agents never write prologue prose; a release check refuses leftover placeholders. No form editors; loka-kgd.194.8 stays parked.
notes:
kernel_api: none expected. Fable developer, weekly 83% at spawn (owner asked). Independent reviewer after.
Owner 2026-10-31, quoted: 'Use Fable for the builder with live preview, as if I were building the game live, or super hyper fast recompiles without any checks as i build it, to make building loop extremely fast.' Scope added: fast unchecked dev recompile, live builder feel. Release checks unchanged.
PLAN 2026-10-31 (branch tools/authoring, one draft PR, one push per slice). Order per owner addition: 1 keep my place, 2 fast loop, 3 checkpoints, 4 author column, 5 still-to-write, 6 scene files.
Spec commit first: docs/decisions/owner-decision-handwritten-prose-2026-10-31.md (+README line, owner-rules line), amend docs/system/cartridge.md (Author preview section) and docs/BUILDERS-GUIDE.md (Preview an edit), add docs/guides/writing-the-game.md.
Design: bin/loka dev --watch (kernel/ts/play/author.ts) gains a local node:http API (LOKA_AUTHOR_PORT, default 19008) that mobile/app/preview-server.cjs proxies at /__author/ (same origin, COEP kept). mobile/app/author/ holds the dev-only client: it wraps the game passed to Book (text overlay, invoke recorder); App.tsx mounts it only when EXPO_PUBLIC_LOKA_DEV_CARTRIDGE=1 and __DEV__ (metro.config.js keeps release/test/e2e pinned; metro.test.ts covers the production throw).
S1 keep my place: record each saved invoke (targets as cartridge refs via a read-only entityIds accessor on the session) and each DevClock advance to localStorage with the artifact hash; after a reload into a new hash, replay through game.invoke/pulse; first non-saved reply names the step and stops. No state cheat; normal commands only.
S2 fast loop: measured baseline mix boot 0.45 s warm, mix loka.compile cellar 0.54 s, showcase 0.79 s; save-to-visible in the browser measured before/after in the PR. Fast path: a text.json-only edit is parsed by author.ts and pushed over SSE as a text overlay; the Book redraws in place with no recompile, reload or replay; the full compile still runs in the background and its diagnostics go to the column; structural edits take the compile+reload+replay path. No persistent compiler: boot is not the cost. Artifacts are only ever full compiles; the overlay lives in the page.
S3 checkpoints: PUT/GET /__author/checkpoints -> <cartridge>/checkpoints/<name>.json (the recorded path), listed and jumped to from the column.
S4 column: third column at ?dev=1 only; diagnostics in plain words, facts/quests/flags from the view, why via kernel/ts/play/why.ts on the recorded path, click line -> POST /__author/open (LOKA_EDITOR, default code --goto), DevClock, checkpoints.

description: Approach E of docs/rnd/design-audit-abilities-authoring-2026-10-23.md: replay a transcript to a step and report per rule whether its trigger matched (which filter failed) and each when-leaf value. No contract change.
notes:
BRIEF (PM-adopted 2026-10-23; after 194.2 merges):
# Brief loka-kgd.194.3: `why.ts`, rule explainer by replay

Read once, then follow: [brief kit](docs/briefs/brief-kit.md) (common rules, handback, Realm
checklist); `AGENTS.md` Simplicity, Writing tests ("Real over mocks": production modules carry
no test-only functions); `.claude/agents/developer.md`; [WORKFLOW step 3](docs/WORKFLOW.md#loop).
Lessons: `docs/lessons/checks.md`, `docs/lessons/mechanics.md` (queries share one command's
budget), `docs/lessons/contracts.md` (kit rule; no schema here). Plan and rationale:
`docs/rnd/design-audit-abilities-authoring-2026-10-23.md` on branch
`docs/abilities-authoring-2026-10-23` (read with `git show`), finding 22, approach E, plan phase
4. Owner approval: Beads epic `loka-kgd.194` (owner order 2026-10-23: phase 0, then 4, then 3).
Spec clause explained: [reaction@1](docs/system/mechanics.md#reaction1-kerneltssrcmechanicsreactionts)
(`docs/system/mechanics.md:599-605`). It says triggers and filters run in rule-key order, and
each rule's `when` reads the writes of the rules and deliveries before it in the same command.

**Handoff threshold 220k tokens.** No subagents.

## Goal

`node kernel/ts/play/why.ts <artifact> <transcript.jsonl> <ordinal> [--recipe <key> | --dialogue <key>]`
replays a transcript up to step `<ordinal>` and decides that step. For each reaction rule it
then reports:

- whether its trigger matched, and which filter failed, for each committed event of that step;
- how many deliveries ran its steps;
- each `when` leaf's value at the kernel's own evaluation point.

On demand it reports the same for one recipe's or one dialogue's `policy`. It is a report for
authors. Nothing is committed and nothing is checked in CI except its unit test.

## Lane, size, order

Hosted PR, alone. Branch `toolbox/kgd194-why` from `main` **after `loka-kgd.194.2` (coverage.ts)
merges**. It imports that tool's `replay` and `marked`. Size **M**. Contract: none (protocol,
save, kernel_api unchanged; no file under `kernel/ts/src/` changes).

## Kernel export finding (settled; no kernel change)

`holds` (`kernel/ts/src/mechanics/policy.ts:53`) evaluates any Policy node, so it needs no hook.
The hard part is where a reaction's `when` is read. `sequence` reads it on the mid-proposal
world `now(p)` (`runtime/proposal.ts:224`), with the clock at the cause's time
(`reaction.ts:150`). The actor and subject come from the private `deliveryActor` and `subject`
(`reaction.ts:152`, `:266-272`, `:400-410`). Exporting those (lifting `reaction.ts:146-152` into
an exported function) would be a kernel source change, and it would still not give a tool
`now(p)`. So do not export anything. Use these instead:

- **Trigger, exact.** Use the exported `FILTERS` (`reaction.ts:61`) on the world **before** the
  step, as `triggered` does (`reaction.ts:101-106`). The proposal matches against `p.world`,
  the step's input world (`proposal.ts:223`; `proposal_adopt.ts:25` passes it). For each
  committed event of the step whose `payload.type === rule.on.event`, report every declared
  filter (each key of `rule.on` except `event`) as `FILTERS[f](before, want, e.payload, e)`.
- **Fired, exact.** Use `marked` from `coverage.ts`: the rule's marker lines in the step's
  decision narration.
- **Leaf values, exact at the first delivery.** For leaf `i` of rule `R`, decide the step again
  from the same before-world, on a shallow copy of the before-`Run` (`{...r, world: {...r.world,
  cartridge: copy}}`), because `decideReplay` changes the Run it is given (`play/run.ts:95-96`,
  and `r.revision` in `outcome`). Otherwise the second probe starts from the first probe's
  after-world. The copy replaces `world.cartridge`. In the copy, `R` is
  `{key, on}` of `R`, `when: {policy_version: 1, root: leaf_i}` and
  `apply: [{op: 'narrate', text: <probe key>}]`, with no `after`. The probe keeps `R`'s map key,
  so it runs at `R`'s place in rule-key order. Everything before `R`'s first delivery is
  unchanged, so the kernel's own `sequence` evaluates the leaf at `reaction.ts:152`, with its
  own world, actor and subject. The probe's marker count is the number of deliveries where the
  leaf held. A spike on `main` confirmed this works (results under Acceptance).
- **Recipe and dialogue policies, exact.** Admission reads them on the step's input world, so
  call `holds` per leaf on the before-world:
  - recipe at `commands/actions.ts:263-265`, target the step's `primaryTarget(payload)`
    (`commands/action_input.ts:128`);
  - dialogue at `mechanics/dialogue/selection.ts:93` and `mechanics/dialogue/shared.ts:94`,
    target `world.entityIds[refString(d.npc)]`.

  Use a fresh `{steps: {n: 0}}` for each call.

If any of this fails in practice (for example a cache keyed on `world.cartridge` that the swap
misses), **stop and ask** before touching `kernel/ts/src/`. Any export there would be a kernel
source change. It would need no protocol, save or kernel_api change, but it still needs a PM
ruling.

## Design

- `kernel/ts/play/why.ts`, in the `friction.ts` / `reach.ts` pattern. Export
  `why(c: Cartridge, trace: ReturnType<typeof replayRecords>, ordinal: number, on?: {recipe?: string; dialogue?: string})`.
  - It replays ordinals `1..ordinal-1` with `replay(marked(c).cartridge, trace, …, ordinal)`.
    That compares those lines to the recording and throws `replay differs at ordinal <n>`.
  - Step `ordinal` itself is decided, not compared, so an edited rule can be explained.
- Output (one canonical JSON document):

  ```
  {ordinal, command: <payload.type>, outcome: <decision outcome or kind>,
   reactions: [{rule: <DefinitionRefString>,
                causes: [{event: <type>, position: <n>, filters: {<name>: bool}}],
                fired: <n>,
                when?: <tree>}],
   recipe?: {rule, policy: <tree>},
   dialogue?: {rule, policy: <tree>}}
  ```

  - `reactions` covers every rule in `cartridge.reactions`, in rule-key order.
  - A rule whose event type is absent from the step has `causes: []`.
  - In `when`, each leaf object gets `held: <deliveries where it held>`; `all`/`any`/`not`
    nodes keep their `op` and children.
  - In `policy`, each leaf gets `holds: <bool>`.
  - Leaves are evaluated one by one, even where `all`/`any` would short-circuit.
- CLI: it loads and refuses as `reach.ts` does (`play/reach.ts:120-132`, exit 1). It reads the
  trace with its own pinned hash (`replayRecords(path, pin)`, `play/replay.ts:6`), so an
  author's recompiled artifact still runs. A replay that differs exits 1, with the transcript named
  repo-relative (never an absolute path). These exit 2: a bad
  ordinal (not an integer in 1..entries), an unknown `--recipe`/`--dialogue` key, both flags
  together, or wrong arguments.
- ponytail limits (one docs line): a leaf's "value" is its truth value (the `held` count, or
  `holds` on demand), not the fact or stat value it read, because that read value at the
  mid-proposal point is out of reach without a kernel hook. For a rule delivered more than once in a step, only the
  first delivery is exact. Later ones run after the probe has removed `R`'s steps. A delayed
  rule's `fired` shows at its job's step, and a job run's narration can be deduplicated
  (`proposal.ts:276`). The recipe target is the payload's primary target, not a detail resolved
  through `detailAt`.
- Size rules: files 300 lines, functions 40. No new `size: allow`.

Signatures you call (`ast-grep outline`):
```
kernel/ts/src/mechanics/reaction.ts  61: export const FILTERS: Record<string, Match>
                                    101: export function triggered(world: World, e: DomainEvent): ReactionRule[]
kernel/ts/src/mechanics/policy.ts    53: export function holds(world, actor, p: Policy, ctx = { steps: { n: 0 } }): boolean
kernel/ts/src/commands/action_input.ts 128: export function primaryTarget(payload: CommandPayload): EntityId | undefined
kernel/ts/play/coverage.ts           (loka-kgd.194.2) marked(c), replay(c, trace, each?, upTo?)
kernel/ts/play/run.ts                26: start   69: decideReplay(r: Run, command: Command)
kernel/ts/play/replay.ts              6: replayRecords(path, content_hash)
```

## Spec first (same PR, first commit)

Add `### Rule explainer (loka-kgd.194.3)` to `docs/system/cartridge.md`, under
[Content reports](docs/system/cartridge.md#content-reports), after "Transcript coverage". Write
the command, the exit codes, the output and the evaluation points above. Link the reaction@1
clause. Add the ponytail line.

## Files

In scope: `kernel/ts/play/why.ts` (new), `kernel/ts/test/why.test.ts` (new),
`docs/system/cartridge.md` (one subsection).
Out of scope: `kernel/ts/src/**` (stop-and-ask above), `protocol/`, `lib/`, `cartridges/` (no
on-disk sampler or transcript change, so sampler-hash and floors are n/a), `mobile/`. In
`kernel/ts/play/coverage.ts`, change nothing beyond exporting a helper it already has.

## Acceptance (literal expected values; independent sources)

Fixture: `protocol/fixtures/cartridge_scene_hash.json` (manifest `scene_sampler`) with
`cartridges/scene_sampler/transcripts/scene.jsonl`. Its one rule is
`scene_sampler@0.0.1:reaction/bell_after`:

- `on: fact_changed` with filter `fact: scene_bell_rung`;
- `when: fact_compare scene_bell_rung equals -1`;
- `apply: fact.assign bell_heard true`.

Edit in-test by copying the canonical, re-hashing and loading (`kernel/ts/test/ferry_probe.ts:30-47`).
Never write a rule to disk.

The answers come from these sources, not from the tool:

- The recorded committed events in `scene.jsonl`:
  - `quest_activated lantern` at 1;
  - `item_acquired` (the lantern) at 2;
  - `choice_opened` at 3;
  - `quest_resolved lantern` at 4;
  - `fact_changed scene_bell_rung` at 4, 5, 6 and 7;
  - `fact_changed bell_heard` at 7 only.
- Scene fact values: line `k` shown is `k`, ended is `-1` (`docs/system/mechanics.md:556`).
  `bell_rung` has 3 lines (`cartridges/scene_sampler/scenes/bell_rung.json`), so the value is
  1, 2, 3 after ordinals 4, 5, 6 and -1 after 7.
- Rule-key order and "reads the writes before it" (`mechanics.md:599-605`).

| # | Input | Expected for the named rule | Break it catches | Engine line |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| W1 | unedited, ordinal 7 | `bell_after`: `causes` = the two `fact_changed` events, `filters {fact: true}` for scene_bell_rung and `{fact: false}` for bell_heard; `fired: 1`; leaf `fact_compare … -1` `held: 1` | **pre-step evaluator** (reads 3 before step 7: `held 0`); filter run on the wrong field | `reaction.ts:61-106`, `:152`; `proposal.ts:223-224` |

| W8 | CLI on a scratch artifact of the unedited canonical, `scene.jsonl 7` | exit 0. stdout parses to W1's `bell_after` row. Ordinal `0` or `8`: exit 2. `--recipe nope`: exit 2 | CLI wiring | `play/reach.ts:120-132` |

A spike on `main` reproduced W3 `[1, 0]`, W4 `0` and `1`, W5 `false`/`true`, W6 `false`/`true`

## Red controls and mutation cases (paste each failing line in the check table)

1. Leaves evaluated with `holds` on the before-world. W1 fails.
2. Leaves evaluated on the world after the step. W4 fails.
3. Probe added as an extra rule keyed after every rule (for example `'~' + R.key`) instead of

4. `fired` from the trigger match. W2 fails.
5. Prefix comparison removed, or step N compared. W7 or W3 fails.
6. A filter reported from the after-world or the wrong payload field. W1 fails.
7. Probe keeps `after`. This is not reachable on the scene fixture. Say so in the check table;

`bin/mutate.sh` narrow (test files importing `play/why.ts`). Focused run:

BRIEF A (PM-adopted):
# Brief loka-kgd.194.4: compile-time `extends` for source definitions

Developer brief (Opus). Common rules: [brief kit](docs/briefs/brief-kit.md) (read once, not copied
here). Process: `AGENTS.md` Simplicity and Writing tests, `.claude/agents/developer.md`,
[WORKFLOW step 3](docs/WORKFLOW.md#loop). Elixir rules: `docs/ELIXIR-CONVENTIONS.md` (`@spec` on every
public function; `mix format` and `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` before each commit). Handoff
threshold: **220k tokens**; at the threshold stop, commit what is green and hand back.

## Goal

A source definition may name a parent with `"extends": "<key>"` and inherit its fields. The Elixir
compiler flattens the source before anything else reads it, so the artifact never carries `extends`
or `abstract`, the TypeScript loader is untouched, and an existing sampler rewritten with `extends`
compiles to the same bytes as before.

Governing records: [owner decision](docs/decisions/owner-decision-authoring-builder-2026-10-23.md)
effect 2; [design audit](docs/rnd/design-audit-abilities-authoring-2026-10-23.md) findings 18, 19 and 21,
approach C, approach D, phase 3 row. The merge rule is the owner-accepted default (audit §5, question 5).

## Lane and branch

Hosted PR, branch `toolbox/kgd194-extends`, worktree `../worktrees.noindex/kgd194-extends`. Push with
`bin/push_slice.sh`. This is the first of four sequential slices; see the run order below.

## Run order and file overlap

Run them one after another: **A (this brief) → B1 bundles → B2 inline prose → C signal and zone**
(`brief-kgd194-5.md`, `brief-kgd194-6.md`). Each slice starts from `main` after the previous one merges.
Why they cannot run in parallel:
- All four add a stage to the one pipeline call at the end of `Loka.Content.Source.load/1`
  (`lib/loka/content/source.ex:58`).
- All four amend the same docs: `docs/system/cartridge.md` Source layout (:3) and the new
  "Source shortcuts" subsection this slice adds, and `docs/BUILDERS-GUIDE.md` Authoring paths (:90).
- B1 changes the classified-kind tuple that this slice's module matches on.

This slice creates the pipeline. The later slices insert their stages in this fixed order:
`Bundles.split → Extends.flatten → Prose.lower → Signals.lower → Zones.expand → (B1's duplicate check)`.

## Facts verified for this brief (cite them; do not re-derive)

- The compiler reads the source directory in exactly one place: `Loka.Content.Source.load/1`,
  defined at `lib/loka/content/source.ex:49`. It returns `{files, diagnostics}` at `:58`. (The audit
  cited :52, which is the glob-escape line.) Its three callers:
  - `Loka.Content.compile/2` (`lib/loka/content.ex:40`)
  - `Loka.Content.Lint` `decoded/1` (`lib/loka/content/lint.ex:22-30`)
  - `test/loka/content_lint_test.exs:273`

  A pass at `:58` therefore gives `mix loka.compile` and `mix loka.lint` the same flattened view.
- The TypeScript loader reads only artifact bytes: `loadCartridge`, `kernel/ts/src/content/cartridge.ts:60`.
  The author preview shells out to the compiler: `kernel/ts/play/author.ts:55`. `reach.ts:126` and
  `ledger.ts:219` load artifacts too. So no TS change is needed.
- Each entry is `{rel, {kind, key}, value}`, where `key` is the file stem (`classify/1`, `source.ex:135-140`).
  A value that failed to decode is `:invalid` (`:68`, `:75`). The compiler keys definitions by that
  stem (`lib/loka/content/compiler.ex:260-261`).
- `lib/loka/content/compiler.ex` is at its size cap (`# size: allow 360`, line 1; it has 360 lines).
  `docs/CHECKS.md` (Size) says a file at its cap splits and never grows. **Add zero lines to
  compiler.ex.** `source.ex` has 263 of 300 lines, so add only the call there and put the pass in a
  new module.
- `DiagnosticCode` is a closed enum (`protocol/cartridge.schema.json`, DiagnosticCode). This slice
  reuses existing codes and adds none (see Contract impact).

## Rules (decided; implement exactly)

1. **Value.** `extends` is a Key string: the key of a definition **of the child's own kind**. This is
   the short-reference convention. It resolves against the loaded entries, so a parent in any file
   of that kind works, including a B1 bundle later.
2. **Single parent, any depth.** Resolve recursively and stop on a cycle.
3. **Merge.** Objects merge key by key, recursively. Everything else (scalars, lists, `null`)
   replaces. There is no append operator and no way to delete an inherited key.
   - Write the delete limit as a `ponytail:` comment on the merge.
   - Corollary for authors: a child cannot shrink an inherited map. In shoo_sampler the deer `sight.narration`
     maps differ by compass direction, so the prototype must not carry them (see Acceptance).
4. **Never inherited.** A child never inherits `extends` or `abstract`. Strip both from every output
   value.
5. **Abstract.** An entry whose value has `"abstract": true` is removed from the files list after its
   children resolve.
   - It is never validated, so placement requirements such as an NPC's required `room`
     (`protocol/entity.schema.json` NpcDefinition.required) do not apply to it.
   - A reference to it elsewhere is an ordinary UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE from the existing checks.
   - `abstract` with any value other than `true` is left in place, and the schema reports UNKNOWN_FIELD.
6. **Kinds.** Every per-definition directory kind in `@dirs` (`source.ex:109-133`). The merge does not
   depend on the kind, so policies, populations, population bundles and the rest come at no extra cost.
   - Root files are not flattened: `cartridge.json`, `facts.json`, `text.json`, `resources.json`,
     `attributes.json` and `map_positions.json`.
   - An `extends` in any root file except `text.json` reaches its schema and is UNKNOWN_FIELD. For
     example, `cartridge.json` gives `cartridge.extends`.
   - In `text.json`, `extends` is a legal TextKey, so it stays a plain catalog entry. Document that.
7. **Invalid parent.** If the parent's value is `:invalid`, the child becomes `:invalid` and gets no
   second diagnostic. The parent's own diagnostic already fails the build; this is the same rule as
   `collect/1` (`compiler.ex:263-271`).
   A definition whose parent chain reaches a cycle without being in it (oak_deer → wild, when wild
   and crow form a cycle) also becomes `:invalid`, with no diagnostic of its own.
8. **Refusals.** Each uses an existing code. `<src>` is `Source.at(rel, [])`. Build every one with
   `Source.diag/3`.

   | Case | Code | Path | data |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | No definition of the child's kind has that key | UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE | `<child src>.extends` | `{"target": "<dir>/<key>"}` |
   | The same key exists only in another kind (the "parent of another kind" case; it cannot resolve, by rule 1) | UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE | `<child src>.extends` | `{"target": "<dir>/<key>", "from": "<that other file's src>"}` |
   | Cycle, including self | SCHEMA_VIOLATION | `<src>.extends` for each member of the cycle | `{"error": "invalid_value", "from": "<its parent's src>"}` |
   | `extends` is not a string | SCHEMA_VIOLATION | `<child src>.extends` | `{"error": "invalid_type"}` |

   The precedent for semantic refusals as `SCHEMA_VIOLATION invalid_value` is
   `lib/loka/content/commerce.ex:67` and `combat.ex:269`. Those causes are documented in
   `cartridge.md`, not in the protocol description.
9. **Provenance scope (decided).** `data.from` goes on the refusals above only. A schema error inside
   an inherited field still reports at the child's path, with no `from`. Audit finding 21's full
   provenance would need the pass to hand a provenance table through `Source.load/1`'s return value to
   a post-pass in `content.ex` `compiled/3` (`:64-69`). That changes the signature and touches three
   callers.
   - Leave a `ponytail:` comment naming this limit.
   - Record it as an open question in the handback.

## Files in scope

- New `lib/loka/content/extends.ex`: `Loka.Content.Extends.flatten({files, diags}) :: {files, diags}`,
  with `@spec`. Keep the moduledoc to one paragraph that links cartridge.md "Source shortcuts".

## B1: area bundles (branch `toolbox/kgd194-bundles`, Hosted PR)

### Goal

A source may hold several definitions of several kinds in one file, `areas/<name>.json`. Its members
are the definition directory names. Diagnostics point into the bundle by path steps. The artifact is
unchanged.

### Rules (decided)

1. **Location and shape.**
   - A bundle lives at `areas/<name>.json`, one directory level only. `areas/x/y.json` stays
     UNKNOWN_FIELD as today (`classify/1`, `source.ex:135-140`).
   - The value is `{"<dir>": {"<key>": <definition without key>}}`, where each `<dir>` is a key of
     `@dirs` (`source.ex:109-133`), for example `rooms`, `npcs`, `dialogues` or `reactions`.
   - No `text` or `facts` member: the root files keep those.
2. **Entry shape.** Every classified entry becomes `{rel, {kind, key, steps}, value}`.
   - A plain file has steps `[]`.
   - A bundle definition has `rel` = the bundle file and steps `[dir, key]`.
   - The compiler takes the steps with a line-neutral edit of `compiler.ex:261`:
     `do: collect(for {rel, {^kind, k, s}, v} <- files, do: {k, definition(rel, s, k, v, contract)})`.
     The drafter ran `Code.format_string!` on it: it stays one line of 98 characters.
   - Existing diagnostics then read `areas/village.dialogues.elder_ward.keyword`, in the path grammar
     of `protocol/cartridge.schema.json` Diagnostic.path. No new path form.
3. **Refusals.** All use existing codes, built with `Source.diag/3` at `Source.at(rel, steps)`.

   | Case | Code | Path | data |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | A member that is not a definition directory | UNKNOWN_FIELD | `areas/<name>.<member>` | `{}` |
   | A member whose value is not an object | SCHEMA_VIOLATION | `areas/<name>.<member>` | `{"error": "invalid_type"}` |
   | Two entries with one `{kind, key}` (plain file and bundle, two bundles, or C's zone copies later) | DUPLICATE_DEFINITION | each site | `{}` |

   - The duplicate check is the **last** pipeline stage (`Bundles.unique/1`), so C's generated copies
     go through it too. It keeps the first entry it meets and reports every site.
   - A bundle that fails to decode contributes no entries; its INVALID_JSON already stands.
4. **Lint view.** `Loka.Content.Lint` `decoded/1` (`lint.ex:22-30`) keys the decoded map by `rel`, and
   `file/3` dispatches on `Path.split(rel)` (`lint.ex:46+`). For an entry with steps `[dir, key]`, use
   the virtual rel `"<dir>/<key>.json"`. A finding about a bundled definition then names its
   definition address (`reactions/elder_hears.json: ...`), not a file path.
   - Document this in Source shortcuts.
   - Add a `ponytail:` comment naming the limit and the upgrade: dispatch on kind and print
     `Source.at/2` paths when a builder needs file-true lint lines.
5. **Lowering order.** Split runs before `Extends.flatten`, so a prototype may live in a bundle.

## B2: inline prose (branch `toolbox/kgd194-prose`, Hosted PR, after B1 merges)

### Goal

A text field may carry its words in place. The compiler lowers each occurrence to a generated text
key and adds the entry to the one text catalog. The artifact equals the hand-keyed original byte for
byte.

### Rules (decided)

1. **Marker.** An object whose only member is `"prose"` with a non-empty string value, for example
   `"short": {"prose": "the elder"}`.
   - It may sit anywhere inside a per-definition value, in a plain file or a bundle.
   - A bare string cannot be the marker: `"lane"` matches TextKey (`^[a-z][a-z0-9_.]*$`,
     `protocol/text.schema.json`).
   - `"prose"` is no property name in any protocol schema (the drafter grepped `protocol/`).
   - Any other `{"prose": ...}` shape is left alone, and the schema reports it at its site.
   - Root files are not lowered.
2. **Key scheme.** `<kind>.<key>.<path>`:
   - `<kind>` is the singular kind name (`Atom.to_string` of the classified kind: `npc`, `room`,
     `dialogue`, `story_point`, ...).
   - `<key>` is the definition key.
   - `<path>` is the steps from the definition root to the marker, joined by `.`, with array indexes
     in decimal.
   - One alias: a step `room_line` is written `room`. The house convention has 550 existing
     `npc.<k>.room` and `item.<k>.room` keys, against 0 for `.room_line`.
   - Literal examples:
     - `areas/village.npcs.elder.short` gives `npc.elder.short`.
     - `...elder.room_line` gives `npc.elder.room`.
     - `dialogues.elder_ward.prompt` gives `dialogue.elder_ward.prompt`.
     - A choice label gives `dialogue.elder_ward.choices.thank.label`. That differs from the
       sampler's hand key `dialogue.elder_ward.thank`, which therefore stays a key.
     - A room variant gives `room.lane.variants.0.description`.
   - A generated key that fails TextKey (a member name outside `[a-z0-9_]`) is reported by the
     existing schema at its site. No new check.

title: Compile-time signal and zone sugar (signal as a generated counter fact, zone rule expanded per tagged room)
description: Approach B, findings 13-14 of docs/rnd/design-audit-abilities-authoring-2026-10-23.md; gate byte-identical artifact. No contract change.
notes:
PM RULINGS 2026-10-23: zones are a source-only room field 'zones' stripped by the compiler (Tag is closed and semantic; supersedes audit finding 14's tag idea); reuse existing Diagnostic codes, no protocol change; B split into B1 bundles (loka-kgd.194.5) and B2 inline prose (new row); data.from provenance on extends refusals only for now; A's gate is byte-identical plus fewer lines (files measured at B1); prose_lint follow-up filed. Run order A -> B1 -> B2 -> C, sequential.
BRIEF C (PM-adopted):
# Brief loka-kgd.194.6: `signal` and zone sugar

Developer brief (Opus). Common rules: [brief kit](docs/briefs/brief-kit.md) (read once, not copied
here); `AGENTS.md` Simplicity and Writing tests; `.claude/agents/developer.md`;
`docs/ELIXIR-CONVENTIONS.md`. Handoff threshold: **220k tokens**.

## Goal

Two compile-time shortcuts for reactions. Each lowers to cartridge JSON that already exists, so there is
no engine change and the artifact is what a hand author would write:
- **Signal.** A reaction can send a named message, and other reactions can listen for it.
- **Zone.** One reaction rule is written once for a set of rooms.

Governing records:
- [owner decision](docs/decisions/owner-decision-authoring-builder-2026-10-23.md), effect 2: `signal`
  and zones as compile-time shortcuts.
- [design audit](docs/rnd/design-audit-abilities-authoring-2026-10-23.md): findings 13, 14 and 20,
  approach B, approach D, the phase 3 row.

## Plan correction (PM: read first)

- **Audit finding 14 and approach B said a zone is the set of rooms carrying a room `tags` value.
  That does not work.** `Tag` is a closed engine vocabulary of 23 values
  (`protocol/entity.schema.json` `$defs.Tag`), and several of them change mechanics:
  - `air`, `chasm` and `water` gate movement;
  - `road` and `marsh` change the fare;
  - `warm`, `cool` and `exposed` feed exposure.

  A tag also needs `tags@1` (`docs/system/cartridge.md` Tag declarations, `:1824`). A story zone such
  as "priory" cannot be a tag without a protocol change, and reusing a mechanical tag would change
  play.
- **Decided here:** zone membership is a source-only room field, `zones`, which the pass strips. It
  never reaches the artifact, so "retag a room, the zone follows" still holds, at compile time.

## Lane, branch, run order

- Hosted PR, branch `toolbox/kgd194-signal-zone`.
- This is the last of **A → B1 → B2 → C** (`brief-kgd194-4.md`, `brief-kgd194-5.md`). Start from `main`
  after B2 merges.
- Shared with the earlier slices:
  - the pipeline call at `lib/loka/content/source.ex:58`;
  - `docs/system/cartridge.md`: Source layout (:3) and Source shortcuts (under Compiler, :196);
  - `docs/BUILDERS-GUIDE.md`: Authoring paths (:90).
- C uses B1's entry shape `{rel, {kind, key, steps}, value}`. It also relies on B1's
  `Bundles.unique/1`, the final stage, for DUPLICATE_DEFINITION on generated keys.
- Stage order: `Bundles.split → Extends.flatten → Prose.lower → Signals.lower → Zones.expand →
  Bundles.unique`.
- Add zero lines to `lib/loka/content/compiler.ex`. It is at its cap (`# size: allow 360`; see
  `docs/CHECKS.md` Size).

## Verified engine facts (cite; do not re-derive)

- **Cascade.** "The resulting events trigger further rules, FIFO, to quiescence, within the deliveries,
  `reaction_depth` and `query_steps` budgets" (`docs/system/mechanics.md:668-669`). The loop is at
  `kernel/ts/src/runtime/proposal.ts:207` and the budgets at `:214` and `:237`.
- **A reaction's `fact.adjust` emits `fact_changed`.** It is lowered to a `fact.assign` at the bounded
  sum (`kernel/ts/src/mechanics/reaction.ts:309-350`, using `bounded` in
  `kernel/ts/src/mechanics/fact.ts:192-217`). `fact_changed` is emitted only for a write that changes
  the value (`fact.ts:254`, the `!same(o.expected, o.value)` filter). The step needs `kernel_api` at
  least 1.47 (row 15, `protocol/reaction.schema.json` fact.adjust).
- **Delivery attribution.** A `fact_changed` delivery runs for `player(cause.scope)`
  (`reaction.ts:406`). For a player-scope fact, that is the character whose fact changed.
- **Rule order.** Reactions run in rule-key order, comparing UTF-8 bytes (`reaction.ts:97` and `:109`;
  `cmp` at `kernel/ts/src/foundation/validate.ts:31`).
- **Room filters.** Only `entity_entered_room`, `rested`, `item_dropped`, `shooed` and `entity_died`
  take an `on.room` filter (`protocol/reaction.schema.json` ReactionRule.on branches). Any other
  branch refuses `room` through the schema.
- The compiler validates every definition key against Key: `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`, at most 64 characters
  (`compiler.ex:330`; `protocol/action.schema.json` Key).
- The compiler drops a reaction's `silent` (`compiler.ex:331`).
- Lint counts `fact.adjust` as a write that needs a narrate step or `silent` (`lint.ex:50-56`).

## Rules: signal (decided)

1. **Sending step.** In a reaction's `apply`, `{"op": "signal", "signal": "<name>"}` lowers to
   `{"op": "fact.adjust", "fact": "signal_<name>", "amount": 1}`, at the same index. Diagnostics the
   lowered step draws (capability, floor) therefore point at the author's step.
2. **Trigger.** `"on": {"event": "signal", "signal": "<name>"}` lowers to
   `{"event": "fact_changed", "fact": "signal_<name>"}`.
3. **Generated fact.** For each signal name used, add this entry to the `facts.json` entry's `facts`,
   creating `{"facts.json", :facts, %{"facts" => %{}}}` if absent:
   ```json
   "signal_<name>": {"version": 1, "value_type": {"type": "int", "minimum": 0, "maximum": 9007199254740991, "default": 0}, "scopes": ["player"], "meaning": "Signal <name> (compiler-generated)."}
   ```
   - The maximum is the largest safe integer the protocol already uses (`docs/system/cartridge.md:646`,
     `protocol/capability.schema.json:22`).
   - Scope is player, so a listener runs for the sending character (Realm item 5).
   - If `facts.json` is `:invalid`, lower nothing into it; its INVALID_JSON stands.
4. **The pass adds nothing to `cartridge.json`.** The author declares the capabilities and the
   `kernel_api` floor (1.47). Missing ones are reported by the existing checks at the signal step's
   path.
5. **Refusals:**

   | Case | Code | Path | data |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | An authored fact named exactly `signal_<name>` | FACT_NAME_COLLISION | `facts.facts.signal_<name>` | `{}` |
   | A listener whose name no sending step uses | UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE | `<rule src>.on.signal` | `{"target": "<name>"}` |

   - The dotted form `signal.<name>` already collides through `collisions/2` (`compiler.ex:302`), with
     no new code, provided the generated name is added beside the authored names.
   - A name that makes an invalid Key reports at its fact through the existing Key check.
6. **Limits (document them; add `ponytail:` comments).**
   - After 9007199254740991 sends, the counter is full: the adjust writes nothing new, and the
     listeners stay silent (`fact.ts:254`).
   - Each send writes the player's fact row, an existing row kind.
   - A rule that only sends is still a write for lint, so its author adds `"silent": true`, which the
     compiler drops.
   - Senders are reaction steps only. Recipes keep `event.emit` / `custom_event`; dialogues keep
     `fact.adjust`.

## Rules: zone (decided)

7. **Membership.** A room's source may carry `"zones": ["<Key>", ...]`.
   - The zone stage removes `zones` from every room, so it never reaches the artifact.
   - A non-list value, or any entry that is not a Key string, is SCHEMA_VIOLATION
     `{"error": "invalid_type"}` at `rooms/<k>.zones`.
8. **Zone rule.** A reaction with `"zone": "<Key>"` and no `on.room` is replaced by one copy per room
   listing that zone, in room-key order. Each copy has:
   - `on.room` set to that room;
   - no `zone`;
   - key `<rule>_<room>`;
   - the authored `rel` and steps, so every diagnostic of a copy points at the authored rule.
     `Content.compile` already removes identical diagnostics (`lib/loka/content.ex:77-81`).
9. **Key scheme and sort.** The key is `<rule>_<room>`, for example `wanderer` in room `hall` gives
   `wanderer_hall`.
   - It reproduces the hand keys of `cartridges/codex_sampler`, which is the gate below.
   - Order consequence, which goes in the docs as a sentence: copies sort by the bytes of
     `<rule>_<room>`.
     - Copies of one rule sort among themselves by room key.
     - `_` (0x5F) sorts after digits and before lowercase letters. So `wanderer9` < `wanderer_hall`
       < `wanderer_mill` < `wanderera` < `wandererx`.
   - An entry or rest event matches only the copy for its room, so the order that matters is between
     a copy and that room's own rules. Pick the zone rule's key for the order you want.
10. **Refusals:**

    | Case | Code | Path | data |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | `zone` together with `on.room` | SCHEMA_VIOLATION | `<rule src>.zone` | `{"error": "invalid_value"}` |
    | No room lists the zone | UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE | `<rule src>.zone` | `{"target": "<zone>"}` |

    Existing checks cover the rest:
    - A trigger without a room filter gives UNKNOWN_FIELD at `<rule src>.on.room`, from the schema.
    - A copy key over 64 characters gives SCHEMA_VIOLATION at `<rule src>` (`compiler.ex:330`).
    - A copy key equal to an authored reaction, or to another copy, gives DUPLICATE_DEFINITION at
      each site, from `Bundles.unique/1`. For example, rule `a` in room `b_c` collides with rule `a_b`
      in room `c`.
11. **Order with other stages.** Prose is lowered before zones, so all copies share one generated
    text key (the authored rule's). Zones first would mint one key per copy. Signal lowering gives the
    same output in either order. A zone rule may `extends`, because flattening runs first.

## Files in scope

- New `lib/loka/content/signals.ex` (`lower/1`) and `lib/loka/content/zones.ex` (`expand/1`), each
  `{files, diags} -> {files, diags}` with `@spec`. Add two stages at `source.ex:58`.
- `cartridges/codex_sampler/`:
  - rooms `hall`, `mill`, `road`, `study` and `yard` each gain `"zones": ["priory"]`;
  - the five `reactions/wanderer_{hall,mill,road,study,yard}.json` become one
    `reactions/wanderer.json` with `"zone": "priory"` and `"on": {"event": "entity_entered_room"}`.

  The drafter's scratch Python model (not committed) showed that the five files differ only in
  `on.room`, and that their expansion
  equals the originals.
- New test fixtures, kept out of `cartridges/` so that no sampler glob, transcript, floor case or
  Impact story picks them up:
  - `test/fixtures/signal_sugar/` (with the shortcuts)
  - `test/fixtures/signal_expanded/` (hand-written JSON)

  Each holds two rooms (`yard`, `hall`) and one player int fact `heard` (0..10, default 0). Its two
  reactions are:
  - `ring`: on `entity_entered_room` into `hall`, `apply [signal bell]`, `silent: true`;
  - `hear`: on signal `bell`, `apply [fact.adjust heard +1, narrate]`.

  The manifest declares what both need, with `kernel_api` at least 1.47.
- `docs/system-graph.gen.json`: regenerate it with `elixir bin/contracts.exs`; CI runs `--check`.
  Its authored-file lists come from the glob `cartridges/*/<map>/*.json`
  (`bin/system_graph_homes.exs:35-49`), so adding or removing a definition file changes it.
- New `test/loka/content_signal_zone_test.exs` and new `kernel/ts/test/signal.test.ts`. Compile with
  `mix loka.compile` the way `kernel/ts/test/speech.test.ts:22-35` does. Re-encode an edited
  cartridge the way `kernel/ts/test/fragment.ts` `bundle()` does.
- Docs, in the first commit:
  - `docs/system/cartridge.md` Source shortcuts: rules 1-11, with the sort sentence verbatim.
  - The Source layout room row: the source-only `zones`.
  - `docs/BUILDERS-GUIDE.md` `:90` table: one row, "A message between rules, or one rule for many
    rooms", linking codex and the signal fixture.
  - `docs/system/mechanics.md` stays as it is. The rule order is already its fact; Source shortcuts
    links to it.

## Out of scope

- An engine `event.emit` reaction step or a zone trigger filter (audit §3: they wait for a measured
  need).
- Signals from recipes or dialogues. Signal payloads.
- Zones on recipes or other kinds. A "this room" parameter inside a zone rule's `when` or `apply`.
- Parameterised behaviours and their `<instance>__<behaviour>__<rule>` scheme (audit finding 20, a
  later row).
- `toolbox_showcase` (open PR #464). TypeScript source code (the tests are TS, the code is not).
  protocol, save.

## Acceptance (literal values)

1. **Zone byte gate, on an existing sampler.**
   - `git diff main -- protocol/fixtures` is empty.
   - `test/loka/content_priory_test.exs:10` is green: `{:ok, expected, []}` against
     `protocol/fixtures/codex_sampler_hash.json`, sha256
     `33814ace8f163e929954abb73a3e88fc6b13248577141704f8c311bbe2821a71`.
   - `kernel/ts/test/codex.test.ts:56` ("the wanderer badge appears on entering the fifth room, not
     before") is green unchanged. It is the existing behaviour test for the expanded rules.
   - Counts: **21 files and 530 lines before; 17 files and about 319 lines after.** Paste yours.
   - The codex tests that edit files touch only `items/mill_ledger.json` and topics
     (`content_priory_test.exs:20-30`; `content_refusals_test.exs:264-290`), so no test rewrite is
     expected.
2. **Signal byte gate.** In `content_signal_zone_test.exs`, `Loka.Content.compile("test/fixtures/signal_sugar")
   == Loka.Content.compile("test/fixtures/signal_expanded")`, and both are `{:ok, _, []}`.
   - The expanded fixture is the independent oracle. It holds:
     - the literal fact spec from rule 3;
     - `ring`'s step `{"op": "fact.adjust", "fact": "signal_bell", "amount": 1}`;
     - `hear`'s trigger `{"event": "fact_changed", "fact": "signal_bell"}`.
3. **Signal behaviour (TS, `kernel/ts/test/signal.test.ts`).** Compile `signal_sugar`, start a world
   in `yard`, then enter `hall`, go back to `yard`, and enter `hall` again.
   - After the two entries, `heard` is **2** and `signal_bell` is **2**. A lowering to a
     `fact.assign true` would give `heard` 1.
   - **Boundary** (brief kit, exact boundary): edit the compiled `signal_bell` default to

4. **Refusals** (Elixir, with literal `{code, path}` and data):

   - signal_sugar copy: `hear` listens to `gong` gives

   - codex copy: `wanderer.json` gains `"room": "hall"` in `on` gives

## Brief E1: showcase walk transcripts, part 1, and the coverage metric (loka-kgd.194.9)

**Lane, branch and model.**
- On `toolbox/authoring-batch-a-walks` in its own worktree, branched from the batch head, in
  parallel with A to D (owner 2026-10-28); the PM merges it into `toolbox/authoring-batch-a`.
- Opus developer. Handoff threshold: about 220k tokens.
- Timebox: 4 districts. At the limit, hand back the walks that replay.
- Read the brief kit once. Lessons: `docs/lessons/evidence.md`.

**Goal.** `coverage.ts` today finds that 0 of 140 reactions fire, 0 of 49 recipes complete, no
dialogue choice is chosen and 0 of 3 quests resolve on the showcase's 7 transcripts. Add one
transcript per district that walks that district's plan. Then report coverage as a metric. It is
not a CI gate; that is .20.

**Spec.**
- `docs/system/cartridge.md` "Transcript coverage" (line 750): read it, but do not edit it.
- `docs/SHOWCASE.md` matrix.
- The district plans in `docs/showcase/*.md`.

**Signatures.**
- `kernel/ts/play/coverage.ts` (ast-grep outline): `marked(c)` :24, `replay(...)` :43,
  `coverage(c, traces)` :71. The default glob is `cartridges/<id>/transcripts/*.jsonl` (:130).
- `kernel/ts/test/transcripts.test.ts:25-62`. Every `transcripts/<name>.jsonl` must replay byte
  for byte, and `<name>` must be a capability owning a command in it (:51-62).
- `kernel/ts/play/run.ts`: `start` :26, `header` :41, `decideReplay` :69.
- `kernel/ts/play/main.ts:4`: `loka play <artifact> [script|--replay]` writes a `game_trace`.

**Design.**
1. **Naming.** `cartridges/toolbox_showcase/transcripts/walk_<district>.jsonl`. In
   `transcripts.test.ts`, a `walk_` file replays like the others but is exempt from the capability
   check; that is one condition.
   - `bin/features.exs:35` reads only `<capability>.jsonl`, so it ignores walks.
   - `coverage.ts` picks them up by default.
2. **Recording.** First find the recipe that produced the existing showcase transcripts, with
   their fixed run ids and seed. Start from `git log --diff-filter=A --
   cartridges/toolbox_showcase/transcripts/` (commit 3403f8114, loka-4hik.27) and `bin/loka play`.
3. **Districts in this brief:** body (with the fire sandbox), world, social (with the consequence
   loop), combat. First confirm which districts are built: the `docs/SHOWCASE.md` header and its
   matrix disagree, and the homestead and traps rooms exist.
4. **Walk source.** Each walk follows its district's pinned test (`kernel/ts/test/showcase_<district>.test.ts`)
   as far as player commands can reach. A step that a test reaches only by editing the world
   (setting the clock or a fact) is listed in the handback, not faked.

**Acceptance.**
1. Every walk replays in `transcripts.test.ts`.
2. `node kernel/ts/play/coverage.ts <showcase artifact>` exits 0. It must not hit the 64-line
   narration cap; split a walk if it does.
3. In the output, `never.quests` no longer lists `carry_letter` or `bounty`, and fewer than 140
   reactions are listed in `never.reactions`.
4. Red control: the exemption is a new skip path (`docs/lessons/checks.md`). Plant a case in
   `bin/red_controls.exs`, next to its transcript case at :132: a `walk_` file whose replay
   differs must fail. Removing the exemption must also fail `transcripts.test.ts` with
   `no walk_body command`.
5. Metric: a "Coverage" line in `docs/SHOWCASE.md` with the command and the measured counts per
   kind (`x of 140 reactions`, `x of 49 recipes`, choices, `x of 3 quests`), dated with the head
   sha.
6. No edit to showcase source; the hash fixture is unchanged.

**Out of scope.** A coverage CI gate (.20). Edits to showcase content. Edits to cartridge.md.

**Scope trigger: stop and ask** if:
- no deterministic recording recipe exists;
- a walk needs a showcase content change;
- the showcase hash moves.

**Realm.** n/a: test transcripts.

HANDOFF THRESHOLD: near 180k tokens stop, push, hand back head + done/left list (no CI wait).

GOAL. Two W1 acceptance gaps (docs/MECHANICS-TOOLBOX.md:188 and :101 "a dropped bone draws a crow"; Beads loka-kgd.22; docs/rnd/depth-and-ux-2026-10-13.md:38 gap 5):
A. `witness` trigger filter: `{event, witness: <npc>}` holds when that NPC is alive in the event subject's room and sees the subject: not `blind`, and the subject not `concealed` from it (row 16's `pierced_by` makes an alert witness see a hidden thief). It reuses row 33's `witnesses(world, body, except?)` in kernel/ts/src/mechanics/senses.ts (one read-only query for the theft rule and the filter; docs/lessons/mechanics.md bullet 3). Gratitude and grudge are then content: `fact.assign {fact, npc: baker}` at the witness (W2 pair fact, player scope).
B. `npc.move {npc?, room?}` apply step: moves the named NPC (else the event's subject when it is an NPC) to `room` (else the event's room: `eventRooms`, kernel/ts/src/mechanics/lookups.ts:22) as a schedule jump does, emitting `entity_entered_room {entity_id, room_id}` (shape of `entered`, kernel/ts/src/mechanics/schedule/behavior.ts:92) so W3 rumours, W10 sight and the FIFO budget compose. Nothing when the NPC is dead, `engaged` (kernel/ts/src/mechanics/combat/shared.ts), already there, in a running scene, or no room resolves (rule 2 of the seams: with no subject it writes nothing).

PM RULINGS (pre-decided):
1. `witness` is added to the trigger branches `item_acquired`, `attack_result`, `item_dropped`, `entity_died`, `action_completed`, `check_passed`, `check_failed` (the events whose subject stands in a room; protocol/reaction.schema.json `on` oneOf, :13-120 and following). Not on `spoken` (the hearer is the witness: the `npc` filter, mechanics.md:2380) nor on `fact_changed`, `clock_hour`, quest, choice, scene or status events. Rejected: a payload field written by every emitter (a stored "seen" is authority state; G6 reasoning, mechanics.md:2237).
2. The witness sees the subject, not the doer: for `item_acquired` the subject is the holder (`SUBJECT`, reaction.ts:185-188: a gift's receiver, a thief's body), for `attack_result` the target, for the doer-subject events the actor's body (subjectOf :215 returns undefined -> use `bodyOf(then, actor)` as `sequence` does at :124). `FILTERS` (reaction.ts:57) take `(w, want, p)`: compute the subject from `SUBJECT[p.type]` inside the filter; no signature change.
3. Range is the room (range 0). G6's two-room cue range is not read: a witness of a shout is the `spoken` hearer already. Known limit, stated.
4. `npc.move` is a jump (no exit crossed, no `npcPassage`, no lock), as W10 schedule moves are (mechanics.md:2315); `walks` for a reaction move is a later field. The event it emits is a delivery event at the cause's logical time; its cascades count against `deliveries` and `reaction_depth` as today (mechanics.md:660-662).
5. Writer group: the delivery's, joined through the advance's `holders` map keyed by the NPC as `moveItem` does for an item (kernel/ts/src/mechanics/containment/react.ts:10-33), so a status job moving the same NPC in one advance composes instead of faulting.
