title: Toolbox row 19b: replenish primitive (harvest regrowth, shop restock, any finite holder) — batch M10
description:
Owner ask 2026-10-11: regrowth plus a general restocking mechanic.

PM design (decided, mechanics lane): no item minting. One composable job kind 'replenish': {from: a roomless reserve holder, to: a holder (harvest seam, shop shelf, chest, room), item template, cap, every: interval, when: optional leaf}. Each due tick moves up to N item instances reserve -> target until the target holds cap. Items stay conserved, so saves, receipts and conservation invariants need no new item kind.
Covers: harvest regrowth (row 19), shop restock (B3/B5 finite stock), refilling chests/forage, later W11 stock-sensitive prices and NPC trade jobs.
Loop with decay (row 41): a decay expiry may move a thing to the reserve instead of the terminal consumed holder, so spoiled stock feeds regrowth (ponytail: a finite reserve is total lifetime supply unless decay feeds it back).
Open for the brief: per-tick count; does a refill of a shelf show to the player (Book line)?; Book wording must not promise regrowth times (book-ui.md:549).
Also fix MECHANICS-TOOLBOX row 19 text, which cites loka-kgd.84 instead of this issue.
notes:
[Pi · anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 · M10 planner]
Written 2026-10-12 06:28 UTC in the Pi harness by anthropic/claude-opus-5-5

BRIEF: toolbox row 19b, replenish primitive (batch M10, wave 1). Size M, one run, no split. kernel_api 1.72 (loka-btpd).

GOAL
Owner ask 2026-10-11 (this issue): regrowth plus restocking. The PM design above stands: no minting; conserved items move from a reserve to a target up to a cap. Covers row 19's "Regrowth. Not built" (docs/system/mechanics.md:2295), shop restock, any finite holder. Row 41 and loka-kgd.107.3 build on it.

LANE
Branch toolbox/m10-replenish off toolbox/batch-m10 (PM gives the head); own worktree under worktrees.noindex; bin/worktree_setup.sh first. Push; hosted CI on the head. Before handoff: full `npm run typecheck` in kernel/ts; prettier as .github/workflows/ci.yml runs it.

SPEC FIRST (same branch, first commit)
Add "## Replenish (toolbox row 19b)" at the end of docs/system/mechanics.md (6b bullet shape) and "## Replenish declarations" in docs/system/cartridge.md after "Harvest tool declarations". Replace the Regrowth bullet (:2295) with a link here. Decided design (answers this issue's open questions):
- Declaration. A top-level section `replenish`, keyed like `populations`. Each entry is `{items, from, to, cap, count, every}`:
  - `items`: an identity set of authored item refs, as `harvest.items`.
  - `from` and `to`: an `ItemLocation` (protocol/entity.schema.json:6; room, npc or item; `template` refused).
  - `cap`, `count`, `every`: integers of at least 1; `every` in clock units. Numbers are content.
- Job. One pending job per entry, `job {kind: "replenish", key}`, first due at start + every. The seed is appended after firstClock in `firstJobs` (kernel/ts/src/mechanics/schedule/behavior.ts:59), so existing cartridges mint the same ids. Dispatch is one line in `decideAt` (kernel/ts/src/mechanics/schedule/rule.ts:42).
- Run. held = `selected(world, items, to, Infinity, steps)` (kernel/ts/src/mechanics/containment/stock.ts:5). Then move `min(count, cap - held)` instances from `selected(world, items, from, …)`, in its EntityId order, by `entity.transfer`. Then `job.complete`, and the next job at due_time + every, a fixed grid. A next due time the advance also crosses runs as its own drain step, as `scheduledJob`'s `crossed`/`next` (schedule/rule.ts:119-133). An empty reserve or a full target moves nothing and still reschedules.
- Host. The elapsed host stops at every non-calendar job (mobile/authority/local-story/elapsed.ts:67): each interval runs once however an absence is chunked. No host change.
- Silent: no line, no event; the Book never promises a time (book-ui.md:549).
- Known limits: a finite reserve is the lifetime supply until row 41 feeds it back; no `when` gate yet; the reserve is any authored holder (a sealed room; reach.ts lists it unreachable).
- Opt-in 1.72 (KERNEL_API_RANGE_INVALID at requires.kernel_api.at_least). Both kernels: a template location or `from` equal to `to` is SCHEMA_VIOLATION; an unresolved ref UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE.
- Also: Book (no new element), Traps (trap 1 holds: due times on the clock), Sampler, composition record.

COMPOSITION RECORD
Consumer: schedule@1 run_job; Harvest, shops and the GameView read the result unchanged. Reads: containers. Writes: `entity.transfer`, `job.complete`, `job.schedule` (existing). Events and save rows: none new. Reused: `selected`, firstJobs, the crossed-hour drain, ItemLocation. New: the `replenish` section, its job kind, `runReplenish`, the 1.72 floor. No foundation change.

FILES (outline signatures; read only these ranges)
- New kernel/ts/src/mechanics/containment/replenish.ts: `firstReplenish`, `runReplenish`.
- kernel/ts/src/mechanics/schedule/behavior.ts:59 firstJobs; kernel/ts/src/mechanics/schedule/rule.ts:42 decideAt, :98 scheduledJob (model).
- kernel/ts/src/mechanics/containment/stock.ts:5 selected.
- Loader: new kernel/ts/src/content/cartridge_replenish.ts, registered beside the other checks. Compiler: lib/loka/content/source.ex:123 (section map), new lib/loka/content/replenish.ex (short-key expansion, same checks).
- protocol/cartridge.schema.json:310 (beside `populations`); protocol/fixtures/invalid.json; regenerate kernel/ts/src/contracts.gen.ts.
- kernel/ts/src/runtime/world.ts:107 kernel_api '1.72'.
- New cartridges/replenish_sampler, kernel/ts/test/replenish.test.ts, test/loka/content_replenish_test.exs.
- docs/MECHANICS-TOOLBOX.md: add row 19b after row 19 (M10, done #N); row 19's "loka-kgd.84" becomes loka-kgd.85. Regenerate docs/toolbox.gen.json, docs/system-graph.gen.json.

SAMPLER
- Mine: a harvest detail `seam` with items ore_01..ore_05, no tool. The mine holds ore_01 and ore_02.
- Store (no exits) holds ore_03..05 and a stone.
- `seam_regrowth`: {items ore_01..05, from store, to mine, cap 2, count 1, every 3600}.
- Trader: an NPC holding nothing. A crate in the store holds apple_01.
- `shelf`: {items [apple_01], from crate (item), to trader (npc), cap 1, count 1, every 3600}.

ACCEPTANCE (replenish.test.ts; literal ore counts)
A. Harvest twice at 0, then Harvest is refused not_found. Wait to 3600: mine 1, store 2. Wait to 7200: mine 2, store 1. Wait to 10800: mine 2, store 1. The stone stays in the store throughout.
B. The two harvests, then one wait 0 to 10800: mine 2, store 1 (the same as A, step by step).
C. No harvest, wait to 3600: mine 2, store 3.
D. Wait to 3600: the trader holds apple_01 and the crate is empty.
E. Both kernels: the floor, a template location, from equal to to, an unresolved item. Schema fixtures: cap 0, an unknown field; then the schema mutant sweep (docs/lessons/contracts.md).
F. A cartridge without `replenish` gets no new job; existing pins and Chapter 1 receipts are unchanged.

RED CONTROLS: ignore cap (C store 2); ignore count (A mine 2 at 3600); no item filter (the stone moves); no reschedule (A mine 1 at 7200); no drain step (B mine 1).

FOCUSED RUNS: node --test replenish, harvest_tool and schedule tests; mix test the new Elixir test (--force for mutants).

READ: AGENTS.md (Simplicity, Writing tests), developer.md, docs/lessons/mechanics.md, storage.md, contracts.md.

OUT: row 41, a `when` gate, the ledger listing replenish (.107.3), mobile/authority, Elixir runtime.

SCOPE TRIGGER (ask the PM): any item minting; a new save section, op or event; a mobile/authority or save-recovery change; fresh-world id changes for existing cartridges; two docs/system clauses disagreeing.

HANDOFF near 180k tokens.

Transfers: creative diversity is the lever we control; one creator per gap; small coached group; keyword-search recruiting (BookTok, IF, MUD, cosy games).
Does not transfer yet: no spend, no pricing, a one-chapter game cannot supply 500+ ads a month, and a % of spend model needs real spend first.

Pilot (6 weeks, $3-6k incl. $1.5-3k Meta spend): 4-6 creators, flat $150-300/video plus a small per-install bonus, 2-3 videos each. Gaps: BookTok reader ("a novel you play"), ex-MUD nostalgia, cosy no-timer gamer, commute/offline reader, optionally one non-US English market. No two videos with the same hook or shot.
Measure: CPI, click-to-install, D1/D7, Chapter 1 completion, Chapter 2 intent per creator. Kill: CPI > ~$3 with D7 < 15% after $2k, or no gap beats the others by 2x. Thresholds are general rules of thumb, not Loka data.

title: Monetization: free chapter 1 + one-time unlock, paid cartridges, ethics guardrails (Right Livelihood)
description:
Tabled monetization model (owner 2026-10-10; Fable advice). Owner constraint (paraphrased): no predatory design, no pay-to-win, no gambling-like mechanics; follow Buddhist Right Livelihood (honest trade, no harm or deception, no exploiting compulsion, fair value).

Recommended launch: chapter 1 free and complete; one-time unlock for the next chapter(s) at $4.99-7.99; later cartridges $2.99-4.99 each plus a complete-book bundle. Patron tier with cosmetic-only book themes and a colophon credit comes in a later release. Creator marketplace later still (needs builder guide, store policy, revenue share, moderation).
Considered: premium upfront (cleanest, but discovery-limited).

Ethics guardrails (adopt as a product rule when the owner decides):
1. Price visible before any tap that starts a purchase.
2. Nothing purchasable is random, timed, scarce or expiring.
3. No purchase changes difficulty, stats, odds, resources or hints; paid content differs only in story.
4. Free content is complete; no mid-scene paywall; one offer shown per chapter end, no reminders.
5. No energy, streaks, daily-login rewards or pull-back notifications.
6. Refund link in app; honor platform refunds without friction.
7. No in-game ads; no tracking beyond what store receipts need.
8. Marketing claims are checked against the shipped build.

Depends on: PREP-03 store-policy review (before any price is published) and an IAP slice in mobile. Pairs with loka-marketing-ugc-pilot-5mrn: creators sell the free chapter; pay per video plus a share of unlock revenue, never per install; real current-build footage only, no urgency language, price stated if buying is mentioned, sponsorship disclosed.
Conversion figures are industry rules of thumb, not Loka data. Owner decides timing.

GOAL. A reaction step `narrate {text}` appends one authored line to the delivery's narration, so an arrival,
a departure, a raid held or sacked is told in words (plan §3 N1, trap 12). Beads: `loka-mytp` (engine half).

change) and `vary` renders them. Add one branch: `else if (step.op === 'narrate') narration.push({ key: step.text })`.

title: Toolbox row 16: sneak and hide (pierced_by reader, engage cures concealment) — batch M13
description: Toolbox row 16 (docs/MECHANICS-TOOLBOX.md:186), batch M13. Fable brief in notes.
notes:
Fable brief 2026-10-14 (s2):
BRIEF toolbox row 16 — sneak and hide (Fable draft 2026-10-14; PM to store in a new Beads issue under loka-kgd). Batch M13 row 3, after FD2 (skill_compare is not needed; FD2 only fixes the branch base). Size S-M, one developer run, engine only (no Book element). kernel_api 1.93 (FD3 takes 1.92). Model: developer, Opus.
HANDOFF THRESHOLD: near 180k tokens stop, push, hand back head + done/left list (no CI wait).

GOAL. A hidden player is ignored by a guard until a failed sneak (docs/MECHANICS-TOOLBOX.md:186). Most of the row already exists: SR8 built the `hidden` concealment status, `concealed()` (kernel/ts/src/mechanics/status/shared.ts:221) and the entry-engagement read (kernel/ts/src/mechanics/disposition.ts:75), and wrote "row 16's sneak is apply `hidden` on a passed check, end it on a failed one" (docs/system/mechanics.md:2502). What is missing is the opposed half: today `hidden` yields to nothing, so no guard can ever catch a hidden player. This row adds one declared reader and one consequence:
(a) `StatusDefinition.pierced_by {skill, attribute}` (both DefinitionRefs, both required; only beside `concealment`): a seer whose `attribute` value is greater than the holder's `skill` level (G5 level, kernel/ts/src/mechanics/skills.ts:23) sees through the concealment. No RNG, no roll, no stored outcome (trap 5; G5 "draws no RNG").
(b) A spotted entrant is caught: when `engage` (disposition.ts:39, called from kernel/ts/src/mechanics/movement/sequence.ts:99) opens an encounter, it also cures every active concealment status on the entering body (`cureOps`, status/shared.ts:185). The engage line is the authored "spotted" text (trap 12).
Hiding itself is content: a detail recipe with an opposed check (`rating` on the hiding place, docs/system/mechanics.md:2013) plus a reaction `{event: check_passed, check: hide}` whose unnamed `status.apply` lands on the doer's body (reaction@1 table, mechanics.md:612 and :637). No recipe step change: `status.apply` in a recipe sequence stays spell-only (protocol/action.schema.json:735-751).

PM RULINGS (pre-decided; the PM edits if it rules otherwise):
1. Opposition is holder skill level vs seer attribute value (NPCs have attributes, G3, and no skills, trap 2). Strictly greater pierces; equal stays hidden. Rejected: a second `perception` kind `see_hidden` (binary, no skill involved) and a per-move RNG roll.
2. A holder with no character (a hidden NPC; `actorOf` undefined, kernel/ts/src/runtime/decision.ts:187) is never pierced: SR8's hidden troll stays hidden. Known limit, stated.
3. The seer's attribute: an NPC by `npcValue` (kernel/ts/src/mechanics/attributes/shared.ts:91); the player's body by `value(world, actorOf(body), attribute)` (:30), so the symmetric case (a pierced_by status on an NPC vs a sharp-eyed player) costs no extra branch but is not sampled.
4. Being spotted ends hiding (ruling b). Rejected: leaving the status active (the player would stay hidden from the second guard after the first shouted).
5. Only entry engagement and, after row 33, the witness read consume this; talk, trade and an NPC already fighting keep SR8's known limits (mechanics.md:2503).

DOCS/SYSTEM CLAUSES (read once; cite in the PR): SR6/SR8 section (mechanics.md:2495-2507: concealment, known limits, composition record; amend the `hidden` sentence and the known limits); G11 entry engagement (mechanics.md:2329, `hostileAt`); G5 level and opposed check (mechanics.md:2013-2023); G3 NPC attributes (mechanics.md:2137); status declarations (docs/system/cartridge.md:1762, SR6/SR8 paragraph :1776); opt-in precedent paragraphs (W6, FD4 at mechanics.md:2985); toolbox slice process and traps (docs/MECHANICS-TOOLBOX.md:217-250); composition record (docs/system/architecture.md#building-mechanics-by-composition); lessons docs/lessons/mechanics.md (bullet 3: view and rule share one read-only query; here `concealed` is that query).

FILES IN SCOPE (signatures at current main):
- kernel/ts/src/mechanics/status/shared.ts: `205 function sensed(world, body)`; `213 export const perceives`; `221 export const concealed = (world, holder, seer) => sensed(world, holder).some(s => s.concealment === 'hidden' || (s.concealment === 'invisible' && !perceives(world, seer, 'see_invisible')))`. Add the pierced clause: `&& !(s.pierced_by && pierces(world, s.pierced_by, holder, seer))` with `pierces` = seer attribute > holder level, false when `actorOf(world, holder)` is undefined or either value is undefined. Lookups only, no query step.
- kernel/ts/src/mechanics/disposition.ts: `39 export function engage(world, actor, body, there, mint, steps)` (returns `{ops, narration}`); append `cureOps(world, body, <concealment statuses active on body>, 0)` to `ops` when `npc` is found. `63 hostileAt` unchanged (its `concealed` call at :75 now reads the clause).
- protocol/cartridge.schema.json: `2524 StatusDefinition` (`concealment` at 2686): add `pierced_by {skill: DefinitionRef, attribute: DefinitionRef}`, required both, `additionalProperties: false`, description naming the row and floor 1.93. Regenerate kernel/ts/src/contracts.gen.ts.
- Loader twins: kernel/ts/src/content/cartridge_status.ts (`11 export function status(c)`) and lib/loka/content/status.ex: `pierced_by` without `concealment` is SCHEMA_VIOLATION at `pierced_by`; `skill` resolves to a skill of this cartridge and `attribute` to an attribute (UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE at `.cartridge.statuses[<key>].pierced_by.skill` / `.attribute`; Elixir `statuses/<key>.pierced_by.skill`), needing skills@1 and attributes@1 (UNDECLARED_CAPABILITY); floor 1.93 (KERNEL_API_RANGE_INVALID at `requires.kernel_api.at_least`). Elixir ref expansion where `modifies[i].attribute` expands today.
- kernel/ts/src/runtime/world.ts:107 `kernel_api: '1.89'` (1.92 after FD3) -> `'1.93'` and the installed-kernel fixtures that pin it.
- Sampler `cartridges/sneak_sampler` (neutral ids): lane (entry) with detail `barrels` (`rating` 0) and recipe `hide` (opposed check, skill `stealth` with growth `[1, 2, 3]`, not taught; cooldown none; duration 0); reaction `on {check_passed, check: hide}` -> `status.apply hidden` (status `hidden`: `concealment: hidden`, `pierced_by {skill: stealth, attribute: alertness}`, `duration` 600, no per_tick, label, applied narration "You slip behind the barrels."); attribute `alertness` (start 0); gate east of the lane with `sentry` (`attributes [{alertness, 1}]`, `attack`, `disposition {hostile: all [], engage: "sentry.spots"}`); keep east of the gate with `captain` (alertness 3, same shape). `world.combat` declared. Text: the engage lines say who spots whom.
- Tests: kernel/ts/test/sneak.test.ts (new); test/loka/content_status_test.exs cases for the twin; kernel/ts/test/status_readers.test.ts must pass unchanged (SR8 bytes: ward_sampler has no pierced_by).
- Docs: docs/system/mechanics.md new section at the end "Sneak and hide (toolbox row 16)" (model: the FD4 section: Declaration, Realm seams nine lines, Opt-in, Book, Known limits, Sampler, Composition record) plus the two one-line amendments in SR8; docs/system/cartridge.md status declarations paragraph; docs/MECHANICS-TOOLBOX.md row 16 -> `done #N`.

OUT OF SCOPE: kernel/ts/src/mechanics/light/shared.ts (the row text's pointer is stale: `visible` already calls `concealed`, light/shared.ts:113), kernel/ts/src/mechanics/combat/behavior.ts (flight and pack plans read no concealment; not needed), kernel/ts/src/mechanics/reaction.ts (FD5 thread), action_recipe `status.apply` outside spells, any Book file, talk/trade concealment reads, a Realm audience filter.

ACCEPTANCE (literal values, sneak_sampler, fresh world per case):
1. Unhidden, move east from the lane: accepted, one `encounter.open` with `sentry`, narration key `sentry.spots`.
2. `perform hide` at `barrels`: accepted outcome `success`; `check_passed` at position 1; `uses_stealth` = 1 (level 1); `hidden` active on the body, `ends_at` = clock + 600; applied line present.
3. Then move east: accepted, no `encounter.open`, no `sentry.spots` line (alertness 1 is not greater than level 1); `hidden` still active.
4. Then move east again into the keep: accepted, `encounter.open` with `captain` (3 > 1), narration `captain.spots`, and `hidden` inactive on the body (the cure's `status.transition` in writer group 0).
5. Loader: a status with `pierced_by` and no `concealment` -> SCHEMA_VIOLATION; `pierced_by.skill` naming no skill -> UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE; manifest at 1.92 -> KERNEL_API_RANGE_INVALID; same three in Elixir.
6. kernel/ts/test/status_readers.test.ts and kernel/ts/test/transcripts.test.ts green with fixtures untouched (Chapter 1 and ward_sampler declare no pierced_by).
RED CONTROLS: remove the pierced clause -> case 4 opens no encounter; remove the engage cure -> case 4 leaves `hidden` active. MUTATIONS: `>` to `>=` -> case 3 engages; read the seer's value with `value(world, actor, ...)` (the player's) instead of `npcValue` -> case 4 fails to engage (player alertness 0); treat an undefined `actorOf(holder)` as level 0 -> status_readers' hidden-troll case breaks.

SCOPE TRIGGER (stop and ask): a change to `hostileAt`'s candidate set, movement/sequence.ts beyond the existing `engage` call, any reaction.ts edit, a new event or save row, a `conflicting_write` between the cure and another status write in the same move.

REALM SEAMS (docs/decisions/owner-decision-realm-seams-2026-10-13.md; answer in the spec section and the handback):
1. Actor: met; `concealed` derives the holder's character by `actorOf(world, holder)` and `engage` reads the command's actor; no new `world.character`.
2. Reactions: n/a; the hide reaction is content on the existing check_passed subject rule (the doer's body).
3. Credit: n/a; no payout.
4. Time: met; the status duration is logical seconds from the cartridge; no clock read.
5. Scope: n/a; no fact; the status row is keyed by body; Realm audience: the concealment is read per seer, so each player sees their own answer.
6. Text: n/a; speech@1 unchanged; the spotted line is authored.
7. Ownership: n/a.
8. Trust: n/a.
9. Instancing: n/a; none built or assumed.

COMPOSITION RECORD. Consumer: `sneak_sampler`; next row 33's witness read and W15. Reads: the holder's status rows and declarations, the holder's skill facts (level), the seer's attribute (NPC declared value, player value). Writes: G3's `status.transition` through `cureOps` on engage (existing op); events: none new (`status_expired` is not emitted by a cure, as today); jobs and save rows: none new. Writer ownership unchanged. Reused: SR8 `concealed`, G5 `level`, G3 `npcValue`, G11 `engage`, `cureOps`, KERNEL_API_RANGE_INVALID, SCHEMA_VIOLATION. New: `StatusDefinition.pierced_by`, the `pierces` clause, the engage cure, the 1.93 floor. Missing invariant: none (no state added). Composes without code: hiding (recipe + reaction), the hiding place's rating, the duration, who is alert (attributes). Named exceptions: none.

title: GameView: NPC worn vs carried items for the Look page
description: Engine slice of the NPC Look epic. GameView splits an NPC's visible items into worn/wielded (seen by anyone) and carried (hidden unless peeked), using the existing worn-slot model the player has (AttributeView worn, combat Worn). Content: showcase NPCs author what they wear. Book: the Look page lists worn items in prose; carried items stop showing (until peek). Protocol + kernel + projection; showcase use; story.
notes:
BRIEF loka-oc5i (drafted 2026-10-30). Kit: docs/guides/brief-kit.md (read once; not copied). Handoff threshold: docs/WORKFLOW.md#token-hygiene (~220k).

GOAL. A visible living NPC's EntityView gains `worn`: the items in its direct custody whose definition declares a `slot` (the player's slot-key model, equipment@1), as ContentViews, shown to anyone who sees the NPC. `contents` (Row 33, theft-gated) is unchanged and additive; the Book derives carried = contents minus worn ids and, until the peek mechanic (loka-0vrs), lists only worn. Owner source: loka-ewtx description (quoted).
Size M. Lane: Hosted PR. Branch feat/npc-worn from main AFTER loka-ysbt merges (same files). Developer Opus. kernel_api 1.124.

MODEL DECISION (drafter 2026-10-30, PM to confirm). NPCs have no slot holders: kernel/ts/src/runtime/fresh.ts:56-58 mints one holder per slot key, all contained in the player's body (runtime/decision.ts:161 `slots` by SlotKey). Real NPC holders = new state, save rows and equipment@1 changes (L). So an NPC's worn-ness is derived from the item's `slot` declaration (ItemDefinition.slot; view.ts:228 already exposes it on items). ponytail limit: a spare slotted item in an NPC's pack reads as worn; showcase authors place only worn slotted items on NPCs until steal needs real holders (loka-0vrs plans that).
SPEC CONFLICT, amended in this PR. docs/system/protocol.md:375-376 "An NPC's possessions and a worn item's contents are never shown (c1-locks)" already disagrees with view.ts:173-180 (theft shows direct holdings, Row 33; docs/system/book-ui.md:476). Rewrite to: an NPC's worn items (`worn`: its direct holdings that declare a slot) show to anyone who sees it; its other possessions show as `contents` only under `world.theft`; a worn item's contents are never shown. Cite loka-oc5i and the owner quote.
GOVERNING. docs/system/mechanics.md:104 (a worn item is in a slot holder) and :156 equipment@1; protocol.md:368-378 (ContentView shape; contents rule); book-ui.md:364 (NPC details: description then `carrying` note) and :476 (Held under theft).
ENGINE THAT MAKES IT POSSIBLE. view.ts:154-186 `within` (npc branch: `inside(..., 'room_contents', steps, true)` = direct custody, visible, lock-filtered, only under `world.cartridge.world?.theft`); :192-214 `inside` (direct=true: `containers[id] === box`); :217-253 `viewOf` (`slot` at :228; `carrying` authored prose key at :252, unchanged); ContentView schema protocol/gameview.schema.json:661-722 (required id, name, kind, container_id, actions).

CHANGE. `within` npc branch: call `inside(world, actor, body, actions, id, 'room_contents', steps, true)` for every NPC (not only under theft); `worn` = its entries whose entity declares `slot` (present only when non-empty); `contents` keeps today's gate and list (theft: the lock-filtered full list; else none). Advertised actions on worn entries come from the same `actions.of` query as contents (shared admission; gameview_agrees_with_admission covers it). Schema: EntityView adds optional `worn` (array of ContentView, minItems 1); bin/regen.sh; world.ts:108 and cartridge.json:8 -> 1.124; hash regen. Elixir: n/a (no GameView projection; no content schema change: `slot` and `location {in: npc}` exist).
Files in: kernel/ts/src/view/view.ts (within), protocol/gameview.schema.json, contracts.gen.ts, runtime/world.ts:108, cartridges/toolbox_showcase/cartridge.json:8, protocol/fixtures/toolbox_showcase_hash.json, docs/system/protocol.md:375-376, one test file (kernel/ts/test/access_locks.test.ts or containment.test.ts, whichever already builds NPC holdings). Out: equipment/, containment/, fresh.ts, mobile/, lib/, cartridges content.

ACCEPTANCE (literal).
1. Showcase at fresh, Aldous seen: `worn` = exactly one entry, the training_sword (items/training_sword.json:9-14: location npc aldous, slot wield), `slot: 'wield'`, `container_id` = aldous's id; it also stays in `contents` (showcase has theft, cartridge.json:313).
2. Nell holds bread (items/bread.json, no slot): `worn` absent; bread in `contents` as today.
3. A test world without `world.theft`: `worn` present with the slotted item, `contents` absent; the worn entry's `actions` contains no `take` (admission refuses it there).
4. After an `entity.transfer` of the sword to the room: `worn` absent.
5. A slotted item inside a container the NPC holds (depth 2) is never in `worn`.
6. An unseen NPC (dark room) is absent as today. `validate('GameView', view)` []; schema mutant sweep.
RED CONTROLS: invert the slot filter -> 1 and 2 fail; drop `direct` -> 5 fails; gate worn on theft -> 3 fails.

SHOWCASE USE. None to author: Aldous already wields the training sword. CONTENT RULE for the handback: a slotted item placed on an NPC means worn.
BOOK CONSUMER + STORY. The Look page is not on main: follow-up for the polish session in loka-aqnc ("He wields a training sword." from `worn` names, designer words it; carried = contents minus worn ids; story Pages/NPC Look, worn variant). Nothing under mobile/ in this slice; the NPC page HELD list is unchanged because `contents` is unchanged.
LESSONS: docs/lessons/mechanics.md, docs/lessons/contracts.md.
SCOPE TRIGGER: stop and ask if `inside` without theft advertises an action admission refuses, if the PM wants real NPC slot holders now, or if a cartridge places a slotted item on an NPC as a pack item.

title: Riddle: wrong answer shows as narration, not a refused line
description: Evidence: PR #330 open items (docs/reviews/2026-10-09-polish-batch4-5-review.md); story Pages/NPC refused answer. A wrong riddle answer renders as plain narration, not the refused log line with its tag that book-ui.md specifies for refusals. Fix in the presenter (logs.ts typed refused line) if the kernel reports it as a refusal; designer confirms.
notes:
Batch B: stopped. book-ui.md:582 keeps riddle wrong-answer narration in the speaker detail; a refused line needs a reason word the spec does not give. Overlaps x6t.17.

Designer ruling draft (2026-10-22). Recommend: stay narration; close as by design. mechanics.md:477-479: a bank-valid wrong answer is ACCEPTED (outcome riddle_wrong) with one authored wrong line (riddle.wrong, required by the cartridge schema); only malformed/impossible-bank answers are rejected, and those already get the x6t.17 refused line. A refused tag ('not now') on an accepted, authored turn would misstate the kernel and wrap cartridge prose in a Book frame. Where it shows: the bound speaker's detail, as book-ui.md:582 says. Alternative B: keep the authored line, add a reason tag 'wrong' (new REASON word, presenter maps riddle_wrong to kind refused). Cost: none for A; S for B (words.ts, received.ts:89 path, spec 582, story). Risk B: refused lines must mean 'nothing happened'; a wrong guess is a committed attempt. Owner Q: wrong riddle answer stays the cartridge's own line in the conversation (A), or shows tagged 'wrong' like a refusal (B)?
close_reason: By design (owner 2026-10-22, went with rec A): a wrong riddle answer is accepted by the engine and shows the cartridge's own line in the conversation; no refused tag.

GOAL. The owner pays the carpenter to raze a built room: its contents move to the site, exits go, the created row stays.

CONTRACT (no `State.built` exists; built rooms are `state.created` rows, origin kind 'built').
- New section `built[id] = {razed_at: LogicalTime}`; op `built.set {writer_group, entity_id, expected: null|row, value}` on the levelling.set pattern. Mismatch or a non-built entity_id -> precondition_failed, both kernels.

Refusals: no live built room there -> invalid_state service.nothing_to_raze; origin.owner !== p.actor_id -> permission_denied; any body or immovable created entity (corpse, movable() false) directly inside -> invalid_state service.occupied. Accepted: payment, clearStatuses(room) (its expiry job then no-ops), one entity.transfer per entity whose container is the room (EntityId order) to the site, built.set.
- Razed rows are excluded from: unbuildable (site_taken, max_total, max_per_owner), builtValid, ruined() (its find must return the live row), knowledge.ts positions().
- hydrate: early return also tests state.built. raise() writes no exits for a razed row (still registers rooms, roomIds, knownEntities for receipts). The apply-path overlay deletes the room's exits and the site exit only when its `to` is the razed ref (a rebuilt hut may hold that direction; load row order is unordered).
- Skipped note: yes, a room holds statuses (compose_status.ts:8 HOLDERS; created()/mended() emit them).
- hs-12: self-built rooms use the same created() (action_recipe/rule.ts:249); raze identically. hs-6: furnishings are floor items and move; nested contents ride with their container; one landing in the site may fire its item_present variant.

title: Settle settle-6: the band (M, content, save: no)
notes:
## BRIEF settle-6: the band (M, content, save: no)

GOAL. The full-moon raid: the band returns and grows; guards adjust `watch`; present: engage and allied
fight; away: held or sacked by the watch; occupation until cleared (plan §4, §7 S4-1). Beads `loka-oxgk`.
Branch `toolbox/settle-6` (after settle-2 and settle-5). Floor 1.103. Precondition met: `loka-kgd.151/.152`
merged (#387).
MECHANISM. Reuse settle-2's `raiders` plan and `raider` NPC; drop the test-only `band_in/out` rules.
`raid` (`clock_hour`, when `all [sky {lunar full}, fact_compare {raided false}]`): `npc.move {plan raiders,
room square}`, `population.spawn {raiders}`, `fact.assign raided true`, `narrate settle.raid_begins` (37a
shape). `calm` (`clock_hour`, when `sky {lunar new}`): `raided` false. HELD tree (equality-only
`fact_compare`, `population_count` at_least; raiders 0..3, watch 0..3): `any [not pc(1), all [any [w=1, w=2,
w=3], not pc(2)], all [any [w=2, w=3], not pc(3)], w=3]` where `pc(n)` = `population_count {raiders,
at_least n}` and `w=k` = `fact_compare {watch, equals k}`. `held` (`fact_changed {raided}`, when `all
[raided false, HELD]`): `npc.move {plan raiders, room hills}`, `fact.adjust renown 1`, `narrate
settle.raid_held`. `sacked` (same trigger, when `all [raided false, not HELD]`): `status.apply {room square,
status sacked}` (SR9), `status.apply {npc smith, frightened}`, `{npc miller, frightened}`, `fact.adjust
larder -2`, `fact.adjust renown -1`, `narrate settle.raid_sacked`; the band stays (occupation). `held` runs
before `sacked` by key; its steps change nothing HELD reads, so exactly one fires. Statuses: `sacked` on the
room, duration 9600, `tick_every 100` (ticks change nothing on a room; settle-7 cures on a tick), room variant
"ash in the square"; `frightened` on an NPC, duration 2400, W6 `short_variants` "the miller, pale". Hiding:
the residents' hour cases gain a first case `{when all [<state> settled, pc(1)], room cellar}`. Guards: authored
`ward_a`, `ward_b` in the square (hp 5, sure hit 1); dialogue `hire` with `lesson_payment 2` -> `hired`,
`staying`, `fighting` true, `fact.adjust watch 1`, `fact.assign ward_a_on_watch true`; `dismiss` -> `hired`
false. Rule `ward_a_off` (`fact_changed {hired}`, when `all [fact_compare {hired, npc ward_a, false},
ward_a_on_watch true]`) -> `watch -1`, flag false (covers dismiss and the wage's dismissal; same for b).
No death rule: members take no combat damage (G8). Raiders engage on entry (G11); a guard strikes as ally
(22a `allyOf`); kill credit: `world.death_credit` fact `raider_slain` for the encounter's character (G8
credit contract, one line in the section).
FILES in: `cartridges/settle_sampler` (reactions, statuses, npcs `ward_a/b`, dialogues, facts `raided`,
`watch` writes, `ward_*_on_watch`, death_credit, text; residents' cases), `kernel/ts/test/settle.test.ts`,
`test/loka/content_settle_test.exs`, `mobile/authority/local-story/settle.test.ts` (cold reopen across a
raid), `mechanics.md` "Settle S4-1" (+ G8 credit line), `docs/MECHANICS-TOOLBOX.md` S4 status. Out: engine.
ACCEPTANCE (literals; residents settled at 700; full at 2400, new at 4800). Watch 0, away 700->5400: the
elapsed receipts' narration holds `settle.raid_begins` then `settle.raid_sacked`; the square holds `sacked`
and reads "ash"; the miller holds `frightened`, reads "pale", stands in `cellar`; `larder` 1, `renown` 1;
one raider stands in `square` (slot 3); entering the square opens a fight (`engage`). Watch 2 (hire both at
700, 4 pennies): away the same span: `settle.raid_held`, the raider is in `hills`, `renown` 3, the square has
no status, the smith is in `cottages` at 5400. Present at 2400 in `square` with `ward_a` hired: round 1 the
guard's ally blow lands (`combat.ally_hit`), the raider (3 hp) dies by 2600, `raider_slain` true for the
player. Second cycle (7200): the surviving band returns from the hills and one more spawns (slot 2): count 2.
Dismiss `ward_a` -> `watch` 1; a wage dismissal (purse short) -> `watch` 0 and no double decrement when
`ward_b`'s fact changes later. Exact boundaries: watch 1 vs 1 raider -> held; watch 1 vs 2 -> sacked; watch 3
vs 3 -> held. Red controls: flip `not HELD` to `HELD` in `sacked` -> both fire (caught by the status/renown
case); drop the `ward_a_on_watch` guard -> double decrement case fails. One advance 700->5400 equals hourly
steps and `(due_time, job_id)` order; reopen at 3000 (`raided` true, band in the square), elapse to 5400: same.
Nothing is taken from the player's body, chest or purse by a sack (assert).
ITEM LOOP. None new (raiders carry nothing; no loot in v1). pennies: sink hire fees.
OFFERED ACTIONS. `choose` hire/dismiss on `ward_a/b` (dialogue admission, `lesson_payment`); `attack` on a
raider (combat admission `attackRefused`; a member guard is `invalid_target`, not offered). View-to-
invocation: `gameview_agrees_with_admission`; one case: Attack offered on the raider and not on `ward_a`.
COMPOSITION RECORD. Consumer: `settle_sampler`. Reads: `sky`, `raided`, `watch`, `population_count`, pair
facts. Writes: `fact.assign/adjust`, `status.transition` (room, NPC), `entity.transfer` (plan move), births
(spawn). Events: `clock_hour`, `fact_changed`, `entity_entered_room`, `status_*`. Jobs: calendar, plan,
status jobs (exist). Save: none. Reused: 37a, 37b, SR9, G3, W6, W10, W12 leaf, G8/22a/22b, G11, N1, N2. New:
none. Missing invariant: none. Risk named in the section: the HELD tree is long; a `fact_compare.at_least`
(S, policy thread) is the honest fix if a reviewer finds it unreadable (plan §9), not an engine raid branch.
BOOK. No new component: Log lines / Away recap (raid begins, held, sacked); the square's prose variant; the
residents' variants; the Combat page; hire cards. One browser interaction: return after a sacked cycle and
read the recap block. Designer (mark): the four raid lines, the sacked room prose, "the miller, pale", and the
status-line question (recommend no `watch` item; the board holds it).
REALM. 1 met (hire reads the actor; jobs read none); 2 met (`clock_hour`/`fact_changed {raided}` have no
subject and write instance facts, room and NPC statuses, narration; `fact_changed {hired}` names the guard);
3 met: a raider kill credits the encounter's character (Story default), "held" credits no one, `renown` is
town state; 4 met (calendar hours, no skip); 5 met (`raided`, `watch`, `larder`, `renown` instance; audience
public, once per world); 6 met; 7 n/a (a sack transfers nothing); 8 n/a; 9: shared-world, one band per world.
SCOPE TRIGGER. Any engine edit; a HELD/`sacked` pair that cannot be made exclusive in content; a reopen
fault across the raid (report as a `loka-kgd.152`-class bug, do not work around): stop.
PM 01da56d0: shared header in loka-mytp notes; PM accepts the drafter's 4 recommendations (smithy via event.emit custom_event; residents authored NPCs moved by npc.move; square repair via room status_ticked subject; buy two -> 5).
PM from settle-2 review: raider disposition.hostile + engage line land here (settle-2 deferred them); restate or drop the 'one long advance equals hourly steps' row (one clock_hour fires per settlement, schedule/behavior.ts:118-121); keep raid order [npc.move plan, spawn, spawn] (spawn-then-move in one cascade faults: loka-kgd.159).
PM: raiders bundle keeps its knife (a bundle needs item unless the plan scavenges: cartridge_population.ts:136); settle-6 makes 'no loot' true by content (e.g. scavenge or a worthless token) or states the knife as the drop.

title: Settle settle-7: protect and reclaim (S, content, save: no)
notes:
## BRIEF settle-7: protect and reclaim (S, content, save: no)

GOAL. `hold_the_square` per holder; raid the hills to cull the band; repair clears the square; renown 3
scales the spawn (plan §7 S4-2). Beads `loka-oxgk`. Branch `toolbox/settle-7`. Floor 1.103.
MECHANISM. Quest (row 38 "Protect objective", RS-4): `called_to_hold` on `entity_entered_room {room square}`
when `raided true` -> `quest.activate {hold_the_square}` (player scope, `current_state` objective `raided
equals false`); `held` gains `quest.resolve {hold_the_square, held}`, `sacked` gains `quest.fail {..., sacked}`
(both per holder). Cull: `hills` is reachable (road -> north); raiders there are hostile and engage (G11);
a dead slot waits `replacement_delay` 4800 before a spawn can refill it (37a). Repair: `sacked` ticks every
100 on the room; recipe `clear_rubble` on the square's detail `rubble`, policy `status_active {subject: room,
status: sacked}` (1.99 room subject), duration 100 -> `fact.assign {mended true}` (instance bool); reaction
`square_mended` on `status_ticked {status: sacked}` when `mended true` -> `status.cure {sacked}` (the tick's
subject is the room, SR9) and `mended` false. State the limit: the cure lands on the next tick (<= 100 units).
Scaling: `raid_grows` on `fact_changed {raided}` when `all [raided true, fact_compare {renown 3}]` ->
`population.spawn {raiders}` (a second bundle that cycle; fires once per flip). 37b aftermaths: `fact.adjust
aftermaths 1` on the calm flip (count only; no new effect).
FILES in: `cartridges/settle_sampler` (quest, reactions, recipe, detail, facts `mended`, `aftermaths`,
text), `kernel/ts/test/settle.test.ts`, `test/loka/content_settle_test.exs`, `mechanics.md` "Settle S4-2".
Out: engine; Book components.
ACCEPTANCE (literals). Enter the square at 2500 (raid on): `hold_the_square` active for the entrant; an NPC
entering activates nothing. New moon with watch 2: resolved `held`; with watch 0: failed `sacked`; a second
raid offers it no more (terminal instance). Kill all three in the hills at 3000 (one at a time; each engages
on entry): at 7200 no spawn (slots due 7800); at 12000 three spawn. At `renown` 3 the 2400 raid births two
(slots 3 and 2) in one receipt; at `renown` 2 one. After a sack: `clear_rubble` offered only while `sacked`;
perform at 5000 -> at 5100 the square has no `sacked` and reads plain; a perform on a sound square: offered
unavailable `invalid_state`. Red controls: drop the `mended` guard -> the first tick cures; drop `raided true`
from `raid_grows` -> it fires at calm. Boundaries: `renown` 2 vs 3; replacement due at exactly 7800 vs 7799.
One advance 600->12000 equals hourly steps; reopen mid-cycle: same.
ITEM LOOP. None new.
OFFERED ACTIONS. `perform` `clear_rubble` (targets `[rubble detail]`, admission `craftRefused`/policy shared
by `view/action_lists.ts` and `commands/actions.ts`; view-to-invocation: the shared invariant plus the
offered-only-while-sacked case). Attack in the hills: combat admission as settle-6.
COMPOSITION RECORD. Consumer: `settle_sampler`. Reads: `raided`, `renown`, `mended`, room status, quest
holders. Writes: `quest.activate`, `quest.transition`, `status.transition` (cure), `fact.assign`, spawn
births. Events/jobs/save: none new. Reused: 38, RS-4, 37a/37b, SR3 cure on the subject, SR9 room ticks, G4/
recipe policy with `subject: room`. New: none. Missing invariant: none. Named exception: none.
BOOK. No new component: the Journal shows the quest and outcome; the rubble card on the square; the hills
fights. One browser interaction: take the quest, wait to the new moon, read the Journal. Designer (mark):
journal and outcome lines, the rubble card label.
REALM. 1 met (activation to the entrant's character; resolve/fail per holder); 2 met (`entity_entered_room`
names the entrant; `status_ticked` the room); 3 met (kills credit as settle-6; the quest pays nothing); 4 met;
5 met (quest player scope; `mended`, `aftermaths` instance); 6 met; 7-8 n/a; 9: one square, shared-world;
every holder's quest resolves on the one world outcome (row 38 audience `instance`).
SCOPE TRIGGER. A recipe `fact.assign` refusing an instance fact; `status_active {subject: room}` refused on a
recipe policy; any engine edit: stop. If the tick-cure reads badly to the reviewer, the honest fix is a
`room` field on `status.cure` (S, engine, next batch), not a workaround.
PM 01da56d0: shared header in loka-mytp notes; PM accepts the drafter's 4 recommendations (smithy via event.emit custom_event; residents authored NPCs moved by npc.move; square repair via room status_ticked subject; buy two -> 5).

title: Kernel wait across two listed hours of one NPC faults nonfuture_job
description: A single wait command whose advance crosses two consecutive daily_schedule hours of one NPC faults nonfuture_job: the first run_job schedules its successor at the next listed hour (kernel/ts/src/mechanics/schedule/rule.ts, nextHour from the job's due time), which is not after the advance's horizon (foundation/compose_job.ts). The host's elapsed settlement ends a step at each due job (mobile/authority/local-story/elapsed.ts boundary), but a player wait goes to step whole. Found in loka-kgd.57; tests there wait one hour at a time.

comments.text: Fix pushed on toolbox/m6-waitfix, head 29d9746e (base 89a277c8). Scope: the fault is older than W10. kernel/ts/test/schedule.test.ts on main has pinned it since 801aa00d (Bram, 19:00 then 06:00). title: CI: shard the e1-recorder job as a GitHub matrix (after polish)
description:
Owner 2026-10-08 (paraphrased): shard the recorder cases on GitHub CI only, after the polish phase. Today e1-recorder (~6m52s) is the slowest CI job; typescript (~4m51s) is next, so the expected saving is ~2 min per CI run. Recorder does not run in pre-push/check_all, so local gains are moot.
Step 0 (measure first): read per-case times from one existing CI e1-recorder log; thirty-days is 725 of 2,177 steps in the 2026-10-07 evidence report.json and cannot split. Stop if the floor leaves under ~1 min of gain.
Shape: matrix of shard jobs (each runs a case subset of kernel/ts/test/e1_cases.ts:267, uploads partial results) + one merge job that keeps the name e1-recorder (bin/ci_base.sh, bin/docs_only_red_controls.sh depend on it); checkRefusals, obligationReport, exit code 0/1/2, report.json and SHA256SUMS built in the merge step; receipts in CASES order.
Test: a sharded run's merged report.json and SHA256SUMS equal a single-process run's (byte for byte). Keep single-process mode for release-candidate evidence (docs/e1-certification.md 'a fixed program'; needs a review decision).
Public repo: standard runners free; mind the 20-concurrent-job limit.

notes:
BRIEF loka-s05w FD7 Book half: "Ask about X" rows on the NPC card (PM 2026-10-15; designer input below). Size S-M, one developer run, Opus. Lane: Hosted PR to main AFTER batch M13 merges (PM says when); build now.
HANDOFF THRESHOLD: near 150k tokens stop, push, hand back head + done/left list (no CI wait).
Branch: book/fd7-ask-rows from toolbox/batch-m13 @56f6bea9 (the kernel half, loka-kgd.144, lives there; the PM merges main in once M13 lands). Own worktree under worktrees.noindex (bin/worktree_setup.sh).

GOAL. Owner decision docs/decisions/owner-decision-settle-and-fd7-2026-10-14.md "FD7 ask about topic": the Book shows "Ask about <topic>" rows on the NPC card over the kernel `ask {actor_id, target_id, topic}` command (speech@1; docs/system/mechanics.md#ask-about-a-topic-toolbox-row-fd7). Today the Book drops every input-bearing action (mobile/app/book/buttons.ts:124 `!a.input.length`), so Ask never shows.

DESIGN (designer input, approved by PM):
1. Pattern: Action card list on the NPC page (docs/BOOK-UI-COMPONENTS.md Action card; docs/system/book-ui.md "NPC dialogue and action details"). Build exactly as `raiseButtons` (buttons.ts:111): for each available `ask` action on that NPC, one Press per GameView `topics` entry: action_key from the action, target_ids [npc], input {topic: t.topic} (DefinitionRef verbatim). Rows sit inside the existing Cards block (mobile/app/book/Npc.tsx:95) after the NPC's other cards (Talk, Give...), before services, in projected `topics` order. Label: LABEL.askAbout ("Ask about") + space + text(t.label) (same TextKey resolution as journal.tsx:70). Put "Ask about" in labels.ts; also move the existing "Ask where" literal (buttons.ts:97) into labels.ts (one-off nit).
2. Result: the answer or unknown line is ordinary narration in the NPC page's detail history (press carries detail = npc id, presenter.ts:166); no conversation latch, foot stays Leave, no page turn, no nested return. A granted topic re-renders rows from the new `topics` at once. A stale press is the existing refused log line ("not now", words.ts:63).
3. States: no known topics -> zero rows, no note (kernel offer stays; the Book expands per topic: this closes the FD7 nit "Ask offered with no known topic"; no kernel change). Hostile/absent: kernel lists unavailable/absent, no rows. Pending conversation: kernel drops ask; Cards hidden in conversation. Many topics: no cap.
4. No new tokens or components.
5. Spec: add section `## FD7 ask details` after "Lore details" in docs/system/book-ui.md with the designer's text (the designer writes/approves it in review; draft it verbatim):
"An NPC that the GameView lists `ask` on shows, after its other action cards and before services, one card per known topic (GameView `topics`, projected order) labelled "Ask about" and the topic's authored label. Pressing it sends `ask` with that topic; the answer or the person's knows-nothing line joins the page's history as narration, the page stays, no conversation opens. A topic granted by the answer adds its card at once. No known topics, no cards and no note; a hostile, absent or unlisted person shows none, as Talk. ([Ask about a topic](mechanics.md#ask-about-a-topic-toolbox-row-fd7))"
PM ruling on label case: authored labels are capitalised ("Ask about The mill"); accepted for now (sampler content only); no lowercasing code.

OFFERED ACTION (WORKFLOW step 2): key `ask`, command `ask`, targets [npc id], input {topic: DefinitionRef}; shared admission = the kernel's ask admission used by execution and GameView (kernel/ts/src/mechanics/speech/ask.ts). Add a controlled view-to-invocation check: for the ask_sampler smith, every Press built from the view, sent as a command, is admitted (reuse an existing same-layer check if one covers input-bearing presses).

ACCEPTANCE (literal):
- Offers test: ask_sampler square, smith -> presses labelled "Ask about The mill", "Ask about The moon" with input topic refs; ask listed with empty `topics` -> zero rows (red control: drop the per-topic expansion and see it fail).
- After asking about the mill: the narration line "The miller ships more than flour. Ask about the smugglers." and a third press "Ask about The smugglers".
- Asking about the moon: line "The smith shrugs."
- One browser interaction: `mise exec -- bin/loka dev cartridges/ask_sampler`, `npm run author`, http://localhost:19006, gate -> Square -> smith -> the above. Phone width screenshot in the PR (redacted, per docs/lessons/evidence.md).
- Extend the label-literal check (ast-grep rule) to "Ask " if such a check exists.

# loka-sgqk: fold saturated status ticks in catch-up

Links: [brief kit](docs/guides/brief-kit.md) (read once; not copied here); `docs/lessons/storage.md`.
**Handoff threshold: about 220k tokens** ([token hygiene](docs/WORKFLOW.md#token-hygiene)).

- **Lane:** Hosted PR. **Branch:** `engine/catch-up-fold`. **Worktree:** `../worktrees.noindex/loka-sgqk`.
- **kernel_api:** 1.130 in `INSTALLED` only (`kernel/ts/src/runtime/world.ts:108`; bump the same derived files as commit 85b080f5d). No cartridge `at_least` change.
- **Showcase frozen:** no edit under `cartridges/toolbox_showcase`, its transcripts or its hash fixture.

## Goal

A ticking permanent status on a pool at its bound stops costing one committed step, one finished job row and one event per tick. With both needs active, a month of catch-up commits about 11 steps instead of one per hour, and the end state equals job-by-job play. The compiler refuses a ticking permanent status on an item or room.

## The fold

Only a **no-op tick** folds. Ticks that change a pool still run one step each, as today. The number of such ticks is limited by the pool's range: at most 10 per need in `needs_sampler`.

This replaces closed-form arithmetic over a draining pool. It needs no sum of ticks and no fatal-time calculation, and it cannot fold across a band change.

**Predicate.** Export `folds(world, job_id, job)` from `kernel/ts/src/mechanics/status/job.ts`. It is true only when all of these hold:

1. The job is `status` kind and `statusHolder` finds its active row, with `row.ends_at === undefined` (permanent).
2. `spec.per_tick` is defined, and the holder is neither an item nor a room.
3. `amount(...)` gives `by === 0` with a readable pool (saturated at its floor for a drain, its ceiling for a gain).
4. The pool cannot move by itself: `resourceSpec` has `gain` 0 and no `regen` (`current` in `foundation/compose.ts` applies both).
5. No reaction has `on.event === 'status_ticked'` with no `status` filter or a filter matching this status.

**Host** (`mobile/authority/local-story/elapsed.ts:67`):

```ts
if (job.job.kind !== CLOCK_JOB && !folds(s.world, id as JobId, job)) until = Math.min(until, job.due_time);
```

The `already-due` guard at line 65 stays first and still applies to every job.

**Kernel** (`job.ts:79-84`, `runStatus`). When the tick is due and `folds` holds, the next tick is the first one strictly after a horizon:

- `horizon = min(world.state.clock, earliest due_time of every other pending job that is not CLOCK_JOB and does not fold)`
- `next_tick_at = tick + (floor((horizon - tick) / tick_every) + 1) * tick_every`, using checked `add`

If that tick is at or before the target, the existing `crossed` / `next` / `tick` path re-runs the job as a sub-step after the other job. The predicate is then re-read against the new pool. If it is past the target, one successor is written.

The horizon is required because `boundary()` protects only elapsed. A Sleep or a long single advance reaches this path with the other job still ahead of it.

`job.ts` has a `size: allow 45` budget on `runStatus`. Put `folds` and the jump in helpers beside `amount`.

## Rulings

**R1. Stop rule (trap 1).** `boundary()` treats a folding job like `CLOCK_JOB`. Host and kernel call the same predicate. A divergence, where the host skips a job the kernel does not fold, makes the drain run one sub-step per tick and fault `budget_exceeded` at `due_jobs_per_advance`. Today's direct month advance survives with one need at 720 sub-steps; two needs would be 1,440 and over the 1024 the comment at `runtime/proposal_hours.ts:14` names (confirm the value in `LIMITS`).

**R2. When a fold must stop (trap 2).** It never crosses any of these:

| Case | Why it stops |
|---|---|
| A tick that changes a pool | predicate clause 3 fails, so it runs at its exact time |
| A fatal tick | `fatal` needs `by < 0` (`job.ts:122`), so clause 3 fails and `fatalTick` runs at its exact due time |
| A pool that can move by itself | clause 4 |
| A `status_ticked` listener | clause 5 |
| Any other pending job (schedule, population, a second status that is not saturated) | host: `boundary()`; kernel: the horizon |

Status bands and narration need no rule of their own: a saturated tick crosses no band, and `by ? say(...)` at `job.ts:83` tells nothing. A saturated tick draws no RNG and writes no fact, so no `fact_changed` arises.

A hp tick folds only at its saturated bound, such as a pool with minimum 1 or a gain at the maximum.

*Known limit, not equivalent to job-by-job play:* the calendar job. It stays "never a stop" and fires once in the step that passes it, at that step's target (`mechanics/schedule/daily.ts` `runClock`), which is the existing rule at `docs/system/mechanics.md:2260`. Today the status stops make it fire once per tick step, so this fix reduces firings during an absence to the same one-per-step rule an absence with no pending jobs already gets. A `clock_hour` reaction therefore reads the state at the target, and one that writes the drained pool or cures the status lands later than in job-by-job play. Pending PM confirmation below.

**R3. Save, events and determinism (trap 3).** There is **no protocol change**: no count field, no new event type, no receipt or delta shape change.

- A folded run writes what one tick writes today: `job.complete`, a `status.transition`, a `job.schedule` (or a sub-step), and one `status_ticked` at the due time. It writes no `resource.adjust`.
- Keeping one event means a single saturated tick stays byte-identical to today, so recorded elapsed traces, each ending at the next job, keep their bytes. Stop and ask if they do not.
- Nothing consumes the event when clause 5 holds. Confirm by grep that `status_ticked` has no consumer other than reaction dispatch (`mechanics/status/fatal.ts` and `contracts.gen.ts` were the other hits; stop if a quest objective or trace reader counts it).
- RNG is untouched; ids stay deterministic: one job id and one event id per run. Replay and receipts are the existing path.
- 1.130 is needed because a multi-tick advance at a bound now has a different receipt.

**Both kernels (Candidate C, `AGENTS.md:27`).** Execution is TypeScript only: status@1 story rules are `portable_capability`, no Elixir host adapter changes, so the `bin/contracts.exs:125` trigger is n/a. Elixir takes only the compiler refusal.

**R4. Player log (trap 4).** No Book change.

- After a month in `needs_sampler` the player's log holds the tick lines already told: 10 for hunger, 10 for thirst, then nothing, since saturated ticks are already silent (`job.ts:83`).
- With `time_policy.recap_after_minutes` authored (showcase: 30; `needs_sampler`: none) the recap groups them as one collapsed "While you were away" entry with " (10 times)" (`docs/system/book-ui.md:865`).
- The recap is only a grouping of receipt narration, with no save or receipt change (`docs/system/mechanics.md:2509`). The Character page shows the present band.

**R5. Checker (trap 5).** In `lib/loka/content/status.ex` (reaction steps; check `lib/loka/content/spells.ex` effect steps too), refuse a status with `duration: "permanent"` and `per_tick` when a `status.apply` names `item`, `room` or `tag`.

The other holder route is the default subject (`holdersOf`, `mechanics/reaction.ts:291-313`): the event's subject, which can be an item or a room on a status event. Refuse that default too when the trigger is `status_applied`, `status_ticked` or `status_expired`. `steps.ex:32` already keeps a scripted action to `npc` and `status`; `edible.applies` lands on the eater.

Diagnostic: existing `SCHEMA_VIOLATION`, `%{"error" => "invalid_value"}`, at `steps[i].<key>` (at `steps[i].status` for the default subject), the shape at `lib/loka/content/reactions.ex:128-134`. No new code.

**No sampler is hit:** the only ticking permanents are the showcase's `hungry` and `thirsty`, applied through `reactions/needs_enter.json` on bodies. Non-ticking permanents (`withered`, `ruin` and others) stay legal. Before coding, grep `kernel/ts` for the kgd.50 permanent hp-maximum refusal: W8 says both kernels refuse it (`docs/system/mechanics.md:2405`). If a TypeScript load check exists, mirror this one there; if not, compiler only and say so in the handback. `job.ts:114` keeps its item branch, since timed item statuses exist.

## Spec to amend first (`docs/system/mechanics.md`)

Own commit before code.

| Line | Change |
|---|---|
| 2053 (row 1) | saturated permanent ticks fold; state the predicate and horizon; the job-rows sentence |
| 2274 (G3 Events) | "Every due tick emits" becomes "a folded run of saturated ticks emits one" |
| 2407 (W8 Catch-up) | replace the one-step-per-tick text with the fold and its bound |
| 723-724 | `boundary` known limit: every pending job except calendar and folding jobs |
| 2260 (`clock_hour`) | the "about five" known limit no longer holds for folded permanents; state the R2 limit |

Also `docs/system/cartridge.md` status declarations: the R5 refusal. Check `docs/system/protocol.md` status composition and `docs/system/save.md:1155` Status recovery: a row whose `next_tick_at` jumped must still validate. Both should need no change; stop if they do.

## Scope

**In:**
- `kernel/ts/src/mechanics/status/job.ts`: `runStatus(world, command, job_id, job, mint, now, carried)`, `amount(visit, body, spec)`, new `folds`
- `mobile/authority/local-story/elapsed.ts`: `boundary(s, target)`
- `kernel/ts/src/runtime/world.ts:108` and derived bump files
- `lib/loka/content/status.ex`: `check/4`, `status/5` (and `spells.ex` if R5 needs it)
- `mobile/authority/local-story/permanent_tick.test.ts`; one invalid row per check in the compiler's `test/loka` suite
- `docs/system/mechanics.md`, `docs/system/cartridge.md`

**Out:**
- `kernel/ts/src/runtime/proposal.ts` and `proposal_hours.ts` (the existing crossed path is reused)
- `protocol/` schemas, except the version bump
- Timed statuses; statuses on regenerating pools; recurring non-status jobs
- Book UI; the showcase; a catch-up cap; pruning of finished job rows

## Acceptance

Fixture: `needs_sampler` patched in the test as `permanent_tick.test.ts:36-38` does, with `thirsty` also permanent. Entering east applies both at `t0`. `hunger` and `thirst` are 0 to 10, start 10, -1 every 3600. `hp` minimum 1, start 10. Drive through `ClockDriver` (see `death.test.ts`), so `boundary` is under test; the existing direct `story.elapsed` call never reaches it. `MONTH = 2592000`, target `t0 + MONTH + 1`. Counts are deltas from just before catch-up. If another sampler job adds a step, stop and report rather than adjusting the literal.

| # | Case | Engine | Expected (hand-computed) |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | month, both needs | `elapsed.ts:67`, `job.ts:79-84` | 11 elapsed receipts: 10 at `t0+3600k` (k = 1..10) and 1 to the target |
| A2 | same, rows | `job.ts:51,82` | +33 job rows: 22 status, 11 calendar |
| A3 | same, events | `job.ts:67` | 22 `status_ticked` (11 per need), 11 `clock_hour` |
| A4 | same, final state after cold reopen | `save.md:1155` | hunger 0, thirst 0, hp 10; both rows `next_tick_at = t0 + MONTH + 3600` (the last tick is `t0+720*3600`) |
| A5 | same, log | `job.ts:83` | tick line of each need exactly 10 times; none after `t0+36000` |
| A6 | exact boundary | `job.ts:79-84` | target `t0+36000`: pools 0, `next_tick_at` `t0+39600`. Target `t0+36001`: same. Target `t0+39600`: pools 0, one more `status_ticked` per need, `next_tick_at` `t0+43200` |
| A7 | fold beside a moving job | horizon | below |
| A8 | fatal in catch-up | `job.ts:122`, `fatal.ts` | hp minimum patched to 0, permanent -1 hp every 3600: first death at exactly `t0+36000`, not at the target |
| A9 | compiler refusals | `status.ex` | `SCHEMA_VIOLATION` at each path in R5 |

**A7 hand trace.** Add a permanent `+1 hunger every 5000`, hunger start 0, applied at `t0` by the same reaction; no ties before `t0+90000`. Hunger:

| Time after `t0` | 3600 | 5000 | 7200 | 10000 | 10800 | 14400 | 15000 | 18000 | 20000 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hunger | 0 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 1 |

Expected **1** at `t0+20000`, through both the driver and one direct `story.elapsed` advance. A fold that ignores the other job gives 4.

## Tests (each names its break)

Add to `permanent_tick.test.ts`:

- **Month, A1-A5.** Breaks: `boundary` still stops at a saturated job (720 steps, hence unbounded rows), or a fold drops a pool change.
- **Equivalence.** Same fixture, two saves: the driver versus a separate `story.elapsed` to each due time for 48 hours, target `t0+172801`. A one-tick `until` is job-by-job play by construction, so production needs no flag. Compare status rows (active, `next_tick_at`), resources, clock and rng, not job ids or event lists. Literal check: pools 0, `next_tick_at` `t0+176400`. Breaks: an off-by-one in the jump or a pool write in the fold.
- **Horizon, A7.** Breaks: the kernel jumps past another job, or the host stops only for non-status jobs.
- **Listener.** Add a reaction on `status_ticked` for `hungry` that adjusts a counter fact; run 48 hours. Expected counter 48. Breaks: clause 5 removed (a fold would swallow firings). This is the red control for the predicate.
- **Regenerating pool.** Patched permanent `-100 mv every 3600` for 3 hours, target `t0+10801`: mv equals the job-by-job comparator, by hand 0. A fold that ignores clause 4 gives about 36. Breaks: clause 4 removed.
- **Fatal, A8.** Breaks: a fold or jump past the fatal point.
- **Save (trap 6).** On the month fixture with real SQLite:
  - `coldReopen(path, bundle)` after catch-up
  - a real failed COMMIT on the folded step (`PRAGMA max_page_count` clamp, `docs/lessons/storage.md:6`), not a discarded success: fenced, then retry gives A4
  - a lost acknowledgement on the folded step: reconcile gives one receipt and A4
  - receipt replay: byte-identical
  
  Report these in the handback with the existing suites' results and one red control (`docs/WORKFLOW.md:215`). No persisted field is new, so no forged-row control applies. Per the brief kit, run every test that compiles a sampler.

**Compiler.** One invalid row in `test/loka` per path: `item`, `room`, `tag`, default subject on `status_ticked`. Add one valid row: ticking permanent on a body, and non-ticking permanent on an item. Each new check gets a red control.

**Red control for the host/kernel link:** remove the `folds` call from `runStatus` only; the month test must fail on `budget_exceeded` or on the literal counts. Record it in the handback.

## Mutants (beyond `bin/mutate_diff.sh`)

| Mutant | Killed by |
|---|---|
| `boundary` drops the `folds` carve-out | month (A1) |
| `runStatus` drops the jump, `boundary` keeps the carve-out | host/kernel red control |
| `by === 0` becomes "any tick" | equivalence (pools) |
| clause 4 removed | regenerating pool |
| clause 5 removed; filter match inverted | listener |
| clause 1 allows timed rows | existing timed tests (`thirsty` expiring at its day, `needs_sampler`) |
| horizon omits other jobs | A7 |
| `floor(...) + 1` becomes `floor(...)` | A6 |
| fold writes no event | A3 |
| checker `item`, `room`, `tag`, default subject each removed | compiler rows |
| checker refuses non-ticking permanents | valid compiler row |

## Composition record

- **Consumer:** elapsed catch-up (`ClockDriver`) and every advance's job drain.
- **Reads:** active status row, status spec, pool level and spec, reactions' `on`, pending jobs.
- **Writes:** existing `job.complete`, `status.transition`, `job.schedule`; events: existing `status_ticked`. Save rows: none new.
- **Reused:** the `CLOCK_JOB` carve-out, the crossed/`carried` sub-step, `amount`, `statusHolder`.
- **New:** `folds`; one compiler refusal.

## Realm checklist

1. Actor: n/a, no command or actor read; a job's holder comes from its row.
2. Reactions: met; no new trigger, and a listener turns the fold off.
3. Credit: n/a.
4. Time: met; no device clock, logical units only, no skip (the clock reaches the same target; only no-op ticks fold).
5. Scope: met; `status_ticked` stays instance-scoped, no new fact.
6. Text: n/a; `speech@1` unchanged.
7. Ownership: n/a.
8. Trust: met; receipts are computed by this authority, nothing new is imported.
9. Instancing: n/a.

## Stop and ask

- Any change to a `cartridges/*/transcripts` replay or a `protocol/fixtures/*_sampler_hash.json`. Replay all of them **before** writing the fold's code and again after.
- A protocol or schema change beyond the version bump; a new event field.
- `status_ticked` has a consumer other than reaction dispatch.
- `save.md` Status recovery or a composer check refuses a jumped `next_tick_at`.
- `needs_sampler` hunger or thirst has `gain` or `regen`, or A1-A3 literals do not hold (report the trace, do not fit the numbers).
- A sampler trips the R5 refusal.

## Pending PM rulings (edit in place when ruled)

1. **`clock_hour` during a fold.** Brief assumes the R2 known limit (one firing per step, as `mechanics.md:2260` already states). Alternative: a stop at each calendar job is exact but keeps one step per logical hour, so no gain for the showcase or `needs_sampler`.
2. **Regenerating pools stay unbounded.** A permanent drain on a `regen` or `gain` pool, or one with a `status_ticked` listener, still costs one step per tick. Brief assumes a known limit in the W8 clause, no cap and no refusal.
3. **Other recurring jobs.** Schedules and similar still stop catch-up, so the showcase's real month (36,000 logical hours at rate 50) stays long by that cause. The developer measures a showcase week's step count, reports it in the handback and asserts nothing. Likely a follow-up before loka-g5hh if the prologue has schedules.

## PM rulings on the drafter's open points

1. `clock_hour` stays never-a-stop, as today. State in the spec that an hourly reaction writing a folded pool is not job-by-job equal; no shipped content does this, and you confirm that.
2. Regenerating or listened-to pools stay unbounded: a known limit, written in the spec. No cap.
3. Schedules still stop catch-up. Measure the showcase month with both needs active (steps, rows, save growth, wall time) and put the numbers in the PR; do not change schedules. A result still above about one minute of catch-up or 50 MB goes to the PM as a finding, with its cause.

title: regen_hash_fixture: also re-pin the cartridge transcripts' content hash
description: Evidence 2026-10-24: #464 changed the showcase hash (lever text); the 7 toolbox_showcase transcripts kept the old hash and hosted kernel failed ('no known answer for toolbox_showcase', transcripts.test.ts:35) after local checks passed.
notes:
2026-10-29 PM: raised to P1. In C3 every parallel slice merge (C, A, V) conflicted in ~30-50 transcript/value-fixture hashes that regen does not re-pin; each cost a developer 20-30 min of scripted re-pinning.
BRIEF loka-tb31 (PM 2026-10-29; folds loka-gsgj). Lane: Hosted PR ([lanes](docs/WORKFLOW.md#delivery-lanes)); branch housekeeping/tb31-regen-hashes from origin/main, worktree ../worktrees.noindex/tb31 (bin/worktree_setup.sh). Model Opus. Handoff threshold: ~220k context, then hand back partial (WORKFLOW Token hygiene). Kit: docs/guides/brief-kit.md. Lessons: docs/lessons/contracts.md, docs/lessons/checks.md.

GOAL: after any cartridge/lib change or a merge of two branches that both moved hashes, `sh bin/regen.sh` alone leaves every compiled known-answer fixture and every transcript pin current, so nobody re-pins by hand.

FACTS (PM checked at main 9e4ce12d6):
- bin/regen.sh:24-37 only re-pins fixtures whose keys are exactly [description, canonical, sha256]; 48 of the 49 protocol/fixtures/*_hash.json carry `value` too (value == decoded canonical in all 48), so today regen re-pins only toolbox_showcase_hash.json. bin/regen_hash_fixture.sh refuses `value` (loka-gsgj).
- Transcript pin: cartridges/*/transcripts/*.jsonl (53 files) carry ids.content_hash on every line; kernel/ts/test/transcripts.test.ts:28-37 needs a fixture whose manifest id == the cartridge dir and sha256 == the pin. regen substitutes old->new only when it rewrote that fixture in this run; after a merge the transcript can hold either side's stale hash, so substitution by "old" misses it.
- Not every fixture is a compile of a current cartridge: sampler_v006..v010 are historical frozen inputs and containers_* are derived by test/loka/cartridge_containers_hash.py from them; several fixtures share a manifest id (cellar_sampler, items_sampler, locks_sampler, reward_storage). capability_lock_hash.json is the capability lock, not a cartridge. Find each fixture's real source (test/loka/cartridge_cross_kernel_test.exs and the other readers) before deciding what regen rebuilds.

DO:
1. regen_hash_fixture.sh accepts the optional `value` key and rewrites it from the new canonical (key order kept). Keep its refusals (other shapes, hash != sha256 of canonical).
2. regen.sh rebuilds every fixture that is a compile of a current source when its inputs changed (same `touched` gate), including value-carrying ones; derived fixtures (containers_*) are re-derived from their generator after their inputs; historical frozen ones stay untouched. If the capability lock fixture has a generator, run it when its inputs change; if not, leave it and say so.
3. Transcript pins: set each transcript's content_hash to its cartridge's current known answer (the fixture matched as transcripts.test.ts matches it, or the freshly compiled hash), whatever stale value it holds now; not only an old->new substitution of this run.
4. Merge recipe: one line in the regen.sh header and in docs/lessons/checks.md (or wherever the existing re-pin lesson lives; fix it, don't add a second): on a conflict only in hash fixtures/transcript pins, take either side and run bin/regen.sh.
5. Update bin/regen.sh's header comment ("fixtures that also carry `value` are rebuilt by hand" goes).

OUT OF SCOPE: re-recording transcripts whose replay bytes change; mutate.sh (loka-tafk); C4 renames.
ACCEPTANCE:
- A test (existing regen_hash_fixture test layer if there is one; LOKA_COMPILED exists for that) on a controlled value-carrying fixture: value and sha256 rewritten, description kept; red control: revert the value handling and watch it fail.
- Controlled demo in your scratch worktree, reported in the handback (not committed): change one sampler's text (e.g. a room description in a cartridge that has a value fixture and transcripts), set one of its transcripts to a third unrelated 64-hex hash, run bin/regen.sh, then the kernel transcripts test and the Elixir hash-fixture tests pass with no hand edit. Revert the content change.
- bin/regen.sh on the clean branch rewrites nothing (prepush idempotence).
- Focused checks only (bash_guard refuses full suites); hosted CI on the head is the gate.
SCOPE TRIGGER (stop and ask): a fixture whose source you cannot identify; any change to protocol/ schemas or kernel code; a regen run that changes replay bytes.
Handback per .claude/agents/developer.md with check table and /code-review medium result.
2026-10-29 PM: #499 handed back b6cfa7390 (CI green). Open for fix round with review findings: hard-coded hashes in lantern_proof.test.ts:29, lantern.test.ts:387, story_points.test.ts (ferry) should read the fixture's sha256; bin/merge_resolve.py GENERATED should list the compiled fixtures. title: Liquid log line binds its vessel so the Book can word the new level (loka-ikat follow-up)
description: Follow-up of loka-ikat (owner 2026-10-30: vessel amounts in words in the Book). Fill/Pour/Drink log lines now show only their sentence; they cannot name the vessel's new level because the engine line (kernel/ts/src/mechanics/liquid/shared.ts:166-180) carries the amount moved and no vessel id. Add a vessel_id (and resulting quantity) binding to that line so the Book can write e.g. "You drink. The waterskin is half full." using mobile/app/book/pick.ts liquidWords. Engine/protocol: leaves the polish session.
notes:
BRIEF loka-tc2e (drafted 2026-10-30). Kit: docs/guides/brief-kit.md (read once; not copied). Handoff threshold: docs/WORKFLOW.md#token-hygiene (~220k).

GOAL. The fill/pour/drink log line binds its vessel and that vessel's resulting level, so the Book can write "You drink. The waterskin is half full." Owner source: loka-ikat (vessel amounts in words).
Size S. Lane: Hosted PR. Branch feat/liquid-vessel-line from main. Developer Opus. kernel_api 1.122.

ENGINE THAT MAKES IT POSSIBLE. kernel/ts/src/mechanics/liquid/shared.ts:166-182 `liquidNarration(world, type, kind, quantity)` -> one Text `{key: liquid.<type>, bindings: {kind, unit_label, quantity}}` with no vessel; :140-164 `consumePlan` and the transition ops (`change(world, id, kind, newQuantity)` at :157-160; drink via `serving` :129) already hold the vessel's new quantity; :184-196 `liquidPayload` names the ids (fill: vessel_id; pour: source_id, receiver_id; drink: vessel_id); kernel/ts/src/mechanics/liquid/rule.ts:14-20 the only caller. Capacity: `world.liquidSpecs[id].capacity` (shared.ts:39-43). Text contract: protocol/text.schema.json:36-95 (`participants` EntityIds; `bindings` TextKey | integer | boolean): no schema change.
CHANGE. `liquidNarration` gains `participants: { vessel }` and bindings `remaining` (the vessel's quantity after the op, read from the transition's op for that vessel, never recomputed) and `capacity`. The vessel named: fill and drink -> `vessel_id`; pour -> `receiver_id` (where the liquid went; the source's level stays on its own page; drafter's choice, designer may reword). Pass what rule.ts:13 already has (the payload and `result.ops`); no new query. Spec: docs/system/mechanics.md B7 well and waterskin contract (:1155) one sentence: each liquid line binds `vessel` with `remaining` and `capacity` (cite loka-tc2e). world.ts:108 and cartridges/toolbox_showcase/cartridge.json:8 -> 1.122; bin/regen_hash_fixture.sh. Elixir: n/a (no line projection in lib/loka). Transcripts record no narration (checked cartridges/toolbox_showcase/transcripts/liquid.jsonl): none re-recorded.
Files in: mechanics/liquid/shared.ts, mechanics/liquid/rule.ts (if the signature changes), kernel/ts/test/liquid.test.ts (+ liquid_fixture.ts:65-67 text keys only if needed), docs/system/mechanics.md, runtime/world.ts:108, cartridge.json:8, protocol/fixtures/toolbox_showcase_hash.json. Out: view/liquid.ts, protocol/, mobile/ (consumer not on main), services (provider-owned `serving` callers).

ACCEPTANCE (literal; the test pins hand-checked integers from the fixture's capacity and serving size, never values computed by the code under test; the kit's boundary rule applies).
1. Fill a vessel holding 1 of capacity 4 from a source holding 10: bindings {kind, unit_label, quantity: 3, remaining: 4, capacity: 4}, participants {vessel: <that vessel>}.
2. Drink one serving s from a vessel at 4: quantity s, remaining 4 - s, capacity 4, vessel = the vessel drunk from.
3. Pour from a vessel at 3 into a receiver at 1 of capacity 3: quantity 2, remaining 3, capacity 3, vessel = the receiver (not the source).
4. A pour that moves nothing stays `invalid_state` (shared.ts:155) with no line.
5. Existing liquid tests unchanged except the line assertions.
RED CONTROLS: bind `quantity` as `remaining` -> row 1 fails (3 != 4); bind the source on pour -> row 3 fails; drop `capacity` -> rows 1-3 fail.

SHOWCASE USE. No content change: the waterskin and cask (cartridges/toolbox_showcase/items/cask.json:13-19 capacity 3, doses) and the existing `liquid.filled/poured/drank` lines (text.json:948-952) are the use; the Book names the vessel from the entity's projected name.
BOOK CONSUMER + STORY (follow-up for the polish session; `amountWords`/`liquidWords` live only on polish/session-2026-10-23, mobile/app/book/pick.ts:29-41, not on main): in `lineWords` (mobile/app/book/words.ts), a line with `participants.vessel` appends ` The <vessel name> is <amountWords(remaining, capacity, kind)>.`, designer words it; story Book/LogLines "Vessel level" there. This slice adds nothing under mobile/; say so in the handback.
LESSONS: docs/lessons/mechanics.md. SCOPE TRIGGER: a caller of `liquidNarration` outside liquid/rule.ts, a line needing both vessels (pour), or any schema change.
SHARED FILES: none with loka-ysbt/oc5i/548k except world.ts:108, cartridge.json:8, the hash fixture. Parallel-safe with every other slice.
