title: Research: local AI in the mobile app (familiar companion, NPC dialogue, subtle LLM uses)
description:
Research (Fable, future, no code): where on-device AI could fit the mobile app. Owner ideas (paraphrased): AI-voiced NPCs; a companion players can ask about the game; an LLM-forward design where a companion or "familiar" records all events and replaces the Journal, answering questions like a chat; other ways LLMs make play more immersive but not intrusive or overt.

Questions: (1) which ideas fit the kernel's rules: deterministic replay, owner-save bytes, receipts as the record of truth, one difficulty, fixed time; where an LLM can only phrase or retrieve, never decide or write durable state; (2) the familiar as a view over receipts and knowledge rows (retrieval, no new save data) vs a stored memory; spoiler and hallucination guards (answers cite events the player saw); (3) NPC dialogue: free text over authored dialogue graphs (intent mapping to existing choices) vs generated lines bounded by cartridge facts; (4) on-device model options for iOS and Android in an Expo/React Native app (size, latency, battery, licence), and a no-model fallback so the game is complete without it; (5) other subtle uses (narration variety on W7, hint phrasing on W23, accessibility, recap on reopen); (6) risks and a smallest first experiment. Output: a ranked list with cost, fit and risk, plus the first experiment; plain English.
close_reason: delivered: ranked research in the 2026-10-10 comment; build rows when mobile resumes

title: Worktree browser checks: Metro cannot resolve expo through linked node_modules; walkthrough harness loads a blank page
description: Session 2026-10-15: FD7 Book developer had to copy node_modules for the browser check; Built S2 developer got a blank page from the walkthrough harness (ashmere walk too); word bar S3 shipped without screenshots. Related loka-wxu, loka-nxg2. Fix bin/worktree_setup.sh or the preview so a slice worktree can run the browser interaction.
notes:
Owner approved 2026-10-15 ("go with your recs").
BRIEF 2026-10-15 (PM): Hosted PR, branch infra/uh5u-worktree-browser from origin/main, worktree ../worktrees.noindex/uh5u. Goal: a fresh slice worktree after bin/worktree_setup.sh can run the Book browser interaction (web preview at 390 px plus a screenshot, and the walkthrough harness) without copying node_modules. Evidence: Metro cannot resolve expo through linked node_modules; the walkthrough harness loads a blank page. Find the root cause (symlinked node_modules vs Metro's resolver and watchFolders, or the harness URL/port). Fix it in bin/worktree_setup.sh, Metro config or the harness, smallest change. Acceptance: in a new scratch worktree, setup then one documented command serves the Book and takes a 390 px screenshot of a sampler room. Add a check or a documented smoke step only if cheap. Never kill the owner's preview servers (:6006, :19006 in the lokacore-preview worktree); use other ports; stop only PIDs you started. Timebox 90 minutes: at the limit, hand back findings. Related loka-wxu, loka-nxg2 (do not fix unless trivially the same cause). Handback under 150 words: PR, head, root cause, the command, a screenshot path, open items.
HANDBACK #397 infra/uh5u-worktree-browser head aca5b019: root cause linked node_modules (Metro cannot resolve expo outside worktree; SQLite worker URL 404 -> blank). Fix: worktree_setup.sh APFS clone of main node_modules (about 8 s). Command: bin/loka dev cartridges/<sampler> then mobile/app LOKA_WALK=<sampler> npm run walkthrough. Screenshot verified by PM. Open: .cache copied; developer.md:20 says links; older worktrees rerun setup.

title: Authoring readiness before the Pro plan: tools the owner builds the game with
description:
# Pre-downgrade audit: what to do on Opus/Fable before ~2026-11-10

Written 2026-10-31 by Fable, read-only on the repo and Beads. Scope per the owner's three
instructions: (1) the authoring tools of PR #530 (`tools/authoring`, head 1f54a3e8f) first, audited as
the owner would use them; (2) the engine, mechanics, docs and process in general, the prologue
outline used only as one example consumer; (3) nothing proposed may have an agent write prose.

Method: a detached throwaway worktree on `origin/tools/authoring` (removed afterwards); real runs under
`nice -n 10`: `bin/loka new` for a cartridge and 21 kinds, `mix loka.compile` on seven realistic
mistakes, a `.scene` file with four mistakes, `bin/loka todo`, `mix loka.lint`, headless `bin/loka play`;
code read for the panel and watcher (browser flows not driven). Paths are on `main` unless marked
`(branch)`. Size: S under half a day of one session, M one to two sessions, L more. "Engine" means
`kernel/`, `lib/`, `protocol/`, `schemas/`, `mobile/authority/`: it needs a fresh reviewer under the lean
default; "tools/docs" needs none.

Already queued, not repeated: #535 (loka-sgqk), #530 itself, loka-g5hh.2, loka-gj82.1, #532.

---

## A. Authoring tools (rank 1 to 13)

### A1. Compiler errors in plain words, with file:line and what to do (M, engine: `lib/`)

Evidence. `mix loka.compile` prints each diagnostic as one JSON line (`lib/mix/tasks/loka.compile.ex:17,21`).
The watcher's `plain()` (branch `kernel/ts/play/author.ts:46-60`) only lowercases the code and appends
`data`, so the panel shows e.g. `error at npcs/bram.hp: schema violation (error "invalid_type")`. Observed on
real mistakes:

| Mistake | What the writer reads | Missing |
|---|---|---|
| unknown field in a room | `UNKNOWN_FIELD path rooms/boathouse.typo_field, data {}` | the valid fields, the line |
| `"hp": "lots"` on an NPC | `SCHEMA_VIOLATION data {"error":"invalid_type"}` | expected type, line |
| text key deleted | `UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE target room.drowned_lantern.title` | "add it to text.json or change the name" |
| half-written JSON | `INVALID_JSON data {}` | line and column |
| `gives: trowel` in a scene (the guide's own example) | `OUTCOME_MISMATCH data {}` plus `UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE target trowel` | that the NPC must hold the item and the cartridge must lock `item_acquired` (`lib/loka/content/dialogues.ex:307-317`) |
| duplicate choice, `narrator:` line, second speaker in a `.scene` | `SCHEMA_VIOLATION data {line, text}` x3 | why each line is bad |
| `when: never_defined` in a `.scene` | nothing (hidden behind the errors above) | the unknown fact |
| layout older than the room list | `SCHEMA_VIOLATION path layout, data {}` | "run `bin/loka new layout` again" |

Also: passes stop at the first failing pass, so the unknown field hid the bad exit until fixed (two
compiles to see two errors). The branch's spec promises `severity: file:line message`
(`docs/system/cartridge.md`, Author preview, branch) and the guide shows
`error: rooms/cellar.json:12 unknown exit target "well"` (`docs/guides/writing-the-game.md`, branch):
neither is what the code produces.

Proposal. One message catalog in Elixir keyed by the ~40 codes, each with a sentence and a
fix hint, and `data` filled at every `diag(...)` site (expected type or enum, the nearest valid key,
the referenced target's kind); a JSON line index so `path` becomes `file:line`; collect errors across
passes where a pass can continue. The watcher prints the catalog text instead of the code.

Why now. Touching every diagnostic site in `lib/loka/content/*.ex` (75 files) and wording 40 codes
is one Opus pass; a cheap model cannot infer what `OUTCOME_MISMATCH` means and will guess.

### A2. The `.scene` format covers a fraction of a conversation (M to L, engine: `lib/`)

Evidence. `lib/loka/content/scene_files.ex` (branch) lowers exactly: `npc:`, `when: <bool fact>`, a
prompt line, `- choice`, a reply, `gives:`. A dialogue choice in JSON also carries `accept`,
`hand_over`, `payment`, `patrol`, `story_point`, a `check`, `receive`, `steps` (fact, quest, status,
item ops; `docs/BUILDERS-GUIDE.md:25-37`). So every conversation that sets a fact, accepts or resolves a
quest, branches a second level, has two speakers, a narration line, a one-shot, or a condition per
choice goes back to JSON. In the outline that is most of them (a leaning choice recorded as a fact at
beats 15, 24, 42, 43; the Rite offers; every quest turn-in).

Proposal. Extend the lowering only (no runtime): per choice `sets: <fact> [<value>]`,
`needs: <fact>`, `quest: accept|resolve <key>`, `then: <dialogue key>`, `once`; `* narration` lines;
nested `- ` choices by indent; a second speaker as `<npc>:` after a `with: <npc>` header; and
`scenes/<key>.cut` for a cutscene (one narrate per paragraph, `---` as await_ack, end), since scenes
are JSON-only today (starter: `scenes/awakening.json`, trigger = quest outcome). Keep the
byte-identical gate on a sampler re-expression.

Why now. Grammar and pass-ordering in `Loka.Content.Source` are subtle; an Opus design pass with
tests leaves Sonnet a closed syntax to document, not design.

### A3. A new cartridge is not playable until the writer wires it by hand (S to M, engine: `lib/`)

Evidence. `bin/loka new cartridge` writes `rooms/start.json` with `"exits": {}`; `new rooms grove`
adds a room with no exit either way (`lib/loka/content/starters/templates.ex`, `room()`); `new npcs
thera` puts the NPC in `c["rooms"]`, the alphabetically first room (`grove`), not the entry; the
populations starter wired its camp to `grove` for the same reason. Headless, after 21 starters and a
clean compile (1.4 s): the game opens on `~ / Exits: none`, `look` answers "You can't do that here",
Thera is unreachable. `new layout` must be rerun after every room or the compile fails (A1 table).

Proposal. `new rooms <name> [--from <room> <dir>]` writes both exits; `new npcs|items` default to the
entry room; the compiler or the watcher regenerates `layout.json` rows for rooms it lacks (drop the
manual rerun); `bin/loka new` ends with one line of what to fill and the next command.

### A4. Checkpoints as the content test; stop the Start-over prompt (M, engine: `kernel/ts/play`)

Evidence. A jump calls `startOver()` (branch `mobile/app/author/panel.tsx:107-115`), which asks the
player's destructive confirm (`mobile/app/App.tsx:105` `window.confirm(startOverAsk)`), so every jump
is a dialog. A checkpoint that an earlier edit breaks says `step 4 refused` and the writer replays by
hand. Nothing replays checkpoints headless; the per-scene regression test the lean default expects
("the affected walkthrough", `docs/WORKFLOW.md` Lean default) is a hand-written TypeScript walk
(`mobile/app/walkthrough/build_sampler.walk.ts`: regex taps), which a writer will not write.

Proposal. (a) In the author preview, jump without the confirm. (b) `bin/loka check <cartridge>`:
compile, open a local session, replay every `checkpoints/*.json` through `place.ts replay()` and print
per checkpoint "ok" or the first refused step in words; CI runs it for a real chapter. Content PRs on
Pro then ship with checkpoints, not walks. (c) A refused step offers "drop this step and continue".

Why now. The replay harness touches `mobile/authority/local-story/session.ts` and the kernel session;
it is engine work with a reviewer, and it is the test every later content PR leans on.

### A5. The panel shows almost no game state; nothing for balancing (S to M, tools)

Evidence. The Book posts only `facts`, `quests`, `steps` (branch `panel.tsx:129-135`); the panel's
State tab lists them (`tools/author-panel/src/sections.tsx:130-160`). No room, people present,
inventory, body pools and bands, statuses, clock or open choice. For numbers (hunger per tick, carry
limits, combat odds) there is nothing: they live in `cartridge.json world.*`, `resources.json`,
`statuses/*.json`, and the only reader is the headless sim (`kernel/ts/test/sim.ts --cartridge`).

Proposal. Post the GameView and show it (room, people, held, pools with bands, statuses, clock,
pending choice). A Numbers tab: every tunable with its file (reuse `sourceOf`, branch `live.ts:76`),
editable in place through the normal file write. A `bin/loka sim <cartridge> <seed>` summary line per
pool over game hours (one table) for pacing hunger and thirst.

### A6. Why tab and finding things (S, tools)

Evidence. Why needs a key the writer must know and prints raw JSON (`sections.tsx:163-188`). Alt-click
finds the first file holding the words (`live.ts:76-87`); there is no search, no "what references this
NPC, fact or item".

Proposal. Why offers the current room's actions and dialogues as a list and renders leaves as
sentences ("fact met_thera is false; needs true"). A Find box: key or words to every `file:line`, and
the reverse (who references `thera`) from the compiler's reference index (`lib/loka/content/leaf_refs.ex`).

### A7. Still to write misses `.scene` placeholders (S, tools)

Evidence. `todo.ts` filters `.json` only (branch `kernel/ts/play/todo.ts:46`); my scene's `thera: ~`
reply is absent from `bin/loka todo` and the panel. Already an open item in loka-kgd.194.23's notes;
confirmed. Also: the release refusal is by text key after lowering, so it does catch it (not verified).

### A8. Lint is invisible to the writer (S, tools)

Evidence. `mix loka.lint` gives good plain findings ("items/trowel.json: nothing takes it out of play",
"details.listen is a scripted action target and has no title") but neither the guide nor the panel
mentions or runs it. Proposal: run it after each successful compile and show the lines under the
Compile card.

### A9. Scene files: unknown fact and unknown speaker (S, fold into A1)

Evidence. `when: never_defined` produced no diagnostic in the same compile; a second speaker line is a
bare SCHEMA_VIOLATION. Proposal: the lowering checks the fact exists and names it; the speaker error
says "only `thera:` may speak here (`npc: thera`)".

### A10. Fix the guide's claims to match the code (S, docs)

Evidence. `writing-the-game.md` (branch) shows an error format and a `gives:` example that do not
work as shown (A1, A2); `cartridge.md` Author preview says `severity: file:line message`. Do this with
A1, on the same PR.

### A11. A dev-only "go to room" and "set fact" in the author preview (S, decision needed)

Evidence. The plan ruled "no state cheat; normal commands only" (loka-kgd.194.23 notes). Result: to
work on room 17 the writer replays 16 rooms of inputs, and every structural edit replays them again
(`author.ts:77-95`). Checkpoints help only while the path survives. Proposal: two dev-only commands
behind `?dev=1` that go through `invoke` as ordinary commands the release build refuses. Owner call.

### A12. Per-kind source reference generated from the schema (M, docs; loka-ivjq.9 in progress)

Evidence. The source schemas are `$ref`s into `schemas/source/defs.schema.json` (452 KB); the prose
references are `docs/system/mechanics.md` (3,840 lines) and `cartridge.md` (1,303). A Sonnet session
or the owner has no page that says, per kind, the fields, types, required-ness and meaning, nor one

# Brief: loka-vx2v engine half, quest offer target

**Goal.** A quest offer may name a fixture or NPC. The offer then draws on that page, never on World, and is neither listed nor admitted when the target is absent, dead or unseen. Bare offers keep working here; the content brief migrates the samplers and turns on the compiler refusal.

**Lane.** Hosted PR. Branch `engine/quest-offer-target`, worktree named after loka-vx2v. One PR with the content brief, which follows on this branch. Hand back after your push; the PM then spawns the content developer. Do not open a second PR.
**Rules.** [Brief kit](docs/guides/brief-kit.md), read once. Lessons: `docs/lessons/mechanics.md`, `docs/lessons/contracts.md`.
**Handoff threshold.** About 220k tokens: commit and hand back a state note (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`, token hygiene).
**Contract.** `kernel_api` 1.129 in `INSTALLED` only (`kernel/ts/src/runtime/world.ts:108`). loka-sgqk holds 1.130.

## Governing docs (spec first, same PR, first commit)

- `docs/system/mechanics.md:216-219`: a detail is also projected when a quest offer targets it. Replace "quest offers stay in `view.actions`" with: a targeted offer draws on its fixture's NoticeView or its NPC's entity entry, never in `view.actions`; only an untargeted offer (loader-level, compiler-refused) stays there. Keep the invariant name.
- `docs/system/mechanics.md:398`: `accept_quest {quest}` is admitted only while the offer's target is in the actor's room and alive (else `unsupported_capability`) and seen (else `invalid_state`). A dialogue choice's `accept` reads no offer target.
- `docs/system/protocol.md:67`, `:242`: the quest offer fills its quest and takes no target; offers listed only with a present target. Note the empty `target_ids` meaning (below).
- `docs/system/cartridge.md:556`: a quest's offer counts as reachable only if its target's room or NPC is reachable; policy still not evaluated. Add `offer.target` to the quest source docs, with the refusal the content brief enables.
- `docs/system/book-ui.md` Room page anatomy (`:33-56`): one sentence: a quest offer draws on its target's page, reading its authored label. Its "content must give it one" already rules.

## Rulings

- **Exact shapes, source and compiled:**
  `offer.target: {kind:'detail', room:<ref>, detail:<key>} | {kind:'npc', npc:<ref>}`. Optional in schema.
- **Key:** the quest key (for example `lantern`), unchanged.
- **Command:** `accept_quest {actor_id, quest}`, unchanged. `protocol/command.schema.json:700-719` is not touched. Precedent: `commands/actions.ts:39`, the action names its own target.
- **Ordered targets:** none, `target_ids: []`, for both kinds. `resolve` (`commands/invocation.ts:119`) already fills the quest. Any supplied target lands in no slot and `validate` rejects it (`unsupported_capability`, `invocation.ts:112`, `:124`).
- **Input:** none.
- **Why not `target_id`:** one invocation shape for both kinds; replay and every `target_ids: []` caller stay valid. The Book's NPC need is met by a projected empty list: `toButton` honours it (`mobile/app/book/buttons.ts:71`).
- **Shared admission (composition first):** `cartridge()` in `commands/actions.ts:135-141`, which both GameView (`resolved` at `view/action_lists.ts:65`) and execution (`resolved` at `actions.ts:238`, `invocation.ts:106`) read. description:

Also: make our own Tidewave-like element picker and delete Tidewave; screenshot baselines later.
Goal: Storybook as a long-haul UI tweaking environment. Batches: W1 process + scripts, H1 hardening (parallel with W1), P1 picker with live tweak loop (after W1), then live polish sessions. Max two agents at once (load).
Live polish session lane: session branch + worktree served to the owner's Storybook (HMR); each owner prompt from the picker is applied at once by a resumed Fable designer (style code, tokens, catalogue line); owner's look = design review; 'Close batch' -> one Opus reviewer quick pass + one pre-push hook -> PM merges; owner Storybook back to main. Mechanics/save/protocol/engine items leave the session as normal Beads issues. Batches stay open liberally; close only for critical items or too much complexity (PM may suggest closing in the picker panel).
notes:
Owner 2026-10-09 (paraphrased): use a lower model for small nits, Fable for overall design; PM decides. PM ruling: PM classifies each picker prompt. NIT (Sonnet designer): one place, existing tokens only: swap which token a style uses, alignment, a value inside one component, wording of a label. BRIEF (branch polish/x6t127-room-anatomy, Hosted PR draft):
# Brief: room anatomy remainder (loka-x6t.127)

**Handoff threshold: about 220k tokens** ([token hygiene](docs/WORKFLOW.md#token-hygiene)). If you pass it, stop and hand the remaining rows to a fresh agent with a short brief.
Common rules, handback and Realm checklist: [brief kit](docs/guides/brief-kit.md). Read it once; it is not copied here.

- **Branch:** `polish/x6t127-room-anatomy`, from `main`, in your own worktree.
- **Lane:** Hosted PR, opened as a draft ([delivery lanes](docs/WORKFLOW.md#delivery-lanes)).
- **Beads:** `loka-x6t.127`. Run `br show loka-x6t.127` for the owner calls. #464 already did the storylet card, the cue block and the unlinked entries.
- **Lessons:** `docs/lessons/mobile.md`.
- **Book UI rules:** [agent rules](docs/BOOK-UI-COMPONENTS.md#agent-rules-for-book-ui-code). Change doc comments, stories and labels in the same slice as the code.

## Goal

The World page draws the five parts of [room page anatomy](docs/system/book-ui.md#room-page-anatomy) (book-ui.md:25-45) and nothing else: title, description, people, items, log. Four leftovers break that today:

1. **Away recap.** It draws as a block above the description (pages.tsx:153). The owner, quoted in loka-x6t.127 (2026-10-23): "It should be a new entry in the event log, meaning at the very bottom, we do have the autoscroll stuff right?"

description: Showcase combat playtest (loka-y6yg.7) G1/G3/G4/G7. With 3-second pulses all of these behave (rounds log one by one; Flee and Eat succeed). The engine is right (due work before input, mechanics.md:212). Open question: why the web clock did not pulse. Candidates: (1) App.tsx:176 useElapsed pauses on AppState background, which on web follows document.visibilityState, so an occluded or unfocused Chrome window in the computer-use harness stops time; (2) the showcase is the first cartridge with recap_after, so the clock waits for booked (App.tsx:173, shell.subscribed in book/updates.ts:34); no stall found by reading, needs a live check. Fix: verify in a focused web tab (Combat page should log a round every 3 s); if (1), record it as a playtest harness rule (keep the tab visible); if (2), fix the booking order. Also consider: a refusal after a press-time catch-up should say what changed (designer, U3).

DESIGN INPUT (commit as docs/briefs/polish/design-input-p1-2026-10-09.md): # Design input: batch P1, Loka picker + polish panel (Beads loka-x6t.3)

Developer tool inside Storybook, not Book UI. Owner words and PM rulings: Beads loka-x6t,
loka-x6t.3; lane: [live polish session](../../WORKFLOW.md#live-polish-session).

## Separation rule

- The addon never imports `mobile/app/book/tokens.ts` or any `book/` module, and never adds a
  node to the story's layout: the preview overlay is `position: fixed`, max z-index,
  `pointer-events: none` except while picking. The Tidewave 74 px strip goes with Tidewave;
  stories get `100vh` back.
- Manager side (panel, toolbar) uses only `storybook/theming` roles (`theme.color.secondary`,
  `.positive`, `.warning`, `.negative`, `theme.textMutedColor`, `theme.appBorderColor`,
  `theme.background.app`, `theme.typography.size.s1/s2`, `.fonts.mono`). `manager.ts` already
  maps the base roles to the Book's light palette; positive/warning/negative stay Storybook's
  defaults, so status colour reads as tool, not page.
- Preview side (overlay) has no theme; it uses two plain values: `#1EA7FD` (Storybook blue,
  separate from every Book palette) and `#FFFFFF`. No other raw colour in the addon.

## 1. Picker overlay (preview iframe)

- **On/off.** Toolbar TOOL button "Pick" (crosshair icon, active state = `barSelectedColor`,
  like the viewport tool); key `P` (unused by Storybook; the preview forwards keydown).
  Turning Pick on opens the Polish panel if hidden. `Esc` clears the pending pick; a second
  `Esc` (nothing pending) turns Pick off. Pick stays on after a submit.
- **While picking** a transparent capture layer takes every pointer event: no click reaches
  the story (a tap would turn the page). Pick off = Storybook as today.
- **Hover.** Outline `2px solid #1EA7FD` at 60 % alpha, no fill, on the hovered element's
  border box (`getBoundingClientRect`, rounded). Label chip, 11 px `ui-monospace`, white on
  `#1EA7FD`, padding 2 px 6 px, radius 2 px, placed above the box's top-left (flipped to below
  when the box top < 20 px; clamped inside the 414 px viewport): `EntityLine › Tap · 382×28`.
  The chain is the React dev fiber owner chain, named components only (RNW `View`/`Text`/
  `Pressable` and Storybook decorators dropped), root-most first, at most 4 deep.
- **Click** pins the element: outline 2px solid 100 %, fill `#1EA7FD` at 12 %, chip gains the
  pick number `1`. **Shift-click** adds up to 4 elements (`2`..`4`); plain click replaces.
  Click on a pinned element unpins it.
- **No note box in the iframe.** The composer lives in the panel (section 2), which is full
  height beside a 414 px story, so nothing ever covers the picked element and a tall pick
  (whole Page) still works; the manager focuses the textarea on pick. The pinned outline stays
  until send or `Esc`.
- **Keys in the composer.** `Cmd/Ctrl+Enter` sends; `Enter` is a newline; `Esc` clears the
  pending pick and text. An element is optional: a feel request ("make it calmer") is text only.

## 2. Polish panel (manager addon panel, `panelPosition: 'right'`)

Set in `manager.ts`; Storybook keeps the owner's dragged width (no API for it). Tab title
`Polish`, with ` · n working` while n > 0. One column, top to bottom:

- **Header (sticky, 40 px).** Left: session pill, 12 px: green dot + branch name
  (`polish/2026-10-09`) when `bin/polish_session.sh` serves a session; grey dot + "No session ·
  picks go to Beads" otherwise. Right: **Close batch**, outline button 28 px high, only while a
  session runs. Click = inline confirm in the same row: "Close batch · 7 items?  Close  Cancel";
  disabled while any item is `working` (`polish_session.sh close` refuses a dirty tree).
- **Conversation (scrolls; newest at bottom; autoscroll only when already at bottom).**
  - Owner item: 3 px left rule in `theme.color.secondary`, padding 8 px 10 px.
    Row 1: element chip(s) (mono 12 px, `appBorderColor` border, 24×24 thumbnail at left) +
    story title in muted 12 px. Row 2: prompt, 14 px. Row 3 (12 px muted): status dot + word ·
    model badge · summary · short sha (mono). Clicking a chip re-pins that element in the
    composer (a follow-up). Clicking the thumbnail toggles the full crop at panel width.
  - Status words and dots: `received` hollow grey; `working` pulsing `secondary`; `done`
    `positive` + one-line summary + `abc1234`; `Beads loka-xxx` `warning` + reason;
    `stopped` `negative` + reason (agent could not, PM note). Model badge: `SONNET` / `FABLE`,
    10 px uppercase, 1 px border, no fill; shown from `working` on (the PM routes first).
  - PM message: full-width card, 1 px `warning` border, label `PM` in muted small caps, text
    ("suggest closing: review load is at 12 items"), buttons **Close batch** (opens the same
    inline confirm) and **Keep going** (dismisses). Any other PM note: same card with
    `appBorderColor`, no buttons.
  - Empty state (session running, no items), centred muted 12 px: "Press P or Pick, then click
    anything in the story. Shift-click adds elements. Type a feel request without picking."
  - No session: same list; new items show `queued for Beads`, then `Beads loka-xxx` after
    `/polish-intake`. Composer stays usable.
- **Composer (sticky bottom).** Pending chips row (each with ×), textarea 3 rows growing to 8,
  hint line 11 px muted "⌘↩ send · esc clear · ⇧click adds an element", **Send** button
  (primary). `fable:` / `quick:` are typed prefixes; no control for them.

## 3. Payload

| Owner sees in the item | Sent to the agent (queue JSON) only |
|---|---|
| prompt; element chain; W×H; thumbnail; story title; `light · iPhone 11` | note, pick id, time; story id; palette; viewport name + size; per element: chain, box (x y w h), computed padding/margin/font-family/size/line-height/colour/background, `innerText` (≤ 200 chars), accessible role + name, `data-testid` if any; crop PNG path (box + 24 px, device pixel ratio 2) |

The owner never sees computed styles or JSON; a `Copy JSON` affordance is not needed.

## Proposed checks (developer slice)

- ast-grep: no `import` from `book/` under the addon directory.
- Overlay off: the story's `#storybook-root` boxes are identical with the addon loaded and
  not (one smoke assertion).
- Raw colour literals in the addon: exactly the two overlay constants; the manager files use
  theme roles only.

## For the owner

1. Composer in the panel, not a floating note box over the story (so a pick never gets
   covered). OK?
2. `P` as the Pick key; `Esc` twice to leave Pick.
3. Close batch disabled while an item is `working` (PM can still close by hand).
4. Screenshot: if the in-page crop needs a small dependency (html-to-image), take it; a
   server-side re-render would not match a Live story.

title: Book: line when an NPC skips its combat turn (stunned)
description: From loka-kgd.98: a status that bars an NPC's attack skips its blow silently. Designer: words for the skipped turn (engine event or presenter line).
notes:

Today a held NPC's skipped turn writes nothing and emits no event (mechanics.md:2542).
Rule (recommend): the engine emits a skip event; the Book tells the status's optional authored narration.held line, else the words.ts default "<Name> does not strike." (same pattern as hostile refusal: optional authored key, else a Book default).
Where: Combat page log, each skipped turn.
Touches: kernel combat + event contract, words.ts, mechanics.md:2542, book-ui.md Combat.
Risk: kernel change: normal reviewer.
Cost: M engine + S Book + optional content.
Owner: A authored line with Book default (recommended), or B Book default only.
OWNER 2026-10-22 (quoted): "Make it something like \"Aldous is too stunned to do anything\" or levels of being stunned or whatever affect that is delaying his round of inaction" = the skip line names the status that caused the skip (e.g. "Aldous is too stunned to do anything."), authored per status, with a default built from the status label.
2026-10-22 BRIEF (skipped combat turn names its cause; batch "polish-engine-1", row 3 of 6; kernel_api 1.112). Kit: docs/briefs/brief-kit.md. Handoff threshold: docs/WORKFLOW.md#token-hygiene.
Goal: when a body's statuses bar its blow (mechanics.md:2542), the fight log says who skipped and why. Owner (quoted above): the line names the causing status, authored per status, default from the status label.
Facts: statuses have no levels or intensity (StatusDefinition: label, narration {applied, tick, expired, observed?}, blocks/allows...); "levels of stun" are separate authored statuses, content only. The Book's text(key) ignores bindings and participants, so the Book composes the default line; an authored key is shown whole.
Player text (default): NPC "<Name> is too <label> to do anything." (label = text(status.label), lowercase by lint); the player's own blow "You are too <label> to do anything."
Contract: StatusDefinition `narration.skipped?: TextKey` (where `narration.observed` lives; kernel_api at least 1.112; key in the text catalog). No new DomainEvent: the Book reads receipt lines and no reaction consumer exists (name it in the handback if the PM wants `turn_skipped` later). The line is a Text: default `{key:'combat.skipped', participants:{actor:<body>}, bindings:{status:<label key>}}` (engine key, as resource.short), authored `{key: spec.narration.skipped, participants:{actor}}`.
Engine (TS): kernel/ts/src/mechanics/combat/round_attack.ts:65 is the silent return; push the note on `r.notes` (round.ts:96 joins notes into the receipt; sibling round_flow.ts:54). The cause: the first active status on the attacker barring `attack` (a `barring` reader beside `statusAllows`, kernel/ts/src/mechanics/status/shared.ts; one scan). Player, foe and ally alike. Loaders: kernel/ts/src/content/cartridge_status.ts:48-52 `floorOf` + `check.text`; lib/loka/content/status.ex:76 `floors` + its narration key check; protocol/fixtures/loader_floors.json case for 1.112, red control in both kernels.
Book: logs.ts narration lines compose `combat.skipped` from `participants.actor` (name as words.ts `answer` does for `located`; the player's body: "You") and `bindings.status`.
Save: none (receipt narration only). Realm: the note names the round's attacker.
Tests, red controls: kernel/ts/test/status_readers.test.ts:121,134 assert the receipt line literal (red: delete the push); an authored `skipped` wins; a fleeing fearful pack member adds no line; both loaders refuse `skipped` below 1.112 and an unknown key. Book: NPC and player defaults (red: swap the name lookup).
Docs: mechanics.md:2542-2544, cartridge.md Status declarations (~:1760), book-ui.md Combat interaction (~:484), docs/MECHANICS-TOOLBOX.md if it lists the gap. Content: none (toolbox_showcase stays at 1.110; the default line covers the golem).

title: Homestead playtest: Book UI findings (designer, polish phase)
description:
Designer issue for the polish phase. Source: blind playtest of the Homestead district (loka-y6yg.22), report worktrees.noindex/playtest-homestead/playtest-homestead-report.md; screenshots in worktrees.noindex/playtest-homestead/playtest-homestead-screens/. Seen at 1440 px only; the phone-width layout is not covered (check at 390 px). The raw "action.take:" key leak is a content bug filed separately.

1. Dialogue card accumulates the transcript; the opener "Knife, axe or saw? ..." repeats on every Talk and after every learn (eight copies by the fifth lesson). Show the current opener plus the last reply.
2. Stale status lines: "Whittling: learned; currently qualified. The carpenter teaches it free."; Character sheet "Carpentry, level 2 - qualified; Cut wood well first (woodcutting 2)." keeps prerequisite text; "Stored." stays on plot and trough cards. Status line should describe current state only.
3. Contextual verbs (Give an apple, Water a plot, Cast the rod at the pond) are three taps deep (Contents > Inventory > item) and last in the item card list; the croft shows Cast as a room action. Surface them as room actions or at the top of the card.
4. Container cards list one "Put X in Y" row per held item, including nonsense (axe in a seed sack, eel in a plot), four rows for four logs. Group identical items; offer sensible targets only.
5. "Nothing to do here." shows above disabled rows (cook card after learning) and beside a status line (cots, pond).
6. Bare exit word: "up"/"down" renders as a lone token after the Word section on the lane and croft pages (screenshot-1792158716781-4.jpg). The room prose cause is in a content issue; the Book should not print a stray token.
7. Word box reads as a command line ("Word / Type a word"); it is Say. Suggest "Say a word". It also vanished on the carpenter's shop page after a Contents visit and returned in the next room.
8. Action label grammar: "Talk the carpenter" (Talk to), "Cast the rod the pond" (into the pond).
9. Two Leave controls on the dialogue card ("Leave" above lessons, "Leave the conversation" below).
10. Inventory does not stack ("a log" x4, "a wooden spoon" x2) and shows no pennies (only on the Character sheet "pennies 0 / 100").
11. Position control is a silent cycle (standing > sitting > resting > sleeping) with no message or picker.
12. Character sheet skill headings clip under the sticky footer ("Forestry" cut by the Back to World bar), screenshot-1792158943989-5.jpg; check at 390 px.
13. Heavy fixtures list a Take row that can never work (plot, pond, trough); consider hiding Take on fixtures rather than a "too heavy" note (design call).
notes: Merged 2026-10-22: x6t.54 homestead verbs read as container moves (plant = Put a seed in a plot; hens offer only Attack a hen; Carve a spoon failure shows only 'The stick splits.'); 390 px walk at e064721d.

AGENTS.md Simplicity and Writing tests, docs/lessons/checks.md. Focused checks only, under nice -n 10;
run the red-control script you change (the slice's own controls only), never a full suite. Every new
control must fail on today's origin/main code (demonstrate it: run it against the unfixed script once).
Before handback merge the latest origin/main into the branch. Self-review: /code-review medium <branch>.
Push with bin/push_slice.sh, then bin/wait_ci.sh <sha> in the background; hand back only on green
ci.yml and book-e2e.yml. Handback: PR number, exact head, check table, /code-review result, open items.
No subagents. Handoff threshold ~220k tokens: past it, commit and hand back a short state note.
Machine load: the PM runs three developers at once; keep long runs in the background.
Stop and ask the PM if: a fix needs a change outside the files in scope, or a doc rule conflicts.

an unset or empty value keeps the default 30; anything not all digits (thirty, 1.5, -1, ' 5') prints a
usage line and exits 2 before any mutant runs. Decide and state whether 0 is valid (today 0 = every mutant
TIMEBOX, which the o6r3 slice may use in its control: keep 0 valid).
Red control in integration_red_controls.sh: MUTATE_MINUTES=thirty exits 2 under both sh and bash; red on
origin/main's mutate.sh. The setup-time budget half of the issue (mutate_diff.sh:101-126) is NOT yours:

runs in parallel. Do not touch mutate_diff.sh, developer.md, reviewer.md or CHECKS.md.

Focused tests only, under nice -n 10, long runs in the background; never a full suite. Every new test or

handback. /code-review medium <branch>. Push with bin/push_slice.sh, bin/wait_ci.sh <sha> in the
background; hand back on green ci.yml and book-e2e.yml: PR, exact head, check table, /code-review result,
open items, under 250 words. No subagents. Handoff threshold ~220k tokens.

title: Homestead playtest: heavy fixture cards show raw key 'action.take:' (showcase text.json lacks action.take)
description:
Playtest (loka-y6yg.22, report in worktrees.noindex/playtest-homestead): every heavy fixture card (seed sack, plot, cot, pond, nest box, trough, croft plot) shows the first line "action.take: too heavy to carry." The key prefix leaks.

Cause: the Book prints an unavailable Take as "<catalog label>: too heavy to carry" (docs/system/book-ui.md "Item details and Take/Drop"). The label is the action label key "action.take". cartridges/toolbox_showcase/text.json has no "action.take" entry (it has action.eat and action.fish only), so the key shows raw. cartridges/ashmere_sampler/text.json:78 defines "action.take": "Take" and the Book test mobile/app/book/polish_detail.test.ts:336 expects "Take: too heavy to carry."

Repro: web Book, Holding farm yard, Contents, tap the seed sack.
Fix: add "action.take": "Take" to cartridges/toolbox_showcase/text.json (check other action.* keys the showcase lacks: drop, give, put) and re-pin protocol/fixtures/toolbox_showcase_hash.json. Add a loader or test guard that every action label key used by the engine resolves in text.
Screenshot: playtest-homestead-screens/screenshot-1792157804986-1.jpg

title: Homestead playtest: barter text 'Your order is still open.' after the trade completed
description:
Playtest (loka-y6yg.22): after "Trade two pelts for a knife" completed and the knife was in hand, the farmer card reads "Your order is still open." It looks like a stuck order.

Cause: the engine refuses a repeat of an entitlement-with-escrow service with the fixed key service.order_open (kernel/ts/src/mechanics/service/shared.ts:58; cartridge_services.ts:110,130). In a barter the entitlement stays true after the trade (docs/system/mechanics.md, Gift and barter: "a retry reads service.order_open"), so the text is wrong there. The showcase text is cartridges/toolbox_showcase/text.json:861. The same key also serves the cook's real open stew order and the build escrow, so one wording must fit all or the key must become per-service.

Repro: farmer, give two pelts via knife_for_pelts, reopen the farmer card.
Fix options: reword service.order_open to something true for all three uses ("That is already settled." or "Already done."), or give the service an authored headroom text key if the schema allows. Re-pin showcase_homestead.test.ts:406 text if it checks wording; re-pin the hash fixture.

title: Homestead playtest: room prose omits exits (farm yard east/south, lane up)
description:
Playtest (loka-y6yg.22): room prose omits exits the sign sends the player to, so a player who trusts the prose thinks the places are missing.

- farm_yard (cartridges/toolbox_showcase/text.json:764): "The lane is north and a glade opens west." Exits also include east (pond) and south (farm_kitchen); the Holding sign names both ("the pond east of her yard", "the cook south of the yard").
- holding_lane (text.json:785): names west, south, east but not up (croft). The Book then shows a bare "up" token after the Word section (also holding_croft).
Repro: read the Farm Yard and Holding Lane pages, compare with the Map.
Fix: add the missing exits to the prose (use the [word](detail) link style the other rooms use). Re-pin the hash fixture. Note the sign (readable.sign_homestead) says "Two timbers raise a hut" and "fell the oak twice"; a timber takes two logs, so a literal reader chops twice and saws once. Consider "four logs" wording (designer text; check with the plan 4 sign line).
Screenshot: playtest-homestead-screens/screenshot-1792158716781-4.jpg

title: Homestead playtest: lane prose and stakes text do not change after the hut is built
description:
Playtest (loka-y6yg.22): after "You raise a timbered hut to the north." the Holding Lane description is unchanged: "...a row of stakes that mark a plot north of the lane." and names no north exit. Only the Map shows "Go north". Room prose lags the built state.

Cause: cartridges/toolbox_showcase/text.json:785 (room.holding_lane.description) has no variant for the built hut, and the stakes detail (text.json:125, detail.plot_stakes: "You could raise a hut here.") keeps promising a hut after one stands. Same for the croft site (holding_croft).
Repro: complete the carpentry loop through Raise a timbered hut, return to the lane.
Fix: add a description variant on the built north room (or a room_line variant on the stakes) that reads "A timbered hut stands north of the lane." Check which condition op can read a built room or the construction row; if none exists, file the gap under loka-kgd as a toolbox finding (kin of loka-kgd.163 item 1). Re-pin the hash.

title: Homestead playtest: fishing says 'you land it' when nothing lands; no hour or weather hint
description:
Playtest (loka-y6yg.22): five casts after the first eel (hours 亥, 子, 丑, 寅, clear then drought) all said "Nothing bites." Nothing says which hour or weather bites, and the cook's stew (two fish) stayed out of reach in 80 minutes.

Verified in the cartridge: the pond bite window is by design (plan 4 step 10: trout 06-18, eel at night, one eel_01, salmon in rain; cartridges/toolbox_showcase/reactions/trout.json, eel.json, salmon.json), so the fish supply is correct. The content bug is feedback:
1. recipes/fish.json (and fish_croft.json): the success outcome narration is always narration.fish.bite "Something bites; you land it on the bank." (text.json:532) even when the bite event replenishes nothing (eel already taken, trout out of window). That line is false in that case. The failure line "Nothing bites." (text.json:533) is the only honest miss, and it fires only on the 50% luck check.
2. No line tells the player the water is quiet for now (hour or weather), the sign says only "bites by the hour and the weather".
Repro: cast at night after the eel is taken, or by day with both trout taken.
Fix: author a quiet-water narration for a bite that lands nothing (replenish.run yielding nothing, if the reaction can branch) or move the "you land it" line behind the replenish; add a room line or the sign a hint of hours ("trout by day, eel by night, salmon in rain"). Check the plan sign text before editing (designer text).

title: Homestead playtest: croft plot has no seed source or hint
description:
Playtest (loka-y6yg.22): "Up the croft is the same again" (Holding sign) but the croft plot has no seed source: no seed sack in holding_croft, and the farm yard sack held one turnip seed, already sown.

Cause: plan 4 says the croft holds "a second plot and a second sack" (docs/showcase/homestead-district.md, Rooms and map), but cartridges/toolbox_showcase has one seed_01 (items/seed_01.json) and no croft sack. reactions/sow.json starts growing and growing_croft together on that one seed, so the croft plot can only grow by carrying the same seed up. Nothing tells the player that.
Repro: go up from the lane, open the croft plot and the room contents.
Fix: either add a croft sack with its own seed (and a sow reaction for it), or add a croft plot description line ("Bring a seed up from the yard") and fix the plan line. Decide with the PM; the test pin is kernel/ts/test/showcase_homestead.test.ts croft sandbox (~l.668).

description:

Known design limit: rest with the cot works only when dropped in the lane (reaction cot_rest authored room holding_lane); resting in the built hut applies nothing (plan 4 Toolbox finding 1, tracked in loka-kgd.163 item 1), and the player rested in the hut.
Repro: carpenter's shop, take the axe, rug, sticks, then Take the cot; later raise the hut, drop the cot there, Rest.
Fix: confirm the load, then add a hint to the cot description or the sign ("drop it on the lane to rest").

# Brief: hosted sim job time regression after #414 (Beads loka-y6yg.37)

Lane: Hosted PR off origin/main. Branch `fix/sim-time-law`, worktree `../worktrees.noindex/sim-time` (`git worktree add -b fix/sim-time-law ../worktrees.noindex/sim-time origin/main`; `bin/worktree_setup.sh`). Model: Opus. Review: one Opus reviewer (record only if engine/save/protocol contract changes). Handoff threshold ~220k tokens. Timebox: 90 minutes to a root cause; if none, stop and return findings.

## Evidence
Hosted ci.yml `sim` job (`npm run test:sim` in kernel/ts = test/sim.test.ts, 10,000 fresh sequences with CI set; timeout 10 min):
- M15 head bdc471e2 (before #414): 297 s.
- #414 heads c57c5a4c and 0da88ad8 (now main, merge 03c10e48-ish): 553 s and 564 s.
- Draft #415 (magic M1, without #414): 366 s. Together they will cross the 10-minute timeout.
#414 (loka-y6yg.32/.33) was content only: the showcase market guard now has `disposition.arrest` into a new cell + drain (cartridges/toolbox_showcase), a `charge` reaction, a jailer dialogue, a grate and force recipe.
Prior lesson (HANDOFF 2026-10-16): the first concealment status made every visibility check sort all statuses and the sim job timed out; fixed in kernel/ts/src/mechanics/status/shared.ts. A content change can create a perf cliff.

## Goal
Find which code path the #414 content makes slow (profile sim.test.ts locally on main vs main with #414 reverted — `git revert -m 1 <#414 merge>` in a scratch branch — e.g. `node --cpu-prof`, or time per sequence), and fix the root cause in shared code once (likely the arrest/hostile check on every move, `hostileAt` in kernel/ts/src/mechanics/disposition.ts, or a reaction/dialogue scan), not by trimming content or lowering the sequence count. Behavior must not change: existing arrest/trial/jail/showcase tests stay green unchanged.
Run the sim test locally ONCE per variant in the background (it is ~5 min under CI=1; tell the PM if a run will exceed 10 min). Report local before/after times and the root cause with file:line.

## Acceptance
- Local sim time with the fix back near the pre-#414 baseline (state both numbers, same machine, same settings).
- If the fix is an engine change: a focused test that names the break if one is natural (a perf budget is not required); mutants on any new conditional.
- No change to cartridge content unless the cause is a content authoring mistake (then say so).

# Brief: split the hosted sim job and cut the harness re-resolve (Beads loka-y6yg.37)

Lane: Hosted PR off origin/main, branch `ci/sim-split`, worktree `../worktrees.noindex/sim-split` (`git worktree add -b ci/sim-split ../worktrees.noindex/sim-split origin/main`; `bin/worktree_setup.sh`). Model: Opus. Review: one Opus reviewer, PR comments. Handoff ~220k. Read docs/lessons/checks.md first.

## Evidence (from the diagnosis, loka-y6yg.37 notes)
Hosted runners are two-speed (~280 s vs ~540 s on the same code); the `sim` job (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:83-95`, `timeout-minutes: 10`, `npm run test:sim` = kernel/ts/test/sim.test.ts) holds the 10,000-fresh test (171 s fast / 352 s slow) and the showcase test (~163 s slow); the magic district adds ~70 s. Harness hot spot: kernel/ts/test/sim.ts:278 re-resolves every shared word on every step (`shared(after).some(w => !check('target_candidates_ordered', {resolution: resolve(...)}))`), ~22% of total.

## Goal
1. Split the sim job into two parallel jobs (fresh sequences; showcase) with the same 10-minute timeout each, so each has headroom on a slow runner. Use the existing test file split mechanism if one exists (node --test name pattern or a separate test file / npm script); keep `CI` set; keep the failure artifact upload per job with distinct names. Update docs/CHECKS.md (and anything listing the job name: grep `sim` in bin/session_status.sh, bin/wait_ci*, docs) so the PM's tools still find both jobs.
2. Cut the harness re-resolve without weakening the check: e.g. check `target_candidates_ordered` only for words whose resolution can have changed, or sample, ONLY if the invariant still fails on a planted misorder (red control: plant a misordered candidate list in a detached scratch worktree and show the check still fails). If no safe cut exists, skip 2 and say why.
Out of scope: engine code (activeStatuses sort, resolve scan: a later scale-benchmark item).

## Acceptance
- Hosted: both jobs appear on the pushed head (`gh run list --commit`); the PM reads their times.
- Local: run each new sim job's test command once in the background, report times (noisy machine; another developer is running tests).
- Red control for part 2 (failing line pasted).

title: Retro (E2 gate): items 1-4 approved, item 5 rejected
description:
Pattern retro after the E2 gate (2026-10-08, Sonnet, read-only). PROPOSED — awaiting owner approval; on approval move approved items into the next housekeeping batch, close rejected ones with a reason. PM recommendation: approve 1-4, reject 5.

# E2 gate pattern retro (2026-10-08)

1. Review findings are prose claims, not code (conf. high). Of ~14 findings in e2-s0..s5 records, 0 blockers and ~12 are overclaimed coverage or wrong citations: s2 nit1-2 (:233-236, reward_storage cite), s3 nit1-2 (r9c_elapsed_jobs.test.ts:213, :297-305), s4 should-fix 1-2 (header :257-259; PR table vs transcripts.test.ts:24), s5 nit1 (r9c_faults.test.ts:5), nit2 (README:117 line cite), gate nit (checklist:34), round-2 note. Every slice S2-S5 needed a fix round. Saving ~100-300k tokens/slice. Fix: developer.md rule: a "catches/only here/every" claim or file:line cite must be copied from a red-control or grep run in the same turn and listed in the PR body; reviewer samples 2.
2. Nit fix loops chain re-checks (conf. high). #321: 18 commits, 8 review-record commits, 5 review passes (Opus, Fable, Opus re-check x2) for 2 doc nits; the round-1 nit fix introduced a new wrong claim (second-opinion:35, "F4 is wrong"). Saving ~150k tokens + 2-3 CI runs per slice. Fix: WORKFLOW review section: comment/doc-only nits are batched or dropped, no re-review agent; PM checks the diff is comment-only.
3. docs/reviews/README.md index is a shared append point (conf. high). 3 of 4 main-merges on S1-S4 touched it on both sides (db10c963, 93fa596c, c913b0c0); each merge or record commit makes a new head. Cancelled PR-branch runs: s5 4, s0 4, s1 2; 12 of 48 main runs cancelled. Saving: ~1 merge and 1-2 CI runs per PR. Fix: delete the index (let check_docs glob docs/reviews) or have records land on the housekeeping branch.
4. Test-only TS diffs take the full pre-push lane (conf. medium). bin/ci_scope.sh treats mobile/authority/local-story and kernel/ts/test as "code", so check_all.sh runs mix test and credo (CI elixir job 65-93s, run 37808875291). Contributes to the load 50-152 timeouts. Fix: in pre-push, skip the Elixir half when the diff is only *.test.ts, kernel/ts/test or docs; cartridge/oracle paths stay full.
5. Draft PRs show a red check (conf. low, noise). ci-green runs `exit 1` when all jobs are skipped: 6 failures, ~3s each (37818225834, 37820341523, 37828128147, 37831054177). Cost is PM confusion, not compute. Fix: ci-green passes on draft when needs are skipped.

PM note on item 5: REJECT — the red ci-green on draft runs is the #315 safety feature (a skipped-everything draft run must not look green to auto-merge).
notes: Owner 2026-10-08: APPROVED items 1-4 (claims and file:line cites backed by a same-turn check and listed in the PR body; comment/doc-only nit fixes verified by the PM without a re-review agent; generate docs/reviews/README.md from record files (keep the one-line verdict from each record's first line); skip the Elixir half of pre-push for TS-test/docs-only diffs, hosted CI unchanged). REJECTED item 5: the red ci-green on draft runs is the #315 safety feature. Next: implement 1-4 in the next housekeeping batch.
close_reason: Owner 2026-10-08: items 1-4 approved -> loka-occ; item 5 rejected (ci-green red on skipped drafts is the #315 safety)

title: GameView: NPC condition band for the Look page
description: Engine slice of the NPC Look epic. GameView exposes each visible NPC's condition as a band (perfect health / lightly hurt / wounded / badly wounded / near death; exact band names and thresholds in the brief), never hp numbers, so the Book can write "She looks to be in perfect health." on the Look page. Protocol + TS kernel + Elixir projection as the repo requires; showcase use; Book consumer wired with a story.
notes:
BRIEF loka-ysbt (drafted 2026-10-30). Kit: docs/guides/brief-kit.md (read once; not copied). Handoff threshold: docs/WORKFLOW.md#token-hygiene (~220k: commit, hand back a state note).

GOAL. Every visible living NPC in GameView `entities` carries `band`, the key of its hp condition band, so the Book Look page (loka-aqnc) can write "She looks to be in perfect health." No hp number leaves the engine. Owner source: loka-ewtx description (quoted there).
Size S. Lane: Hosted PR. Branch feat/npc-band from main. Developer Opus. kernel_api 1.123 (assigned up front; see the epic run-order note). Composition: a derived query, no state, no writes.

GOVERNING. docs/system/protocol.md:387-396 (band rule: first row whose cut reaches, pool bands else world.bands else engine default; the combat opponent `band` precedent "only while the player sees it and it lives"); docs/system/mechanics.md:305-306; docs/system/cartridge.md:158 (band tables); docs/system/book-ui.md:705-707 (combat band phrase from `band.<key>` cartridge words, "no number") is the wording precedent the Look page reuses. Owner decision mechanics-vs-numbers (AGENTS.md): no new names or thresholds in the engine; the keys are the cartridge's own (showcase hp bands cartridges/toolbox_showcase/cartridge.json:172-187 = ready 100 / hurt 50 / dying 0; engine default kernel/ts/src/view/resources.ts:10-24 perfect_health..dying).
ENGINE THAT MAKES IT POSSIBLE. kernel/ts/src/view/resources.ts:47-56 `bandOf(world, holder, k)` -> {current, maximum, band, tone}; kernel/ts/src/view/combat.ts:39-42 uses it per foe; kernel/ts/src/view/view.ts:154-186 `within` already filters `living` and `visible`, :217-253 `viewOf` builds the EntityView (no hp field today).

CHANGE. view.ts `viewOf`: `...(e.kind === 'npc' && { band: bandOf(world, id, 'hp').band })` (only `.band`; never spread the object). Schema: protocol/gameview.schema.json EntityView (:488-588, additionalProperties false) adds optional `band` typed as the combat opponent's `band`; regenerate with bin/regen.sh (contracts.gen.ts). Bump kernel/ts/src/runtime/world.ts:108 and cartridges/toolbox_showcase/cartridge.json:8 to 1.123; bin/regen_hash_fixture.sh cartridges/toolbox_showcase protocol/fixtures/toolbox_showcase_hash.json. Spec: one sentence in docs/system/protocol.md after :396: each visible living NPC entity carries `band` by the same rule and table (cite loka-ysbt). Elixir: n/a (lib/loka has no GameView/EntityView projection; only `mix loka.compile` via the hash regen).
Files in: view/view.ts, protocol/gameview.schema.json, kernel/ts/src/contracts.gen.ts (generated), runtime/world.ts:108, cartridges/toolbox_showcase/cartridge.json:8, protocol/fixtures/toolbox_showcase_hash.json, docs/system/protocol.md, one test in kernel/ts/test/npc_hp.test.ts (or view_actor.test.ts). Out: resources.ts, combat.ts, mobile/ (consumer not on main), lib/.

ACCEPTANCE (literal; expected values hand-checked, not from bandOf).
1. Showcase goblin (npcs/goblin.json hp 6/6) seen: `band: 'ready'`; hp 3 -> 'hurt' (300 >= 50*6); hp 4 -> 'hurt'; hp 2 -> 'dying'; hp 0 -> the NPC is absent from entities (living filter), no band on a corpse.
2. A test world with no world.bands and no pool bands: 10/10 -> 'perfect_health'; 9/10 -> 'slightly_scratched'; 5/10 -> 'many_nasty_wounds'; 1/10 -> 'almost_dead'.
3. Items and the player's body never carry `band` (`'band' in itemView === false`).
4. No `current`, `maximum`, `hp` or `tone` key on any entity.
5. `validate('GameView', view)` is [] (as kernel/ts/test/c4_pack.test.ts:83); schema mutant sweep per docs/lessons/contracts.md.
RED CONTROLS: `.tone` instead of `.band` -> row 1 fails; spreading `...bandOf()` -> row 4 fails; dropping the npc guard -> row 3 fails.

SHOWCASE USE. No content change: goblin hp 6 and the showcase hp bands; the Book reads existing `band.ready/hurt/dying` keys (text.json:65,58,55).
BOOK CONSUMER + STORY. The Look page is not on main: follow-up for the polish session in loka-aqnc: condition sentence from `bandPhrase` (mobile/app/book/model.ts:191 on polish/session-2026-10-23), designer words it; story Pages/NPC Look gains a band variant there. This slice adds nothing under mobile/. State this in the handback.
LESSONS: docs/lessons/mechanics.md, docs/lessons/contracts.md.
SCOPE TRIGGER: stop and ask if `bandOf` can throw for an NPC (resource.ts:72 `level` undefined -> `!`), if the Book needs `tone`, or if a per-NPC band table is wanted.
SHARED FILES: with loka-oc5i view.ts viewOf, gameview.schema.json EntityView, protocol.md GameView clause (never concurrent); with every epic slice world.ts:108, cartridge.json:8, the showcase hash fixture (PM keeps the higher version and reruns the regen at merge).
PM 2026-10-30 ruling: band only for an NPC with its own hp (as living() tests); no hp -> no band (cannot be hurt, Book writes no condition sentence). Developer found NaN level -> TypeError in bandOf for regen pools without NPC hp (7 samplers).

description: Found in loka-ysbt /code-review (2026-10-30): kernel/ts/src/view/combat.ts:42 calls bandOf for a foe; an NPC foe with no hp of its own in a cartridge whose hp pool has regen gets a NaN level (foundation/resource.ts:62) and bandOf (view/resources.ts:52) throws a TypeError, crashing the combat view. notes: BRIEF (PM 2026-10-30; owner: 'also do daha and zvwh this session'). Lane: hosted PR, bug fix, S. Branch fix/zvwh-combat-band, worktree zvwh-combat-band. Check every bandOf caller (ast-grep) and the schema: combat opponent band must be optional if it can now be absent (if the schema requires it, make it optional and say so). Acceptance: on a regen-hp sampler with an hp-less NPC foe (theft or fear sampler; pick one that can start combat), the combat view builds without throwing and the foe has no band; a hp foe still gets its band. Red control: revert the guard, the test throws TypeError. No kernel_api bump unless the schema changes (then the next free version above main and at_least on affected cartridges, release-pin rule in epic loka-ewtx notes). Focused tests, nice -n 10.
